## Reproduction

Node v22.23.2, live main `a074172f` (04:35Z).

Pure guard + reachability, one script:
```
node --import tsx --test .local/ipv4-mapped-ssrf-repro.test.ts
```
3/3 fail; and an end-to-end check of the same URL:
```
guard: accepted | fetch status: 200 body: LOCAL-LOOPBACK-RESPONSE
```
(run against a local server bound to 127.0.0.1 — `assertPublicUrl("http://[::ffff:7f00:1]:<port>/")` returns instead of throwing, and `fetch` then reaches loopback.)

## Current vs expected

Current: `isBlockedAddress("::ffff:7f00:1")` and `("::ffff:a9fe:a9fe")` return `false`, so `assertPublicUrl` accepts the hex IPv4-mapped/compatible forms and `web_fetch` can reach loopback and the link-local metadata endpoint.
Expected: every IPv4-mapped/compatible IPv6 literal is judged by its embedded IPv4, so both are rejected with `PublicUrlError("local and private network URLs are not allowed")`.

## Code evidence (live main a074172f)

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts:58-69`:
```ts
function ipv6Blocked(address: string): boolean {
  const value = normalizeIpv6(address);
  ...
  // IPv4-mapped/compatible forms must be judged by their embedded IPv4.
  const embedded = value.match(/(\d{1,3}(?:\.\d{1,3}){3})$/);
  if (embedded?.[1]) return ipv4Blocked(embedded[1]);
  return false;
}
```
The regex only matches the dotted form; `::ffff:7f00:1` / `::ffff:a9fe:a9fe` (and `0:0:0:0:0:ffff:7f00:1`) fall through to `return false`. `:72-77` dispatches every IPv6 literal here. Gate: `packages/data-source/src/web/native/index.ts:167` `: await assertPublicUrl(input.request);`.

## Suggested red test

Extend `packages/data-source/src/web/native/providers.test.ts` → `web_fetch refuses private and loopback targets`:
```
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("::ffff:7f00:1"), true);
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("0:0:0:0:0:ffff:a9fe:a9fe"), true);
await assert.rejects(assertPublicUrl("http://[::ffff:7f00:1]:8080/"), PublicUrlError);
await assert.rejects(assertPublicUrl("http://[::ffff:a9fe:a9fe]/latest/meta-data/"), PublicUrlError);
```
Command: `cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/web/native/providers.test.ts`. Verified red on current main (3/3, `false !== true` and `Missing expected rejection.`).

Fix: expand the IPv6 literal to 8 hextets; when the first six are 0 and hextet 7 is `0xffff` (mapped) or all seven are 0 (compatible), build the dotted quad from the last two hextets and reuse `ipv4Blocked`. `services/runner/src/egress-gateway.ts:123` repeats the dotted-only regex, but its input comes from a resolver, so this path is the one reachable from a model-supplied URL.

## Duplicate check (open + closed, REST search)

`ipv4-mapped`, `isBlockedAddress`, `url-guard`, `SSRF`, `assertPublicUrl`, `web_fetch private network`, `"::ffff"`, `mapped address` → 0 hits. Nearest: #326/#329 (closed; the opposite — public URLs falsely rejected). No open PR touches `url-guard.ts`.

issue:666.body:
## Summary

This issue is the **desktop shell** of the Windows desktop delivery (#400): the Electron application that turns the platform layer (#639) and the runtime (#643) into a double-clickable Windows product. The shell owns the backend stack lifecycle (start, readiness mirroring, teardown), drives the assisted first-run wizard, loads the web UI with the local access token injected, and packages the backend tree into a per-user NSIS installer.

It lands as a new top-level `win_desktop/` directory, which answers #400's open question about where the shell lives in the repo. It is a build host, not a workspace package: `win_desktop/` keeps its own pnpm workspace (own lockfile) so the root tree is untouched.

## Where the product stands today

| Area | Current state |
|---|---|
| Packaging | No Windows installer; a Windows user runs the backend from a dev checkout. |
| First run | Nothing walks a non-developer through a data-directory choice or port conflicts. |
| Robustness | A single busy service port (e.g. a stale instance still bound) kills startup with a raw bind error; a failed install leaves no install-time log; uninstall leaves shortcuts and >260-char data trees behind. |
| UI entry | No single window that injects the local access token into the SPA. |

## Goals

- **Lifecycle**: start the full stack via `scripts/start-stack.mjs` (delivered by the runtime issue), mirror its readiness stream into a loading stage with per-step heartbeats, and tear everything down on exit — even when the renderer is gone.
- **Assisted first run**: a wizard reduced to the one decision that must precede everything — the data directory (warns at 180 path chars, blocks past 240; the choice is mirrored to a file the uninstaller reads). Boot, self-check and model setup stay in the SPA.
- **Port resilience**: epoch-based allocation that bind-probes the whole service family, not one port, so one busy consumer shifts the family and the URL tracks it.
- **Installer**: per-user NSIS without UAC (license → directory → progress → finish); install diagnostics written into `$INSTDIR\logs`; a clean-uninstall story — shortcuts always removed, long-path-safe data removal, ghost uninstall-registry-key self-heal, silent uninstall never deletes user data.
- **Failure feedback**: when the stack fails, the wizard sees one line per conflicted port plus guidance, and "open log" always has a file to open.

## Non-goals

- No backend logic — everything the shell starts comes from #639/#643.
- No macOS/Linux desktop packaging (the shell is Windows-focused; cross-platform packaging is a separate discussion).
- No auto-update channel (the payload layout is blockmap-friendly by construction; serving updates is out of scope).
- No code signing.

## Root decisions

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Location | top-level `win_desktop/`, standalone workspace | #400 left the shell's home open. A build host with its own lockfile and one `app-builder-lib` patch must not perturb the root workspace — root globs do not match it, so root-level `pnpm -r` is unaffected. |
| Relationship to `apps/*` | the shell *loads* the web UI, never contains it | `win_desktop/` is the Electron host; the frontend it loads stays under `apps/`. |
| Payload layout | backend tree as plain `extraResources` files | No physical split: unchanged big payload blocks keep their blockmap entries, so differential updates never re-download them. |
| Payload source | assembled from this repo's checkout (`--repo` overrides) | One source of truth: `scripts/assemble-backend.mjs` deploys `@sciencediscovery/api`, stages the runner, and rewrites venv trampolines to the install layout. |
| Port allocation | bind-probing epochs per service family | The field case that forced this: a stale instance held one non-epoch port while every epoch port was free — a single-port probe missed it and the stack died on bind. |
| Uninstall data policy | keep by default, opt-in delete, silent never deletes | Automation safety: `/S` must never wipe user data; deletion is an explicit checkbox only. |
| Install diagnostics | markers into `$INSTDIR\logs` | An install-time failure otherwise leaves nothing to look at — the user cannot find user-data logs before first run ever happens. |

## Delivery

- `win_desktop/src/` — main process; wizard (state machine + data-dir evaluation + api); `stack.ts` / `bootstrap.ts` (lifecycle + payload path substitution); `ports.ts` (epochs); `proxy.ts` / `preload.ts` (token injection); `loading-stage.ts` (heartbeat mapping); `window-state.ts`; `ui-retry.ts`.
- `win_desktop/test/` — 14 `node:test` suites, no Electron launch needed.
- `win_desktop/scripts/` — esbuild build, dev runner, backend assembly, icon generator.
- `win_desktop/build/` — NSIS include (presentation, diagnostics, uninstall options), uninstall helper (C# + PowerShell long-path removal), license, icons.
- `win_desktop/patches/app-builder-lib@26.15.3.patch` — NSIS progress-bar presentation fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pnpm -C win_desktop install`, `typecheck`, and `test` green on a real Windows host (113 tests across 14 suites).
- [ ] The root workspace untouched: no root file changes; root globs do not match `win_desktop/`.
- [ ] No internal planning shorthand in comments, test names, or identifiers.
- [ ] Real-machine installer evidence: install log under `$INSTDIR\logs`; uninstall keeps data by default; silent uninstall never deletes.

## Open questions

1. The shell's `node:test` suite needs no Electron — should a `windows-latest` CI job eventually run it (same CI gap as #639/#643)?
2. Update serving is unaddressed (the layout is ready for it) — separate issue if auto-update is wanted.

## Related

- Parent: #400
- Stacks on #639 (platform) and #643 (runtime): assembling a full payload requires the runtime's startup chain, so the merge order is platform → runtime → shell.
- The web UI the shell loads stays under `apps/` and is not part of this issue.

issue:668.body:
## Goal

Track the remaining external-agent interoperability work after PR #424 merged the initial Specialist runtime slice. This issue deliberately keeps two protocol directions separate while coordinating their shared safety, session and artifact requirements.

## Delivered baseline

PR #424 merged support for explicit Specialist tasks using Codex, Claude Code and ACP executables, normalized task/event/handoff behavior, independent concurrent Workspace/Runner execution, configuration cards and thin runtime diagnostics. It does **not** complete either original Issue’s full acceptance criteria.

## Workstream A — ScienceDiscovery hosts external Specialist runtimes (remaining from #385)

Keep the existing Specialist model and require explicit `task(specialistId=…)` targeting for non-native execution. The platform remains the authority for Workspace, permissions, secrets, artifacts, audit and cancellation.

- [ ] Validate and document a successful live-auth matrix for supported Codex, Claude Code and ACP providers, including task completion, cancellation, timeout and declared-artifact handoff. Report unavailable credentials/providers as blocked, never passed.
- [ ] Decide and implement the supported iCode adapter path, or explicitly defer it with product rationale.
- [ ] Complete the Skills/MCP/tool bridge so an external runtime can request platform-governed tools without gaining undeclared native permissions.
- [ ] Finish the product configuration surface aligned with #278: persisted/this-run/alternate credential choices, usable error recovery and no secret leakage to catalog bodies, argv, logs or artifacts.
- [ ] Add the deferred UX: runtime picker/probe, fallback controls and handoff/diagnostics visibility.
- [ ] Add the deferred reliability coverage: multi-SDK stress, escape/isolation regressions, protocol backpressure/error bounds and process-crash recovery semantics.
- [ ] Evaluate deferred orchestration/operations separately: quota/priority/dependency graphs, shared pools only with an isolation design, and fuller metrics/cluster/multi-tenant monitoring.

## Workstream B — ScienceDiscovery is an ACP v1 Agent for editors (remaining from #64)

Editors are ACP Clients; ScienceDiscovery is the spawned ACP Agent. This is not the same as Workstream A, where ScienceDiscovery drives an external agent.

- [ ] Provide a supported ACP v1 stdio JSON-RPC entry point and `initialize` capability negotiation; do not multiplex it with MCP stdio or require a browser first.
- [ ] Implement session lifecycle mapping: `session/new`, `session/prompt`, streaming `session/update`, `session/cancel`, recoverable Project/Session/Run context and absolute workspace mapping.
- [ ] Map ACP permission requests to the existing governance and sandbox path; the ACP route must not be less restrictive than the Web UI.
- [ ] Return standards-compliant JSON-RPC errors and advertise only implemented capabilities; document any research-specific extensions.
- [ ] Verify against an actual ACP Client (for example Zed or a VS Code ACP extension): launch, prompt, streamed text, at least one tool call and denied permission behavior.
- [ ] Add unit, conformance and isolated E2E coverage for version negotiation, cancellation, authentication if enabled, sandbox equivalence and secret/session-body log redaction.
- [ ] Publish editor configuration documentation. ACP Registry publication is a separate product decision and must not block local interoperability.

## Shared boundaries

- Secrets never enter Specialist catalog bodies, argv, artifacts or unauthenticated ACP traffic.
- Existing sandbox, artifact provenance and permission controls remain authoritative.
- ACP v2 remains non-default until it is stable and separately accepted.

Supersedes the remaining scope of #385 and #64. PR #424 is delivered baseline, not proof that the above acceptance is complete.

issue:669.body:
## Goal

Make literature reports and review outcomes honestly verifiable: readers should see the evidence supporting material claims, know when evidence could not be verified, and never mistake a partial Quick review for full claim-fidelity verification.

## Workstream A — claim-to-evidence excerpts (from #415)

- [ ] For each material quantitative or clinical claim in a literature report, retain a short source excerpt or structured claim-to-evidence table with stable identifier and usable locator (for example PMID/DOI plus abstract/full-text location where available).
- [ ] Include the evidence in saved report/review artifacts without flooding model context; preserve source provenance and retrieval metadata.
- [ ] When an excerpt cannot be obtained, record an explicit evidence gap rather than silently presenting the claim as fully supported.

## Workstream B — visible unverifiable states (from #560)

- [ ] Extend the evidence/review schema with a visible `UNVERIFIABLE` status (or equivalent reasoned states such as identity unresolved and provider unavailable).
- [ ] Preserve the reason, affected claim/citation and review coverage in reports and review summaries. Do not silently discard identity-resolution or provider-availability findings.
- [ ] Keep the existing policy distinction: provider failure is not proof that a citation is false; it is an explicit limitation on verification.
- [ ] Align reviewer Skill instructions and runtime normalization so emitted states are representable and auditable.

## Workstream C — truthful automatic-review scope (follow-up to closed #414)

- [ ] A format/provenance-only Quick review must present itself as partial/format-only and disclose skipped claim checks with a reason.
- [ ] A claim-checked literature review must identify which claims were checked, supported, unsupported or unverifiable.
- [ ] Add regressions for stale report reviews, missing primary deliverables and the prior false-looking `ACCEPT_AND_PROCEED` Quick outcome.

## Validation

- [ ] Reproduce the CRISPR base-editing literature-report scenario from #415 and verify human-readable claim evidence or explicit gaps.
- [ ] Cover identifier mismatch, unresolved identity, unavailable provider, conflicting evidence, missing locator and provider timeout paths.
- [ ] Test Quick/Deep UI and saved artifact semantics independently; mocked provider success alone is insufficient.
- [ ] Document the distinction among supported, unsupported, unverifiable and not-reviewed claims.

Consolidates the unfinished scope of #415 and #560 and retains the relevant transparency regression from closed #414.

issue:671.body:
## Summary

The desktop source viewer closes a triple-quoted string on the first `"""` that follows an odd *or even* number of backslashes. An even count does not escape the delimiter, so a legal, terminated string swallows the rest of the file: every following line is tokenised as `string`.

## Repro (live main `1e886583`)

Node v22.23.2, from the repository root:

```bash
cat > /tmp/t1.ts <<'TS'
import { highlightPython } from "./apps/desktop/src/app/python-source.ts";
const src = 'x = """a\\\\"""\ny = 2\n';
highlightPython(src).forEach((l, i) => console.log(i + 1, JSON.stringify(l)));
TS
node --import tsx /tmp/t1.ts
```

Observed:

```
1 [{"text":"x = "},{"kind":"string","text":"\"\"\"a\\\\\"\"\""}]
2 [{"kind":"string","text":"y = 2"}]
```

Expected: line 2 carries no `string` token, because `"""a\\"""` is a complete Python string (`\\` is one escaped backslash, so the delimiter is unescaped) and `y = 2` is code.

## Cause

`apps/desktop/src/app/python-source.ts:130-132`:

```ts
// An escaped delimiter is part of the string, not its end.
while (end > 0 && source[end - 1] === "\\") end = source.indexOf(delimiter, end + 1);
```

The test is "a backslash precedes the delimiter", not "an odd number of backslashes precedes it". `"""a\\"""` has two, so the real terminator is skipped and scanning resumes at the next `"""` — or at end of file, which is the failure above.

## Expected fix

Count the run of `\\` before the candidate and only skip when the count is odd (~5 lines, same function).

## Suggested red test

`apps/desktop/tests/python-source.test.ts` (exists; 8 tests, none covers an escaped backslash before a delimiter) — `a triple-quoted string ending in an escaped backslash does not swallow the code after it`:

```ts
const lines = highlightPython('x = """a\\\\"""\ny = 2\n');
assert.equal(lines[1]?.some((token) => token.kind === "string"), false);
```

```bash
node --import tsx --test apps/desktop/tests/python-source.test.ts
```

## Dedupe

Searched open+closed for `highlightPython`, `triple-quoted string view`, `"source view" python`: 0 hits. `#537` (closed) added highlighting to the web artifact preview, a different module.

Filed by ScienceDiscovery Product.

Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claim-Id: e973d679f15d40cb95aa52543bc510b2
Branch: dev2/fix/html-entity-single-pass
Base: 1e8865838ce8
At: 2026-10-29T04:56:50Z

## What is wrong

`decodeEntities` in `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:35-43` decodes in a loop over the `ENTITIES` table (`:25-33`), feeding each replacement's output into the next one, and the table starts with `&`. Escaped markup therefore decodes twice: `&lt;` becomes `<` and then `<`, `&amp;` becomes `&`. The numeric-reference branch (`:39-42`) accepts the whole `1 .. 0x10FFFF` range, so UTF-16 surrogate code points survive as lone surrogates.

## Reproduction (live main `1e8865838ce80b8519063e26b5910a5b23ff2027`)

The two functions copied verbatim from that blob, run with `node` (no dependencies):

```
$ node -e '...decodeEntities copied verbatim...'
"&lt;" -> "<"
"&amp;" -> "&"
"'" -> "'"
"'" -> "'"
"�" -> "\ud800"
" &lt;" -> " <"
```

## Expected

- One pass: every reference is consumed once and its output is not rescanned, so `&lt;` -> `<`, `&amp;` -> `&`.
- Numeric references that are surrogate code points (`0xD800`-`0xDFFF`) or non-characters (`0xFFFE`, `0xFFFF`) are left as written instead of being turned into invalid text.
- `'` (capital `X`) keeps working like `'`.

## Why it matters

The free search engines read public result pages and hand titles and snippets to `textOf`, which strips tags first (`:45-48`) and then calls `decodeEntities`. After the double decode, escaped markup is indistinguishable from real markup in the returned text, and a lone surrogate can reach JSON output and break UTF-8 encoding downstream.

## Fix scope

A single pass built from the same table: map each reference to its character, run one alternation regex over the input, and reject surrogate/non-character code points in the numeric branch. Tests in `packages/data-source/src/web/native/` alongside the existing ones. No new dependency.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claim-Id: 8a1b7dbd95c149489c75d01defcd079d
Branch: dev1/fix/fetch-document-codepoint-truncation
Base: 1e8865838ce8
At: 2026-10-29T04:57:48Z

## What is wrong

`document()` in `packages/data-source/src/web/native/fetch.ts:105-107` truncates the vendor's text with a raw `slice(0, 4_096)`, so a UTF-16 surrogate pair that straddles the budget is cut in half and the document handed to the model ends with a lone high surrogate.

## Reproduction (live main `1e8865838ce80b8519063e26b5910a5b23ff2027`)

`renderExaContents`/`renderTavilyExtract` both funnel through `document()`. Same logic copied verbatim, run with `node`:

```
$ node -e 'const MAX=4096; const text="x".repeat(MAX-1)+"😀"; console.log(JSON.stringify(text.slice(0,MAX).slice(-2)))'
"\ud83d"
```

The last code unit is `0xd83d` (high surrogate) with no low surrogate after it - an unpaired surrogate in the fetched document.

## Expected

Truncate at a code-point boundary, the way `#663` now does it for the artifact preview: drop the whole character instead of half of it, so the result is never longer than the budget and never contains a new unpaired surrogate.

## Why it matters

`web_fetch` output is fed back into prompts and can be cached and re-serialised as JSON; an unpaired surrogate is invalid UTF-8 text and `JSON.stringify` escapes it into a `\ud83d` sequence the model reads as a broken glyph. The same defect was reported for the artifact preview in `#660` and fixed there by `#663`; this call site is a different module (`packages/data-source/src/web/native/fetch.ts`) and is still raw, so this is not a duplicate.

## Fix scope

One small helper in the same file (or reuse of an existing code-point truncation helper if one is exported) plus its call in `document()`; tests next to the existing `renderExaContents`/`renderTavilyExtract` ones. About 10-15 lines, no new dependency.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claim-Id: 887ec7de37ba4023a1cc05f9ad23111f
Branch: dev2/fix/xlsx-1900-serial-epoch
Base: 1e8865838ce8
At: 2026-10-29T04:59:33Z

## What is wrong

`apps/desktop/src/app/xlsx.ts:170` fixes the 1900 date-system epoch at `Date.UTC(1899, 11, 30)` and `serialToText` (`:173-183`) applies it to every serial. The 1899-12-30 epoch is the compensation for Excel's fictitious 1900-02-29 and is only correct from serial 61 on; for serial 1-59 it lands one day early, so every date from 1900-01-01 to 1900-02-28 is displayed one day before the day Excel shows.

## Reproduction (live main `1e8865838ce80b8519063e26b5910a5b23ff2027`, Node v22.23.2)

A mock workbook built with `fflate`, `styles.xml` carrying `numFmtId="14"`, column A holding the serials below, read back through `readWorkbook`:

```
$ node --input-type=module -e '<mock workbook + readWorkbook, serials 1, 59, 60, 61, 45292>'
[["1899-12-31"],["1900-02-27"],["1900-02-28"],["1900-03-01"],["2024-01-01"]]
```

Expected (the Excel 1900 date system): serial `1` -> `1900-01-01`, `59` -> `1900-02-28`, `61` -> `1900-03-01`, `45292` -> `2024-01-01`. Serial `60` is Excel's non-existent 1900-02-29.

## Expected

Serials below 61 are counted from 1899-12-31 and serials from 61 on keep the 1899-12-30 epoch, i.e. a per-serial epoch (about five lines in `serialToText`). The 1904 date system branch is unaffected.

## Why it matters

Spreadsheet cells formatted as dates are one of the two things this preview exists for; silently shifting a whole two-month window in 1900 is a wrong answer with no visible error, and the same helper backs the cell text in the grid.

## Fix scope

One conditional epoch inside `serialToText`; a regression test in `apps/desktop/tests/xlsx.test.ts` (9/9 green today, no coverage for these serials). No new dependency.

issue:679.body:
Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claim-Id: dae5b8d1b8af4de3885faca176d3c50a
Branch: dev2/fix/cas-has-corrupt-object
Base: ad34dd7847f6
At: 2026-10-29T05:08:29Z

## What is wrong

`CasStore.has()` in `packages/cas/src/index.ts:74-82` answers the boolean existence question by calling `read()`. `read()` re-hashes the bytes and throws `CAS integrity failure` when a stored object no longer matches its digest, and `has()` only maps `ENOENT` to `false` (`:79`), so a corrupt object makes `has()` throw. Its sibling `verify()` (`:84-92`) deliberately maps the same condition to `false`. Two predicates over the same store therefore disagree: `verify()` says "not valid", `has()` raises.

## Reproduction (live main `ad34dd7847`, file blob `584cf1eaefc7ec9b5c4c2125de7bf13c39039ba0`)

```
$ node --import tsx -e '<put "hello world" via CasStore, then overwrite the blob with "HELLO WORLD">'
put -> b94d27b9934d 11
has before -> true
verify after corruption -> false
has after corruption -> THREW CAS integrity failure
```

The overwrite keeps the byte length, so this is exactly the "same size, different bytes" corruption case the store already detects elsewhere.

## Expected

`has(hash)` is a total boolean predicate: `true` only when the object is present and valid, `false` when it is missing **or corrupt** - the same answer `verify()` gives. A caller deciding "is this object still usable, or must I republish?" must not have to catch an untyped integrity error to find out.

## Why it matters

The store is used as a cache in front of publication paths (`put` / `retain` / republish decisions): those call `has()` to choose between "reuse" and "write it again". With a corrupt blob they crash with `CAS integrity failure` instead of taking the republish branch, and the error is thrown from a method whose contract is a boolean. PR `#657` made vanished refs republish; corrupt bytes are the neighbouring case and still have this shape.

## Fix scope

Extend the `has()` catch to map the integrity failure to `false` the way `verify()` already does (about two lines), plus one test next to the existing `index.test.ts` cases. No new dependency, no behaviour change for a valid or a missing object.

issue:8.body:
### 🚀 背景描述

ScienceDiscovery 已通过 operational logger 将服务日志写入数据目录下的 `logs/`，默认位置为 `.sciencediscovery-data/logs/`。其中 `api.log` 已包含 API 启动、部分组件状态与未分类异常，`runner.log` 记录 Runner 请求和沙箱执行，`run.log` 记录 Agent Run 生命周期。

当前缺口集中在 **Agent/LLM 看不到的框架内部链路**：

- MCP 客户端连接、重连、关闭及工具目录加载缺少完整的成功/失败日志；
- MCP stdio 子进程的 stderr 被忽略，进程启动或协议握手失败时缺少服务端原始线索；
- MCP 代理配置解析和运行时切换存在静默失败，且日志无法区分“配置了代理”和“当前传输实际应用代理”；
- 远端 Runner 的主机探测、直连、断线与 SSH 隧道错误主要停留在内存状态中，进程退出后难以追溯；
- 启动阶段部分组件初始化失败缺少统一、可检索的阶段事件。

本功能的目标是复用现有滚动日志，为这些框架链路补齐结构化、可关联、经过脱敏且有体积上限的诊断事件，让开发人员在 MCP、代理、远端 Runner 或启动组件发生故障时，能够仅通过日志定位失败阶段、目标、错误类别、耗时和重试情况。

本方案不是 Agent 操作审计能力，不要求 Agent 或 LLM 感知这些日志。

### 设计思路

#### 1. 存储与日志形式

- 复用现有 `<dataDir>/logs/api.log`，默认即 `.sciencediscovery-data/logs/api.log`；
- 继续使用 operational logger 的文本行格式、级别过滤和滚动策略；
- 沿用 `SCIENCE_AGENT_LOG_LEVEL`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_LOG_DIR`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_LOG_MAX_BYTES`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_LOG_MAX_BACKUPS` 配置；
- 默认单文件上限 10 MiB、保留 5 个备份；
- 不新增独立 audit JSONL、日志索引、日志文件清单、数据库表或 UI。

日志事件采用稳定事件名和扁平字段，例如：

```text
2026-09-10T08:00:00.000Z INFO [api] event=mcp.connection.succeeded serverId=... transport=stdio durationMs=42
```

#### 2. 覆盖范围

| 链路 | 需要记录的事件 | 关键字段 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 框架启动 | 组件初始化开始、成功、失败 | `component`、`durationMs`、`errorCode`、`error` |
| MCP 连接 | 开始、成功、失败、关闭、关闭失败 | `serverId`、`transport`、`endpointProtocol`、`endpointHost`、`durationMs` |
| MCP 工具目录 | 全部加载成功、单服务加载失败 | `serverId`、`toolCount`、`errorCode`、`error` |
| MCP 代理 | 配置加载、配置变更、解析失败 | `proxyMode`、`proxyApplied`、代理协议与主机 |
| MCP 调用 | 非语义性传输/服务端/超时/限流失败及重试调度 | `serverId`、`toolName`、`requestId`、`attempt`、`delayMs`、`errorCode` |
| 远端主机 | SSH 主机探测开始、成功、失败 | `hostId`、`host`、`port`、`durationMs`、`errorCode` |
| 远端 Runner | 连接开始、成功、失败、断线、关闭 | `runnerId`、`connectionMode`、`endpointHost`、`durationMs` |
| SSH 隧道 | 转发、stream、socket 失败 | `hostId`、`runnerId`、`errorCode`、`error` |

启动组件首批覆盖 Skill Catalog、自定义 MCP Server、Session Store、Artifact 恢复和 Run 恢复。已有 Runner、Memory Graph 等模块的日志继续使用原通道，本功能不重复记录其业务载荷。

#### 3. MCP stdio stderr

MCP stdio 子进程的 stderr 从忽略改为受控采集：

- 内存中最多保留 4 KiB 尾部，避免持续输出导致内存增长；
- 仅在连接、调用或关闭失败时附带最后 4 个非空行；
- 单条日志中的 stderr 摘要不超过 1 KiB；
- 成功路径不输出 stderr 内容；
- 摘要进入日志前执行统一脱敏。

该内容用于保留 MCP Server 自身的启动报错、依赖缺失、协议错误等直接证据，同时避免把完整进程输出写入日志。

#### 4. 代理语义

日志必须区分：

- `proxyMode`：当前解析到的代理配置模式；
- `proxyApplied`：当前 MCP transport 是否实际应用了该代理。

例如 stdio transport 不经过 HTTP 代理；HTTP/SSE transport 若底层实现尚未接入代理，也不能仅因存在代理配置就记录为已应用。日志只记录代理协议和主机，不记录完整 URL、用户名、密码或敏感查询参数。

#### 5. 脱敏、体积与可靠性边界

- 统一通过 `redactLogValue` 处理日志字段；
- 脱敏 Authorization/Bearer、token、secret、password、cookie、URL userinfo 及敏感 query 参数；
- 不记录 `args`、`body`、`content`、`input`、`messages`、`output`、`prompt`、`request`、`response`、完整 stdout/stderr 等大载荷；
- 错误消息及 stderr 摘要设置明确长度上限；
- 用户会话内容、模型输入输出、工具参数、工具结果正文不进入框架诊断日志；
- operational logger 保持 best-effort，日志目录创建、写入或轮转失败不能打断服务主路径。

#### 6. 代码落点

- `services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts`：框架组件初始化，以及 MCP/远端计算 logger 注入；
- `services/api/src/mcp/node-client.ts`：MCP 连接、目录、代理、调用重试与受控 stderr；
- `packages/executor/src/remote-compute.ts`：主机探测、远端 Runner 与 SSH 隧道生命周期；
- `packages/operational-logging/src/index.ts`：URL 凭据和敏感查询参数脱敏。

#### 7. 明确不在本功能范围内

- 不提供日志查看、搜索或下载 UI；
- 不生成日志索引或所有日志文件的清单；
- 不新增 Agent 可见事件，也不改变 Agent、Tool、MCP 的业务返回值；
- 不把用户会话、LLM 请求/响应、工具输入/输出复制到框架日志；
- 不实现代理健康检查、自动故障转移或代理管理面板；
- 不将本日志定义为不可篡改的合规审计账本；
- 不在本轮扩展 Paper Worker、模型供应商 SDK、Web Search 或 Memory Graph 的业务级事件。若后续确认这些模块存在框架故障不可定位的缺口，再分别补充稳定事件。

### 涉及到的对外API

无对外 API、SSE schema 或 UI 变更。

内部构造接口增加可选的结构化 logger 注入：

- MCP Node Client 使用 API 现有 operational logger；
- Remote Compute 依赖最小 `info/warn/error` logger 契约，避免 executor package 反向依赖 service；
- 未注入 logger 时保持兼容，不改变已有调用行为。

运维侧继续使用现有日志环境变量，不增加新的必填配置。

### 与其他模块的相关性描述

- `services/api`：作为 composition root 注入已有 operational logger，并记录启动阶段和基础设施 adapter 的生命周期；
- `packages/executor`：通过最小 logger 接口记录 Remote Compute 生命周期，不反向依赖 API service；
- `packages/operational-logging`：继续负责文件写入、级别过滤、轮转和集中脱敏；
- MCP Tool Registry、Agent Runtime、SSE 与 UI：业务接口和事件 schema 不变，不接收本功能新增的框架诊断事件；
- Runner 与 Memory Graph：保留各自已有日志通道，不将既有业务日志重复写入 `api.log`。

### 测试设计与测试计划

#### 功能测试

- [ ] API 启动成功时，组件初始化产生 start/ready 事件并包含耗时；初始化失败时产生 failed 事件且原异常行为不变；
- [ ] MCP stdio Server 正常连接、加载工具目录和关闭时，事件顺序及 `serverId`、`transport`、`durationMs` 正确；
- [ ] MCP Server 不存在、握手失败或调用失败时，记录错误码、有限错误消息和重试信息；
- [ ] MCP stdio 子进程输出大量 stderr 时，仅保留 4 KiB 尾部，失败日志最多包含最后 4 行/1 KiB；成功日志不泄露 stderr；
- [ ] HTTP/SSE/stdio 各 transport 的 `proxyMode` 与 `proxyApplied` 符合真实应用情况；运行时代理变更产生变更事件；
- [ ] 远端 Runner 直连成功、连接失败、断线和关闭均产生对应事件；
- [ ] SSH 主机探测及隧道 forward/stream/socket 失败包含可关联的 `hostId`/`runnerId`。

#### 安全与可靠性测试

- [ ] URL 中的用户名、密码、token/secret 等查询参数不可出现在日志；
- [ ] Authorization/Bearer、password、cookie 等敏感字段不可出现在日志；
- [ ] 工具参数、响应正文、用户会话和 LLM 内容不进入框架日志；
- [ ] 错误消息、stderr 和重复事件在极端输入下不会突破体积边界；
- [ ] 日志写入与轮转失败不会改变 MCP、远端 Runner 或 API 初始化主路径结果；
- [ ] 轮转继续遵守 `maxBytes`/`maxBackups` 配置。

#### 工程验证

- [ ] MCP、Remote Compute、operational logging 定向单测通过；
- [ ] `packages/operational-logging`、`packages/executor`、`services/api` 类型检查通过；
- [ ] 架构依赖检查通过，executor 不反向依赖 API service；
- [ ] 在 Linux/WSL 环境完成涉及真实子进程与文件轮转的回归验证。

issue:84.body:
### 🚀 Background Description ScienceDiscovery's backend is currently the TypeScript `services/api` (port 4310, `http/index.ts` at about 3,500 lines, `store.ts` at about 5,600 lines, depending on about 50k lines of `packages/*`, with the agent loop also running in Node). The frontend `apps/web` talks to it through about 260 HTTP endpoints plus SSE. [JiuwenSwarm](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm) already provides general agent capabilities: multi-agent team/Swarm, skills and skill self-evolution, permission approval, sessions and projects, MCP, scheduled tasks, and the jiuwenbox sandbox. This issue proposes: **keep the existing TypeScript frontend, reuse JiuwenSwarm as the main Agent backend as much as possible, and keep the science-specific modules (evolve, idea-tree, memory-graph, artifact/provenance, etc.) as standalone backends.** E2E cases serve as the acceptance spec for the migration. ### Goals and plan **Short term (Sep 30):** 10 E2E cases pass with no quality regression, and the corresponding 10 scenarios are usable; release a minor-version RC. **October:** Refine step by step, complete the migration, and make all E2E cases usable. **Long term:** Gradually switch to the componentized version of JiuwenSwarm (the `AgentRuntime` public API) and evolve in sync with JiuwenSwarm; gate on contract tests, switching the chat core first and the remaining domains afterward. The 10 E2E cases will be decided by Zhang Yi by Sep 21. **Baseline version:** Fixed on JiuwenSwarm 0.2.6. The interface and event analysis in this issue was read from the local `0.2.5.beta1` code and needs to be rechecked against 0.2.6. ### Overall migration philosophy 1. **Reuse JiuwenSwarm first and do not modify it by default; intrusive modification is allowed when necessary.** Use its chat, sessions, team/Swarm, permissions, skills, MCP, and scheduled tasks directly. Intrusive modifications are applied as patches on the fixed version (0.2.6) and merged back upstream later. 2. **Keep the frontend contract unchanged and translate in one place only.** The frontend speaks HTTP + SSE (32 event types); JiuwenSwarm speaks WebSocket (`req / res / event`, about 400 methods). A new **adapter** does the translation, with essentially no frontend changes; the goal is to eliminate endpoints that need a wrapper to adapt. 3. **Scientific value stays in standalone backends.** artifact, provenance, review, evolve, idea-tree, memory-graph, and runner each have their own process, data directory, and token; the frontend reaches them through the adapter's reverse proxy, and the agent calls them through MCP tools. 4. **Each piece of state has exactly one owner.** Sessions and projects belong to JiuwenSwarm, science metadata belongs to each standalone service, and the adapter only handles what nobody else owns (run event log, settings and secrets, permission audit, usage statistics). 5. **Tests are the spec, and the agent implements by "red-to-green".** First turn the existing E2E and contract tests into an acceptance baseline that can target any backend, then implement feature domains one by one; behavior without a covering case does not count as migrated. 6. **Switching can be done in batches.** For routes not yet migrated, the adapter can fall back to the old `services/api` and switch traffic domain by domain (this requires both sides to share session IDs, see Open decisions). ### Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR UI["Web UI (apps/web, TypeScript, essentially unchanged)"] subgraph ADP["Adapter (newly written, Python)"] direction TB A1["HTTP + SSE routes (about 260)"] A2["Bearer auth, users mapped to user_id"] A3["run registry and event log (seq, resume)"] A4["Event mapping (32 frontend event types)"] A5["Storage for settings, secrets, permission audit, usage statistics"] end subgraph JW["JiuwenSwarm (reused, not forked)"] direction TB GW["Gateway /ws"] AS["AgentServer"] CAP["Sessions and projects / Team and Swarm / Permission rails
Skill and evolution / MCP client / Cron / jiuwenbox"] GW --> AS --> CAP end subgraph SVC["Standalone backends (own process, data directory, token)"] direction TB S1["artifact / provenance / CAS
extracted from services/api"] S2["evolve
Python already exists, TS orchestration layer moved in"] S3["idea-tree
split out of evolve"] S4["memory-graph
already a standalone service"] S5["paper parsing"] S6["runner + compute
environments, execution, remote hosts, NPU"] S7["science MCP services
biomedicine / UniProt / llm-wiki"] end UI -->|"HTTP + SSE"| ADP ADP -->|"WebSocket req / res / event"| GW ADP -->|"reverse proxy"| SVC CAP -->|"MCP tools"| SVC ADP -.->|"Fallback for unmigrated routes (optional)"| LEGACY["old services/api"] ``` In the short term the adapter connects to the Gateway's WebSocket (broadest coverage); in the long term it switches to the `AgentRuntime` componentized interface.
The two ways to connect the adapter, and a few facts about JiuwenSwarm's connection layer **The two ways to connect the adapter:** | | A. Connect to the Gateway's WebSocket (recommended for the first version) | B. Embed `AgentRuntime` in-process | |---|---|---| | Coverage | All about 400 methods, including team/swarm, skills, mcp, config | Only covers single-agent sessions, chat, permissions, and model and mode catalogs; the Process CLI docs explicitly do not accept Team / Workflow / AutoHarness root modes | | Types | Handwritten, no schema | Python dataclasses, typed | | Stability | Protocol is ready-made, validated by the React frontend and the TUI | Public API was only just completed (`f29c060c`, `8773691e`), stability unknown | **A few facts about JiuwenSwarm's connection layer (which the adapter must fill in itself):** - Identity comes from connection parameters (`user_id`, `session_id`, `mode`, `agent_id`, `app_id`) or request headers, and no token validation was found, so the frontend's existing Bearer auth must be done by the adapter. - `seq` and `stream_id` on event frames are optional fields, and no mechanism was found for replaying by sequence number after a disconnect, so the frontend's `runs/:id/events?after=N` resume relies on the adapter storing its own event log. - The payloads of `chat.delta / final / reasoning` are flat `{session_id, content}`; `chat.tool_call / tool_update / tool_result / ask_user_question / subtask_update / subagent_activity / usage_*` and similar keep their full payloads.
### Migration approach per module | Scope | Migration approach | |---|---| | Chat, sessions, projects, permissions, models, MCP, skills | **Reuse JiuwenSwarm + adapter mapping** (59 approximate mappings, 21 direct mappings) | | Runs and event log, settings and secrets, permission audit, skill library versions, usage statistics | **Adapter-built** (JiuwenSwarm has none, 66 items) | | Science toolset (run_shell, execute Python, web, artifact, etc.) | **Provided again as MCP** to JiuwenSwarm's agent (a new major item) | | artifact / provenance / CAS, review | **Standalone service**: reuse the existing TS packages plus a thin HTTP layer, no rewrite | | evolve, idea-tree, memory-graph, paper | **Standalone service**: the evolve orchestration layer moves into Python, idea-tree is split out of evolve, memory-graph is almost as is, paper gets a wrapper layer | | runner, environments, remote hosts, NPU | **Keep runner + pass through**; remote host and NPU logic moves out with runner, in the second batch | | Scheduled tasks, science gateway MCP | **Reuse directly** JiuwenSwarm's `schedule.*` and MCP config | | Frontend | Essentially unchanged; hide unsupported entry points and clean up dead code |
Full module migration table (current state → target → approach) Legend: **Reuse** = use JiuwenSwarm directly; **Adapt** = the adapter does the mapping; **Build ourselves** = JiuwenSwarm does not have it; **Standalone** = standalone backend; **Keep as is** = essentially untouched. | Module | Current state | Target | Migration approach | |---|---|---|---| | Chat and agent loop | `native-agent`: 128-round loop, parallel tools, loop-guard, deferred `tool_search` | JiuwenSwarm's agent loop | **Reuse + adapt**: `chat.send / interrupt / user_answer`; the adapter adds a run registry, event log, and SSE resume, and synthesizes events such as `run.queued / started` that upstream does not have | | Context assembly and compaction | `packages/context` (about 3.5k lines) | JiuwenSwarm's context compaction | **Reuse**, our own assembly is not migrated | | Sessions and projects | JSON blob in `catalog_state` | JiuwenSwarm's session and project storage | **Adapt**: `session.*`, `project.*`; Public interfaces involved, and relationship to other modules **Public interfaces involved** - **Frontend contract (unchanged)**: the `/api/*` HTTP interfaces, the SSE events of `RunStreamEvent` (`packages/schema/src/session.ts`), Bearer auth, and the dev-environment Vite proxy for `/api` and `/health` (`127.0.0.1:4310`). - **New**: the adapter's WebSocket calls to the JiuwenSwarm Gateway (depending on the `ReqMethod` / `EventType` enums); the MCP tools each standalone backend exposes to the agent. - **Existing external interfaces of each standalone backend** (which the adapter must connect to): runner's 39 route groups, evolve's 7 (`/runs` returns NDJSON, `/idea-tree/*`), memory-graph's 27. - **Callback direction**: the evolve sandbox calls `/internal/evolve-llm/:runId/v1/chat/completions` (run-level token, not user auth), which the adapter provides after migration. **Relationship to other modules** - `services/api`: gradually replaced by the adapter; during migration it can serve as the fallback target for unmigrated routes. - `packages/*`: artifact-manager, cas, provenance, workspace, trajectory and so on are extracted and reused as the artifact service; `context`, `orchestration`, `plan`, `native-agent` and so on are replaced by JiuwenSwarm together with the agent loop. `packages/schema` (about 8.4k lines) is the contract hub shared by frontend and backend, and must be taken along or the contract generated when extracting services. - `scripts/check-architecture.mjs`: the boundary rules between packages (packages must not import `services/` or `apps/`, etc.) remain useful when splitting; the new adapter and services must follow them. - CI: contract tests and E2E need reworking; the externally facing contract part of `services/api/src/server.test.ts` (about 7500 lines) can be turned into contract tests for the adapter.

The parameter keys of `chat.send`, the payload keys of each response, and the behavior when multiple clients subscribe to the same session are **not verified**. - The following are marked "to be confirmed": the backend route for the frontend login handshake, stopping and resuming a single sub-agent, whether MCP deletion and OAuth are covered by JiuwenSwarm, and the semantics of agent-set timers. - The total number of features is 58 (35 core, 15 auxiliary, 8 experimental). `agent-runtime`, `direct-mode`, `plan-mode`, `execution-modes` and `science-sources` under `packages/` no longer have `src`, only stale build artifacts, and do not count as features. **References:** - JiuwenSwarm: https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm - JiuwenSwarm's E2A protocol and event enums: `docs/en/E2A-protocol.md`, `jiuwenswarm/common/schema/message.py` - JiuwenSwarm single-agent Runtime public API and one-shot execution entry: `jiuwenswarm/runtime/service.py`, `docs/en/Process_CLI_Machine.md`

### 背景与本 issue 的定位 #84 已经给出了迁移理念、整体架构、259 条接口清单、32 类事件映射与模块级工作量，并推荐「新写一个 adapter 接 JiuwenSwarm Gateway 的 WebSocket」。 本 issue **不重复**接口清单与事件映射，聚焦 #84 未展开的一个前置问题： > 我们复用的边界，应该划在 **agent-core（`openjiuwen`）** 还是 **JiuwenSwarm（`workswarm`）**？ 这个问题之所以是前置的，是因为一轮只读代码盘点得到一个结论：**我们想复用的能力，大部分实质在 agent-core，不在 JiuwenSwarm**；而我们未来想改的基础算法（上下文组装、多 agent 探索），**替换缝全部在 agent-core**。边界划错，会导致 循环、上下文引擎、记忆、检索、47,454 行工具库（含 25,026 行浏览器自动化）、rails 机制、agent_teams 与 swarmflow 引擎、symphony、rsi、agent_evolving，约 64.8 万行。 2. **替换缝在 agent-core。** 想改上下文组装或多 agent 探索，用到的是 `ContextEngine.register_processor`、`ContextEngine.register_window_mutator`、`agent_teams/workflow/engine/seam.py` 的 `use_provider()`、`register_{rail,tool,subagent}_provider`、`ModelContext(ABC)`、`AgentRail`——**没有一个在 JiuwenSwarm**（详见第五节）。 3. **穿过 JiuwenSwarm 会造成双层 pin。** JiuwenSwarm 的 `pyproject.toml` 把 agent-core pin 在一个 git rev 上（当前 `d0bd8335`），并有 `make update-openjiuwen` 滚动跟随 agent-core `develop`。若我们经 JiuwenSwarm 间接依赖 agent-core，就**不能自己决定 agent-core 版本**——而所有替换缝都在 agent-core，这是结构性矛盾。 4. **装配成本没有想象中高。** agent-core 的 `openjiuwen.harness` 导出公开工厂 **`create_deep_agent(...)`**（约 30 个关键字参数）与 `DeepAgentConfig`（50+ 字段，全部带文档）。JiuwenSwarm 的 `agent_adapter` 36,050 行里，`interface_code.py`（2,809，code 模式）、`team_helpers.py`（4,411）、`evolution_*`（1,347）、`browser_runtime_security`、`statusline_setup_agent` 等是 **JiuwenSwarm 的产品特性**，不是 agent-core 装配。按本项目自己的产品面（无 IM、无多端、无 code 模式、无 team 模板）重估，**自建装配层约 4,000–8,000 行**。 **与 #84 的差异**：#84 把 JiuwenSwarm 作为复用单位、adapter 接 Gateway WebSocket。本方案把 agent-core 作为硬依赖、JiuwenSwarm 按块可选。两者不是互斥的实现路径，而是**依赖方向的取舍**，建议在第 0 阶段 spike 里一并验证后再定。 --- ## 三、目标后端架构 ### 3.1 `on_get_context_window`）、6 个内置压缩器 + 4 个卸载器。四个改造层级，均**零源码改动**： | 层级 | API | 能改什么 | |---|---|---| | L1 注入 | `AgentRail.before_model_call(ctx)` 改 `ModelCallInputs` | 加删消息、加 prompt section | | L2 换处理器 | `@ContextEngine.register_processor` | 压缩 / 召回 / 卸载算法本身 | | L3 换最终窗口 | `agent.context_engine.register_window_mutator(fn)`，`fn: (ModelContext, ContextWindow) -> Awaitable[ContextWindow]` | **最终送进推理的窗口** | | L4 换整个模型 | 实现 `ModelContext(ABC)` 子类 | 整个上下文语义 | L3 正好承接我们现有 `packages/context` 的「model-aware 原子窗口选择 + 最终校验」。**待验证**：`register_window_mutator` 的执行点是否确实在所有 processor 之后。 ### 5.2 多 agent 探索 `openjiuwen/agent_teams/workflow/engine/seam.py` 文件头原文： > "The provider seam: the indirection that lets the engine be swapped. … The engine installs its `EngineProvider` for the duration of a run; **a different implementation … can install its own provider instead, and workflow scripts never change**." API：`Provider(Protocol)` 覆盖 `agent()` / `parallel()` / `pipeline()` / `map_parallel()` / `agent_session()` / `human()` / `budget`，配 `use_provider(p) -> Token` / `reset_provider()`。因为存在 `contextvar` 里，**科学探索 run 与普通 run 可在同进程并存**。 于是把 `services/evolve` 的 PUCT 搜索或 `packages/idea-tree` 的想法树升级成多 agent 分支探索，做法是实现一个 `ScienceExploreProvider` 装上去，**workflow 脚本一行不改**。 另有按名覆盖：`register_subagent_provider(name, factory)` 的文档写明「a later registration for the same name overrides it」，内置探索子智能体名为 `core.explore_agent`。 ⚠️ 注意两张表语义相反：`harness/manifest/catalog.py` 的 `add_descriptor()`（元数据）**拒绝重名并抛 `ValueError`**；provider 注册表（工厂）**后注册覆盖**。要覆盖内置算法走 provider 注册表，不要重复同名的 `@harness_element` 声明。 --- ## 六、侵入分析 侵入要分三种： - **A 型（源码侵入）**：必须改 JiuwenSwarm 的文件 - **B 型（协商性侵入）**：不改今天的行为，但要求冻结或新增扩展点 - **C 型（反向侵入）**：不改 JiuwenSwarm 一行，但**它的运行期假设侵入我们**——改进程状态、强制数据目录布局、注入依赖树 前两种此前讨论过，**C 型是这轮新发现的，也是「按块复用」的真正门槛**。 ### 6.1 C 型：三个全局副作用源 **(1) `jiuwenswarm/common/config.py` 在导入期修改 `sys.path`**（第 48–57 行）： ```python _user_config = os.getenv("JIUWENSWARM_CONFIG_DIR") if _user_config: _CONFIG_MODULE_DIR = Path(_user_config) elif get_config_dir().exists(): _CONFIG_MODULE_DIR = get_config_dir() if str(_CONFIG_MODULE_DIR) not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, str(_CONFIG_MODULE_DIR)) # 插到最前 ``` 进程级、导入即生效、不可撤销。若该目录含同名 `.py` 会**静默 shadow** 我们的模块；且行为取决于环境变量与目录是否存在，同一份代码在不同机器上 `sys.path` 不同。`get_config` 被 185 个文件使用。 **(2) `common/utils.py`（2,954 行）假定 `~/.jiuwenswarm` 工作区布局**：解析顺序 `JIUWENSWARM_DATA_DIR` → `JIUWENSWARM_HOME` → `~/.jiuwenswarm`，并期望其下有 `config/config.yaml`、`agent/workspace/` 等结构。我们若 import 依赖它的块，就必须在自己的数据目录下再造一个最小 JiuwenSwarm 工作区。 **(3) 依赖树注入**：`workswarm` 的 `dependencies` 含 `chromadb`、`faiss-cpu`、`playwright`、`tree-sitter`、`sqlite-vec`、`pgvector`、`opentelemetry-*`，以及对本项目完全无用的 `python-telegram-bot` / `discord.py` / `slack-bolt` / `dingtalk-stream` / `wecom-aibot-sdk`。 ### **无** | | **Skill 文件/归档原语**（`skill_files` `archive_store`） | 0 | 0 | 无 | **无** | | **jiuwenbox** | 0 | 0 | 无（本机 HTTP 服务） | **无** | | cron store | 0 | 1（一个路径函数） | 无 | **低** | | **Skill `workswarm`**，Python 代码对 `jiuwenswarm` 零引用；JiuwenSwarm 自己也是通过 HTTP 调它。我们可以 `pip install "jiuwenbox @ git+#subdirectory=jiuwenbox"`，零侵入。 - **cron**：只要一个路径函数。建议照抄 cron 表达式与 store 语义到 `catalog.sqlite` 形成双主；会话回溯用 L0 的 `core/session/vcs` 底座自己做产品化。 **新增设计约束**：`adapters/swarm/` 每个适配器要在文件头声明它拖进来的 C 型侵入，由 `check_layers.py` 校验声明与实际 import 一致；未声明的 import 直接失败。 ### 6.3 A 型：必须改 JiuwenSwarm 源码的场景，已缩到 2 条 本方案下**不再适用**的四条：新增 `ReqMethod`（我们不跑 AgentServer）、改 `agent_adapter`（我们自己装配）、换协作调度内核（走 agent-core 的 seam）、复用 JiuwenSwarm 前端组件（前端用我们自己的）。 仍然适用的： | # | 场景 | 触发条件 | 处置 | |---|---|---|---| | **A1** | jiuwenbox 增加 macOS 隔离后端 | 要保住 macOS 源码模式**同时**采用 jiuwenbox（jiuwenbox 目前 Linux-only；我们的 `seatbelt.ts` 在 47 个文件被引用） | 上游 PR；或不采用 jiuwenbox，继续用 `services/runner` | | **A2** | `skill_manager` 解耦工作区与全局 config | 要接 Skill 包管理，且不接受 6.1 的 C 型侵入 | 上游 PR（改为构造参数注入）；短期用 6.2 的选择② | 另有 A3（`common/config.py` 去掉导入期 `sys.path` 变更）只在「后端完全合并为单一 Python 进程」的形态下出现；本方案的 Node + sidecar 形态天然规避。 ### 6.4 B 型：建议向上游提出的扩展点 | # | 对象 | 诉求 | 不给的代价 | |---|---|---|---| | B1 | **agent-core** | 明确 `register_{rail,tool,subagent}_provider` 与 `ContextEngine.register_processor` 的**覆盖生效时机窗口** | 改基础算法只能依赖未文档化的时机 | | B2 | **agent-core** | 明确 `register_window_mutator` 在处理器链中的**执行点** | 窗口权威降级为尽力而为 | | B3 | JiuwenSwarm | 给出**可外部复用模块清单**并脱离 beta | `adapters/swarm/` 全部建立在内部模块上 | | B4 | JiuwenSwarm | **Skill Hub HTTP API 版本化**（现有 `hub_asset_port.py` 是 Python 端口稳定声明，HTTP 层无版本） | 被动跟随；最坏退回本地库 | | B5 | JiuwenSwarm | `skill_manager` 路径/config **改为注入式** | 见 A2 | | B6 | JiuwenSwarm | `common/config.py` 提供**无副作用导入模式** | 单进程形态下有静默 shadow 风险 | | B7 | JiuwenSwarm | jiuwenbox 发布到 PyPI | 便利性诉求，可用 git 子目录安装替代 | **B1、B2 最该优先推动**——「改基础算法」的能力完全取决于它们。 ### 6.5 反向：我们会不会侵入 JiuwenSwarm 不会，且是结构性的：单向依赖（`workswarm` 按 extra 引入、jiuwenbox 按本机服务引入），JiuwenSwarm 对我们零依赖；我们不跑它的进程、不实现它的协议、不改它的配置语义。若要贡献科学能力，走 Rail 插件 / Skill / MCP 的正向 PR，对它是加法。 --- ## 七、工作量 估算口径：同语言搬运约 800–1,500 行/人周；跨语言重写含测试约 250–400 行/人周；协议与语义对齐按耦合点计。不含产品需求变更与跨团队协同开销。**未做原型验证，第 0 阶段完成后需重新校准。** | 阶段 | 内容 | 乐观 | 可能 | 悲观 | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | M0-a | 证伪 spike（四个判据，见第八节） | 2 | 3 | 5 | | M0-b | `sd-agent` 骨架 + `sd-api` 的 `agent-client` + 37 类事件映射 | 10 | 14 | 22 | | M0-c | 分层护栏、`ports/` 定稿、`adapters/native/` 兜底 | 3 | 4 | 6 | | M1-a | 工具面迁移 + 13,675 行域包加 HTTP 外壳 | 12 | 17 | 26 | | M1-b | 上下文三语义 + 证据门禁与评审检查点 | 6 | 9 | 15 | | M1-c | 科学探索 Provider（PUCT / idea-tree） | 8 | 12 | 20 | | M2-a~d | 按块接 JiuwenSwarm（Hub / Skill 包 / jiuwenbox / cron） | 15 | 22 | 36 | | M3-a | 分发：Python 运行时进单可执行文件 payload（双架构）、Docker | 8 | 11 | 17 | | M3-b | 测试与 CI：增 Python 层；E2E 大部保留（REST/SSE 与 Web 不变） | 6 | 9 | 14 | | **合计（M2 全接）** | | **70** | **101** | **161 人周** | | **不接任何 JiuwenSwarm 块** | | **55** | **79** | **125 人周** | **M2 各块彼此独立**，可以只接 Skill Hub 不接 jiuwenbox，或反过来。这是本方案与「整体二选一」的主要差别：**JiuwenSwarm 从一次性决策变成逐块定价**。 **不可逆点**：M1-a 完成后，工具实现不再留在 Node 侧。M0 全程可回滚。 --- ## 八、第 0 阶段的证伪判据 | # | 判据 | 决定什么 | |---|---|---| | ① | `create_deep_agent()` 跑通一次带工具调用 + 审批中断 + 流式的会话，并映射成现有 37 类 SSE | 自建装配的 4,000–8,000 行估算是否成立 | | ② | `register_window_mutator` 注入的受保护段，能否存活到最终 LLM 窗口（构造一个会被内置压缩器改写的长会话） | 上下文三语义能否等价迁移，还是要接受行为回退 | | ③ | 实现一个最小 `Provider` 并 `use_provider()`，验证 workflow 原语被整体替换后行为正确 | 科学探索能否成为多 agent 范式 | | ④ | `pip install workswarm` 后做依赖裁剪试验，量出可接受的最小依赖集 | M2 各块的分发成本 | 判据 ①③④ 直接决定路线，判据 ② 决定产品行为是否回退。**在第 0 阶段之前讨论总工期意义不大。** --- ## 九、待决定事项 1. **复用边界**：agent-core 直接依赖（本 issue）还是经 JiuwenSwarm Gateway（#84）。建议在 M0-a 一并验证后再定。 2. **是否采用 jiuwenbox**：采用则获得 Landlock、cgroup、推理隐私代理，但 **macOS 源码模式会失去沙箱**（jiuwenbox Linux-only）。需要产品明确。 3. **是否接 Skill 包管理**：涉及 6.2 的高 C 型侵入，三个选择需要拍板。 4. **控制面语言**：本方案保持 `services/api` 为 Node（保全约 81% 后端代码）。若未来要合并为单一 Python 后端，M0–M2 完成后可平滑过渡，但会额外触发 A3。 5. **差异化定位**：如果本项目的差异化主要在科学域能力（工具、连接器、证据溯源、科学环境、NPU），现有分层足够；如果在 agent 算法本身（上下文、探索、检索、演进），则应进一步收紧对 agent-core 的直接控制。这决定第 5 节各层级的使用频度。 --- ### 补充说明 - 本 issue 的全部结论来自上述基线 commit 的只读代码盘点，**未改动任何仓库**，未建分支、未提 PR。 - 归属用的「依赖率」是「模块内 import `openjiuwen` 的 `.py` 文件数 / 该模块 `.py` 文件总数」，是**代理指标**而非逻辑占比的精确度量；每条归属结论另有行数对照或具体文件路径佐证。 - C 型侵入的判定口径是「模块文件是否 import `jiuwenswarm.common.config` / `jiuwenswarm.common.utils`」，是传递依赖的一级近似；真正接入前应在 M0/M2 用一次真实 import 验证完整传递闭包。 - 与 #84 互为补充，不替代。

pr:168.body:
This PR adds an opt-in, user-perspective JiuwenSwarm → `antibody-design` Skill → Ascend NPU journey, alongside the lower-level mocked NPU binding test. It depends on Skill backport PR #159; duplicate Skill PR #167 was closed.

## User journey

A fresh Project/Session is created with a live model and selected 131 Runner. The driver uploads the user's two PDBs and sends a high-level request through the public Session Runs API. It does not invoke any model script, choose a Python environment, or preseed model assets. The real Agent must load the Skill, inspect/select a managed environment, push inputs, perform first-use preparation and validation, run RFdiffusion → ProteinMPNN → Protenix → screening on NPU, pull results, declare report/CSV/CIF Artifacts, and explain the result. The test observes automatic wake Runs, committed execution receipts, nonempty remote and local stage files, completed transfers, and final Artifacts. It never resubmits an accepted user Run; a pipeline retry is accepted only after the preceding execution has a confirmed, committed failure. Any `unknown`/unconfirmed execution fails the test.

The real case is tagged `npu:required`, `model:real`, `status:external`, collected but deselected by ordinary PR CI until gated NPU hardware exists. The mocked binding/ST case remains for CI.

## Real-hardware verification (2026-09-24)

- **Full-Agent E2E: PASS (1/1)** on a fresh Project `9df41ef6-e2ea-4096-8e3a-6f8f5783e546`, Session `fb3dbdac-e218-40d5-a50c-565167421e4e`, initial user Run `a62cd447-a1e6-4570-8ddc-de3937edb97d`. The Agent loaded `antibody-design` itself, selected a managed environment, pushed inputs, and completed first-use preparation `74864a72-89e7-475d-af6e-ebf34495deaf` and validation with committed zero-exit receipts. One NPU pipeline Execution `a91eb590-1457-491a-977e-be73e98ba73c` finished `completed / committed / exitCode=0` on the selected remote Runner. RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN, Protenix, and screening each produced files. Report, CSV, and CIF were transferred to the Session, declared as Artifacts, and explained by the Agent across the original and an automatic wake Run.
- The full live submission used the test driver at `9afed0fa`; the final `ae556055` driver passed by **read-only observation of the same Run**, after fixing a test-only assertion that had incorrectly required three `declare_artifact` tool calls even though the Agent legitimately declares multiple Artifacts in one call. No extra NPU job was submitted for that verification. The final Agent response also names the report, CSV, and CIF. The WSL product source snapshot was labelled `89a3ac7c` and included the Skill backport.
- Earlier fresh full-Agent Run `8d3814fa-f681-4957-a647-a55c81ac06e8` is **not a pass**: first-use preparation `4eb49ef9-8c60-4708-8996-9db8fec44500` became `unknown/unconfirmed` after `fetch failed`. A first pipeline attempt then had a confirmed Runner workspace-snapshot `ENOENT` on a transient MindScience `__pycache__` file; the Agent recovered and its later NPU pipeline/output delivery succeeded, but the preparation receipt remained unconfirmed. This is a real stability risk to address separately, not a result hidden by the passing rerun.
- The older prepared-environment NPU Run `c1ba1acc-2968-417f-8714-7947ee3e1b32` is lower-level evidence only, not the full-Agent E2E result.
- `node --check`, CI contract, E2E metadata (0 errors, 11 pre-existing legacy warnings), and diff whitespace checks passed locally. The previous CI run had ST, UT, Docker, both binary builds and CLA passing; the latest push starts a fresh CI run, so its final state is not yet claimed. The hardware case is intentionally deselected in CI.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`
User impact: no runtime code change; adds regression coverage for the complete Agent-to-NPU workflow.
Compatibility: merge Skill backport PR #159 before this PR.

pr:196.body:
Users who route through Requesty currently have to set it up as a custom OpenAI compatible provider by hand. This adds it as a built-in preset alongside OpenRouter, with the same shape: OpenAI chat completions, `GET /models` discovery, and a models.dev mapping for catalog facts and prices.

## Preset
`packages/schema/src/model-provider-presets.ts` gets a `requesty` entry right after OpenRouter: base URL `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, `apiVariant: "openai"`, `modelDiscovery: "openai-models"`, docs `https://docs.requesty.ai`, key page `https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys`. `ModelProviderPresetId` in `model-provider.ts` gains `"requesty"`. The wizard and settings UI read the preset list, so nothing else changes there. Requesty is not made a default anywhere.

## models.dev mapping
models.dev publishes a `requesty` provider whose `api` is `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, so the host check in `pricesApplyToPreset` accepts its prices for this preset. It is mapped after OpenRouter, in the aggregator block, so first publish wins still hands capability facts to the vendor listings. The ordering test in `packages/model/src/models-dev.test.ts` now counts `requesty` as an aggregator so a misplaced insert would fail it.

## How to test
Pick Requesty in the connect wizard, paste a key from https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys, and choose a listed model such as `openai/gpt-4o-mini` or `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`. For EU routing, edit the base URL to `https://router.eu.requesty.ai/v1`.

## Validation
Run on macOS arm64 at ae150eb, with deps installed only for `@sciencediscovery/model` and its workspace dependencies.
- `pnpm typecheck` in `packages/schema` and `packages/model`: clean.
- `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs`: OK, 276 package source files checked.
- Package unit tests with `node --test "src/**/*.test.ts"`: schema 12 passed / 0 failed, model 45 passed / 0 failed (including "every aggregator mapping sits after every vendor mapping"). These files are tagged `os:linux`, so on macOS I ran them with `process.platform` reported as linux; nothing else was changed.
- Live check through the package's own code: `listProviderModels` with the preset's `baseUrl` and discovery strategy returned 762 models including `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, and `streamModelTurn` with the preset's protocol and variant streamed a reply from `openai/gpt-4o-mini` with usage reported.
- Not run: `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` and `apps/web` tests. The UT and E2E layers need a bubblewrap sandbox on Linux, which this macOS host does not have.

## E2E user journeys
BLOCKED on this host (no Linux sandbox for the local stack). The change adds one entry to a list the connect wizard already renders, and the live check above covers the provider's discovery and chat path. Happy to add or rerun a journey if you want one for this.

## Release
Release category: release:feature (label pending a maintainer, I cannot apply labels)
User impact: Requesty appears as a provider preset in the model connect wizard.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Disclosure: I work at Requesty. Happy to adjust anything to match project conventions.

## Summary

Ready for maintainer review and merge. This PR extracts Idea Tree from the evolve process into an independently runnable Python service and exposes its research capabilities as session-scoped MCP tools.

Current candidate: `d81b7bf3ebc8d9b1ed09914a439768f43a5abd3a` (one squashed commit). Related to #101 and #84; partial delivery of the broader integration acceptance scope, so keep #101 open. This establishes the service boundary ahead of the evolve migration in #102.

## Changes

- Move the Idea Tree engine, service layer, models, prompts and templates out of evolve's vendored implementation into `services/idea-tree`. Preserve the existing research algorithm and remove the old evolve router registrations.
- Add a dedicated FastAPI process with a health endpoint, shutdown cleanup, internal-token authentication and loopback port `4314`. Require a single ASGI worker because active research tasks and short-lived capabilities are process-local.
- Persist research, trees and settings in a service-owned data directory. Copy legacy records once without deleting originals; conflicting destination records fail migration rather than overwrite data.
- Publish `create_idea_research`, `get_idea_research`, `control_idea_research` and `view_idea_tree` through scoped MCP endpoints. Project/session identity and model callback credentials come from the trusted control plane rather than model arguments. Capabilities expire after five minutes; revoking a transport capability does not stop autonomous research.
- Replace the old API Python client with `IdeaTreeServiceClient`. Discover tool schemas from the service, preserve historical graph reads, research-created messages and SSE forwarding, and keep the six existing frontend research/graph/settings routes and response shapes.
- Include the service in stack startup, Docker packaging, isolated browser-test configuration, test discovery and coverage. Update English and Chinese developer documentation.

## Review fixes included

- Restore complete `evolveAvailability` initialization and bootstrap wiring.
- Restore the actual `research_service.py` service layer instead of the accidentally duplicated engine module.
- Migrate remaining tests away from the removed Python client and evolve vendor modules; remove the unused compatibility adapter.
- Remove the Evolve-readiness guard from independent Idea Tree routes.
- Disable Uvicorn access logging in the application lifespan as well as the launcher, preventing MCP capability URLs from being logged with direct `uvicorn ...:app` startup. Include a direct-Uvicorn regression.
- Correct stale developer-document paths and replace the redundant listener-address type assertion identified by CodeCheck with a runtime guard.

## Validation

GitHub Actions for the current candidate: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40816521503

pr:261.body:
Closes #260. `E2E_SWARM_TASK` was a test-only declaration: `.ci/run-e2e.sh` exported it for the JiuwenSwarm backend and twelve specs gated on it. It verified nothing, was always `1` in CI, and made DRB, TC-E2E-01 and BiomniBench report BLOCKED on the native loop, although that loop delegates sub-agents through the platform `task` tool as well. The stack now says how it runs agent turns, and the journeys check that instead.

## `/health` reports how agent turns run

`services/api/src/http/index.ts`: `/health` and `/api/health` include `agent: { executor, subagents }`, taken from the same `jiuwenSwarmConfigFromEnv()` result the API uses to start agent turns. `executor` is `jiuwenswarm` or `native`; `subagents` is `task` or `jiuwenswarm`, and always `task` on the native loop. This lives in the API rather than the adapter's `/agent/info` because the API decides delegation in both modes, and a native stack has no adapter. The adapter forwards `/health` to the API, so a JiuwenSwarm stack answers the same way.

The L1 contract baseline (`test/contract/baselines/legacy-linux.json`) records `/health` bodies and will show the added `agent` key on a manual `--compare`. The baseline is not regenerated here: its README reserves that to a human review, and the comparison is not part of any CI layer.

## Journeys check the stack instead of a variable

`test/helpers/e2e.ts` adds `requireAgentStack()`. It reads `/health` and fails as BLOCKED, quoting what the stack reported, when sub-agents are not delegated through `task`. With `{ executor: "jiuwenswarm" }` it also requires that executor.

- Journeys that test JiuwenSwarm's own behaviour require the JiuwenSwarm executor: `swarm-research`, `swarm-specialist-mcp`, `swarm-tool-failure`, `artifact-revision` and the four `literature-review-*` specs.
- The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) require only `task` delegation and run on either executor. Their score metrics now record the reported executor instead of a constant `"jiuwenswarm"`, so a native run is labelled native.
- Combined gates are split. `E2E_SWARM_EXCLUSIVE` and `E2E_LITERATURE_FIXTURE` keep their own checks and messages, as do `E2E_SWARM_COMPACTION` and `E2E_MCP_FAULT_PROXY`. They protect exclusive stacks and fixtures, not the stack's identity.

`E2E_SWARM_TASK` is removed from `.ci/run-e2e.sh`, the specs, `jiuwen_swarm/README.md`, `jiuwen_swarm/tests/README.md` and the three benchmark READMEs. `git grep E2E_SWARM_TASK` finds nothing.

## Validation

Local host, on `9f8fcc6a`, with a scratch `HOME` so the layers use a JiuwenSwarm instance of their own (see #251).

| Layer | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| UT (`pnpm ci:ut`) | 3714 | 3714 | 3714 | 0 | 0 |
| ST (`pnpm ci:st`) | 2 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| E2E mocked (`pnpm ci:e2e`, profile `pr`) | 70 | 70 | 70 | 0 | 0 |

- New API test "health reports how agent turns run": passed natively (`agent` = `native`/`task`) and in the UT layer, which runs the API on JiuwenSwarm (`jiuwenswarm`/`task`); both `/health` and `/api/health` are checked.
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` passes for the changed specs and helper.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS** on `9f8fcc6a`, local isolated stack with the JiuwenSwarm backend. The research batch (20/20) contains every Swarm-gated mocked journey: each one now passes its precondition by reading the stack's `/health` through the adapter, with no `E2E_SWARM_TASK` set anywhere. The standard (44/44) and literature (6/6) batches also passed.

The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) cannot run on a pull request. Their gate now accepts either executor as long as sub-agents use platform `task` delegation, which is what a native Nightly needs. Their next run will show it.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none for product use. `/health` gains an additive `agent` field describing the deployment.
Compatibility and migration: anyone running journeys by hand no longer sets `E2E_SWARM_TASK`; the stack's own configuration decides. A stack older than this change does not report `agent` and its Swarm-gated journeys report BLOCKED.

pr:269.body:
CSV 重复 ID 处理生成的后缀可能与输入中已有的 ID 相同，导致多条记录共用一个内部标识。点击值为 `333` 的记录时，会同时高亮两行，详情面板却显示 `111`。

## 保证 CSV 记录的内部标识唯一

- 为记录分配内部标识时，检查其是否与已分配的标识冲突；缺少原始 ID 时生成的标识也执行相同检查。
- 为每个基础标识记录下一次可尝试的后缀，避免大量重复 ID 反复扫描已占用的后缀。
- 保留原始 CSV 单元格值和解析结果的确定性，每条受影响的记录只计入一次重复 ID 警告。

复现数据：

```csv
id,value
sample#4,111
sample,222
sample,333
```

打开 CSV 可视化，切换到 **Data table（数据表）**，点击值为 **333** 的记录。修复后只高亮这一行，详情面板显示 **333**。

## 验证结果

测试提交：`82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7`，基于 `main` 的 `c33c1ae2b7100ab86de451afb02aefe0bd7a3045`。

- CSV 测试：**通过 29 / 失败 0 / 跳过 0**。其中三项 ID 冲突回归用例在修复前均失败。
- 性能回归：包含 20,000 个已占用后缀 ID 和 20,000 个重复 ID 的 40,000 行 CSV，在加入后缀游标前超过子进程的 10 秒时限；加入游标后，本地测试约 287 毫秒完成。
- UT（`pnpm ci:ut`）：计划 **3723**，执行 **3723**，通过 **3723**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- ST（`pnpm ci:st`）：计划 **2**，执行 **2**，通过 **2**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 静态检查（`pnpm ci:l1`）：计划 **4**，执行 **4**，通过 **4**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 使用模拟模型的浏览器 E2E（`pnpm ci:e2e`）：计划 **71**，执行 **71**，通过 **71**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 加入后缀游标后，独立代码审查未发现仍需处理的问题。

此前测试失败及原因：

- 首次 UT **3721/3723** 通过：本机 bubblewrap 0.6.1 不支持 `--disable-userns`，且克隆固定版本的研究评估器时发生 TLS 连接中断。
- 另一次 UT **3720/3723** 通过。其中两项评估相关失败在未修改的 `main` 上同样出现（**3717/3719** 通过）：Python 3.14 与固定版本的 SciPy 不兼容，以及全局评估器路径覆盖使另一项契约检查暴露出依赖缺失。将固定版本的评估器准备到预期缓存位置，并使用 Python 3.12.13 后，两项问题均解决。其余一项权限队列断言属于间歇性失败：该用例在 `main`、较早的修复分支测试，以及使用全新服务状态的最终完整测试中均通过。
- 首次完整浏览器测试执行 **71** 项，**通过 70 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**；CSV 流程已通过。唯一失败是 J3 的托管 Python 环境前置条件，Conda 下载依赖时出现 `SSL routines::unexpected eof while reading`。未修改的 `main` 执行 **70** 项，**通过 69 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**，复现了相同问题。修复分支重新测试时使用单独复制并补齐的依赖缓存。

## E2E 用户流程

提交 `82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7` 在浏览器和本机进程运行的产品环境中验证**通过**。完整模拟模型浏览器测试 **71/71** 通过，**失败 0 / 阻塞 0 / 跳过 0**。

CSV 流程的 **4/4** 个用户步骤全部通过：通过真实沙箱生成并声明 CSV 产物、打开可视化、点击 **333**，再依次切换 **111 → 222 → 333**。预期与实际结果一致：始终只高亮一条记录，选中数量为 1，详情值与所选记录一致，并保留原始 ID。同一操作也已在正在运行的本地产品中手动验证。

可复用用例位于 `test/journey-inspect-csv-records.spec.ts`，纳入 `pnpm ci:e2e`。该流程使用独立的本地模拟模型，覆盖无需真实模型凭据的 PR 测试场景。最终完整测试使用单独复制并补齐的科学计算依赖缓存，J3 的环境创建、使用、审计和删除流程也全部通过。

## 发布说明

发布类别：`release:fix`

用户影响：选择存在 ID 冲突的 CSV 记录时，详情面板显示该记录的数据，并且只高亮所选行。

兼容性与迁移：无需迁移。原始 CSV 值保持不变；重新打开 CSV 时，受影响的内部行标识会重新生成为唯一值。

贡献者账号没有上游仓库写入权限，GitHub 的 `release:fix` 标签需由维护者添加。

## Summary

Fixes #264.

Make proxy setup usable from one **Network and proxy** settings entry, and keep local application transport independent of outbound proxy failures. Reuse the existing proxy registry, downloader cache/retry, and environment-readiness mechanisms rather than adding an automatic external-network startup gate.

## Changes

- Offer environment configuration, a custom HTTP(S)/SOCKS5 proxy, or direct access. Keep named proxies, bypass hosts and Web/MCP overrides under advanced settings; existing model overrides remain compatible.
- Stage proxy changes across settings tabs. The footer saves them; Cancel/X discards unsaved changes. Add an authenticated, non-persisting download-source connection diagnostic.
- Declare and lock Python HTTP/WebSocket SOCKS dependencies. Adapter loopback HTTP/WebSocket connections explicitly bypass outbound proxies; external HTTP clients are initialized lazily.
- Add small source-loadable shared routing/download helpers. Resolve model requests against their actual target, respect bypass rules, and pass the global policy to managed environment setup/create/install operations without mutating process-wide environment variables.
- Resolve environment mode on the remote Runner itself. Reject forwarding a host-local custom proxy to a remote Runner, with recovery guidance.
- Preserve underlying, redacted network errors and existing pinned versions, SHA-256/TLS verification, caches and retries. Update English/Chinese configuration, architecture and REST documentation.

## Validation

No real LLM API calls or paid tokens were used.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Workspace build and typecheck | Passed before rebase; upstream changes are E2E helpers/tests/docs only |
| Proxy transport, diagnostics and Runner environment tests | 28 passed |
| Model, downloader, Runner client and resolver regression tests | 41 passed |
| Targeted settings persistence / Runner policy propagation | 3 passed (overlaps Runner regression coverage) |
| Adapter hermetic tests | 234 passed; live gateway and real-model test files excluded |
| Proxy settings component tests | 4 passed |
| L1 checks | 4 passed on the rebased head |
| Browser settings journeys | 2 passed in 36.6s on the rebased head |
| Swarm mocked contracts | 9 passed before final rebase; unchanged product code |

The browser journeys use a real local API/Swarm stack, not mocked settings storage. They cover basic defaults; custom proxy save/cancel; cross-tab drafts; reload persistence; NO_PROXY; Web/MCP overrides and inheritance; rejection of deleting an in-use proxy; and removing references plus deleting the proxy in one save. Only the first journey's connection-test response is browser-mocked; transport ST tests exercise local HTTP/SOCKS proxy fixtures and authentication failures without external access.

The legacy layout E2E is adapted but remains quarantined and was not run. No production service was restarted.

## Scope and boundaries

- This does not grant sandbox network access or add an automatic direct fallback when a configured proxy fails.
- The manual diagnostic checks one download source, not every provider or model credentials. There is no new startup preflight framework or traffic dashboard.
- Saving multiple settings sections is sequential, not a cross-section transaction: a later failure does not roll back earlier successful requests. Unsaved changes remain drafts.
- SOCKS5 support in Undici remains experimental. Remote end-to-end proxy reachability, binary installation and real external providers have not been newly exercised by this PR.

## Summary

Add all **132 DeepResearchBench II tasks** as a release-only L5 benchmark, following the existing tagged Playwright real-E2E framework. L5 now selects **151** real cases (19 inherited + 132 DRB II); L4 remains 19. No new paid cases enter PR/L2 or merge/L3 gates.

## Design and scope

- Statically declare every task identity; collection is offline and cannot silently shrink when data or credentials are absent.
- Each task receives an isolated research worker through the existing matrix/reconciliation path. Preserve original task text and blocked-source instructions; only append artifact delivery instructions. Rubrics are never research-Agent input.
- Do **not** carry over the experimental two-subagent prompt cap. Product quotas still apply and are recorded. Memory Graph is disabled for DRB II workers.
- Download upstream only at execution time: `imlrz/DeepResearch-Bench-II@b38f360603db9531b102aef8c166cedb8509b6f6`, shallow/blob-filtered/sparse checkout of necessary files, locked Python dependencies, and dataset/evaluator hash checks. No upstream dataset or report corpus is vendored. Verified local `.git` size was about 708 KB.
- Reuse upstream rubric prompts and scoring; add strict response completeness/type checks and a non-destructive JSON parser (upstream's repair regex can corrupt valid compact JSON).
- Account for upstream task 116's duplicate rubric texts: 56 raw entries / 50 distinct scored entries, matching upstream text-keyed output rather than making the task fail permanently.
- Record reports, rubric results, per-call Judge usage including retries, model/config identity and separate generation/evaluation durations. Delivery/evaluation failure fails the case; valid low scores are review evidence, **not** hidden failures or an invented quality threshold.

## Configuration and release impact

Uses the existing `nightly-ci-ds` generator/Judge settings. `DRB2_JUDGE_API_STYLE` defaults to `openai`; set it to `deepseek` for DeepSeek transport. Judge output starts at 32,768 tokens and increases on truncation up to 65,536. One Judge request at a time, 15 rubrics per batch, at most three attempts.

Generation budget: 120 minutes/task; evaluation: 30 minutes/task; existing research job ceiling: 240 minutes including preparation. The workflow retains two concurrent jobs. At 30 minutes generation/task, DRB II alone is approximately 66 worker-hours / 33 wall-clock hours, before setup and judging. **A tag-triggered release now incurs this full paid benchmark and waits for its gate.** A timeout is not a spending cap.

DRB II workers do not require DRB I, HF or Jina evaluator prerequisites. Configured research providers may separately require keys. Per-task upstream licenses still apply, notably CC BY-NC for tasks 26 and 110.

## Verification

- CI contract suite: **59/59 passed**, including new selection/sharding, prompt isolation, score completeness and mocked Judge transport tests.
- L1: **4/4 passed**.
- Actual offline Playwright collection: **151 release identities**, exactly **132 DRB II**; daily remains **19**.
- Runtime shallow/sparse preparation and pinned checks: passed.
- Local transport smoke against the **actual pinned upstream evaluator and all 132 task rubrics**, with a synthetic loopback Judge: **132/132 passed**, no LLM tokens. This proves evaluator plumbing, **not research quality**.
- E2E metadata check: 0 errors (existing legacy warnings unchanged).
- Documentation checks, lint of modified runbooks, and `git diff --check`: passed.

## Explicit limitations / not claimed

- Full 132-task paid Agent execution was **not** run as part of this PR. Prior local four-report real experiments are not a full-suite result and are not this branch's E2E verification.
- No historical quality regression threshold and no claim of official leaderboard comparability; Judge model and execution conditions matter.
- Existing session token summaries can omit intermediate/child calls and are labelled **not a billing total**. Judge calls have their own detailed usage ledger.
- This PR does not fix the existing 5-second status-poll recovery policy, long-task resource pressure, or persistence performance. Failures remain failures; assertions are not relaxed to hide them.

Runbook: `test/benchmarks/deepresearchbench-ii/README.md`.
