## Summary

Fix protocol-specific token usage parsing and make provider accounting non-gating in real E2E. No provider-specific workaround, Swarm source modification, or relaxation of task/delivery/quality assertions.

## Problem and evidence

The October 14 manual daily run (38546559384) completed the functional steps of seven basic journeys but failed each on `outputTokens > 0`. The preceding official-DeepSeek nightly passed the same checks.

A short Chat Completions probe returned both standard `completion_tokens: 31` and an extra `output_tokens: 0` (input 35, total 66). The shared normalizer preferred the latter. The model gateway then forwarded the incorrect zero to Swarm. No credentials or live response payloads are committed.

## Changes

- Require the requested protocol when normalizing usage. Chat Completions reads prompt/completion token fields; Responses reads input/output token fields, including its cache detail object.
- Preserve legitimate zero values. Do not reconstruct missing input/output counts from totals or fall back to another protocol's fields. Missing/invalid accounting remains unavailable and does not fail model generation.
- Remove provider token counts and usage availability as real basic-journey pass criteria. Preserve usage evidence (or an unavailable diagnostic) and the existing request ledger. Functional assertions remain unchanged; accounting does not gate scoring.
- Document this boundary. Deterministic parsing and gateway tests remain gating.

## Validation

- Model package tests: 50 passed.
- Model gateway tests: 35 passed, including streaming/non-streaming accounting propagation and completion without reported usage.
- Regression cases cover conflicting fields, null/missing/invalid values, legitimate zero, and final usage-only streaming chunks.
- Test TypeScript check (`tsconfig.tests.json`): passed.
- API dependency build: passed.
- Documentation checks: passed (126 files); `git diff --check`: passed.

The seven paid real journeys and full nightly suite have not been rerun for this PR. This fixes accounting and CI policy, not the separate evolution thinking-budget or research-team timeout failures. Token usage is provider-reported telemetry, not a guarantee of billing completeness or a reliable budget limit when the provider omits it.

pr:311.body:
## What does this PR do / why do we need it

Implements the **full three-layer plan** for natural-language program evolution (GitHub issue #310): turn `/evolve-design` from a hidden slash command into something a natural-language sentence can trigger, with the framework actively recommending a tree-search evolution and the interaction staying natural-language end to end.

Today `/evolve-design` is a hidden slash command: a user must already know the prefix to start an evolution search, and the only visible entry is a button in the artifact detail modal that fills the composer with `/evolve-design make the artifact X better: ` (still requiring manual completion). The interaction is command-shaped, not natural-language.

### Layer 1 — Composer intent recognition (frontend)

- **`apps/web/src/evolve/intent.ts`** (new): pure `detectEvolveIntent(message)` — true only when an improvement verb pairs with an evolvable target (`program` / `code` / `algorithm` / `function` / `model` / `script` / `artifact` …). Non-evolvable targets (`formatting` / `layout` / `description` / `explanation`) never match, and bare "better" with no target never matches. `isEvolveDesignCommand()` separates the explicit slash command from natural language.
- **`EvolveSuggestionBar`** (new): a low-intrusion confirmation bar. Detection only *offers*; the user must explicitly accept before the algorithm picker opens — an evolution search spends real budget (mutations + sandboxed evaluations), so a false positive is worse than a missed suggestion.
- **`App.tsx`**: an explicit `/evolve-design` command opens the algorithm picker directly (existing behavior preserved); a natural-language intent shows the confirmation bar first, and only an accepted suggestion opens the picker. Both flags reset when the message leaves evolve intent.

### Layer 2 — Agent-driven recommendation (backend)

- **`packages/evolve/src/index.ts`**: the `create_evolve_run` tool description now tells the agent to **recommend** an evolution search when the user asks in natural language to improve a program / code / algorithm / model / result against a measurable target — not only when they type `/evolve-design`. The agent phrases it as a plain suggestion ("this looks like a search-shaped problem; want me to run an automated search that keeps the best-scoring variant?") and starts only after the user confirms. This builds on the evolve-design skill, whose description already lists natural-language triggers.

### Layer 3 — Visible entry points (frontend)

- **Composer**: a new sparkle "program evolution" button fills a natural-language prompt (`Improve the program: ` / `改进一下这个程序：`) instead of a slash command; `detectEvolveIntent` recognises it and offers the suggestion bar.
- **Artifact detail modal**: the evolve button now fills a natural-language seed prompt (`Make the artifact X better: ` / `让产物 X 变得更好：`) instead of the `/evolve-design ...` command text.
- **`intent.ts`**: adds `artifact` / `产物` as evolvable targets and `变得更好` as an improvement verb so both seed prompts are recognised.

### Why confirmation before the picker?

A search spends real budget. Detection is a guess, so it must only offer; the user's explicit accept is the gate. This is the core false-positive guard — a user saying "优化一下" while discussing formatting is never routed into an expensive search.

### Why verb+target pairing?

Intent detection is deliberately narrow: `优化一下界面布局` / `improve workflow steps` / `这个更好` / `make this better` all stay silent; only sentences pointing at an evolvable target (program / code / algorithm) match.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Closes GitHub issue [#310](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/310).

## Test Plan and Test result

Verification commit: `f9fe5846` (9 files, +192/-5, single commit, based on GitHub main `cc974a14`)

- Web typecheck: `tsc --noEmit` passed, 0 errors
- Web unit tests: **107 passed / 0 failed** (includes 8 new evolve-intent tests)
- Web vite build: passed
- evolve package typecheck + tests: passed

Intent recognition behaviour verified:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `improve the program` / `优化一下这个程序` / `让程序跑得更好` | triggers |
| `Make the artifact X better` / `让产物 X 变得更好` | triggers (seed prompts) |
| `make this better` / `这个更好` | no trigger (no explicit evolvable target) |
| `优化一下界面布局` / `improve workflow steps` / `改进一下说明文字` | no trigger (non-evolvable target) |
| `the first one is better` | no trigger (ordinary conversation) |
| explicit `/evolve-design` command | opens the picker directly, no confirmation bar (existing behavior preserved) |

## Self-checklist

- [x] **Design**: follows the issue's three-layer plan; confirmation-bar guard and narrow verb+target detection address false positives and budget protection
- [x] **Tests**: `evolve-intent.test.tsx` (8 tests) ships with this PR; typecheck and web unit tests pass
- [x] **Verification**: behaviour matrix recorded above with the verification commit
- [x] **Interface**: no public API change; reuses the existing `/api/evolve/runs` chain, `EvolveToolRuntime` and `EvolveAlgorithmPicker`
- [x] **Docs**: no website-doc change required for this frontend layer

pr:315.body:
# 学科知识引擎：摄取/生长/消解/消费全链 + 会话绑库与反幻觉运行时

> 与 GitCode MR [!125](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/merge_requests/125) 内容一致（对应 GitCode issue #86）。

把「学科知识」做成 SD 的一等资产：文献与结构化源摄取为带锚点溯源的知识图谱，图谱可离线生长、实体消解、社区聚类；对话内绑定知识库（kb scope）后，图谱成为受约束的知识来源，输出必须引用锚点，与证据账本 / 新颖性检查 / 引用核验构成多层反幻觉链路。

**283 文件，+50.8k，4 个按路径分组的 commit**（KE 核心 / agent 运行时 / Web / 技能与测试）。

---

## 新增功能

### 1. 知识引擎核心（`packages/knowledge-engine` + `services/api/src/knowledge-engine`）

- **存储域**：SQLite（知识库/文档/锚点/实体/边/社区/合并/作业/引用/公式），带迁移机制；算法核与存储分离，可独立评测
- **摄取**：LaTeX-first arXiv 通路（tar.gz 解包 + `\input` 递归内联）、JATS XML、视觉增强 PDF 解析；溯源门抽取——每个抽取结论挂文档锚点
- **生长**：离线 grow job，MMR + anchor-aware 多样本选择、收敛信号、结构化反思 directive 反哺下一轮
- **实体消解**：在线门 + 离线 job、物理合并与回滚（`ke_entity_merges`）、louvain 社区、根实体、社区报告
- **消费面**：`kb_search` / `kb_expand` / `doc_grep` 工具、entity_unified_search、三级文档阅读器（全文/结构/锚点）、引用 API（意图徽章 supporting / contrasting / mentioning + Similar / References / Cited-By）
- **REST**：`/api/ke/*` 全套 + 前端知识引擎页（cytoscape 图谱画布、生长控制面板、阅读器、引用面板）

### 2. 会话绑库（kb scope）

- session 设置新增 `kbScopeKbIds` / `kbScopeWebSearch` 运行时覆盖项；composer 底部选择器一键绑定/解绑，写路径为 fresh-GET 读改写，避免并发选择器互相回滚
- resident-summary 上下文贡献者持续注入**在库**图谱摘要（成熟度分级）；范围外知识库对工具面与摘要均不可见（防泄漏包装）
- 系统 prompt m8.3.1：上下文时钟、kb-scope 自管理指引、反编造纪律句——均在既有 5000 字符保护段预算内

### 3. 反幻觉与研究运行时

- 三级注入：证据账本（`evidence_ledger`）、新颖性检查（`novelty_check`）、引用核验（`verify_citation`）；KE 工具输出逐字文本打 nonce 不可信围栏
- finish-gate 收尾审计：技能声明 `metadata.pre-finish-audit` 即在收尾前注入审计 directive，有界续跑（≤2 次）
- 研究世界模型 `research_state`：目标钉住 / 计划生命周期 / 未决问题 / 已排除路径防复活 / 已试去重，JSON 文件锁崩溃可恢复
- 审批门计划生命周期（`packages/plan-mode`）：`propose_plan` / `revise_plan` 工具、约束级审批、版本绑定决策、决策日志；与上游 `update_plan` 快照机制共存（`AgentRunBindings` 同时携带 `planRepository` 与 `planStore`）
- stall-guard：模型调用无进展按空闲窗踢出重试（≤3 次），外层空闲看门狗兜底
- 记忆图谱镜像 `observeSessionPlan`；MCP 配置文件内容签名失效（保留上游按服务器签名比较，叠加文件级变更检测）

### 4. 技能包与评测

- 15 个方法论技能：knowledge-engine-explore/grow、evidence-notes、hypothesis-tournament、tree-search、robin-chain、virtual-lab、idea-debate、systematic-review、precise-qa、long-form-writing/audit、progressive-report、report-writer、table-analysis（多数声明 pre-finish-audit）
- 评测套件 `scripts/ke-*-eval.mjs`：growth delta-recall、discoverer 诚信维度、pairwise、citation（ALCE 三指标）、resolution、bench 539 题；`skill-test-runner` + ER 数据集构建器
- KE 旅程 E2E 9 条 + kb-scope / finish-gate 旅程，ke-stub 离线可跑

## 验证

Linux（Ubuntu WSL2），分支 `pr/knowledge-engine`（基于 upstream/main 最新 `ef65b6f`，4 个按路径分组的 commit）。

- 29 个 workspace 项目全量构建通过（含 web vite build）；`architecture:check` 通过（293 文件）
- 触及包测试全绿：workspace 119/119、context 50/50、tools 61/61、runtime-core 36/36、memory 35/35、schema 12/12、plan 5/5、plan-mode 2/2
- **services/api 全量套件 1020 tests / 1019 pass / 0 fail**（`node --test dist/*.test.js dist/**/*.test.js`，123s 干净退出）
- 与纯 upstream/main 对照树同环境跑 server.test.js 验证无回归：upstream 86/86，本分支 86/86；期间修复了三处合并引入的问题（MCP transport 双重 close、内置技能清单落位、保护段预算超限），并把 KE sqlite 连接补上服务器关闭回收（否则每个 boot 泄漏 db+wal+shm 句柄并在进程退出时挂起 drain）
- 双计划系统共存验证：propose_plan 审批门与 update_plan 快照在同 run 注册、互不干扰（context-assembly 集成测试覆盖）

pr:372.body:
Session-enabled connectors stayed listed, and the agent received none of their tools, when the MCP server was switched off or could not connect. The catalog already recorded that state. The connector list ignored it.

## Disabled servers stay out of the picker and the agent

A server that is turned off, or that never entered the resolved server table, is reported as `disabled` once a catalog has been applied. `GET /api/connectors` omits those connectors, so the composer, settings, the project form, and the specialist form no longer offer them. Tool injection is unchanged: a disabled source has no available tools, so the agent is not given `mcp__<source>__*` tools even when the session still names the connector. The MCP server settings page still shows the disabled server and its switch, so it can be turned back on. Turning it back on returns the connectors to the picker with the previous selection.

## Connection failures stay visible

An enabled server that fails to connect or to list its tools stays in the connector list. Each of its connectors carries `connectionError`: the server's error text and the time the catalog was checked. The picker shows that text under the connector. The composer control shows a failure count when a selected connector failed. A partial tool mismatch (`degraded`) and a catalog that was never refreshed are left as they were: they are not hidden, and they are not labeled as connection failures.

A direct edit of `extensions_config.json` appears after the next catalog refresh (process start, `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload`, or saving a custom server). That is the same moment the agent sees the change.

## Compatibility

When an applied catalog does not contain a server, source status is `disabled` rather than `unavailable`. The governance broker rejects a call in that case with `MCP server is disabled or not configured: <id>`. Connectors of a disabled server are absent from `GET /api/connectors`.

Related to #325.

## Validation

Recorded on `4c9baed756f8b0ebbb33eaf967197e970e07af53`.

- Typecheck for the web, api, mcp, data-source, schema, and artifact-manager packages, plus `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`: passed.
- Package tests: web 890/890, data-source 51/51, mcp-sources 28/28, schema 12/12, mcp 1/1, artifact-manager 2/2.
- `services/api`: 1128 passed, 3 failed. The failures are PDF extraction tests and exit with `spawn … ENOENT` because `services/paper/.venv` is not present in this checkout. They do not call the connector list.
- `pnpm docs:check`, `pnpm architecture:check`, and `pnpm ci:selftest` (55/55) passed. The E2E meta check reported 0 errors.

`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. Those layers provision JiuwenSwarm outside the repository tree, which this environment does not allow. This pull request is a draft until those layers have results.

## E2E user journeys

PASS for the connector journey on `4c9baed756f8b0ebbb33eaf967197e970e07af53`. Local stack, native executor, runner and API on ports 4480 and 4481.

`test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts`: 3 passed, 0 failed. Two custom MCP servers are used, one healthy and one that exits during the handshake. Both appear, and only the failing one shows its error. Turning the healthy server off removes its connector from the picker and from the next run's tool list; the settings row and switch remain. Turning it on brings the connector back, still selected.

`journey-plugin-composition`: the connector-panel step passed. A later step expects `todo_create`, which the native executor does not provide. That failure is outside this change.

The mocked `pnpm ci:e2e` layer was not run.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: connectors whose MCP server is off disappear from the picker and are not offered to the agent. A connector whose enabled server fails to connect stays listed and shows the connection error.

Compatibility and migration: callers that treated "missing from an applied catalog" as `unavailable`, or that expected those connectors to remain in `GET /api/connectors`, need to handle `disabled` and the shorter list. No configuration change is required.

pr:390.body:
This PR exports the existing main-agent/independent-worker Issue-to-PR workflow as opt-in contributor tooling. Scheduling decisions stay with the main agent rather than a script-driven queue controller. It does not modify ScienceDiscovery's research agent runtime, CI policy, repository settings or the operator's running pipeline.

## Scope

- Add `.agents/skills/repo-issue-pipeline` with the coordination policy, worker contract and operational guidance: claim before admission, reproduce before implementation, full accepted-scope delivery, original-thread resume, change-driven discussion/CI/conflict maintenance, independent main-agent review and explicit human/authority boundaries.
- Export a portable one-turn Codex SDK transport with an optional executable override instead of a machine-specific CLI path. Requests explicitly acknowledge full host access; per-session locks prevent concurrent hosts, saved threads resume in their original worktree, and private session/events/final/failure records survive handoff. An incomplete or failed stream cannot be reported as successful.
- Add 16 hermetic tagged tests to the existing `scripts/*.test.mjs` discovery path, without introducing a second CI definition or requiring model tokens.
- Add English/Chinese developer overviews and contributor navigation, plus a setup guide covering private ledgers, configurable repositories/concurrency/inspection interval, resource and cost limits, continuation, systemd examples, recovery and raw-log sensitivity.

## Deliberate boundaries

This is an opt-in developer tool, not a product background service or automatic installer. No real task ledger, account, credentials, logs, host-specific services or legacy migration code are included. Cloning/installing the skill starts nothing. Workers have explicitly authorized full host access, so this must not be attached to untrusted PR/webhook execution. Worktrees are not sandboxes. Raw private logs can contain tool secrets and must not become public CI artifacts.

Periodic wake-up is documented but must be configured and verified on the target host. Completion-event wake-ups and a cross-platform daemon installer are not implemented. The main agent, not the host script, enforces the task-pool cap and repository authority. Successful SDK turns and green CI do not establish full Issue acceptance. Merging/enqueueing/releases/settings/secrets/gate changes and paid real-model tests need separate matching authority.

## Validation

- `node --test --experimental-test-coverage scripts/repo-issue-pipeline.test.mjs`: **16 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Host line coverage **97.64%**, branch coverage **96.00%**, function coverage **50.00%** in this direct Node report. Do not interpret these as repository-wide coverage.
- Coverage gaps: the real SDK dynamic import/constructor and CLI signal callback wiring were not exercised through a live Codex process. CLI child-process coverage is not merged into the parent report. Factory injection verifies start/resume/options/event/failure behavior, but does not prove account/CLI compatibility or model scheduling quality. No paid Codex smoke, actual OS-signal integration or service-manager installation test was run.
- Skill metadata validation, JavaScript syntax check, architecture check and CI catalog check passed.
- Markdown lint: **0 issues**. Documentation links: **141 tracked Markdown files checked**, no broken targets.
- Full local UT/ST/browser E2E are **not claimed passed**. The clean checkout has not been provisioned with all package-local dependencies/build outputs: shared UT collection stopped at missing `react` in an existing web test. Initial pnpm entry-point checks also encountered dependency-layout verification; no shared dependency tree was purged. The host's serialized heavy-test lock was occupied by an existing worker, so this PR does not interrupt that task or start competing full-stack runs. Full CI remains pending.

## E2E user journeys

ScienceDiscovery product E2E: **not applicable to the changed product path**, because there is no application UI/API/agent-runtime behavior change. Full browser-suite execution is nevertheless unverified as noted above. The new contributor tool is covered by offline request-to-session/output tests; a real Codex-account-to-fork-PR journey remains an explicit integration gap and must not be represented as a mocked product E2E pass.

## Release

Release category: release:internal

User impact: optional contributor tooling only; no automatic process or new application dependency.

Compatibility and migration: none for application users. SDK dependencies are isolated in the skill's optional host package. Existing private pipeline state is neither imported nor modified.

## Follow-up: Issue-as-Interface + OSS ops skills

Added on top of `repo-issue-pipeline` (commit `01f1df6`):

- **IAI delivery:** `issue-as-interface-contract`, `issue-review-agent-ready`, `iai-developer-patrol`, `iai-worker-implement`, `iai-reviewer-patrol`, `iai-reviewer-execute`, `magpie-pr-review-pipeline`
- **OSS ops (parallel):** `oss-ops-newcomer-gfi`, `oss-ops-stale-sweep`, `oss-ops-maintainer-stats`, `oss-ops-repo-health`
- **Docs:** [zh](docs/zh/developer-docs/issue-as-interface.md) / [en](docs/en/developer-docs/issue-as-interface.md) (+ links from CONTRIBUTING and issue-pipeline pages)

Still opt-in documentation/skills only — installing does not start bots. Reviewer execute authority is skill text for hosts that enable it; this PR does not merge or change CI policy.

pr:441.body:
Researchers can now inspect and retrieve structured scientific data from five built-in database connectors, then download selected files through governed artifact jobs. GEO uses actual provider file listings and bounded sample metadata queries; AlphaFold DB adds retrieval of existing predictions and confidence files. The change also strengthens ChEMBL measurement filtering, ClinVar submission preservation and experimental PDB provenance.

Refs #420. **Partial fix; keep #420 open.** This is a draft because broad verification is not green and provider failure-path coverage remains incomplete.

## Scope

- GEO: discover real matrix/SOFT/supplementary files, validate download selection, preserve study/sample/platform metadata, paginate sample annotations and avoid bulk-query timeouts. Correct accession request parameters and GEO directory buckets.
- ChEMBL: validate measurement constraints and preserve units, relations, target/molecule/assay identifiers and assay confidence. Advance pagination over scanned provider rows even when local confidence filtering returns an empty page.
- ClinVar: retrieve versioned VCV/RCV records and preserve individual SCV assertions and conflicting classifications, without inventing a consensus. Reject oversized XML explicitly.
- RCSB PDB: preserve experimental-method/revision evidence and include it with structure download candidates.
- AlphaFold DB: add existing-prediction lookup by UniProt accession and governed model/confidence downloads, with explicit predicted status and model version. This does not run prediction software.
- Reuse the existing Inspector for built-in sources, using the same broker/audit path; preserve AlphaFold selections across store reloads, refresh changed connector caches, register evidence graph tools and document all five sources in English and Chinese.

## Reproduction and acceptance evidence

Baseline: `0d31e155a206c23f6d6a0c9632e44f516b326bbe` (GitHub history). Product-validation candidate: `42a96f3f2613d34487ecc6041c61b5854b692d4c`. PR head: `bcd56b74bd9b79564e392da33e4977d94dd65034`. The final commit only relocates the unchanged connector-persistence test to avoid an append-at-end conflict with current main; production code and other tests are identical to the product-validation candidate.
The requester explicitly waived baseline reproduction for this feature. The baseline capability/gap assessment was source inspection, not a baseline live-service result. The candidate journeys below used built production API/Runner entry points, the bundled stdio MCP server, isolated Session/data state and official live providers. Agent validation used the native executor and a deterministic local model stub; it does not certify JiuwenSwarm or real-model behavior.

| Acceptance area | Candidate evidence | Status / remaining limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Five sources discoverable, enabled and callable | Production sources API, saved Session selections, five live Inspector calls; browser Inspector journey | PASS for representative paths; Agent tool execution exercised with AlphaFold, not every source |
| GEO metadata/files/verified matrix | GSE1000, sample annotations and actual directory listing; completed matrix download, SHA-256 and parsed 22,283 probe rows × 10 samples | PASS; identify expression profiling by array and avoid assuming raw counts |
| ChEMBL constrained measurements/pagination | CHEMBL203 activity query, two distinct provider pages, units/relations/assay metadata/confidence retained | PASS for representative query |
| ClinVar individual assertions/conflicts | Versioned VCV000014206 live lookup with distinct SCV submissions; structured XML/conflict fixtures | PASS for selected live record and fixture contracts; not an exhaustive clinical interpretation |
| Experimental structure and downstream reading | 1CRN completed download and checksum, parsed 327 atoms in chain A | PASS |
| Existing prediction/model/confidence | P69905 model CIF and confidence download, checksums, predicted marker/version, 142 pLDDT values | PASS |
| Evidence retained after analysis | Actual files read and analysis output persisted with source IDs/URLs/retrieval metadata | PASS in native product journey |
| Invalid/missing inputs and provider/download failures | Gateway/domain boundary tests, broker/artifact tests; invalid Inspector accession rejected and next turn usable | PARTIAL: full representative rate-limit/download-failure and all-backend coverage not established |
| Setup, supported operations and scientific limits | English/Chinese guides and reproducible examples; L1 documentation check | PASS |

## Validation

Previously executed local checks at the product-validation candidate are reported below; no unexecuted check is counted as passing. At the final PR head, the relocated persistence test was rerun (1 passed), L1 was rerun (4 planned / 4 executed / 4 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped), and `git diff --check` passed. A three-way merge-tree check against upstream main `9191d552d649612a81ec5852638020bcc1f30b7e` completed without conflicts; the merge result has not been executed. The earlier broad and product journey results remain attributed to their original tested SHA.

- `pnpm -r build`: passed. Test TypeScript check passed. `git diff --check`: passed.
- Gateway Python suite: **38 passed** (includes 10 new domain tests).
- MCP sources tests: **30 passed**.
- API MCP tests, run from the API package directory: **62 passed**.
- Artifact manager tests: **2 passed**. AlphaFold selection persistence test: **1 passed**.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: planned **4**, executed **4**, passed **4**, failed **0**, skipped **0**.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: **BLOCKED before case collection** by JiuwenSwarm/adapter startup readiness; wrapper exit 2. Case counts were not emitted.
- `pnpm ci:st`: planned **2**, executed **2**, passed **1**, failed **1**, skipped **0**. Native agent-loop smoke passed. SDK contract suite failed: 33 passed / 33 failed out of 66, with test-server startup reporting `self.server.started == False`. The exact failing `TransportTests::test_concurrent_results_remain_correlated` was rerun on both the pristine baseline and candidate with the same SDK interpreter and failed identically (1 failed each). This establishes that representative startup failure on the baseline; it does not independently attribute every SDK failure.
- `pnpm ci:e2e`: planned **71**, executed **0**, passed **0**, failed cases **0**, skipped **0**; overall layer **FAILED/BLOCKED** by stack/MCP proxy startup. No browser subset pass is claimed.

## E2E user journeys

Candidate SHA: `42a96f3f2613d34487ecc6041c61b5854b692d4c`.

1. `DOMAIN_DATABASES_LIVE=1 node --import tsx test/api/domain-databases-journey.mjs`: **PASS, 11/11 steps**. Starts production API/Runner, selects all five sources, calls each official provider through the product Inspector, completes and verifies GEO/PDB/AlphaFold downloads, reads actual artifact content, persists provenance, executes an AlphaFold tool through the Agent, rejects invalid input and completes a subsequent Session turn. Provider calls are real; model responses are local deterministic fixtures. This command requires a clean committed worktree, built packages, the gateway environment and Bubblewrap.
2. Focused browser journey `Inspect domain scientific databases`: **PASS, 1 case / 3 steps**. Five built-in sources visible, built-in Inspector schema exposed, malformed accession rejected and navigation back to GEO usable. This validates UI integration; it is separate from the blocked full JiuwenSwarm browser slice.

## Remaining work and issue disposition

Keep #420 open until JiuwenSwarm product behavior, remaining representative provider/download failure paths and the full required UT/ST/E2E gates have passing evidence or independently resolved infrastructure failures. The current branch is based on the recorded baseline; these results do not certify later upstream commits or a future merge result.

## Release

Compatibility and migration: no manual migration; changed connector versions invalidate old cached results. Existing permission and artifact-download approval flows remain in use.

pr:470.body:
Pull requests from `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]` stay mergeable when `license/cla` has appeared and is not `success`. If that check never appears, the merge gate does not fail because of it. For every other author, including other bots, an appeared non-success check fails the gate. `license/cla` is not added to the ruleset required checks: a required check that never runs would block pull requests the CLA app did not mark.

## CLA policy
The merge gate calls `claGate` after the existing job aggregation. The workflow only fetches commit statuses and the pull request author.

The newest status whose context is exactly `license/cla` on the head SHA wins (GitHub lists statuses newest first). An absent context passes. `success` passes. `pending`, `failure`, `error`, and any other non-success state fail, unless the pull request author has `type` `Bot` and login exactly `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]`. The comparison is case-sensitive and includes the `[bot]` suffix. The author is the pull request `user`, not `github.actor`. Another bot such as `dependabot[bot]`, a `User` with that login, a human, and an unknown author are not exempt.

A failed status read fails closed for every author, including `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]`. It is not treated as an absent check. On `merge_group`, if the pull request number or author cannot be resolved, there is no exemption: an absent context or `success` still passes, and a present non-success status fails.

On `merge_group`, the pull request number is parsed from the single `gh-readonly-queue` head ref and that pull request's user is loaded. Statuses are read on the queue head SHA, not the original pull request head. `push`, `workflow_dispatch`, and `schedule` are not subject to this check.

The merge-gate job requests `contents: read`, `statuses: read`, and `pull-requests: read`. The workflow permission stays `contents: read`. No status or pull-request write scope is added. The same rule is stated in `.ci/README.md`. The `Require CLA policy` step has no `if:` and sets `CI_CLA_RESULT` to `${{ steps.cla.outputs.result }}`. An empty result fails closed.

## Current head

pr:498.body:
Importing a research evidence package restores the conversation and the evidence needed to inspect and continue the original work. The `.sdresearch` plugin exports and imports workspace file versions, artifacts and provenance, execution history, trajectory details, and scientific memory.

## Behavior

- Imported sessions are read-only snapshots. **Create a new session to continue research** creates an independent, writable copy of the imported conversation and evidence. The copy runs as a background task that remains tracked after switching sessions; new research preserves the original snapshot.
- Workspace files open in a preview dialog. Text previews are limited to 256 KiB, supported images including PNG use the original bytes, and downloads preserve the original filename and complete contents.
- Trajectory export preserves model inputs, reasoning fragments, and tool-detail payloads. Import, restart, and continuation retain access to verified detail objects. Older packages cannot recover evidence they never contained.
- Necessary exports omit optional history and diagnostics while retaining required evidence dependencies. Complete exports offer independent checkboxes for full trajectory details and the full scientific-memory graph; deselecting the graph retains its summary. Export selections and source limitations survive import and repeat export.
- Export-size previews are keyed to the session revision and selection. Relevant changes invalidate previous results and trigger background preparation; unchanged sessions reuse their results without a fixed one-minute expiry. Pending results are shown as calculating rather than as a stale final size.
- Exports can run as persistent background jobs with status tracking, completion feedback, and original-name downloads. Downloading a job after its source revision changes is rejected rather than silently returning outdated evidence. Gzip compression is asynchronous; archive assembly still uses an in-memory tar buffer and is not a streaming implementation.
- User messages have a copy action; assistant reply copy actions remain available. Completed assistant replies offer **Branch to a new chat**, creating a writable conversation prefix through that reply. A persistent **Continue from chat** link returns to the immediate source reply. Imported read-only snapshots cannot be branched directly.
- Branching preserves attributable historical evidence, execution results, and reviewer-audit records, and discloses unavailable history. Busy sessions are rejected and request retries are idempotent. Import and continuation integrity checks compare the supported restored representation without inventing missing evidence.
- Importing a legacy package without scientific memory no longer fails snapshot capture solely because the graph service is unavailable. Packages containing scientific memory still require successful graph restoration. The scientific-memory summary is included in the snapshot payload type.

pr:544.body:
A terminal user can start an evolve search or an Idea Tree research and then only see an id. Progress and stop live on the Web cards. `evolve` and `idea` call the HTTP routes those cards already use, and they read the bearer token from the same data directory as `run`.

Fixes #50

## Commands

```text
ScienceDiscovery evolve list [--session <id>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve get <run-id> [--candidate <hash>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve watch <run-id> [--after <sequence>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve stop <run-id>

ScienceDiscovery idea list --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea get <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea watch <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea pause|continue|stop <research-id> --session <id>
```

`evolve stop` posts `POST /api/evolve/runs/<id>/stop`, the dashboard Stop route. `idea stop` posts `operation: "end"`, the card's End research route. Pause and continue are only on Idea Tree, because an evolve search has no pause. `evolve list` stays global; `--session` only forwards the route's existing `sessionId` filter. There is no `run --wait`. A long run is followed with `watch`.

Output matches `run`: readable text on a terminal, and one JSON object per line when stdout is a pipe, so `jq` works. `watch` adds `reconnect` lines and a final `result` line. A failure is an `error` line.

`watch` replays, then follows live, and returns when the engine stops running. A dropped connection reconnects for about three minutes. Evolve continues after the last printed event sequence, so an event is not repeated. An Idea Tree frame is a full snapshot with no sequence, so a reconnect shows the current state and skips a frame already shown. `--after <sequence>` continues an evolve watch in a new process.

Ctrl-C stops watching and exits 130. It does not stop the engine. `stop` does that. This is different from `run`, where Ctrl-C cancels the turn `run` started.

Exit status follows `run` (0 completed, 1 failed, 130 cancelled):

| Exit status | evolve | idea |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `succeeded` | `completed` |
| 130 | `stopped` | `ended` or `paused` |
| 1 | `failed` or `budget_exhausted` | `interrupted` |

A paused Idea Tree research exits 130 whether a person paused it or the token budget paused it. The engine records both as `paused`. `watch` also exits 1 when the run is missing, the token is refused, or the stream cannot be recovered.

## Validation

On `dada3d08c9ac343492e26e87cf95141eac92b28e` (parent `9c33627b5ffc3c3ef397c114e267de6e6cc6dd10`, clean worktree):

- `node --import tsx --test services/launcher/src/engine-commands.test.ts` — 26 pass, 0 fail
- `cd services/launcher && pnpm typecheck` — no errors
- `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` — exit 0
- `cd services/launcher && pnpm test` — 188 pass, 0 fail (includes the CLI journey below)
- `node test/api/engine-cli-journey.mjs` — `outcome` PASS, repeated 5 times on this commit
- L1: architecture boundaries OK; CI test catalog OK; `docs:check` 0 issues; e2e metadata 0 errors (11 pre-existing legacy warnings)

`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. The single-file binary smoke was not run; `run --help` is unchanged.

## E2E user journeys

PASS on `dada3d08c9ac343492e26e87cf95141eac92b28e`. Surface: CLI against the API process. Not a browser journey.

Command: `node test/api/engine-cli-journey.mjs`

The built CLI reads the token from the data directory. The journey uses a local fake model server and the evolve sidecar venv.

| Scenario | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recorded evolve search: list, get, candidate source, watch, `--after`, stop, missing id | Piped output is JSON. Watch of a finished success exits 0. Resume does not replay earlier events. Stop of an already finished success stays `succeeded`. A missing id exits 1. | PASS. Watch printed 6 events and exited 0. `--after 4` printed 2 events. |
| Live evolve watch, dropped connection, then CLI stop | Event sequences stay contiguous with no repeat. Stop uses the dashboard route. The run becomes `stopped` and watch exits 130. | PASS |
| Idea Tree watch, then pause | Watch follows the running research and exits 130 once it is paused. | PASS |
| Continue that research, then stop | Stop sends the card's end operation. The research ends. | PASS |
| A second research runs to completion | Watch exits 0. | PASS |

The live evolve step mounts the real evolve route handlers and orchestrator inside the API process. The public HTTP API has no route that creates a search, and API startup marks an unfinished search failed, so that step is not a separately started product process. Its sidecar is a stub. The same SSE routes forwarded through the default JiuwenSwarm adapter were not run. The CLI calls the same paths the Web cards call.

## Release

User impact: from a terminal, evolve searches and Idea Tree researches can be listed, inspected, watched, and stopped. Idea Tree research can also be paused and continued. The commands, options, and exit statuses are in `help` and in the English and Chinese CLI reference.

Compatibility and migration: none. Existing `run` behavior is unchanged.

Head is now `fa363435e4c2a57d6439797319a7fed0a5c7bc53`, a merge of `dada3d08` with `origin/main` `f4ceca57`. The merge keeps `--effort` and `--thinking` for `run` only, and keeps `--token` on `run`, `evolve`, and `idea`. The diff against main is still the same 13 files, +1961/−43. No `run --wait` was added.

GitHub Actions run 40210068505 succeeded for L1, UT, ST, Coverage, the four mocked L2 E2E jobs, and merge-gate. `CodeCheck (GitCode)` failed on both `dada3d08` and `fa363435`. The call now checks that the parsed engine settings exist and passes them on, so a missing action is a usage error. List scope, watch exit status, and stop behavior are unchanged.

pr:548.body:
Nightly real-model E2E treated a single transient model-gateway HTTP 500/503 the same as a product run that finished and failed to deliver, so one provider outage failed the whole Daily gate while other cases in the same job still passed. This change keeps the provider error visible, soft-classifies those faults, optionally repeats an early fault once, and leaves product failures hard-failing.

**The required real-E2E check now has a floor: a planned case that only faulted is an unverified case, and the check does not pass on it.** A soft classification is not a soft green.

After the optional early repeat, a case that passes on the repeat is a genuine `PASS` and the check may go green; a case that still faults keeps the `PROVIDER_FAULT` status and makes the check non-pass.

Closes #232

## The gate floor

| Outcome | Status | Exit code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Every planned case passed | `PASS` | 0 |
| A provider fault remains, no product failure | `PROVIDER_FAULT` | non-zero |
| A product failure | `FAIL` | non-zero |

The two failure kinds stay apart: a provider fault is still reported as `PROVIDER_FAULT: <case>` and never as `FAIL: <case>`, and a product failure is never softened into an outage. Neither one is a pass. The floor is the same in every place that decides, for the daily, merge L3 and release L5 profiles alike — no profile can turn an outage into a green required check:

- **`verifyResults`** (`test/support/tagged/plan.mjs`): the exit code is 1 whenever a provider fault or a product problem remains; the status is `PROVIDER_FAULT` for a fault, `FAIL` for a product failure, `PASS` only for a run without either.
- **the worker** (`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`): a repeat that did not work is audited in the accounting (`PROVIDER_FAULT_REPEAT_FAILED`, `PROVIDER_FAULT_REPEAT_REPORT_MISSING`) instead of only in the log; a batch that faulted as a whole is probed with a couple of repeats instead of re-running every case; a worker whose only failures were provider faults is not double-counted as an opaque worker failure, and the summary's exit code is 1 while a fault remains.
- **the suite reconcile** (`.ci/real-report.mjs`): a provider-fault shard is valid evidence — the identity checks still apply — whose results are folded into the suite accounting; the suite's exit code comes from that accounting, so a remaining fault makes it non-zero. The provider-fault problems stay visible instead of being flattened into an opaque `SHARD_FAILED`, and a shard cannot hide a fault behind a `PASS` it did not earn.
- **the shared-plan summary** (`.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`): a provider fault is a problem of its own, `planned == executed == passed` is still required, and `passed + provider faults == planned` is no longer enough for green.

## The detector

The provider context has to name the gateway itself: its `181001` model-call code, the wording of a failed model call, the API it answers on, or its own routing failure. Bare words — "provider", "llm", "gateway", "upstream" — are not context: a product delivery failure that mentions one beside a `500` is the product's own failure and stays a `FAIL`. A delivery miss or an assertion diff is the product's own report in the first place and is never soft-classified.

The gateway's own report is unchanged: the `181001` model-call code, the openAI API stream error and the routing failures recorded in the Nightly of 2026-10-06 are still detected as provider faults, and the provider's text is still kept verbatim.

## What changed
- `test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs`: the tightened provider context, the product-report reject, and the audit codes a failed repeat leaves behind.
- `test/support/tagged/plan.mjs`: the exit-code floor in `verifyResults`; the status of a provider fault stays `PROVIDER_FAULT`.
- `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`: the audited repeat, the capped outage probe, and the worker-failure pairing with the attempt whose exit code it explains.
- `.ci/real-report.mjs`: the reconcile keeps a provider-fault shard's evidence and the suite's exit code follows the accounting.
- `.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`: a provider fault is a problem of its own.
- Docs in `.ci/README.md` and `test/support/tagged/README.md`.
- Tests in `.ci/provider-fault.test.mjs`.

Product agent loop, model client, and run orchestration are untouched: only the CI harness and its accounting changed.

## Scenario coverage

pr:612.body:
Inherited standalone JiuwenSwarm settings could redirect ScienceDiscovery setup to another instance and overwrite its configuration. This change keeps the existing variable names but requires `SCIENCE_AGENT_JIUWENSWARM_OVERRIDES=1` to enable documented overrides, isolates SDK child environments, and resolves stack endpoints from the SD-owned instance. It also adds a reusable Docker persisted-volume restart journey.

Closes #592. Refs #593 — every acceptance case of #593 is re-verified on this tip (see the journey table); the issue stays open because it still carries `needs-human` for the sanctioned-override policy that this pull request proposes as a breaking change, so closing it is left to the maintainers reviewing it.

## Behavior and compatibility

- Ignore inherited `JIUWENSWARM_*` controls unless explicitly enabled; even then, forward only documented controls.
- Give SDK processes an SD-owned home and a limited OS/proxy environment. The packaged launcher also strips standalone runtime controls and injects its own adapter endpoints.
- Refuse setup/start/status/env/stop against an existing custom SDK runtime without the SD ownership marker. Do not migrate or delete ambiguous standalone state. Preserve the established SD default and Docker persisted layouts.
- Keep ownership state after an invalid setup value so a subsequent corrected setup can recover.
- Update internal callers, Compose examples and deployment documentation. Direct adapter startup with the JiuwenSwarm executor requires opt-in and both explicit endpoints.

## Baseline and tested versions

- Baseline main: `863969c2265a0645aa4d5333e0a8f7d0cae59a1f` (this branch is rebased onto it; the previous base was `76b5a44fcc814a5a69adddb8659eccd2afecc0c9`).
- PR head: `20d8209435224a37ad2e88bd156fca5c194b8f64`.
- Product/build snapshot and every journey driver: `20d820943`. All numbers below come from runs on that SHA, except where a baseline row is labelled as such.
- Validation ran on Linux amd64 with a container engine (Docker 29.9.2), a pinned JiuwenSwarm install at tag `workswarm0.2.6`, and a separate detached worktree on unmodified `origin/main` for the baseline comparison.

pr:614.body:
A Project could be created from the sidebar but never renamed or removed, so
the name typed at creation was permanent and the only way to drop a project
was to leave the app and edit the data directory. This adds the two writes to
the project fold, using the gestures the neighbouring Session rows already
have.

## Rename from the fold, like a Session

Double-clicking a project's name opens it for editing in place, and the row's
new `⋯` menu offers 重命名 for anyone who does not guess the gesture. The row
shows the Project the server returned rather than the typed text, because the
server is what trims the name and refuses a duplicate. `Renaming` in
`Sidebar.tsx` becomes one union of "project" and "session", so only one field
is open at a time and the input, its Enter/Escape handling and its blur commit
are shared rather than duplicated.

## Delete behind the same gate a Session has

The `⋯` menu's 删除 opens a confirmation dialog — no typing the project name
back, matching the Session dialog. The body states the consequence: the
Project's Sessions, their workspaces and their artifacts go with it. Accepting
calls `DELETE /api/projects/:id` with `confirmationId`, which the server
already requires and already refuses with a 409 while one of the Project's
Sessions has an active run; that refusal reaches the user as a toast and
nothing is removed locally.

When the open conversation belonged to the deleted Project, the app moves the
active project back to the inbox and starts a draft before refreshing the
lists. Without that step the next message would be written to a Project that
no longer exists.

## Tests

`apps/desktop/tests/api-sessions.test.ts` covers the DELETE body
(`confirmationId`) and the PATCH body (`name`) as separate calls, and
`apps/desktop/tests/sidebar.test.tsx` pins the row's two menu items and the
double-click hint. The browser mock now answers `DELETE /api/projects/:id` and
enforces the confirmation-id gate, so a client that stopped repeating the id
would fail rather than pass quietly. A new `apps/desktop/e2e/projects.spec.ts`
proves renaming through a reload, cancelling and then confirming a delete, and
deleting the Project that holds the open Session — which must leave a draft
rather than a conversation whose Session is gone.

| --- | --- |
| `pnpm ci:ut` | 5252 planned / 5252 executed / 5250 passed / 2 failed |
| `pnpm ci:st` | 24 planned / 24 executed / 22 passed / 2 failed |

| `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` | passed |
| `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test` | 564 passed / 0 failed |

The four layer failures are outside this diff, which touches `apps/desktop`
and nothing else:

- UT `packages/executor/src/sandbox-network.test.ts` — this host's bubblewrap
  has no `--disable-userns` (`bwrap: Unknown option --disable-userns`).
- UT `services/api/src/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts` — `unable to open database
  file` while provisioning the Swarm trajectory store.

  `test_mcp_boundary.py::BoundaryTests::test_100_concurrent_calls_keep_identity_and_execute_once`

The two UT failures were re-run on unmodified `upstream/main` in a detached

pr:617.body:
fix(model): treat an empty terminal turn as a model failure and record per-request wire diagnostics

Part of #245

## Not delivered

Criterion 3 (relay-vs-direct numbers) is not delivered by this PR. The harness is; a real measurement is not, because this host has no relay or model credentials. That measurement is tracked in #618 and #245 stays open as partially delivered.

## Limits

The summary staging step runs only in the real E2E workflow (`real-e2e.yml`), and `L4/L5 real E2E` is skipped in CI because it needs credentials, so no CI artifact can demonstrate the staged file — I verified that the governed mocked-E2E artifact from run 40650829410 on this tip has 72 entries and none is `.ci-results/model-wire-summary.json` — and the file is first observable on an owner-hosted real E2E run. An empty completion is rejected, not retried: a flaky relay that returns an empty `stop` now fails the request with 502 rather than shipping an empty answer; a bounded retry (only when `hasText=false`, `hasToolCalls=false`, `sseParseErrors=0`, `finishReason=stop`, retry budget unchanged) is a deliberate non-goal of this PR and would be a follow-up if relay flakiness shows up.

## Why

The Biomni perf evidence in #245 shows runs that finish with no assistant answer and no tool call, and a latency picture that cannot be attributed because the only evidence in the artifacts is aggregate. On `main` a provider stream whose last record is `finish_reason=stop` with no text and no tool call is accepted as a successful turn, and nothing per request is recorded about endpoint, status, framing timing, retries or provider request ID, so a relay problem and a research-quality problem look the same in CI.

Reproduced on the pre-fix sources (synthetic SSE: one role delta, one empty `stop` delta, `[DONE]`):

```
model client turn: {"content":"","toolCalls":0,"completionObserved":true}
gateway status: 200
gateway body:   (empty assistant answer, reported as success)
```

Two changes, one per failure class: record privacy-safe per-request wire evidence, and refuse an empty terminal answer instead of shipping it to the agent.

## What changed

### 1. Per-request wire diagnostics (criterion 1)

`packages/model/src/client.ts` now records one `ModelWireDiagnostics` per model request on both the native fetch path and the custom streamer path, and reports it through a new `onWireDiagnostics` callback (including on failure):

- identity: `requestId`, `endpoint` (origin only), `protocol`, `model`;
- timing: `startedAt`/`dispatchedAt`/`headersAt`/`firstByteAt`/`firstRecordAt`/`completedAt` plus ms offsets;
- framing: `httpStatus`, `upstreamRequestId` from `x-request-id`/`request-id`/`openai-request-id`/`x-oneapi-request-id`/`x-amzn-requestid`, `transportChunks`, `bytes`, `sseRecords`, `sseParseErrors`;
- outcome: `hasText`, `hasToolCalls`, `finishReason`, `truncated`, `attempts`/`retries`, `retryErrors[]`, `error.classification`.

`startModelGateway` logs exactly one line per model request:

```
[model-sse-summary] {"requestId":…,"endpoint":"https://…","protocol":…,"model":…,"attempts":1,
"retries":0,"httpStatus":200,"upstreamRequestId":…,"startedAt":…,"timeToHeadersMs":…,
"timeToFirstByteMs":…,"timeToFirstRecordMs":…,"transportChunks":…,"bytes":…,"sseRecords":…,
"sseParseErrors":0,"hasText":false,"hasToolCalls":false,"finishReason":"stop","truncated":false,
"retryErrors":[],"error":{"classification":"empty_completion"},"gatewayRequestId":…,"purpose":"task"}
```

The native agent loop logs the same summary on its own failures (`services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts`), so a run that dies in the loop still leaves evidence.

**Privacy:** the endpoint is reduced to scheme+host before it is recorded (no path, query string or credentials); no prompt, answer, tool arguments or request headers are ever carried. `upstreamRequestId` is a provider-assigned identifier, taken only from the allowlisted header names. A unit test asserts the credentials, path and query string of a base URL never appear in the recorded identity.

### 2. An empty terminal turn is an error (criterion 2)

New `EmptyModelTurnError` + `isEmptyTerminalTurn`: a completed turn with no text and no tool calls is no longer a successful answer. It is raised in `packages/model/src/runtime-client.ts` and again in the gateway for alternate streamers, and the error message preserves the upstream request ID and framing summary:

```
Model returned an empty terminal turn (no text and no tool call)
[requestId=model-… endpoint=http://127.0.0.1:38603 model=stub httpStatus=200
 upstreamRequestId=upstream-req-1 sseRecords=2 sseParseErrors=0 finishReason=stop retries=0]
```

The gateway now answers such a task request with `502` and `type: "model_gateway_error"`; auxiliary/compaction calls and legitimately truncated turns keep their existing behaviour. The same synthetic case after the fix, same script:

```
gateway status: 502
gateway body: {"error":{"message":"Model returned an empty terminal turn (no text and no tool call) […upstreamRequestId=upstream-req-1 sseRecords=2 …finishReason=stop…]","type":"model_gateway_error"}}
```

### 3. Relay vs direct comparison harness (criterion 3)

`scripts/model-endpoint-compare.mjs` sends the same model alias, the same request body bytes and the same prompt/workload/concurrency to two base URLs and reports per-request latency distributions (`p50`/`p95`, time-to-headers, time-to-first-byte, time-to-first-record, total) and tokens/errors separately from agent duration:

```
node scripts/model-endpoint-compare.mjs --model <alias> \
  --a-base-url <relay> --b-base-url <direct> \
  --a-token-env A_TOKEN --b-token-env B_TOKEN \
  --body-file <identical-body.json> --requests 20 --concurrency 2 --out compare.json
```

It refuses to compare two different model aliases and refuses a workload where the two bodies would differ, so a latency delta cannot come from a body change. Its mechanics are covered by `scripts/model-endpoint-compare.test.mjs` against two local stub endpoints with controlled latency.

### 4. CI summaries separate the failure classes (criterion 4)

`classifyModelWireError` maps every failure to one bucket: `provider_http`, `network`, `timeout`, `aborted`, `parse`, `invalid_response`, `empty_completion`, `unknown`, and records a per-attempt `retryErrors[]`. `.ci/model-wire-summary.mjs` reads the `[model-sse-summary]` lines, aggregates per endpoint/model/classification and writes `.ci-results/model-wire-summary.json`; `prepare-real-e2e-results.mjs` stages it and `real-report.mjs` prints it next to research outcomes, so a provider failure, an empty completion and a local parse/mapping failure are reported as such rather than as a failed research result. Wiring is covered by `.ci/model-wire-summary.test.mjs` and the contract test; the workflow gains one artifact-staging step. These are reported, not added as a second gate: run outcomes still decide pass/fail.

## Acceptance criteria

| # | Criterion | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Privacy-safe per-request diagnostics in real E2E artifacts | Implemented: fields above, one log line per request, staged into `.ci-results/model-wire-summary.json` and aggregated in `real-report.mjs`; no credentials/bodies recorded. Verified against a synthetic SSE server and in unit/CI tests, not yet in an owner-hosted real E2E artifact. |
| 2 | Empty terminal assistant turn with no tool call is an error, preserving upstream request ID + framing summary | Implemented and red→green: `runtime rejects a completed terminal turn with no text and no tool call`, `gateway rejects a completed empty terminal turn instead of reporting success`; gateway returns `502` with request ID + framing summary. |
| 3 | Relay vs direct with same model/body/workload/concurrency, latency separated from agent duration/tokens | **Not delivered** — harness delivered and verified against two local stub endpoints; a real relay/direct measurement was not run here because this host has no relay or model credentials. Tracked in #618. |
| 4 | CI summaries separate provider/empty/local failures from research quality | Implemented and tested: 8 classification buckets, per-attempt retries, aggregate artifact, report section; reported, not gated. |

## Files changed (19)

.ci/README.md +8 −0
.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs +11 −1
.ci/model-wire-summary.mjs +205 −0
.ci/model-wire-summary.test.mjs +107 −0
.ci/prepare-real-e2e-results.mjs +28 −1
.ci/real-report.mjs +35 −2
.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml +3 −0
docs/en/developer-docs/agent-backend.md +30 −0
docs/zh/developer-docs/agent-backend.md +8 −0
jiuwen_swarm/README.md +11 −0
packages/model/src/client.test.ts +92 −0
packages/model/src/client.ts +317 −20
packages/model/src/runtime-client.test.ts +8 −0
packages/model/src/runtime-client.ts +6 −0
scripts/model-endpoint-compare.mjs +235 −0
scripts/model-endpoint-compare.test.mjs +106 −0
services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts +92 −2
services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts +27 −0
services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts +15 −2

## Ran

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/model test` — 131 pass / 0 fail (includes the new endpoint-identity privacy test).
- `node --import tsx --test src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts` (services/api) — 47 pass / 0 fail, including the new empty-turn cases.
- `node --test .ci/model-wire-summary.test.mjs .ci/ci-contract.test.mjs` — 33 pass / 0 fail.
- `node --test scripts/model-endpoint-compare.test.mjs` — 3 pass / 0 fail (two local stub endpoints, controlled latency).
- `pnpm typecheck` — exit 0.
- `pnpm docs:check` — 0 issues, 144 links checked.
- `pnpm ci:selftest` — 91 pass / 0 fail.
- Synthetic empty-`stop` stream reproduction before/after the fix (output above; local script, not committed).

## Not run

- The real relay-vs-direct A/B against real endpoints (criterion 3): no relay or model credentials on this host.
- Full `pnpm ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e`: this host lacks the uv/browser prerequisites; a full `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` run gives 1492 tests, 1487 pass, 5 fail — 4 are missing service venvs (`services/evolve/.venv/bin/python`, `services/paper/.venv/bin/python` ENOENT) and 1 (`always-allow executes subagent code without permission requests or grants`) fails identically on unmodified `ca98c195`, so none are caused by this change.
- `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` has one 1/72 environment failure (`RACE contract` cannot create `/home/xuke/.cache/uv/...`: read-only filesystem), also unrelated to this change.

## Release

`release:fix` — behaviour change: a completed model turn with no text and no tool call now fails the request (502) instead of producing an empty successful answer, and API logs gain one `[model-sse-summary]` line per model request.

pr:621.body:
fix(desktop): cap the SSE frame decoder buffer so an unterminated frame stays bounded

Status: `514ba9fa` supersedes the approved `e5e8cecf`. The approval given at `e5e8cecf` is void by this push — `514ba9fa` is the only tip to score. Re-reading that approved code turned up one more edge (fourth, below); it is fixed here with two red-first tests.

## Problem

`SseFrameDecoder` keeps a partial frame in memory until it sees the `\n\n` terminator, and nothing bounds that buffer while the stream is open. A writer that keeps sending bytes for a frame it never terminates therefore grows the retained buffer for as long as the stream lives — the live window, which is exactly the case of a running run. Because `drain` re-normalised the whole buffer on every chunk, the work also grew quadratically: measured on the old code, 5 000 pushes cost 181 ms, 10 000 cost 1 056 ms, 20 000 cost 4 350 ms for 680 000 characters.

This is pre-existing on `main` and is a framing failure, not a `JSON.parse` failure: no complete frame is ever handed to the parser. #616 covered the end-of-stream tail and the unparseable payload; this closes the live window.

## Contract as the issue now states it

The ceiling is a module constant, `MAX_FRAME_CHARACTERS = 8 * 1024 * 1024` — no setting, consistent with #505.

Past the ceiling the frame is dropped **once**: bytes are discarded up to and including the next `\n\n` (that terminator closes the oversized frame, it does not start a new one), the dropped tail never reaches `JSON.parse`, and parsing resumes after the terminator, so later well-formed frames still arrive and one bad frame does not end a live run. The skip is reported through the skipped-frame path that #616 added: `skipped += 1` and `onEvent(null, id)` in `pump`, with the single existing "Skipped N updates that could not be read." notice — no second notice and no new error mode.

The cursor of a dropped frame comes only from an `id:` line that was fully received (newline-terminated) before the drop; an `id:` line still waiting for its newline may be the prefix of a longer number, so it yields nothing and the replay cursor stays at the last fully received frame. Bytes after the drop are never parsed, so a crafted `data:` line in the tail cannot be re-interpreted as a new event.

Also included, as the issue's optional item: only newly arrived text is normalised now (`pendingCarriageReturn` plus an `unscanned` search offset), which removes the quadratic term while keeping a `\r\n` split across chunks a single line break.

Out of scope and unchanged, as the issue says: a peer that simply stops writing still keeps the stream open (stall/liveness, not memory), and a clean close with no parsed terminal remains silent on the follow path (`use-workspace.ts`, `closeRunStream` sets `terminal: true`). This change does not address either.

## Red-first evidence (first round)

The cap test, with the ceiling guard disabled:

```
not ok - a frame that never terminates stops at the cap and is reported as a skipped frame
Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
+ actual [] - expected [ 4 ]
```

The terminator test, with the drop reset at the drop point instead of discarding through `\n\n` (so the crafted tail reaches the parser):

```
not ok 1 - the decoder resynchronises at the next blank line after a dropped frame
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected

    + [
    +   {
    +     data: '{"type":"injected"}more tail'
    +   }
    + ]
    - []

  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
  operator: 'deepStrictEqual'
  stack: TestContext.<anonymous> (apps/desktop/tests/api-client.test.ts:273:10)
```

Both probes exit 1; the code was restored afterwards and the tree is clean.

## First review round: the discard could swallow the next frame

`zy95-12` (blocking) and the upstream bot (Medium) found this on `6e1d2dfc09`: while `discarding` was true the decoder looked for `"\n\n"` only inside the current chunk, so a blank line split across two chunks (`push("\n")` then `push("\n")`) never matched, `discarding` never cleared, and the next well-formed frame was discarded as if it belonged to the oversized one — with `takeSkipped()` undercounting.

Observed before the fix, at `6e1d2dfc09`:

```
skipped after overflow: [7]
push('\n'): []
push('\n'): []
valid frame after it: []        <- id: 8 swallowed
```

Fixed by carrying one newline across the chunk boundary on the discard path (`sawOneNewlineWhileDiscarding`, the same idea as `unscanned` on the assemble path), plus a red-first test `a dropped frame ends when its blank line arrives split across chunks`. The same probe after the fix:

```
push('\n'): []
push('\n'): []
valid frame: [{"data":"{\"type\":\"run.status\"}","id":8}]
skipped total: []
```

## Second review round: the carry must win over the next frame's own terminator

`zy95-12` blocking review `5680942212` and `HongyeZhou` review `5680995412` at `45388fb5` found the remaining ordering hole: with a carried `\n` pending, `push` still searched the chunk for `\n\n` first, so a chunk shaped `"\n" + a complete next frame` had that frame's own `\n\n` taken as the oversized frame's terminator — the next frame was discarded and `takeSkipped()` undercounted. Fixed by testing the carried newline before the in-chunk search: those two bytes close the dropped frame and the rest of the chunk assembles normally.

Two boundary defects from our own Security read at the same tip, fixed and pinned in the same push:

- `frameCursor` returned the first fully received `id:` line while `parseFrame` uses the last, so a dropped frame with two ids moved the replay cursor by the wrong one;
- a legal frame whose content is exactly `MAX_FRAME_CHARACTERS` was dropped when its blank line arrived split, because the first terminator byte made the buffer `MAX + 1`; one trailing `\n` is framing, not payload, and no longer counts toward the cap.

Each blocking finding has its test:

| Finding | Test |
|---|---|
| `zy95-12` `5680942212` / `HongyeZhou` `5680995412`: in-chunk `\n\n` beats the carried newline and swallows the next frame | `a dropped frame does not swallow a complete frame carried in the same chunk` |
| internal: `frameCursor` used the first `id:` line while `parseFrame` uses the last | `a dropped frame moves the cursor by the last id line it fully received` |
| internal: a frame exactly at the ceiling was dropped when its terminator split | `a frame exactly at the ceiling still parses when its terminator is split` |
| internal (found by re-reading the code after the `e5e8cecf` approval): an empty or lone-CR chunk in the middle of a discard cleared the carried newline, so the next legal frame was swallowed | `an empty chunk does not lose the carried newline while discarding`; `a lone carriage return between the two halves of a blank line keeps the resync` |

Red on `45388fb5` (its `stream.ts` blob `ce2db31d` is identical to `af16898b`). The three tests failed there:

```
(a) a dropped frame does not swallow a complete frame carried in the same chunk
    + actual [] - expected [ { data: '{"type":"run.status"}', id: 8 } ]
(b) a frame exactly at the ceiling still parses when its terminator is split
    + actual [] - expected [ { data: 'zzz…' (8 388 580 chars), id: 9 } ]
(c) a dropped frame moves the cursor by the last id line it fully received
    + actual 3 - expected 4
```

The old decoder observed directly shows the same three failures: `skipped [7]` then `frames []` after the carry, `skipped [9]` with `0` frames at the cap boundary, and `skipped [3]` instead of `[4]`.

## Fourth edge, found after the approval

Review re-read at `e5e8cecf` (this is the same blob this PR was approved on, `stream.ts` `6c7ffb2c`) found one more way for the discard path to swallow a legal frame — the invariant the previous two rounds closed, with an edge neither review nor I had covered.

Shape: while `discarding` is true, a chunk that ends with `\n` sets `sawOneNewlineWhileDiscarding`. If the **next** chunk normalizes to the empty string — a lone `"\r"`, i.e. the CR of a CRLF blank line arriving in its own one-byte read, or an empty chunk — line 106 ran `this.sawOneNewlineWhileDiscarding = chunk.endsWith("\n")` and cleared the carry. The chunk after that then had its own `\n\n` taken as the dropped frame's terminator, so that legal frame was consumed and never parsed, and the skip counter still said one.

Reachability: entering the state needs a frame past `MAX_FRAME_CHARACTERS` (8 MiB) first, so an honest server never gets there and a malicious one already owns the stream — impact on both is nil. It is a correctness defect in this new state machine, not a widening of the security surface.

Reproduced at `e5e8cecf` with a probe importing the real `SseFrameDecoder` (`node --experimental-strip-types`), before the fix:

```
A lone-CR-then-frame-8:  frames: []  skipped: [null]                     <- frame 8 swallowed
B empty-chunk-then-9:    frames: []  skipped: [null]                     <- frame 9 swallowed
C control (no empty chunk): frames: [{"data":"{}","id":10}] skipped: [null]
```

Fixed by returning early from `push` when the normalized chunk is empty (`if (chunk === "") return [];` right after normalization): an empty chunk carries no information, so the carry, `pendingCarriageReturn` and the buffer all stay as they were. Same probe after the fix: A `[{"data":"{\"type\":\"run.status\"}","id":8}]`, B `[{"data":"{}","id":9}]`, C unchanged. Two red-first tests pin it: `an empty chunk does not lose the carried newline while discarding` and `a lone carriage return between the two halves of a blank line keeps the resync`. Both fail on the approved blob unpatched (`6c7ffb2c`, `ERR_ASSERTION`, exit 1):

```
(a) an empty chunk does not lose the carried newline while discarding
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual [] - expected [ { data: '{"type":"run.status"}', id: 8 } ]
(b) a lone carriage return between the two halves of a blank line keeps the resync
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual [] - expected [ { data: '{"type":"run.status"}', id: 9 } ]
```

## Verification

On tip (rebased onto `080a8c80`, current `main`):

- `apps/desktop/tests/api-client.test.ts`: **32/32 pass**
- full desktop suite: **579/579 pass** (89 suites)
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck`: **exit 0**
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: **exit 0**

Tests added or strengthened in `apps/desktop/tests/api-client.test.ts`:

- `a frame that never terminates stops at the cap and is reported as a skipped frame` — exactly at the ceiling nothing is dropped; one character past it the frame is skipped once with its cursor, and `flush()` returns nothing.
- `the decoder resynchronises at the next blank line after a dropped frame` — a crafted `data: {"type":"injected"}` tail yields no frame and no extra skip; the terminator closes the frame and a following valid frame arrives intact.
- `a dropped frame moves the cursor only by an id line that fully arrived` — `[undefined]` when the `id:` line never completed.
- `a dropped frame ends when its blank line arrives split across chunks` — after a drop, `push("\n")` then `push("\n")` ends the discard, and the following `id: 8` frame is delivered while the drop is still counted once.
- `a dropped frame does not swallow a complete frame carried in the same chunk` — after a drop, `push("\n")` then a chunk that starts with `\n` and carries a complete `id: 8` frame closes the drop and delivers id 8; that frame's own `\n\n` is not mistaken for the drop's terminator.
- `a frame exactly at the ceiling still parses when its terminator is split` — content exactly `MAX_FRAME_CHARACTERS`, first newline alone, second closes it; the frame is delivered and nothing is skipped.
- `a dropped frame moves the cursor by the last id line it fully received` — `id: 3` then `id: 4` before the drop yields `[4]`, matching `parseFrame`.
- `a live stream keeps delivering frames after an unterminated one is dropped`.
- `a frame below the ceiling still parses in full` — a 1 MiB report frame.
- `the frame ceiling is a module constant, not a configurable setting` — `MAX_FRAME_CHARACTERS === 8 * 1024 * 1024` and `SseFrameDecoder.length === 0` (zero-argument constructor, so no options object can carry a cap in).
- `a CRLF split across chunks is still one line break`.
- `an empty chunk does not lose the carried newline while discarding` — after a drop, a chunk ending in `\n` then `push("")`; the carry survives and the following `id: 8` frame is delivered.
- `a lone carriage return between the two halves of a blank line keeps the resync` — the same, with the empty-slot chunk being a lone `"\r"` (a CRLF blank line split across two reads): the frame is still delivered.

## Why 8 MiB

`MAX_BODY_BYTES` 1.5 MB for the largest request the client sends, `DEFAULT_TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES` 50 KiB for a whole tool result, a workspace listing capped at 500 entries (about 125 KB of paths and sizes), and `artifact.upserted` carrying a CAS reference rather than the artifact's bytes. The largest legitimate frame is a long model report — a few hundred KiB even with a raised token budget — so 8 MiB leaves well over an order of magnitude of headroom while still bounding a stalled writer.

Fixes #619

Release: fix

pr:625.body:
Unauthenticated API and Runner health responses currently expose sandbox policy, execution identity, versions, quotas, and other deployment details. This change keeps the existing health routes public for liveness while returning deployment details only to callers with a valid bearer token.

## Change

- Public API `GET /health` and `GET /api/health` return exactly `{service,status}`; public Runner `GET /health` returns exactly `{status}`. Missing and wrong tokens both receive only liveness.
- Valid tokens retain the existing detailed response. RunnerClient now sends its token and still learns the remote clock from the Date header before signed execution.
- Direct Runner connections check authentication before platform compatibility, preserving useful invalid-token errors with both old and new Runner health shapes.
- Update existing detail-reading tests, the E2E stack helper, and English/Chinese usage documentation. Add a reusable production-process HTTP journey.

## Scope and issue disposition

Refs #267. Partial fix; keep #267 open.

The requested implementation is present, but validation is incomplete. This draft must not automatically close the issue. Complete the remaining verification, address any resulting failures, and update the issue disposition before considering it fully resolved.

## Baseline and candidate

- Baseline: `5a86d0593a887e825d3a3da136f760b62807f797` (upstream main).
- Baseline analysis: API and Runner returned details before bearer validation; RunnerClient omitted authentication on health requests.
- Tested candidate: `064e97b4f6916f6dc6b2a35a3c04c8c51a5e6254`.
- Environment: Linux; Bubblewrap 0.11.0 and isolated temporary directories. The system Bubblewrap 0.6.1 lacks the flag used by existing network tests.

## Acceptance evidence

| API health, both routes, missing/wrong tokens | Exactly service/status; HTTP 200; no Runner record | API health regression and production-process journey | PASS |

| Valid tokens and API-to-Runner aggregation | Existing details and capabilities remain available | API/Runner tests and production-process journey | PASS |
| Initial Runner clock synchronization | Remote Date header is observed before subsequent signed calls | RunnerClient test with a simulated remote clock offset | PASS |
| Direct connections to old/new Runners | Valid credentials connect; wrong credentials receive a token error | remote-compute tests for both health shapes | PASS |
| Runner outage | Public API remains live; authenticated diagnosis reports degraded/unavailable | Production-process journey | PASS |
| Existing Runner health detail consumers | Authenticated TCP/Unix-socket/network tests retain their assertions | Full Runner server file and sandbox-network tests | PASS |

`pnpm build`, `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`, and `pnpm docs:check` passed. The focused tests above total 89 executed/89 passed, in addition to the four journey steps and L1.

## E2E user journey

The driver starts the production API and Runner entry points on isolated loopback ports. Its four steps start the services, assert six missing/wrong-token responses with exact public bodies, verify authenticated details and API aggregation, then stop Runner and verify public liveness plus authenticated degradation diagnostics. Four steps passed, zero failed. It uses no external model or service and cleans up its own processes and data.

The earlier `pnpm test:shared` attempt was stopped during Python dependency preparation before tests ran. The separate local UT/ST/mocked-browser-E2E attempts and their results are recorded below. Incomplete preparation or a timed-out run is not a passing suite. Actual Docker/binary/start-stack and macOS execution remain unverified.

## Release

Release category: release:breaking

User impact: anonymous callers can check liveness but can no longer inspect deployment details.

Compatibility and migration: scripts and clients that inspect health detail fields must send the configured bearer token. Upgrade the API and Runner together, or upgrade API first: an older API omits the Runner token on health requests and will not receive details from a new Runner.
