pr:626.body:
## Problem and change

A host data symlink can exist in a Session workspace yet resolve to an unreadable location inside the sandbox. A command can then silently take a synthetic-data fallback and report success. Check workspace symlink readability in the actual execution sandbox before Shell or Python/R evaluation, and reject inaccessible links with the link path and actionable copy/upload guidance.

Valid relative, chained, sandbox-visible absolute and runtime links remain supported. Reused Shell/scientific sessions recheck their mounted workspaces. Filenames are passed as NUL-separated raw bytes, preserving Linux filenames and avoiding shell interpolation. English and Chinese documentation explains workspace paths, materialization and the managed-workspace-only scope of `workspace_transfer`.

## Scope and issue disposition

Refs #433. Partial fix; keep #433 open pending complete repository verification and review.

The operator selected explicit rejection and import guidance instead of automatic copying. This PR does not introduce an arbitrary-host-directory mount/import UI. Validation happens before evaluation; this is not a filesystem watcher and does not guarantee detection of unmanaged changes after preflight or links created within the same command. Direct host execution is unchanged.

## Baseline and candidate

- Reproduction baseline: `7bef5b2661e92fb881d96eb50f94f4b2775652d2`. Through production Runner HTTP, an absolute host data link caused `SYNTHETIC_FALLBACK`, exit code 0, and an execution marker.
- Tested implementation: `576db3d098b15edd54d925a45fbae21112e42305` on Linux with bubblewrap, isolated data/ports, matching service lockfiles, and the previously installed pinned `workswarm0.2.6` environment. Editable Python packages point at the tested checkout.
- PR head: `de9ee975c` rebased onto main `3d223ede7bce633de8f954e2ec8a23c695a5de23`. The unrelated coverage change from the reproduction baseline is excluded. Results below belong to the tested implementation SHA; no complete current-head CI pass is claimed.

## Acceptance evidence

| Scenario | Expected and observed result | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Host-only absolute data link | Reject before Shell code, name the link, explain real-file import; no execution marker | Production Runner HTTP journey, step 2 |
| Python and accepted background Shell | Python rejects; background state is queryably failed with guidance; neither writes its marker | HTTP journey, step 3 |
| Materialize real data, then use a relative link | Same workspace recovers; Shell and Python both compute and persist 5 from the real input | HTTP journey, steps 4–5 |
| Valid relative/chained/sandbox-absolute/runtime links and raw filenames | Remain readable and usable | Runner regression tests |
| Relative escapes, dangling/cyclic links and special filenames | Reject clearly without executing injected filename content | Runner regression tests |
| Read-only parent and reused Shell | Use actual nested mount paths; recheck on reuse and recover while retaining Shell state | Runner regression tests |
| Import guidance | Describe sandbox visibility and copy/upload/managed transfer boundaries | English/Chinese reference docs; L1 |

## Repository checks

| `pnpm typecheck` | — | — | — | — | — | PASS |

Known full-suite failures:

- UT: the Agent-created Skill draft assertion (`0 !== 1`), sandbox-network test (`bwrap: Unknown option --disable-userns` on the host's old bubblewrap), and research Python check (pinned `pandas==2.3.3` needs a compatible cached distribution under offline preparation). Each was reproduced with targeted checks at the unmodified `7bef5b26` baseline; this is not a claim that the full baseline suite passed.
- ST: the pinned standalone Python distribution download failed (`fetch failed`), and the MCP 100-concurrent-call contract timed out. The MCP failure also reproduces in a targeted baseline check. These checks remain failures; assertions and selection were not weakened.

pr:634.body:
fix(desktop): keep the carried newline when the next chunk normalizes to nothing

## Why this is a separate PR

#621 was merged at `863969c2265a0645aa4d5333e0a8f7d0cae59a1f` — the merge queue's group commit, built from that PR's **pre-fix** head `e5e8cecf`. What landed on `main` is therefore the tree as it stood before the last fix in that PR: `apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts` blob `6c7ffb2cac0711b61474a54c6c372306df24513e` (no `if (chunk === "") return [];`), tests at 30. The fix commit `514ba9faa7e99592c3fc64c41f10397651bad5b3` is not an ancestor of `main`.

The defect below is on `main` now. This PR carries that one-line guard and its two tests, rebased onto current `main`, and nothing else: `stream.ts` `+5/−0` (4 comment lines and the guard), tests `+34/−0` (two tests, 30 → 32).

## The defect, on current `main`

While the decoder is discarding an oversized frame, a chunk that ends in `\n` sets `sawOneNewlineWhileDiscarding`. If the next chunk normalizes to the empty string — a lone `"\r"`, i.e. the CR of a CRLF blank line arriving in its own read, or an empty chunk — `stream.ts:106` runs `this.sawOneNewlineWhileDiscarding = chunk.endsWith("\n")` and clears the carry. The chunk after that then has its own `\n\n` taken as the dropped frame's terminator, so that legal frame is consumed, never parsed, and the skip counter still says one.

Reachability: entering the state needs a frame past `MAX_FRAME_CHARACTERS` (8 MiB) first, so an honest server never gets there and a sender that got there already owns the stream — impact on both is nil. It is a correctness defect in the state machine #621 added, not a widening of the security surface.

Red on `main`'s blob `6c7ffb2c`, probe importing the real `SseFrameDecoder` (`node --experimental-strip-types`):

```
A lone-CR-then-frame-8: frames: [] skipped: [null]                     <- frame 8 swallowed
B empty-chunk-then-frame-9: frames: [] skipped: [null]                 <- frame 9 swallowed
C control (no empty chunk): frames: [{"data":"{}","id":10}] skipped: [null]
```

The two tests added here, lifted verbatim and run against that same blob:

```
not ok 1 - an empty chunk does not lose the carried newline while discarding
  Expected values to be strictly deep-equal: + actual [] - expected [ { data: '{"type":"run.status"}', id: 8 } ]
not ok 2 - a lone carriage return between the two halves of a blank line keeps the resync
  Expected values to be strictly deep-equal: + actual [] - expected [ { data: '{"type":"run.status"}', id: 9 } ]
# tests 2  # pass 0  # fail 2        (ERR_ASSERTION, exit 1)
```

Run against this tip's blob the same two tests pass, and the pre-existing CRLF-split test is green on both blobs, so the red is specific to the two new paths and the normal path is unaffected.

## The fix

`if (chunk === "") return [];` immediately after normalization and before the `discarding` branch: an empty chunk carries no information, so the carry, `pendingCarriageReturn` and the buffer all stay as they were. `pendingCarriageReturn` is set before that point, so the early return cannot lose a held `\r`.

Same probe after the fix: A `[{"data":"{\"type\":\"run.status\"}","id":8}]`, B `[{"data":"{}","id":9}]`, C unchanged.

## Verification

On this tip (rebased onto `863969c2`, current `main`):

- `apps/desktop/tests/api-client.test.ts`: **32/32 pass**
- full desktop suite: **663/663 pass** (92 suites) — the count is larger than the one in #621 because `main` has gained tests since that branch was cut
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: **exit 0**
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`: **exit 0**

## Queue facts behind the merge (stated, not argued)

- The queue entry predates the fix commit: `enqueuedAt 2026-10-29T00:35:29Z`, group commit `863969c2` built from head `e5e8cecf`.

pr:642.body:
Fixes #641

`VersionStore.putWorkspaceFile` decided reuse from `fstat` identity only (`dev`/`ino`/`size`/`mtimeNs`/`ctimeNs`) and returned the cached `DataRef` without reading the file. A same-size in-place rewrite inside one filesystem timestamp tick therefore kept the stale bytes in workspace snapshots. The cached *object* identity had the same blind spot, so a same-size tamper of an existing CAS object was reused with no verification at all. The class comment already said "file metadata is never taken as evidence"; the implementation contradicted it.

Branch cut from live `main` `d72cdf8c` (the issue's `5e56ea77` line is the filing snapshot; `packages/cas` did not change in between, `versioning.ts` is still blob `679f5a61`).

## What changes

- Reuse now requires both: the current bytes hash to the cached ref, and `verifyRef` re-verifies the stored object. Metadata still narrows the work (a changed identity skips the digest pass) but it never decides reuse.
- Changed bytes fall back to the existing streaming publish path; an unchanged file still avoids the temp write, the `fsync`, the `link` and the directory `fsync`, which is the cost the cache exists to save.
- `objectIdentity` is removed: copying the object's stat fields into the cache is exactly what made a same-tick tamper invisible, and the byte verification supersedes it.

## Red → green

Red before the fix — the loop fails on the second round, not merely "sometimes":

```
not ok 1 - a same-size in-place rewrite never reuses stale workspace bytes
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly equal:
    + actual - expected
    + 'bbbbbbbbb0'
    - 'aaaaaaaaa1'
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

Measured on `d72cdf8c` over 200 rounds: `digest_reused=171 first_put_stale_bytes=174 second_put_stale_bytes=171` (the digest-count difference is cross-round reuse of the previous round's ref).

Green after the fix:

```
ok 1 - a same-size in-place rewrite never reuses stale workspace bytes
ok 2 - unchanged workspace bytes are still reused without republishing
# pass 2
# fail 0
```

Same 200-round probe: `digest_reused=0 first_put_stale_bytes=0 second_put_stale_bytes=0`.

## Validation

Ran on `25272529` (local tree; fork commit `abc6f8c5` carries the same tree):

- `cd packages/cas && node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"` — **3 consecutive runs, 36/36 pass, 0 fail each** (34 existing + 2 new).
- 200-round reproduction from the issue (with a byte check on the returned ref): **0/200 stale**, was 171/200 reusing the stale ref.
- `tsc -p packages/cas/tsconfig.json`: build exit 0, `--noEmit` exit 0.

Not run locally: `ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e`. This diff only touches `packages/cas`, whose UT suite is the one above; the full-repo layers are the gate in this pull request's own CI run.

## The existing `Missing expected rejection` flake at `versioning.test.ts:290`

It is the same root cause, not an unrelated flake, and the assertion is unchanged. On this host it passed 20/20 standalone and 3/3 full-suite runs on `d72cdf8c`, so it did not reproduce here; it only fails when the tamper write lands inside the cached object's timestamp tick. A direct probe that tampers the object immediately after caching reproduces the same gap **197/200**, and after this fix that probe is **200/200 `Object integrity failure`, 0 silent reuse** — so the test no longer depends on tick luck.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable: no user-observable path changes. `packages/cas` is internal storage; the CAS suite above is the coverage.

## Release

Release category: release:fix (the GitHub label needs a maintainer; it is pending, not applied)

User impact: a workspace snapshot no longer records stale bytes after a same-size in-place rewrite, and a tampered CAS object is reported instead of being reused.

Compatibility and migration: none.

pr:648.body:
Fixes #647

Owner: Dev1
Written-by: Dev-1
Branch: `dev1/fix/647-web-test-module-resolution`

## Problem

A clean tree cannot run the web test suite. Every workspace package publishes its runtime entry from `dist/` (`packages/*/package.json` → `"default": "./dist/*.js"`) and no `dist/` is committed, so a package-level run that does not build first resolves those imports to files that do not exist:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx
# tests 448
# pass 385
# fail 63
# Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../apps/web/node_modules/@sciencediscovery/operational-logging/dist/diagnostics.js'
#   imported from .../apps/web/src/ErrorDiagnosticActions.tsx
# Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../@sciencediscovery/schema/dist/index.js'
#   imported from .../apps/web/src/Markdown.tsx
```

The repo's own `pnpm test` hides this because it runs `pnpm build` first; the per-package script (`tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx`) does not. The 63 victims are not defects — they fail at import time, before any assertion runs.

The failure is not specific to `operational-logging`: `schema`, `skill`, `plugin-sdk` and their transitive workspace dependencies fail the same way.

## Commits (red first)

1. `test(web): prove the suite dies when the workspace packages are unbuilt` — one test asserting that every `@sciencediscovery/*` entry the web app imports resolves to a file that exists. Red on the unbuilt tree:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/workspace-package-dist.test.ts
not ok 1 - every workspace package the web app imports resolves from its built entry
  error: '@sciencediscovery/artifact-json/manifest resolves to
   .../apps/web/node_modules/@sciencediscovery/artifact-json/dist/manifest.js,
   which does not exist; the workspace packages need building first'
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

Full suite on the same tree: **449 tests / 385 pass / 64 fail** (63 pre-existing + this one).

2. `fix(web): build the workspace packages the test suite imports` — `apps/web`'s `test` script now runs `scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs .` before `tsx --test`. The script walks `apps/web`'s workspace dependencies transitively and builds only the packages whose `dist/` is missing, using the repo's `typescript` and each package's own `tsconfig.json` — exactly what `pnpm build` would produce. It is a no-op once they are built, so the CI path that already ran `pnpm build` pays one directory listing and nothing else.

No test file is modified, and production resolution is untouched: the runtime entry stays `dist/`, which `node dist/server.js` and vite both need.

3. `test(scripts): pin the ensure-workspace-dist skip and build order` — the builder had no test of its own behaviour. Two cases run against a throwaway workspace (a copy of the script, fixture packages, and a stand-in `tsc` that records where it was pointed and writes the `dist/` the compiler would emit, so no TypeScript build is paid for):

- a package without `dist/` is built, a package that already has `dist/` is not rebuilt (its `dist/` is left untouched), and a second run of the script is silent;
- a package is built only after everything it depends on (`leaf` → `middle` → `top`, plus an unrelated sibling, built in that order).

Both cases are green as written. Their red side is a mutation, checked locally on the working tree and not committed: dropping the `dist/` skip fails the first case (`a second run must not rebuild a built package`), and moving `ordered.push(dep)` before the dependency visit fails the second.

## Verification

Red (clean tree, before the fix) → green:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx     # no dist/
# tests 449   # pass 385   # fail 64
$ node scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs apps/web
built workspace packages without dist: @sciencediscovery/operational-logging,
@sciencediscovery/external-urls, @sciencediscovery/schema, @sciencediscovery/cas, …
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx     # deps built
# tests 1131   # pass 1131   # fail 0
```

The suite grows from 449 to 1131 because the files that could not load now run. Typechecks: `apps/web` `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` → 0; repo `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` → 0. A second run of the builder prints nothing (idempotent).

## Labels and timing

`agent-ready` could not be applied to the issue by the team (the token gets 403 on label writes) and the owner's 60-minute deadline takes precedence over the usual 24-hour wait, so this is pushed ahead of the label being restored.

## Ran

- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/workspace-package-dist.test.ts` → 0/1 before the fix, 1/1 after
- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` → 385/449 before, **1131/1131 after**
- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` → 0
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` (repo root) → 0
- `node scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs apps/web` twice → 17 packages the first time, silent the second
- `node --test scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.test.mjs` → 2/2, and the same two cases fail under the two mutations above
- `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` → 70/71: the one failure is `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`, which shells out to `uv` and dies on the read-only `~/.cache/uv` on this host, unrelated to this change
- `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check` → `CI test catalog OK: 7 cases, 24 tags, 4 layers`

## Not run

- The shared tagged plan end to end (`node test/support/tagged/shared.mjs list`): on this tree it stops during collection with `DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION: apps/web/tests/markdown-math.test.ts:16`, a file this branch does not touch and which fails the same way alone at the base commit. The new file was collected on its own instead (`node-collect.mjs` → 2 cases, `category:ut`).
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` verbatim: on this host pnpm's dependency-status check aborts with `ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY` / `EROFS` on the pnpm store (outside the workspace, read-only), so the script's two commands were run directly, in order.

Release: fix

pr:652.body:
Fixes #649

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

**Label note.** `agent-ready` could not be applied from this account (403 with both REST and the connector, same as #641); this PR is proposed ahead of the 24 h label window because of the owner's 60-minute deadline. Claim record: issue comment `6487087449`.

## The defect

`parseNotebook` (`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts:373-408`) truncated `rawCells.slice(0, maxCells)` *before* dropping cell types the preview does not support, so a `heading` cell (or a malformed entry) consumed the budget and was then discarded: `maxCells=2` over `[heading, code, code]` returned one cell instead of two. `truncated: totalCells > maxCells` inherited the same mistake — it reported truncation against the raw cell count even when every supported cell was on screen.

## What changes

- Map and filter to supported cells first, then `slice(0, maxCells)` the supported list, so unsupported entries never consume the budget.
- Derive `truncated` from the supported count, so dropping an unsupported cell is no longer reported as truncation.
- `totalCells` keeps counting every raw cell, because it describes the document, not the preview budget.

## Red → green

Test: `notebook preview fills maxCells with valid cells after skipping unsupported cell types` — `cells=[heading, code, code]`, `maxCells=2`; it asserts `totalCells===3`, two visible cells, both `code`, and `truncated===false`.

```bash
cd services/api
node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "notebook preview" src/dashboard.test.ts
```

Before (red-test commit `d462439d`, first tip on this branch):

```
  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
  name: 'AssertionError'
  expected: 2
  actual: 1
  operator: 'strictEqual'
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

After (this tip):

```
# pass 3
# fail 0
```

## Validation

Ran:
- `node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts` in `services/api`: **32/32 pass, 0 fail**.
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: exit 0.

Not run locally:
- repository-wide layers (`ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e`): the pnpm wrapper aborts with `ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY` in this container; this PR's own CI run is the authority for those.

## Release

`release:fix` — label to be applied by a maintainer (labels are not writable from this account, 403).

## Known limitation (recorded, not fixed here)

`maxCells` is no longer a work bound for `parseNotebook`. The previous code mapped only the first `maxCells` raw cells; this change maps every raw cell and then filters to the supported ones, so the work scales with the whole notebook and array-form `source` values are joined once per cell.

Measured on extracted copies of the two implementations, 100k cells: array-form source 145 ms / +44 MB before, 200 ms / +75 MB after; string-form source 69 ms / +26 MB before, 93 ms / +38 MB after. That is a linear 1.5-1.7x, with no cliff and no new unbounded path, so it is recorded rather than fixed in this pull request.

If `maxCells` has to bound the work again, the shape to use is a single scan that stops as soon as `maxCells + 1` supported cells have been collected, keeping `totalCells` as the raw count so `truncated` stays accurate.

pr:653.body:
Fixes #650

Owner: Dev1
Written-by: Dev-1
Branch: `dev1/fix/650-csv-quoted-cells`

## Problem

The dataset preview splits `.csv`/`.tsv` text on raw newlines and then on the raw delimiter, with no quote state:

```ts
// services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts:246 before this change
function splitDelimited(source: string, delimiter: RegExp): string[][] {
  return source.split(/\r?\n/).filter((line) => line.length > 0).map((line) => line.split(delimiter));
}
```

So an RFC 4180 field that contains the delimiter, a newline, or a doubled quote breaks the table: the quoted cell is split into extra columns, and a newline inside quotes inflates `totalRows` and shifts every later row. Any spreadsheet the user exports with a comma in a cell is shown mangled.

## Commits (red first)

1. `test(api): prove quoted csv cells shift columns in the dataset preview` — durable test in `services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts`, input `name,note` / `Alice,"hello, world"` / `Bob,"say ""hi"""`. Red on the unbuilt fix:

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern="parses quoted csv cells" src/dashboard.test.ts
not ok 1 - dataset preview parses quoted csv cells
  Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
  + actual - expected
    [
      'Alice',
  +   '"hello',
  +   ' world"'
  -   'hello, world'
    ]
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

2. `fix(api): split csv and tsv records with quote state` — `splitDelimited` walks the text once with a quote state: a delimiter or newline inside quotes stays in the field, `""` inside quotes is one `"`, a quote opens a field only at its start (so an apostrophe or a quote mid-cell is left alone), CRLF and a trailing newline are handled, and blank lines are still dropped. `parseDelimitedTable` now passes the delimiter as a string (`,` / `\t`). `totalRows`, `truncated` and the row limit keep their meaning; `parseNotebook` and everything else in the file are untouched.

## Verification

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts
# tests 32   # pass 32   # fail 0

$ node_modules/.bin/tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit
exit 0
```

Two cases checked against the built preview with a throwaway copy of the test file (not committed), because they are not in the issue's assertions: a quoted newline stays one cell and `totalRows` counts records (`Alice,"line one\nline two"` with CRLF line endings → 2 rows, row 0 is `["Alice", "line one\nline two"]`), and a TSV quoted tab stays one cell while a blank line in the middle of the file is dropped (2 rows).

## Labels and timing

`agent-ready` cannot be applied to the issue by the team (the token gets 403 on label writes) and the owner's deadline takes precedence over the usual 24-hour wait, so this is pushed ahead of the label being restored.

## Perf follow-up — `5f946116` (spans, not per-character concatenation)

The quote state machine above built every field with `field += char`. An unclosed quote makes the whole file one field, so one malformed csv built one string node per character: Security measured **8 MB → 1.27 s / 359 MB RSS, 16 MB → 4.67 s / 628 MB, 32 MB → 6.27 s / 1.17 GB** on `29a49360`, against 17–58 ms / 68–76 MB for the pre-#650 splitter — 30–100× CPU and 15–35× memory, i.e. seconds of blocked event loop from a single preview request over unauthenticated content.

The field is now kept as spans of the source and joined once when it ends: an ordinary run is a single `slice`, and only an escaped quote (`""`) closes a span early. The state machine, the blank-line rule and `totalChars` / `truncated` are untouched.

New test: `dataset preview keeps an unclosed quote as one field` — 64 KB body, asserts one column that equals the whole quoted body, `rows` empty, `totalRows 0`, `truncated false`. It pins the parsed result only; no timing assertion, since CI machines are noisy.

Behaviour equivalence: 400 randomized csv/tsv inputs (fixed seed; alphabet includes `,`, `\t`, `\n`, `\r`, `"`, spaces, non-ASCII) produce an identical sha256 digest of every payload (`mode`, `columns`, `rows`, `totalRows`, `truncated`) before and after this commit. Security additionally ran 200k random inputs plus 12 targeted cases with identical output.

Local cost of the same unclosed-quote file through `buildArtifactVersionPreview` (one process per size, this host):

| file | before `29a49360` | after `5f946116` |
|---|---|---|
| 8 MB | 1764 ms / 421 MB RSS | 118 ms / 174 MB |
| 16 MB | 3708 ms / 674 MB RSS | 353 ms / 190 MB |

The 32 MB row and the 200k-input differential run are Security's, from their local probe; the 8/16 MB pairs are mine.

## Ran

- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern="parses quoted csv cells" src/dashboard.test.ts` → 0/1 red on the test commit, 1/1 green after the fix
- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts` → **32/32**, and **33/33** with the perf commit (the new unclosed-quote case is the 33rd)
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` → 0
- quoted-newline + CRLF, quoted-tab + blank-line checks described above → both green

## Not run

- The whole `services/api` suite (it is long and needs every workspace package built): only `src/dashboard.test.ts`, the file that owns the preview, plus the package typecheck.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` verbatim: on this host pnpm's dependency-status check aborts on the read-only store (`EROFS`), so the commands were run directly.

pr:657.body:
Fixes #646

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

**Label note.** `agent-ready` could not be applied from this account (403 with both REST and the connector, same as #641); this PR is proposed ahead of the 24 h label window because of the owner's sprint deadline. Claim record: issue comment `6486721604`.

## What the problem is

`putWorkspaceFile` re-derived the source digest and then re-read the stored object on every cache hit, so one hit cost two full reads (`unchangedWorkspaceBytes` → `verifyRef`). At 1 MiB that was 9.404 ms median, with the two halves costing the same (source hash 4.591 ms, object hash 4.682 ms): the cost is SHA-256 throughput, not syscall overhead. `services/runner/src/execution-manager.ts:96` snapshots the workspace after every shell execution, so it was paid per execution.

The source re-hash stays. It is the only criterion that survives a same-size in-place rewrite inside one filesystem timestamp tick — that is #641, where metadata-based reuse served stale bytes in 171 of 200 iterations. The object read is the removable half: the object is content-addressed, written once through `link` + `fsync`, and this store already records what it verified in `admitted`, whose entries `checked` revokes on any integrity failure.

## Trust boundary

A `VersionStore` instance verifies a stored object once and then admits it; the source bytes are still re-hashed on every reuse, so a same-size in-place rewrite of the workspace file is still caught. An admission is evidence that *this instance* saw those bytes, not that they are still the verified ones. The admission assumes no writer outside this process changes an object after this process verified it — the same assumption `validateClosureForCommit` has relied on since before this change. Every path that hands bytes to a caller re-hashes and fails closed (`Object integrity failure`), so a tampered or vanished object can never be delivered as good data; a vanished object makes the next cache hit republish it.

Attribution, so this is not read as a regression: `admitted`, and `validateClosureForCommit` skipping already-admitted objects, are pre-existing. #642 brought the source re-hash on reuse, the object verification, and `checked()` clearing admissions. This PR changes exactly one thing: `unchangedWorkspaceBytes` no longer calls `verifyRef` for an already-admitted ref (`packages/cas/src/versioning.ts:146-152`), turning per-reuse verification into per-instance verification, with the #641 fix untouched. A size/mtime shortcut was deliberately not added, and the admission was deliberately not narrowed to a single snapshot or put sequence: the first would reopen the blind spot #642 closed, the second would remove the benefit this PR exists for.

Known limitation, deliberately kept: an admission means only that this instance saw those bytes. Existence is re-checked on every admitted read; content is not. A same-size, same-mtime replacement of an *object* is therefore not detected by the admission itself, and surfaces only as a fail-closed error (`ENOENT` or `Object integrity failure`) at the next read, audit or new-instance rehash that touches those bytes. On the commit path (`validateReachable` with `trustAdmitted`, used by `validateClosureForCommit`) an admitted record is stopped at that existence check: its bytes, and the closure behind them, are not re-read, so a replaced-but-present record is accepted by the commit and fails closed only when something later calls `read` / `readRecord` / `validateClosure` on it. That skip of already-admitted objects is pre-existing — this PR only puts the existence check in front of it. The admission can never make a tampered object be delivered as good data.

## Commits

- `1889093442a7db831c2a22c2932df2387fe0c063` — the red test only: `a cache hit does not re-read the stored object on every call`.
- `f54ef875a78db25f58ad294528b83badf04d4d17` — the fix: admit the object after its first successful `verifyRef` and skip the re-read afterwards (one verification per object per store instance), and document that in `putWorkspaceFile`/`unchangedWorkspaceBytes`.
- `32c45733f7b083c2a3fccaef0cf45670513e4f86` — follow-up to the reviewer finding: a cache hit `stat`s the admitted object before trusting the admission, so a blob that disappeared under a live process falls back to the existing `return undefined` → republish path, plus the regression test for it.

- `da2036e653c1907759816d885405a37885db61f1` — red tests for the second admitted reader: the fail-closed read assertion in the republish case, and a case where an admitted root is removed before the next ref commit.
- `37fb64bdbf673e2b187a3d9aef3883741e2a5075` — the fix for it: one shared `dropIfVanished` helper, called before trusting an admission in **both** readers.

All five commits are on the head branch, in order, each on top of its predecessor; `git fetch` of a bare SHA needs the fork remote or `refs/pull/657/head`. No amend, no force-push.

## Red → green

```bash
cd packages/cas
node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "cache hit does not re-read" src/versioning.test.ts
```

Before (`a074172f` + the red-test commit):

```
  error: |-
    the stored object is verified once per store instance, not once per cache hit

  expected: 1
  actual: 2
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

After (this tip):

```
# pass 1
# fail 0
```

The test also rewrites the file in place afterwards and asserts a new digest is published, so the source re-hash cannot be traded away for the object cache.

Second pair, for the commit path (`da2036e6` red, `37fb64bd` green):

```bash
cd packages/cas
node --import tsx --test src/versioning.test.ts
```

Before (`32c45733` + the red test commit): **18 tests, 17 pass, 1 fail**

```
# Subtest: a ref commit re-verifies an admitted object that disappeared instead of trusting the admission
not ok 18 - a ref commit re-verifies an admitted object that disappeared instead of trusting the admission
  error: 'Missing expected rejection.'
  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
# pass 17
# fail 1
```

After (this tip): **18 tests, 18 pass, 0 fail** in that file, and `src/**/*.test.ts` is **39/39 pass, 0 fail**.

## Cost, measured

Harness: node v22.23.2, single thread, ext4, page-cache warm, 25 iterations after 3 warm-ups, one `putWorkspaceFile` cache hit, median / max in ms.

| file | before (`a074172f`) | after (this tip) | source-hash-only lower bound |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 KiB | 1.202 / 2.225 | 0.617 / 1.467 | 0.596 / 0.788 |
| 1 MiB | 9.404 / 11.050 | 4.748 / 5.339 | 4.701 / 5.167 |
| 8 MiB | 68.317 / 71.872 | 34.062 / 35.194 | 34.103 / 48.020 |

After the fix the hit cost sits on the source hash, i.e. the second read is gone. Aggregate through the real `snapshotWorkspace` on a 64 × 1 MiB workspace, all hits: **588.4 ms → 309.4 ms**. A repeat run on a loaded machine inflated both the after column and the source-only bound by the same factor (9.06 / 9.10 ms at 1 MiB), which is the expected shape when only one read remains.

## Review finding: an admission outlived its object

`sciencediscovery-bot` (review `5692570203`, inline `4408458539`, `versioning.ts:147`, Medium) showed that the admission turned "verified on every hit" into "verified once per process": if the blob disappears while the process lives, the next cache hit reuses the ref instead of republishing, and a record can be committed pointing at a missing object.

Reproduced on `f54ef875` and on `a074172f` with the same probe (put → put → `rm` blob → put → `readData`):

| step | `a074172f` | `f54ef875` |
|---|---|---|
| `BLOB_RESTORED` after the third put | `true` | `false` |
| `readData(ref)` | `OK` | `ENOENT` |

Fix: before trusting an admission, `stat` the object (`ENOENT` → the existing `return undefined` → republish branch). One syscall against a source re-hash that is milliseconds per hit. Regression test: `a cache hit republishes a stored object that disappeared after its first verification` — red on `f54ef875` (`expected: true / actual: false` at the post-republish `existsSync`), green after the `stat`.

Security follow-up (same review, wider scope): the existence check was only on the put path, while `admitted` has two readers — `unchangedWorkspaceBytes` and `validateReachable` (used by `validateClosureForCommit`). Removing an already-admitted record and committing without an intervening put therefore still produced a version that pointed at missing bytes. `dropIfVanished` is now shared by both, uses `lstat` + `isFile()` so an object replaced by a directory or a symlink is treated the same as a missing one, and revokes every admission exactly like `checked()` does; the commit path then reaches `readRecord`/`verifyRef`, which throws `ENOENT`. The helper is existence evidence only — it never claims the bytes are still the verified ones. Scope, so this is not read as a rewrite: `validateReachable` already skipped admitted objects on `main`, so the gap was pre-existing; this PR adds one `dropIfVanished` call at that reader rather than restructuring it. Still out of scope, as directed: a vanished *transitive dependency* of an admitted record (a different change), and any size/mtime shortcut.

## Validation

Ran:
- `cd packages/cas && node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"` on this tip: **39/39 pass, 0 fail**.
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p packages/cas/tsconfig.json` and `--noEmit`: exit 0.
- The red test on `a074172f` + the first commit (output above).

Not run locally:
- repository-wide layers (`ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e`): the pnpm wrapper aborts with `ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY` in this container; this PR's own CI run is the authority for those.

## Release

`release:fix` — label to be applied by a maintainer (labels are not writable from this account, 403).

The BOM is an encoding marker written by Excel's "CSV UTF-8", not part of the first header cell; a client matching headers by name currently misses that column.

It also drops the now-unused `STRUCTURE_ATOM_TRUNCATION` constant and the one note assertion from the red test, because the payload type is intentionally left unchanged.

pr:663.body:
Fixes #660

- Owner: Dev1
- Written-by: Dev-1
- Base: `a074172f60e5667e72ff04246316a0a41552cb46` (live `main` when the branch was cut)
- Claim record: pickup-ok `6487423422` named Dev-2; the Lead's append-only reassignment `6487508566` records `#660` as Dev-1 on `dev1/fix/660-truncate-code-point`. No `dev2/fix/660-*` branch or PR ever existed.
- `agent-ready` is not on this issue (the fork cannot apply labels, HTTP 403), so this PR is opened ahead of the 24h label window under the owner's deadline.

## Red first — `b6a87d12` (tests only)

Five tests in `services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts`. The artifact content is `"a".repeat(9) + "\u{1F600}" + "tail"` — 9 ASCII characters, then U+1F600 (two UTF-16 units), then `tail` — previewed with `maxChars = "10"`, so a code-unit cut lands between the two halves of the emoji.

1. `markdown preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair` (`markdown-source`)
2. `latex preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair` (`latex-source`)
3. `structure preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair` (`structure-source`)
4. `json-source preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair` (`json-source`, i.e. the `jsonSourceOf` path shared with `rawJson`)
5. `an ascii markdown preview still cuts at exactly maxChars` — pure ASCII must keep today's result byte for byte (`"x".repeat(10)` from 20), the guard against a code-point rewrite quietly changing ordinary text.

Each surrogate test asserts the payload `source` contains no lone surrogate (the issue's regex, `[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])|(?<![\uD800-\uDBFF])[\uDC00-\uDFFF]`) and that the cut sits on a character boundary — the whole U+1F600 is kept or dropped, never half. `totalChars` / `truncated` keep their current meaning and are asserted unchanged.

```console
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern="surrogate pair|ascii markdown preview" src/dashboard.test.ts
not ok 1 - markdown preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair
    source carries a lone surrogate: "aaaaaaaaa\ud83d"
not ok 2 - latex preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair
    source carries a lone surrogate: "aaaaaaaaa\ud83d"
not ok 3 - structure preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair
    source carries a lone surrogate: "aaaaaaaaa\ud83d"
not ok 4 - json-source preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair
    source carries a lone surrogate: "aaaaaaaaa\ud83d"
ok 5 - an ascii markdown preview still cuts at exactly maxChars
# tests 5
# pass 1
# fail 4
```

Every failing payload ends in `\ud83d`, an unpaired high surrogate: invalid UTF-16 that only the web renderer's one path patches (`SourcePreview.tsx:62` strips a trailing high surrogate), while `json-source`, `structure-source` and the raw-JSON view get no guard.

## Fix — `57146c51`

One helper, called by all four truncating paths:

```ts
function truncateAtCodePoint(text: string, maxChars: number): string {
  if (text.length <= maxChars) return text;
  const last = text.charCodeAt(maxChars - 1);
  const next = text.charCodeAt(maxChars);
  const splitsPair = last >= 0xd800 && last <= 0xdbff && next >= 0xdc00 && next <= 0xdfff;
  return text.slice(0, splitsPair ? maxChars - 1 : maxChars);
}
```

pr:664.body:
Fixes #662

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

**Label note.** `agent-ready` could not be applied from this account (403); this PR is proposed ahead of the 24 h label window because of the owner's sprint deadline. Claim record: Lead's pickup-ok on #662 — issue comment 6487523184.

## The defect

`ipv6Blocked` (`packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts:58-69`) extracted an embedded IPv4 only from a dotted-quad tail. IPv4-mapped and IPv4-compatible IPv6 literals written in hex carry no dots, so they fell through to `return false`; `isBlockedAddress` then reported them as public and `assertPublicUrl` accepted them. `web_fetch` takes a model-supplied URL, so this is the SSRF gate itself, not a downstream check.

## What changes

- Expand the IPv6 literal to its eight hextets (compressed `::` and full form both).
- When the address is IPv4-mapped (80 zero bits, then `ffff`) or IPv4-compatible (96 zero bits), rebuild the dotted quad from the last two hextets and hand it to the existing `ipv4Blocked`.
- `ipv4Blocked` and the existing dotted-quad path are untouched; public IPv6 keeps being accepted.

## Commits

- `b9a10c6b1aac5554c6382bee030156f335de871e` — red tests for the hex mapped/compatible literals and the reverse direction.
- `b3d6112fbb228f3787816a6014f0410882b9240d` — red tests for delegation to the existing IPv4 range table and for the resolver path.
- `fc803262da45092ccc184bc27f9c38c9569db00a` — the guard change above.

No amend, no force-push.

## Tests

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/providers.test.ts`:

- `web_fetch judges IPv4-mapped and IPv4-compatible IPv6 literals by their embedded IPv4` — hex mapped and compatible literals are blocked, including the full eight-hextet spelling; the gate rejects them; the dotted-quad path keeps its behaviour.
- Reverse direction in the same test: public mapped and compatible forms stay unblocked and the gate still accepts them, so the change cannot become an over-block.
- Delegation in the same test: embedded addresses outside the `127/10/192.168` prefixes (carrier-grade NAT, benchmarking) are blocked, proving the judgement is delegated to the existing IPv4 range table rather than re-implemented.
- `web_fetch applies the same judgement to resolved addresses, not only literals` — a resolver returning a mapped literal must reject, so the DNS path stays covered.

Before (red-test commits, on `a074172f`):

```
not ok 1 - web_fetch judges IPv4-mapped and IPv4-compatible IPv6 literals by their embedded IPv4
  error: |-
    false !== true
# pass 0
# fail 1

not ok 2 - web_fetch applies the same judgement to resolved addresses, not only literals
  error: 'Missing expected rejection (PublicUrlError).'
# pass 0
# fail 2
```

After (fix commit):

```
# tests 15
# pass 15
# fail 0
```

## Out of scope

The guard still does not decode embedded IPv4 from NAT64 (`64:ff9b::/96` and `64:ff9b:1::/48`), 6to4 (`2002::/16`), Teredo (`2001::/32`), the IPv4-translated range (`::ffff:0:0:0/96`) or the deprecated site-local range (`fec0::/10`). Those are a separate next fix; this PR does not claim the gate is fully closed.

What this change closes: the two spellings that need no translator to reach a target, namely IPv4-mapped (`::ffff:a.b.c.d` in hex) and IPv4-compatible (`::a.b.c.d` in hex), on both the literal path and the resolved-address path. What it does not close: any address family that only reaches a target through a gateway or translator, listed above. Keeping the judgement delegated to the existing IPv4 range table is what makes the next fix a decoder addition rather than a second policy.

pr:675.body:
Fixes #672

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

## What the problem is

`decodeEntities` applied one `replaceAll` per entry of a table whose first entry is `&`, and only afterwards ran a numeric-reference pass. Each pass sees the output of the previous one, so a page that escaped its own markup is decoded twice:

- `"&lt;"` → `"<"` (the `&` pass produces `<`, the next entry consumes it) instead of the two characters `<`
- `"&amp;"` → `"&"`
- `"&#65;"` → `"A"` (the named pass feeds the numeric pass)

`textOf` runs this on every free-engine title and snippet, so the extracted text no longer round-trips what the page actually said.

The numeric pass also accepted every integer in `1..0x10FFFF`, including the surrogate block, so `"�"` produced the lone surrogate `\uD800`. A lone surrogate cannot be encoded as UTF-8 or carried verbatim in JSON output, so it corrupts anything downstream that serialises the extracted text. Hexadecimal references were not recognised at all (`"A"` stayed literal, `"'"` stayed literal with an uppercase `X`).

## What changes

One pass over the source, replacing every reference exactly once; replacement text is never scanned again:

- A single `RegExp` matches a decimal reference, a hexadecimal reference (`x` or `X`), or a named reference; `String.replace` visits the source once.
- Named references live in a `Map` (`amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot`, `nbsp`) instead of a sequential table.
- Decimal and hexadecimal references are decoded by the same branch; `"'"` and `"'"` both become `'`.
- A code point is decoded only when it can be represented downstream: `1..0x10FFFF`, excluding the surrogate block `0xD800..0xDFFF` and non-characters (`0xFFFE`, `0xFFFF`, and the other `FDD0..FDEF`/`xF FFE..xF FFF` forms). Anything else stays as the literal reference text, which is what the previous code did for out-of-range values.

No new dependency, no new allocation beyond the replacement string, and the number of passes over the input drops from 7 + 1 to 1.

not ok 3 - leaves surrogate and non-character scalars as literal text

pr:677.body:
Fixes #674

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

## What the problem is

`serialToText` converts an Excel date serial with a single epoch, `Date.UTC(1899, 11, 30)`. That epoch is correct for the 1900 date system only from serial 61 on. Excel's own phantom leap day (serial 60 is 1900-02-29, a date that never existed) shifts everything before it by one day, so serials 1–59 render one day early:

| serial | Excel shows | this reader showed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1900-01-01 | 1899-12-31 |
| 59 | 1900-02-28 | 1900-02-27 |
| 61 | 1900-03-01 | 1900-03-01 (already right) |
| 45292 | 2024-01-01 | 2024-01-01 (already right) |

Any date-formatted cell in January or February 1900 therefore displayed the wrong day in the sheet panel. The 1904 date system is unaffected: `SERIAL_EPOCH_1904` has no such discontinuity.

## What changes

`serialToText` keeps the epoch it is given, except for the 1900 system below serial 61, where it counts from `1899-12-31`:

- `SERIAL_EPOCH_1900_BEFORE_MARCH = Date.UTC(1899, 11, 31)` is selected when `epoch === SERIAL_EPOCH_1900 && serial < 61`.
- Serial 60 (Excel's phantom 1900-02-29) still resolves to 1900-03-01, the same value it had before, because that date cannot be represented.
- The 1904 branch, the time-of-day path (serial < 1) and all non-date cells are untouched.

Five lines of production code; no new dependency.

pr:680.body:
Fixes #679

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

## What the problem is

`CasStore.has()` answered the existence question by calling `read()` and mapped only `ENOENT` to `false`. `read()` re-hashes the bytes, so an object whose bytes no longer match its digest made `has()` throw `CAS integrity failure` — from a method whose contract is a boolean. Its sibling `verify()` already maps the same condition to `false`, so the two predicates over one store disagreed:

```
put -> b94d27b9934d 11
has before -> true
verify after corruption -> false
has after corruption -> THREW CAS integrity failure
```

The overwrite keeps the byte length (11 → 11), i.e. exactly the "same size, different bytes" corruption the store detects elsewhere. Callers use `has()` as a cache probe in front of `put` / `retain` / republish decisions: with a corrupt blob they crashed instead of taking the republish branch.

## What changes

`has()` now maps the integrity failure to `false` the way `verify()` does:

```ts
// A corrupt object is not usable, so has() answers as verify() does: absent.
if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT" || (error as Error).message === "CAS integrity failure") return false;
```

`has(hash)` is a total boolean predicate again: `true` only when the object is present and valid, `false` when it is missing **or corrupt**. `read()` still rejects a corrupt object with `CAS integrity failure` — the detection is unchanged, only the boolean answer is. A valid object and a missing object behave exactly as before. Two lines of production code; no new dependency.

- `15247383034b21965143ab7e21d0aa681b77a6ad` — the red test only.
- `dfbc783d4a24913d113fcab6e7516271c292ee23` — the fix.

pr:681.body:
Five things went wrong in one round of using the desktop app, and they are fixed
together here because they were found together. The seeded sample Session opened
with every subagent it delegated showing an empty record; a subagent line in the
transcript turned the right panel back into the artifact and workspace tabs when
it was pressed a second time; the first-run wizard asked the provider whether it
answers, and then asked again; and a dropped file whose name carried path
segments was reported as 上传失败 although its bytes were already stored. The
rail also now draws the product's own mark instead of the placeholder flask.

## The sample's children were never in the catalog

A Session that arrives as a recording — the sample is one — is rebuilt by replaying
the run it has on disk. A run stream deliberately keeps `subagent.updated`
snapshots without their steps: the steps are appended to each child's own
`subagent-<id>` substream, which a replay does not read. The catalog
(`SessionStore.catalog.subagents`, served at `GET /api/sessions/:id/subagents`) is
the one place a finished child's execution is complete, and only a *live* child
writes it. The seeding path restored the run and the messages but never the
children, so the panel — which fills a replayed child's steps from the catalog —
had nothing to fill them with.

Seeding now restores the recorded children: the snapshot from the run's own log,
the steps from the substream the snapshot names. A child still marked `running` is
skipped, because loading a run closes it as interrupted and a catalog row would
then contradict the transcript. A row that is already present is left alone, so
running the seed again does not duplicate anything.

## Opening a record is idempotent, and the panel draws its own way back

Pressing a subagent line opened the child in the right panel; pressing the same
line again closed it, because the handler toggled. The line is a row the reader
chose to read, and taking the record away on a second, slightly-off press reads as
a misread rather than a decision. The only way back was that same line, in a
transcript the reader has usually scrolled away from.

Opening is now idempotent: the line asks for that child, and a repeat press asks
for the same thing. The panel gains a back control in its header — 返回产物和文件 /
*Back to artifacts and files* — which is the one explicit way out of a record. Tool
input and result text share the mode, so they follow the same rule.

## The wizard tested the same model twice

测试并继续 saves the provider and its profile and runs the connectivity test; the
开始使用 button that appears once that passes saved the same records a second time
and ran the same test again, so the reader watched the same spinner and the same
连接成功 line twice before the workspace opened.

`ModelForm` is shared by the wizard and 设置, and its 保存 path is written to be
safe on its own: create the provider, add the model, test it, then point the
default at it. That is right when 保存 is the first thing the user presses. It is
not right after 测试 has just done the first three steps with exactly the same
values.

A passing test now hands the saved profile forward, and the action that follows
writes the default onto that record instead of saving and testing it again. The
pass is keyed to the form's contents: every edit that could change what would be
sent — preset, protocol, base URL, key, model name — clears it, so a form that was
changed after being tested still pays for its own test, and so does one where the
user skips 测试 entirely. The verdict on screen is not overwritten, so the reader
does not see a second "testing" state at all. 设置 gets the same behaviour for
free, since it renders the same form.

## A dropped file's card was settled against the wrong name

`uploadWorkspaceFiles` puts only the last segment on the multipart part — the
route stores the file under the name it is given, so `../outside.csv` must travel
as `outside.csv`. The composer's card kept the browser's own name, and
`mergeUpload` matched the answer's `originalName` (which can only be
`outside.csv`) against that. Nothing matched, no entry was found, and the card
fell back to "failed" — the branch that exists for a file the answer did not
mention at all.

The name a part travels under is now one exported function beside the request
that uses it, and the merge compares against the same string. The card still
shows the user's own file name; only the matching changed, and the answer's error
list is looked up the same way.

The browser case for this had stopped covering it: it asserted `已上传 outside.csv`,
the toast copy that the composer-tray rework replaced with cards, and that rework
updated the two neighbouring upload journeys and missed this one. The stale
assertion meant the case never reached the state where the card was drawn. It
asserts the card now — name, size, and that it reads as stored — and a unit test
pins the merge on its own.

## The rail's mark

`apps/desktop/src/views/Rail.tsx` drew a hand-rolled flask SVG. The rail now draws
the product's own `app-mark.png` through the stylesheet, so the mark the desktop
window and the rail show is one asset.

## Validation

Run on head `a7b8eee0`, in this repository's own layers:

| Layer | planned | executed | passed | failed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pnpm ci:l1` | 4 | 4 | 4 | 0 |
| `pnpm ci:ut` | 5524 | 5524 | 5519 | 5 |
| `pnpm ci:st` | 24 | 24 | 22 | 2 |
| `pnpm ci:e2e` | 131 | 131 | 127 | 4 |
| desktop browser suite | 96 | 96 | 96 | 0 |

None of the eleven layer failures is in a path this diff touches: every changed
file is under `apps/desktop/` or `services/api/`. Each failure was attributed by
running it again, and where it reproduced, on unmodified `upstream/main`
(`d72cdf8c`) in a separate worktree:

- **`packages/cas/src/versioning.test.ts`** — flake under parallel load. Run
  alone it passes 13/13 on this head, and fails 12/13 alone on the baseline.
- **`services/runner/src/sandbox-network.test.ts`** — `bwrap: Unknown option
  --disable-userns`: this host's bubblewrap does not have the option, and the
  same case fails on the baseline.
- **`scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`** — `bash .ci/run-research-python.sh race`
  reached the layer's timeout on this host.
- **`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts`** — "the run's
  trajectory is recorded…" fails when run alone on the baseline too (103 of 104
  there, the same single case).
- **`test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts`** (ST, 2 subtests) — it fetches the
  pinned Python runtime from a GitHub release asset, and this host cannot
  download it; a ranged request for the same asset stalls past 60 s.
- **`journey-prepare-environment`** (E2E) — `BLOCKED: managed Python base is not
  ready (failed: micromamba setup failed)`.
- **`journey-local-token-onboarding`** (E2E) — passed when the four failing
  journeys were re-run alone; a timing flake.
- **`journey-artifact-viewer-large-screen`** (774 px against a 760 px limit) and
  **`journey-model-connect-wizard`** (598 px against a 580 px footer) — both
  reproduce on re-run, but they assert pixel bounds of `apps/web` screens
  (`apps/web/src/Markdown.tsx`, `apps/web/src/ModelConnectWizard.tsx`), and
  `git diff --stat <base>..HEAD -- apps/web test/` is empty: this diff cannot
  change what they measure. They read as this host's font metrics rather than
  as behaviour, and the repository's CI runs them in its own image.

Green and covering this change: L1; the desktop unit cases inside the UT layer
(`apps/desktop/tests`, including the two added here); the API seeding test
(`services/api/src/sample-session/index.test.ts`); and the browser cases added
or repaired below.

## E2E user journeys

PASS for the journeys below, on `a7b8eee0`, in a browser against the isolated
local stack.

- **Seeded sample Session → press a delegated subagent's line.** Expected: its
  steps and its answer in the right panel, and a second press keeps the record
  open with a way back. Actual: both, and the panel carries no artifact tabs
  while the record is open. `apps/desktop/e2e/panel-interactions.spec.ts` (new);
  it replays a recorded run and serves the catalog the runner writes.
- **First-run wizard → 测试并继续, then 开始使用.** Expected: the provider is
  asked once. Actual: exactly one `POST /api/models/{id}/test` across both
  presses. `apps/desktop/e2e/setup.spec.ts` (assertion added; it fails with two
  calls before the change).
- **Drop `../outside.csv`.** Expected: the card reads as stored. Actual: one
  card, `is-uploaded`, showing `../outside.csv`, with `outside.csv` in the
  workspace. `apps/desktop/e2e/workspace.spec.ts:116`.

The uploaded-file journey is the one that had stopped covering its own defect:
it asserted a toast the composer-tray rework had replaced, so it never reached
the card. Its assertion now pins the card.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix`
User impact: the seeded sample Session shows what each subagent did — its steps
and its answer — where it used to open empty; a subagent line pressed twice keeps
its record open, with a back control to return to artifacts and files; the
first-run wizard asks the provider once, so 开始使用 no longer waits on a second
connectivity test; a file whose name carried path segments is listed as stored
instead of reporting 上传失败 about bytes the workspace already holds; the rail
draws the product's own mark.
Compatibility and migration: none. The seed only adds catalog rows that are
missing, so a data directory seeded before this change gains the sample's
children on its next start.

Related to #400. Partial fix; keep #400 open.

## Reproduction

On `main` (`5cf904ff`), Node v22.23.2, repo root:

```bash
node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern="empty objects" .local/json-empty-objects-repro.test.ts
```

`.local/json-empty-objects-repro.test.ts` is `services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts` with absolute imports plus one added test; the durable test belongs in that file (existing `createFixture` / `seedArtifact`).

Artifact: `kind: "json"`, content `[{}, {}]` (`logicalName: empty.json`).

## Current behaviour vs expected

Current: `mode === "dataset-table"` with `columns: []` and `rows: [[], []]`, i.e. the viewer renders a grid with one column-less row per record — an empty table with no way to see the document.

Expected: `mode === "json-source"`, so the JSON text `[{}, {}]` is shown, because a record array with no keys has nothing to put in a grid. The code comment at `jsonRecordArray` already states the invariant: *"Anything else — a top-level object, an array of scalars, a mixed array — has no row/column mapping and must be shown as JSON text instead of an empty grid."*

```text
an array of empty objects has no columns, so it must not become a table
expected: 'dataset-table'  actual: 'dataset-table'   (notStrictEqual)
```

## Code evidence

`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts:276-281`:

```ts
function jsonRecordArray(parsed: unknown): Record<string, unknown>[] | undefined {
  if (!Array.isArray(parsed) || parsed.length === 0) return undefined;
  const records = parsed.filter(
    (entry): entry is Record<string, unknown> => typeof entry === "object" && entry !== null && !Array.isArray(entry),
  );
  return records.length === parsed.length ? records : undefined;
}
```

The guard only checks element *shape*; `[{}]` and `[{},{}]` pass, and `recordArrayTable` (`:285`) then derives `columns` by unioning keys — an empty list. The table branch is taken at `:333-341`.

## Suggested red test

Name: `a json artifact of empty objects renders as JSON text, not an empty grid`

Assertion: `assert.notEqual(payload.mode, "dataset-table")` (and, after the fix, `payload.mode === "json-source"` with `payload.source` deep-equal to the re-indented document).

Run: `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts`

Reproduced red before filing.

## Fix

In `jsonRecordArray`, after the shape filter, also require at least one key across the records:

```ts
if (records.length !== parsed.length) return undefined;
return records.some((record) => Object.keys(record).length > 0) ? records : undefined;
```

Single file, no schema change.

## Duplicate check

GitHub search (open + closed): `jsonRecordArray` 0 hits; `"empty grid"` 0 hits; `dataset table` open hits only PR #467 (header alignment styling) and closed #429/#368/#375 (alignment, JSON truncation). No open issue, no open PR for this shape.

## Reproduction

On `main` (`5cf904ff`), Node v22.23.2, repo root:

```bash
node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern="claim truncation" .local/structure-truncated-repro.test.ts
```

`.local/structure-truncated-repro.test.ts` is `services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts` with absolute imports plus one added test; the durable test belongs in that file (existing `createFixture` / `seedArtifact`).

Artifact: `kind: "structure"`, `logicalName: "many.pdb"`, 9 000 lines of `ATOM  <n>  C   ALA A   1` (~99 KB), preview requested with `maxChars=1000000`.

## Current behaviour vs expected

Current: `payload.source.length === source.length` (the complete 99 KB document is returned) **and** `payload.truncated === true`, because `atomCount (9000) > STRUCTURE_ATOM_TRUNCATION (8000)` is folded into the flag even though nothing was cut. The UI therefore tells the user the preview is truncated while showing the complete file, with no note explaining the atom budget.

Expected: `truncated === false` when the returned `source` is the whole document. If the 8 000-atom budget is meant to limit the *payload*, the payload should actually be cut at that boundary; either way `source` and `truncated` must agree.

```text
truncated must be false when nothing was cut
true !== false
```

## Code evidence

`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts:498-508`:

```ts
      const atomCount = countStructureAtoms(source);
      const charTruncated = source.length > maxChars;
      const atomTruncated = atomCount > STRUCTURE_ATOM_TRUNCATION;
      return {
        ...
        source: charTruncated ? source.slice(0, maxChars) : source,
        atomCount,
        totalChars: source.length,
        truncated: charTruncated || atomTruncated,
      };
```

The slice at `:506` is governed only by `charTruncated`; `atomTruncated` influences the flag alone. Constant `STRUCTURE_ATOM_TRUNCATION = 8_000` at `:220`.

## Suggested red test

Name: `structure preview does not claim truncation when the whole source is returned`

Assertions: `payload.atomCount === 9000`, `payload.source.length === source.length`, `payload.truncated === false`.

Run: `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts`

Reproduced red before filing.

## Fix

Either drop `atomTruncated` from `truncated` and expose it as its own field / note (e.g. `note: "Showing the document; the viewer highlights the first 8000 atoms."`), or apply the atom budget to `source`. Single file; the minimal honest fix is `truncated: charTruncated` plus an explanatory note when `atomTruncated`.

## Duplicate check

GitHub search (open + closed): `STRUCTURE_ATOM_TRUNCATION` 0 hits; `structure preview` 0 open hits; `atomCount` 0 open hits. Closed #368 / #375 covered JSON truncation explicitness, not the structure branch. No open issue, no open PR for this flag.

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## Symptom

`PUT /api/settings/idea-tree` still accepts `maxRounds`, `candidatesPerRound`, `maxSearchRounds`, and `assessorActivity` / `assessorStability` / `assessorSustainability`. Those values pass bounds validation, are written to the catalog, are returned verbatim by `GET /api/settings/idea-tree`, and `IdeaTreeSettingsDetails` still exposes them to callers.

No research run ever reads them. The engine overwrites all of them from the research template and the exploration intensity before the run starts. A caller therefore gets a completely silent no-op: the request returns 200, the value reads back unchanged, the type definition says it is configurable — and nothing about the run changes.

## Reproduction

1. `PUT /api/settings/idea-tree` with body `{"maxRounds": 10, "candidatesPerRound": 5}` → 200, and the response echoes `maxRounds: 10`, `candidatesPerRound: 5`.
2. `GET /api/settings/idea-tree` → still 10 and 5.
3. Start an Idea Tree research run with `explorationIntensity` set to `standard`.
4. The run does 3 rounds and asks for at most 3 candidates per round — the `standard` preset. The 10 and the 5 have no effect, and nothing reports that.

**Expected:** either the two values take effect, or the endpoint rejects them / says they are no longer configurable.
**Actual:** accepted, validated, persisted, read back, then silently discarded.

## Mechanism

The budget fields are overwritten wholesale by the intensity preset:

- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research_service.py:149` builds the run's settings with `apply_intensity(c.settings.model_dump(), c.settings.explorationIntensity)`.
- `apply_intensity` in `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/templates.py:51` returns `{**settings, **INTENSITIES[intensity], 'explorationIntensity': intensity}`. The preset is spread last, so it always wins over whatever the caller stored.
- `INTENSITIES` supplies `maxRounds`, `candidatesPerRound` and `maxSearchRounds` (plus `maxActiveDirections`, `explorationSlots` and `candidateConcurrency`, which are preset-only and were never part of the schema).

The assessor configuration is superseded by the template instead:

- `assessors()` in `research.py` returns the assessor list straight from the template snapshot, and `role_prompt()` resolves assessor roles from the same place.
- Scoring uses `weights = [spec['weight'] for spec in self.assessors()]` (`research.py:341`), so the weights also come from the template.
- The three assessor fields in settings therefore take part in no assessment at all.

The write path's validation is fully intact, which is precisely the problem: `normalizeIdeaTreeSettings` (`services/api/src/store/settings.ts:519`) bounds `maxRounds` to 1..100 and `candidatesPerRound` to 1..20, then persists them.

## Scope

One schema now mixes two kinds of field, and the type definitions give no way to tell them apart:

**Dead (overwritten or superseded)**
`maxRounds`, `candidatesPerRound`, `maxSearchRounds`, `assessorActivity`, `assessorStability`, `assessorSustainability` (including their `weight`, `systemPrompt` and `scoringCriteria`).

**Still effective**
`maxDepth`, `maxNodes`, `maxTokens`, `maxTokensPerCall`, `scoreDirection`, `designSystemPrompt`, `aggregatorSystemPrompt`, `propagateInsightSystemPrompt`.

## Traces the migration left behind

1. **The assessor weights are validated twice and read zero times.** On the TypeScript side, `services/api/src/store/settings.ts:568` throws `Assessor weights must sum to 1.0` when all three weights are supplied. On the Python side, the `Settings.weights` model validator in `research_service.py` requires `Assessment weights must sum to 1` and additionally checks the type and length of `systemPrompt` / `scoringCriteria`. Both guard data that has no reader.
2. **The front end kept an empty validation hook.** `ideaTreeWeightsValid()` (`apps/web/src/IdeaTreeSettingsEditor.tsx:29`) now returns `true` for any draft, yet it is still the precondition on the save action at `apps/web/src/App.tsx:2611`.
3. **The shapes do not even line up.** Settings hard-code three assessors — activity, stability, sustainability — while the default template `scientific-hypothesis-general/v1` has `scientificValidity`, `evidenceReadiness` and `feasibility`. Only `water-treatment-materials/v1` matches the settings' three.

## Suggested resolution

Two directions, depending on whether template + intensity is the intended contract:

1. **It is.** Remove the overwritten fields from `UpdateIdeaTreeSettingsRequest` and `IdeaTreeSettingsDetails`, stop persisting them, and delete the now-unreachable weight validation (both the TypeScript and the Python copy) along with the `ideaTreeWeightsValid` stub. The interface would then say what the runtime does.
2. **It is not.** Make `apply_intensity` treat the preset as defaults rather than overrides — fill only the fields the caller did not set explicitly, so explicit configuration keeps working.

Either way, a test that pins the persisted settings against the settings the engine actually runs with would be worth adding; otherwise the next change to an intensity preset drifts the same silent way.

## Note

The mocked E2E journey `journey-idea-tree-fixture` used to configure a run through the budget inputs that were removed from the settings pane. It has been rewritten separately to configure template + intensity. This issue is about the API/schema contract itself, not that test.

Tracked on GitCode as https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/100.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] Idea Tree settings: budget and assessor fields are still validated and persisted, but the runtime always overwrites them from the template/intensity preset

## Reproduction

On `main` (`5cf904ff`), Node v22.23.2, from the repo root:

```bash
node --import tsx --test .local/csv-preview-repro.test.ts
```

That file is a copy of the `dataset preview parses csv tables and truncates rows` test in `services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts` with the CSV replaced by RFC 4180 content:

```text
name,note
Alice,"hello, world"
Bob,"say ""hi"""
```

The durable test belongs in `services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts`.

## Current behaviour vs expected

Current: `rows[0]` is `["Alice", "\"hello", " world\""]` — the comma inside the quoted field splits it, and a newline inside a quoted field would also inflate `totalRows`.

Expected: `columns === ["name","note"]`, `totalRows === 2`, `rows[0]` deep-equals `["Alice","hello, world"]`, `rows[1]` deep-equals `["Bob","say \"hi\""]`.

```text
Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
['Alice', + '"hello', + ' world"' - 'hello, world']
```

## Code evidence

`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts:248-250`:

```ts
function splitDelimited(source: string, delimiter: RegExp): string[][] {
  return source.split(/\r?\n/).filter((line) => line.length > 0).map((line) => line.split(delimiter));
}
```

It splits on raw newlines and then on the raw delimiter with no quote state machine, and it is called by `parseDelimitedTable` at `:255`. Any quoted field containing the delimiter, a newline, or an escaped `""` shifts columns and row counts.

## Suggested red test

Name: `dataset preview parses quoted csv cells`

Assertions: `columns` deep-equals `["name","note"]`, `totalRows === 2`, `rows[0]` deep-equals `["Alice","hello, world"]`, `rows[1]` deep-equals `["Bob","say \"hi\""]`.

Run: `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts`

Reproduced red before filing.

## Fix

Replace `splitDelimited` with a small quote-aware record splitter (handles `""` escapes and quoted newlines), keeping the existing `.csv`/`.tsv` delimiter selection and the row limit. Single file.

## Duplicate check

GitHub search (open + closed): `parseDelimitedTable` 0 hits; `quoted csv` only closed #449 / #446 (large numeric CSV size limits, not quoting); `"dataset preview"` has one open PR #467 (header alignment styling, different defect). No open issue, no open PR for CSV quoting.

## Problem and user outcome

Researchers need to verify that a PDB structure contains the same protein target and chemical compound as a ChEMBL activity record. Matching a structure title or compound name is insufficient: salt forms, different protein targets, and label/auth chain identifiers can produce incorrect cross-database associations.

The current PDB MCP connector supports full-text structure search, entry lookup and download preparation, but does not expose protein/nonpolymer entity or Chemical Component Dictionary (CCD) lookup tools. A representative ChEMBL → PDB validation therefore required direct official HTTPS calls outside MCP to complete identity verification.

Provide these operations through the existing PDB MCP connector, with structured evidence, source/version metadata and the existing governance/audit path.

## Existing evidence

Source-inspected candidate: `bcd56b74bd9b79564e392da33e4977d94dd65034` (PR #441). This describes that candidate, not an assertion that latest main has been independently reproduced.

A deterministic validation through the production Inspector/API successfully queried ChEMBL and PDB, downloaded a real mmCIF through governed artifact jobs, checked its SHA-256, and parsed actual coordinates. It did not establish a real-model automated Agent journey.

Positive example:

- Human EGFR: ChEMBL target `CHEMBL203`, UniProt `P00533`.
- Canertinib free molecule: `CHEMBL31965`; activity `121735`, IC50 = 74 nM, relation `=`, assay `CHEMBL683041`, assay type B, target confidence 9.
- Canertinib dihydrochloride: `CHEMBL545315`, parent `CHEMBL31965`; its complete InChIKey differs from the free molecule.
- PDB `9OS6`: protein entity 1 maps to `P00533`; nonpolymer entity 2 identifies CCD `A1CEA`.
- CCD `A1CEA` and free Canertinib share complete InChIKey `OMZCMEYTWSXEPZ-UHFFFAOYSA-N`.
- Protein label/auth chain is A/A; ligand label/auth chain is B/A. These naming systems must remain distinguishable.

Negative example:

- PDB `5VCW` contains Pelitinib, but protein entity 1 maps to MYT1 (`Q99640`), not EGFR (`P00533`). It must not be presented as an EGFR complex solely because Pelitinib has EGFR activity elsewhere.

Official records: https://www.rcsb.org/structure/9OS6 and https://www.rcsb.org/structure/5VCW.

## Requested MCP capabilities

Reuse the existing PDB adapter, source selection, transport, validation, Inspector, Agent tool registration, standard evidence normalization and permission/audit mechanisms. Suggested operations (names are implementation proposals):

1. `pdb_get_polymer_entity(pdb_id, entity_id)`
   - Entity description/type, source organism, UniProt/reference mappings, chain identifiers, sequence/coverage and construct/mutation information when available.
   - Preserve `label_asym_id` versus `auth_asym_id`; distinguish a kinase-domain construct from a full-length receptor.
2. `pdb_get_nonpolymer_entity(pdb_id, entity_id)`
   - Ligand/component ID, entity identity, label/auth chain mappings and provider cross-references when available.
3. `pdb_lookup_chemical_component(component_id)`
   - CCD name, formula/charge, InChI, complete InChIKey, available SMILES variants, and provider cross-database identifiers with mapping provenance.
   - Support valid extended component IDs such as five-character `A1CEA`, rather than assuming all CCD identifiers are three characters.

Also expose a discoverable way to enumerate the relevant entity IDs from a PDB entry. Reuse IDs already returned by entry lookup if sufficient; do not require users to guess entity IDs.

Equivalent bounded expansion of the existing entry lookup is acceptable if it satisfies these user-facing requirements without unbounded responses or extra requests for every ordinary lookup.

Official APIs used in the validation:

- `https://data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/polymer_entity/9OS6/1`
- `https://data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/nonpolymer_entity/9OS6/2`
- `https://data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/chemcomp/A1CEA`
- `https://data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/polymer_entity/5VCW/1`

## Data and integration requirements

- Return useful structured domain fields and nonempty standardized evidence records, including stable IDs, canonical URLs, retrieval times, attribution and provider version/revision when available.
- Preserve missing mappings explicitly. Missing UniProt/InChIKey must not be replaced by a name-based assertion of identity.
- Preserve salt/parent relationships and stereochemistry-aware complete identifiers. A parent relationship is not an assertion that salts or measured activity values are interchangeable.
- Treat covalent adducts, modified components or conflicting mappings as unresolved or explicitly qualified unless the evidence supports a stronger relationship.
- Reuse provider allowlists, rate limits, timeouts, input validation and error normalization; handle unknown entities/components and partial failures visibly.
- Provide concise model-facing summaries and retain complete provider content as traceable evidence rather than flooding model context with full sequences, synonym lists, cross-references or molfiles.
- Keep structure file transfer on existing governed artifact jobs, with checksums and source provenance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the target version, document the existing gap and show the new operations in source discovery, Inspector schemas and the selected Session's Agent tools.
- [ ] Retrieve `9OS6` entity IDs through MCP, then verify protein entity 1 → UniProt `P00533` and nonpolymer entity 2 → CCD `A1CEA` through MCP.
- [ ] Retrieve CCD `A1CEA` through MCP and compare its complete InChIKey with ChEMBL `CHEMBL31965`; preserve the distinct salt record `CHEMBL545315` and its parent relationship.
- [ ] Preserve and display protein A/A and ligand B/A label/auth chain mappings without confusing protein and ligand instances.
- [ ] Retrieve `5VCW` protein identity through MCP and reject it as an EGFR complex because its target is `Q99640`, despite the compound-name association.
- [ ] Complete a selected mmCIF download via governed artifact jobs, verify it, read the actual file, and retain the cross-database evidence in saved analysis outputs.
- [ ] Run a product-level Agent journey that completes the identity checks using MCP tools, without direct HTTPS/web-fetch fallback for the requested metadata. Separately record Inspector, stub-model and real-model results; a successful direct API script alone is insufficient.
- [ ] Add meaningful coverage for extended CCD IDs, missing/invalid entities, missing chemical/protein mappings, rate-limit/timeout/partial-failure feedback, and label/auth chain distinctions.
- [ ] Add English/Chinese documentation describing supported operations, identity-matching limits and the reproducible positive/negative cases.

## Scope boundaries

This request exposes official metadata and supports verifiable identity comparisons. It does not add docking, affinity prediction, a universal chemical standardization engine, or permission bypasses. Geometric contacts do not establish potency, and IC50 is not Kd.

Related to #420 and PR #441. This is a concrete follow-up for the entity/chemical-identity lookup gap discovered during cross-database validation.
