closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #102](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/102) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

### 🚀 Background Description

ScienceDiscovery’s primary entry today is local `serve` plus a browser UI (default `http://127.0.0.1:4310`). The agent runs inside the product’s own control plane: the Web UI submits work, the API orchestrates Runs, the sandbox executes code, and MCP connects external tools. Users who already live in Zed, VS Code, JetBrains, or other editors cannot plug ScienceDiscovery in as a standard coding agent; they have to leave the editor and open a browser.

The [Agent Client Protocol (ACP)](https://agentclientprotocol.com/) is an open standard for communication between editors (Clients) and coding agents. Zed published it in 2025; it is now an Apache 2.0 standard. It uses JSON-RPC 2.0 (typically over stdio) for initialization, sessions, prompt turns, streaming updates, permissions, and cancellation — LSP for coding agents. Any compliant Client can drive any compliant Agent without a per-editor private integration. The stable wire protocol is **ACP v1** (`protocolVersion` negotiated in `initialize`). ACP v2 docs shipped as Draft in 2026-07 and are **not** the default target of this issue.

ACP and the product’s existing MCP sit on different layers and do not replace each other:

| | ACP | MCP (already in the product) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Connects | editor / IDE ↔ coding agent | agent / host ↔ tool and data servers |
| Standardizes | how to launch, drive, and render an agent session | how to discover and call external tools |

This repository has no ACP implementation (no `agent-client-protocol`, no stdio JSON-RPC agent entry). Nearby issues are not this work:

- GitCode [#23](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/23) / the HTTP CLI: a **CLI client of `serve`**, not an editor↔agent protocol;
- GitCode [#44](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/44): an internal pluggable-capability / Pending Mode design, not external ACP.

User-observable outcome: in an ACP-capable editor, select ScienceDiscovery, prompt against the current workspace, see streaming output and tool calls, approve sensitive actions through ACP permissions, and still use the product’s sandbox, scientific connectors, and Skills — without opening the browser.

### Design Ideas

**Default role: ScienceDiscovery as an ACP Agent** (the editor is the Client). That matches “put the research agent inside standard editors.” Whether to also be an ACP Client (drive Claude Code / Gemini CLI / etc. from this product’s UI) is an open question and must not block phase 1.

Phase 1 should implement the **ACP v1 baseline methods** (https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/overview):

1. **Transport**: the editor spawns this product’s ACP subprocess; JSON-RPC 2.0 newline-delimited JSON on stdin/stdout. Do not bind ACP to the existing HTTP `:4310` control plane by default.
2. **Lifecycle**: `initialize` (version and capability negotiation) → optional `authenticate` → `session/new` (or `session/load` when advertised) → `session/prompt` / `session/update` / `session/cancel`.
3. **Session mapping**: one ACP session maps to a recoverable Project/Session/Run context in the product; workspace paths follow ACP’s absolute-path rule.
4. **Permissions and sandbox**: Client `session/request_permission` and optional `fs/*` / `terminal/*` must align with existing permission cards and the Bubblewrap/Seatbelt sandbox. The default security posture must not be looser than the Web UI; ACP must not become a bypass around the sandbox.
5. **Capability advertisement**: `initialize` must report only capabilities that are actually implemented (`loadSession`, image prompts, MCP passthrough, …). Research-specific features (literature connectors, artifacts, memory graph) that have no v1 field should use ACP `_meta` / `_`-prefixed custom methods and be documented — do not invent a private JSON-RPC.
6. **Discoverability (can follow)**: ship a launch command and manifest editors can configure. Listing in the [ACP Registry](https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/registry) is not decided.

**Alternatives considered**

- Extra subcommands on the HTTP CLI (#23) without ACP methods: editors still cannot connect.
- ACP Client only, never an Agent: users still cannot use ScienceDiscovery inside a standard editor.
- Wrapping the product’s private event stream and calling it ACP: no interoperability with Zed / VS Code / JetBrains clients.
- Targeting ACP v2 Draft as the only goal in phase 1: v2 is still draft; implement against the stable spec at implementation time, with v1 as the default acceptance line.

**Open questions (need a decision before implementation)**

- Whether to ship an ACP Client in the same phase;
- Whether phase 1 lists the agent in the ACP Registry (the registry currently requires authentication support);
- How ACP cwd / workspace maps to a product Project, and whether a full Gateway/Runner stack is required when `serve` is not already running;
- Whether permission prompts are owned by the editor’s ACP UI or still fall back to in-product permission cards.

### Involved Public APIs

- **ACP wire protocol**: expose ACP v1 JSON-RPC over stdio to editors. This is a new external contract, not an alias of the existing REST/SSE API.
- **Existing HTTP control plane**: may be reused locally for Project/Session/Run, but users must not have to open a browser before ACP works. If the ACP process embeds or starts the control plane, that should be one launch command.
- **MCP**: stays on the agent↔tools axis; do not multiplex MCP stdio and ACP stdio on the same pipe.
- **No anonymous public ACP service**: default remains trusted local/workstation use, consistent with “not a multi-user production service.”

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- Launcher / CLI: add an ACP Agent entry alongside `serve` and GitCode [#23](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/23); they do not replace each other;
- Session / Run / permissions / sandbox: ACP prompt turns must hit the same execution and governance path;
- MCP: an ACP session should still use configured MCP servers;
- Web UI: not a required surface for this issue; whether ACP sessions appear in the web session list is undecided;
- GitCode [#44](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/44): the internal capability framework may be reused if the composition layer is in the way; acceptance is external ACP interop, not the internal plugin protocol.

### Test Design and Test Plan

**Protocol conformance**

- [ ] Complete `initialize` against a reference ACP Client (or the official schema / SDK): negotiate v1 (or the then-stable version); advertised capabilities match behavior;
- [ ] `session/new` → `session/prompt` completes one scientific turn (user message, streaming `session/update`, explicit stop reason);
- [ ] `session/cancel` interrupts an in-flight prompt turn;
- [ ] Privileged tool calls go through `session/request_permission` and do not run when denied;
- [ ] Errors use JSON-RPC 2.0 `error` objects; notifications have no response.

**Product constraints**

- [ ] Python / shell execution stays in the existing sandbox; the ACP path is not looser than the Web UI;
- [ ] Tokens, API keys, and session bodies do not leak into ACP logs or unauthenticated client traffic;
- [ ] Formal E2E must not use the human trial port 4310 or its fixed data directory.

**Interop / user journey**

- [ ] In at least one real ACP Client (e.g. Zed or a VS Code ACP extension): configure the launch command → prompt against the open workspace → see streaming text and at least one tool call;
- [ ] Focused unit tests for JSON-RPC dispatch, failed version negotiation, and unauthenticated calls if `authenticate` is enabled;
- [ ] Docs include a Client configuration example (launch command, workspace, auth).

### Additional Information

Public spec and repos:

- Protocol overview: https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/overview
- Schema / reference implementation: https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/agent-client-protocol
- Registry: https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/registry

The product entry remains `./ScienceDiscovery serve` plus the browser. This issue adds an editor-spawned ACP Agent process, not another private chat protocol.

## Summary
**Effect / quality:** literature artifact cites papers but **numeric claims have no claim→evidence excerpt** (quote or locator), so reviewers cannot quickly verify fidelity.

## Repro context (shared)
- **Product:** ScienceDiscovery local source `main` @ `a0cf9c7`
- **Session id:** `a11aaecd-d8ef-4517-b6a8-7c1f22992c77` (local UI: http://127.0.0.1:4310/projects/39f9fe2c-a4c1-4911-9232-14de38dbfbd3/sessions/a11aaecd-d8ef-4517-b6a8-7c1f22992c77)
- **Artifact:** [`crispr-base-editing-scd-scan.md`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zy95-12/sciencediscovery/evidence/literature-scan-2026-10-19/crispr-base-editing-scd-scan.md)
- **Review JSON:** [`artifact-review.json`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zy95-12/sciencediscovery/evidence/literature-scan-2026-10-19/artifact-review.json)
- **Evidence screenshots:** [https://github.com/zy95-12/sciencediscovery/tree/evidence/literature-scan-2026-10-19](https://github.com/zy95-12/sciencediscovery/tree/evidence/literature-scan-2026-10-19)
- **Reviewer Specialist:** On · **Automatic review:** On · level **Quick**

### User prompt (exact)
```text
Do a brief literature scan on CRISPR base editing for sickle cell disease. Summarize 3–5 key recent findings with citations, then write a short markdown report artifact. Keep it focused.
```

![user prompt in timeline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zy95-12/sciencediscovery/evidence/literature-scan-2026-10-19/01-user-prompt.png)

## What went wrong (locate here)
### Prompt asked for
“Summarize 3–5 key recent findings **with citations**” — citations exist; **excerpts do not**.

### Problematic passages in `crispr-base-editing-scd-scan.md`
**Finding 1 (BEACON)** — bibliographic line is present, but numbers have no adjacent quote:

> At 6 months: **mean 67.4% on-target edited alleles**, **mean HbF >60% of total hemoglobin**, **HbS <40%** (n=13)

![BEACON numbers without excerpt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zy95-12/sciencediscovery/evidence/literature-scan-2026-10-19/04-artifact-key-findings.png)

**Finding 3 (Mayuranathan)** — same pattern:

> Homozygously edited erythroid colonies expressed **81 ± 7% HbF** versus **17 ± 11%** in unedited controls.

Citation header is there; **no abstract sentence / locator under the claim**.

![citation present, no claim excerpt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zy95-12/sciencediscovery/evidence/literature-scan-2026-10-19/05-artifact-no-excerpt.png)

## Expected
For each quantitative / clinical claim: PMID + short evidence excerpt (or structured claim→evidence table) usable by humans and Deep review.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Literature report artifacts include claim-level excerpts or an evidence table for key numbers.
- [ ] Missing excerpt is an explicit gap, not silent.

Related: #414 (shallow Quick pass makes this worse).

closed_recent.author: JinhZhao
closed_recent.body:
`skills/citation-reviewer/SKILL.md:17-20` instructs the reviewer to classify identity and availability failures as `CITATION_IDENTIFIER_MISMATCH`, `CITATION_IDENTIFIER_NOT_RESOLVED`, and `CITATION_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`.

The runtime whitelist contains only `CITATION_CLAIM_NOT_SUPPORTED` (`packages/provenance/src/citation-review.ts:39-41`), and other codes are dropped at `:133-136`, setting an internal `discardedUnverifiedFinding` flag.

We read the comment at `:35-38` and agree with the design intent: identity resolution is established by the execution layer before the model sees a source snapshot, and a provider failure is not evidence of a bad citation. This is not a request to change that policy.

However, the current design treats unverifiable content as if it never existed. When a citation identity cannot be resolved, or a provider fails, the reader sees no signal that the system tried and could not confirm. In a citation-dense report — for example, two near-duplicate ACS papers on the same catalytic system whose DOIs are confused — the suppressed case is precisely the one worth showing, because it tells the reader that identity resolution failed for this cluster and coverage is accordingly limited.

**Suggested fix:** Add `UNVERIFIABLE` (or `IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED` / `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`) to `EvidenceAssessment` (`packages/schema/src/provenance.ts:177`), so that suppressed findings are recorded as evidence with a visible status rather than silently dropped. The review summary could then report "N identity/availability findings suppressed as UNVERIFIABLE" with reasons, and the Skill text would align with the runtime instead of asking the model for codes it can never act on.

**Related:** #414 (review depth), but this is a schema-level gap, not a review-quality issue.
closed_recent.title: [Feature] Evidence grading should express UNVERIFIABLE status, not silently drop uncertain findings

closed_recent.author: zy95-12
closed_recent.body:
## Problem

Today a Specialist is a **role profile** (instructions + skills + connectors) injected into ScienceDiscovery’s native AgentLoop (`packages/schema/src/specialist.ts`, `docs/en/core/specialists.md`: *“A Specialist is not a new execution environment”*). Users can already `POST /api/specialists`, and `builtin-code-engineer` runs Python/R in the platform sandbox — but there is **no way to plug an external coding agent** (Codex SDK, Claude Agent SDK, iCode, Cursor SDK, OpenHands, …) in as the execution surface for a delegated `task`.

Users want to register custom specialists such as “code expert = Codex / Claude Code / iCode” and have the lead Agent collaborate with them on the same job (plan → `task` → artifacts → synthesize).

## Maintainer decisions (2026-10-18)

1. **Reuse the Specialist concept** — extend it; do not invent a parallel “External Agent” directory/API.
2. **Add a `runtime` field** when defining a Specialist:
   - `native` — current behavior (default when omitted).
   - **Known agents** — first-class SDK adapters, e.g. `codex`, `claude-agent`, `icode`, … (each with its own thin adapter).
   - **Unknown third parties** — `acp` (spawn command + argv; JSON-RPC/stdio per [Agent Client Protocol](https://agentclientprotocol.com/)).
3. Orchestration stays unified: lead Agent still uses `task(specialistId, …)` → independent Workspace / `inputPaths` / Brief / artifacts / `specialistConfigHash`. External runtime only replaces **who runs the model loop**.
4. Permissions: Always-allow is execution permission only; secrets still go through in-conversation config cards (#278: persist / this-run / alternate).
5. No platform-visible sub-`task` nesting; external agents may use their own internal subagents.

Related but **different** work: #64 is “ScienceDiscovery as an ACP **Agent**” (editors drive SD). This issue is “ScienceDiscovery as an ACP/SDK **Client/host**” (SD drives external coding agents via Specialist runtime). Share protocol knowledge; do not merge scopes.

## MVP decisions 2026-10-19 (Asia/Shanghai)

Locked by maintainer for the first Develop slice (do not implement full #385 in one PR). Full comment: see latest `repo-agent:status` MVP comment.

1. **Missing config**: Interactive config card so the user completes Codex auth/config in-conversation (do not wait for full #278).
2. **First SDK**: **Codex**.
3. **Process placement**: External runtime may run on **host** for MVP.
4. **Secret boundary**: Secrets **must not** enter specialist body / catalog argv; platform secret channel only.
5. **Usage**: Non-native allowed via explicit `task(specialistId=…)`.
6. **`specialistConfigHash`**: Only non-native `runtime` is hashed; native/omit keeps legacy hash.

### MVP acceptance (this slice)
- [ ] Schema/API optional `runtime` (default native) + `SpecialistRuntimeAdapter` + normalized event sink
- [ ] `task(specialistId)` non-native → Subagent/timeline/artifacts compatible
- [ ] Codex thin adapter end-to-end; code execution via platform channel
- [ ] Interactive config card for missing Codex config
- [ ] Hash policy (#6) + focused tests + minimal docs

### Out of MVP
UI runtime picker, ACP path, more SDKs, #64, full Skills/MCP bridge, full #278 product surface beyond the focused card.

## Proposed model (summary)

```text
SpecialistV2 = capabilities + role + runtime(native | sdk:<provider> | acp)
task(...) → SpecialistRuntimeAdapter.invoke(req, sink)
  → events: started | progress | tool_call | file_change | need_input | done
  → SpecialistResult (summary, artifacts, usage, runtimeSessionId)
```

Platform owns permissions, Workspace, artifact registration, audit. Adapter owns provider-specific session/stream/cancel.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Schema + API: `CreateSpecialist` / `Specialist` accept optional `runtime` (+ `capabilities`); omit → `native`; old clients unchanged.
- [ ] `SpecialistRuntimeAdapter` contract implemented for at least one known SDK (prefer iCode or Codex) and one `acp` third-party spawn path.
- [ ] `task(specialistId=…)` with non-native runtime creates a Subagent record, streams normalized events into the existing timeline, and returns compatible `subagent_result` / `artifacts[]`.
- [ ] Missing provider secrets emit `need_input` → #278-style config card; Always-allow does not skip secret provision.
- [ ] Probe fails → clear error + optional fallback guidance to `builtin-code-engineer` (no silent hang).
- [ ] Docs: user-facing “custom specialist runtime” + developer adapter guide; cross-link #64 / #278.
- [ ] Tests: adapter event mapping; cancel/timeout; artifact handoff; secret-not-persisted-in-specialist-body.

## Suggested milestones

1. Contract + native default path unchanged.
2. First known SDK adapter (iCode or Codex) end-to-end via `task`.
3. ACP fallback for unknown third-party commands.
4. Additional SDK adapters (Claude Agent, …) + UI runtime picker / probe.

## Non-goals (v1)

- Turning ScienceDiscovery into an editor ACP Agent (#64).
- Bridging all SD Skills/MCP into every external runtime (open follow-up).
- Multi-tenant sharing of `~/.codex` / `~/.claude` home state without isolation design.

## References

- Internal design draft discussed 2026-10-18 (Specialist dual-layer + adapters).
- Codex TS SDK, Claude Agent SDK, iCode `icode acp`, ACP, #278, #64.

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## What happened

Nightly real-model E2E fails the whole Daily gate when a single request to the configured OpenAI-compatible model gateway returns a provider error. Other cases in the same job still pass, and the same case can pass on another run the same night.

On 2026-10-06, main Nightly run [37529799288](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529799288) (`7a032425`) executed 10 real cases: 5 passed, 5 failed, 0 skipped, in 3.0 hours. The job uses `E2E_LLM_MODEL=deepseek-v4-flash` and `E2E_LLM_BASE_URL=https://yibuapi.com/v1`. Playwright is configured with `retries: 0` and one worker.

Three of those failures were gateway responses, and the product already showed them:

- **DRB-75** failed in 9.3 seconds. No subagent and no tool call ran. The page showed error 181001: HTTP 500 from the gateway, body `Database error, please contact the administrator`, type `new_api_error`.
- **PUCT-COMPRESS** failed in 11.5 seconds with the same HTTP 500 text in `run.error`. No search started.
- **workspace plan and run-anchored subagent** failed after 7.0 minutes. The page already showed HTTP 503: `No available channel for model deepseek-v4-flash under group default (distributor)`, code `model_not_found`, wrapped as the same 181001 gateway error. The test then waited out a 420 second timeout for a plan section that never appeared.

The other five cases in that job passed, including DRB-58 after 51.0 minutes and TC-E2E-01 after 43.0 minutes. The same three cases passed on the release-branch Nightly [37529816020](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529816020) (`releases/v0.3.0.beta` at `6d3c49a8`) the same night. The previous night, that same beta commit passed all 10 real cases in [37382672011](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37382672011).

## Why this is a product/CI problem

The gateway is failing one request at a time, not the whole job. A 500 or 503 still fails the real-E2E job, which fails Nightly. There is no retry, and the suite does not record these as an external provider fault separate from a product regression.

## Expected

A transient gateway 500 or 503 is visible as that provider error. One such request does not have the same meaning as a product run that finished and failed to deliver. Cases that passed in the same job stay visible as passes.

## Evidence limits

This does not say the gateway was down for the whole job. It also does not cover the research cases that ran for about 20 minutes and then ended without a report; those are separate failures.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] ci: Nightly real E2E fails the gate on one transient model-gateway 500 or 503

closed_recent.author: qingkwl
closed_recent.body:
## Problem

`services/api` has Windows-specific OS behavior requirements with no platform seam (#491):

- Owner-only (0600/0700) file semantics rely on `chmod`, which only toggles the read-only bit on Windows; the most sensitive files in the service (encrypted model/MCP credential master key, generated SSH private keys) are left unprotected.
- Atomic replace via rename transiently fails on Windows with EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY while antivirus scanners or search indexers hold the destination; callers currently see raw errors.
- At-rest secret protection has no Windows story at all (POSIX file permissions carry the protection; Windows needs per-user encryption).

PR #492 carried an earlier version and was closed; this re-lands the API platform facade with a clean scope (platform layer only, no consumers rewired yet), a green typecheck, no unresolvable references, and Windows real-machine evidence.

## Expected

1. `services/api/src/platform/os/` provides the facade: `types.ts` (adaptation surface), `index.ts` (single dispatch point), `posix.ts` (transparent passthrough), `win32.ts` (Windows implementation).
2. Adaptations: `restrictToOwner` (icacls owner-only ACL, SID-based grantee for locale-safety), `renameReplace` (retry with backoff on transient locks), `wrapSecret`/`unwrapSecret`/`isWrappedSecret` (DPAPI per-user encryption, identity on posix).
3. POSIX behavior unchanged (chmod, plain rename, identity wrapping).
4. `node:test` suites cover both adaptations, including a real DPAPI round-trip on Windows.
5. Consumer rewiring (secrets store, ssh-config) lands in follow-up PRs stacked on this one.

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — Windows facade behaviors

Preconditions: Windows host.
Steps: Run `node --import tsx --test services/api/src/platform/os/win32.test.ts`.
Expected / pass: 9/9 green, including a real DPAPI wrap/unwrap round-trip of a master-key-sized blob and icacls-based restrictToOwner assertions. **Verified on Windows 11 23H2, Node v24.21.0.**

### Case 2 — POSIX unchanged

Steps: Run the posix suite; on Linux CI the posix file is a passthrough by construction.
Expected / pass: posix suite green; no behavior change vs main.

### Case 3 — Facade only, no consumers yet

Steps: Inspect the diff.
Expected / pass: New files only; no existing api file is modified in this PR (consumers arrive as separate stacked PRs).

## Related

- Implements #491 (API OS platform abstraction)
- Parent: #400
- Re-lands the api-platform portion of the closed #478/#492 per their review feedback (typecheck green, platform-only scope, no internal references, Windows evidence)
closed_recent.title: [Feature] API OS adaptation facade (owner-only permissions, replace-with-retry, at-rest secret wrapping)

closed_recent.author: qingkwl
closed_recent.body:
## Problem

`services/runner` has Windows-specific behavior requirements with no platform seam:

- Killing a child with POSIX signals does not tear down the process tree on Windows (#482): the runner needs `terminateTree` semantics (`taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F`), while POSIX must keep the current signal-based behavior unchanged.
- Owner-only (0600) permission semantics rely on `chmod`, which only toggles the read-only bit on Windows (#477 covers the general platform work; the runner side needs `restrictToOwner` through the facade).
- Conda environment specifics (delay-load DLL directories, the bundled m2-bash shell location, win-64 package substitution guidance) are spread over platform branches today.

PR #478 carried an earlier version of this work but was closed; this re-lands the runner-platform portion with a clean scope (runner only), a green typecheck, no unresolvable references, and real-machine Windows evidence.

## Expected

1. `services/runner/src/platform/` provides the facade: `types.ts` (adaptation surface), `index.ts` (single dispatch point), `posix.ts` (transparent passthrough), `win32.ts` (Windows implementation: `terminateTree` via taskkill, `restrictToOwner` via icacls, conda path/shell helpers).
2. Runner call sites use the facade only: `killSandboxProcess` goes through `terminateTree`; server-side 0600 semantics go through `restrictToOwner`. No direct `process.platform` branches for these concerns in consumer code.
3. POSIX behavior unchanged (signals, chmod).
4. `node:test` suites cover both adaptations.

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — Windows tree kill (matches #482 Case 1)

Preconditions: Windows host; a Node child that spawns a grandchild that stays alive.
Steps: Call `terminateTree(child)`; inspect the process list for both PIDs.
Expected / pass: Both PIDs are gone; helper returns true. **Verified on a real Windows 11 machine** with the packaged runner build: child + grandchild gone within 1s (evidence script `verify-482-case1.mjs` run recorded 2026-10-28).

### Case 2 — POSIX unchanged

Steps: Run the runner suite (`pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/runner test`).
Expected / pass: 37/37 green on Windows with the posix passthrough; on Linux the behavior is identical to main (posix file is a passthrough only).

### Case 3 — Facade only

Steps: Inspect runner call sites for tree-kill/permission paths.
Expected / pass: All go through `platform/index.ts`; no raw taskkill / chmod outside `platform/`.

## Related

- Implements the runner half of #482 (tree-kill) and part of #477 (owner-only permissions)
- Parent: #400
- Re-lands the runner-platform portion of the closed #478 with review feedback addressed (typecheck green, runner-only scope, no internal references, Windows evidence)

closed_recent.author: HugoXK
closed_recent.body:
## Problem

`SseFrameDecoder` in `apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts` keeps a partial frame in memory until it sees the `\n\n` terminator. On `main` at `ca98c195`:

- `push` appends the chunk to the retained buffer — `apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts:41-44` (append at line 42);
- `drain` re-normalizes the whole buffer with `this.buffer.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n")` and only then looks for a blank line — `apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts:51-70` (lines 55 and 56);
- `flush` is only reached when the stream ends — `apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts:46-49`, called from `apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts:111`.

If a stream keeps sending bytes for a frame that never receives its terminating blank line, the buffer grows for as long as that stream stays open. Memory grows with bytes received, and because the whole buffer is re-scanned on every chunk, total work grows quadratically. While the stream is open nothing bounds it and nothing reports it; if the stream ends, the tail reaches `flush()` and is counted as a skipped frame (#616). The gap this issue closes is the **live window**. Growth needs continuing bytes after an unterminated frame — a server that merely stalls sends nothing and so grows nothing.

**This is pre-existing on `main` and is not introduced by PR #616.** #616 handled a payload that does not parse (`stream.ts:129-140`); this is a framing failure, where no complete frame is ever handed to `JSON.parse`. #616 does cover the end-of-stream case (an over-long tail reaches `flush()` and is then counted as a skipped frame), so the remaining gap is only while the stream is still open — which is the case for a live run. The decoder region is byte-identical at `ca98c195` and at #616's head.

`pump` (`apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts:105`) is the only production consumer. The API's own writer always terminates a frame with `data: <json>\n\n` (`services/api/src/runs/index.ts`, `writeSse`), so a normal server does not trigger this; it needs a stream whose writer omits the terminator while continuing to send data.

## Expected

> Contract note: #616 merged into `main` at `5b25c260` on 2026-10-28. The skipped-frame path exists now, so this issue specifies skip-once-and-continue, not a stream-ending failure.

- The decoder's retained buffer is bounded by a constant, so an unterminated frame cannot grow memory without bound.
- On exceeding the ceiling, the decoder discards bytes up to and including the next `\n\n` — that terminator closes the oversized frame, it does not start a new one — and never hands the dropped tail to `JSON.parse`, so a crafted tail cannot be re-interpreted as a new event.
- #616 is merged into `main` (`5b25c260`, 2026-10-28), so the skipped-frame path is available: the drop is reported **once** through it (the existing "Skipped N updates that could not be read." wording), the frame is counted once, and the stream continues instead of ending. No second notice and no new error mode.
- No bytes after the drop are parsed, and no event or cursor id is taken from the dropped tail. On reconnect the client's cursor is whatever the last fully received frame set it to.
- Clean streams and frames below the bound behave exactly as today.
- An earlier revision of this issue said the drop should end the stream as a bounded framing failure, because `main` had no skipped-frame path at the time. That is no longer the contract: #616 landed, and skip-once-and-continue is what this change does.

## Repro shape (unit level)

```ts
const decoder = new SseFrameDecoder();
for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i += 1) decoder.push('id: 1\ndata: {"type":"run.started"}');
// no frame is emitted, no error is raised, and decoder.buffer keeps growing
```

Then append `'\n\n'` plus a valid frame: at `main` the retained buffer has no upper bound, and only the later terminator releases it.

## Suggested guard (sketch, not prescriptive)

- Add a `MAX_FRAME_CHARS` constant to the decoder; pick it with headroom over the largest event the API emits (live tool results are the biggest frames).
- When no boundary is found and the buffer exceeds it, discard bytes up to and including the next `\n\n` — that terminator closes the oversized frame, it does not begin a new one — never hand the dropped tail to `JSON.parse`, count the frame once, and resume parsing after it so later well-formed frames still arrive. Report it through #616's existing one-notice path; do not add a second notice or a new error mode. Advance no cursor from bytes that were not fully received.
- Optional, same change: normalize only the newly appended part of the buffer instead of re-scanning all of it on every chunk (`stream.ts:55`) — this removes the quadratic term.
- Reuse the existing wording ("Skipped N updates that could not be read.") rather than adding a second notice.

## Verification cases

1. **Endless unterminated frame** — the retained buffer stays at or below the bound; the frame is given up on, its terminator is consumed, and the stream continues, so one bad frame does not end a live run.
2. **One failure, not many** — the oversized frame is counted once and reported once through the existing notice; a stream without such a frame reports nothing; the dropped tail is never parsed (a crafted tail that would parse as JSON still yields no event and no cursor advance).
3. **Clean stream unchanged** — every frame delivered, no error (existing `apps/desktop/tests/api-client.test.ts` cases stay green).
4. **Large but legal frame** — a frame below the bound still parses fully.
5. **No cursor from unread bytes** — the drop produces no event and no cursor advance; the replay cursor stays at the last fully received frame's id, and a cap drop never hands over an id from bytes that were never fully read.
6. **No new setting** — the ceiling is a module constant, not user configuration, preserving #505's "no new setting" constraint.

## Context

Found while reviewing PR #616 at `c7d49f79` (static review, no tests run). Adjacent to #505 but a different failure class (framing vs `JSON.parse`), so it is tracked separately. Client-only; no server change and no protocol change is needed.

Out of scope, stated so it is not mistaken for covered: with bounded memory, a peer that simply stops writing still keeps the stream open forever — `running` stays true and the follow path never settles. That is a stall/liveness question, not a memory one, and it exists on `main`. This issue does not address idle or stalled streams, and it does not change the pre-existing fact that a clean close with no parsed terminal is silent on the follow path (`use-workspace.ts:892-910`: `closeRunStream` marks `terminal: true`, a run still executing server-side can look finished). That is a separate liveness/wording item, unchanged by this fix.

Owner: ScienceDiscovery Dev-1 (desktop). Labels and milestone deliberately left to the maintainer: #505 sits on `v0.3.0`, and this repo-side label write is not available to us.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] desktop: cap the SSE frame decoder buffer so an unterminated frame cannot grow without bound

## Problem
Settings › Runtime remote host credentials are write-only (good): empty fields keep the stored secret. The register/update API already accepts `password` / `passphrase` / `privateKeyPath: null` to forget, but the desktop UI never sends null, so there is no way to clear stored credentials from the dialog.

## Expected
A clear/forget control (or equivalent) sends null for the chosen secret fields so `hasPassword` / `hasPrivateKey` clear and later probes fail until a new secret is set.

## Verification cases

1. **Empty save keeps secret (current)**
   - **Preconditions:** Remote host with a stored password (`hasPassword` true).
   - **Steps:** Open credentials; leave password empty; save.
   - **Expected / pass:** `hasPassword` remains true (keep-on-empty behavior preserved).

2. **Explicit forget**
   - **Preconditions:** Same host with stored password.
   - **Steps:** Use the clear/forget control; save; re-open credentials / probe connect.
   - **Expected / pass:** `hasPassword` false; probe fails without a new secret.

3. **Re-set after forget**
   - **Preconditions:** Credentials cleared per (2).
   - **Steps:** Enter a new password; save; probe.
   - **Expected / pass:** `hasPassword` true; probe succeeds with the new secret.

Follow-up from review of https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/502. Out of Act-on scope for that PR (Escape stacking is in-scope there).

closed_recent.author: JinhZhao
closed_recent.body:
`docs/en/advanced-setup/configure-skills.md:7` tells users to provide a non-empty `description` in the skill frontmatter.

However, `packages/specialist/src/skills.ts:565` defaults `description` to `""`:

```typescript
const description = typeof parsed.frontmatter.description === "string"
  ? parsed.frontmatter.description
  : "";
```

And `validateSkillPackage` (`:529-628`) performs no emptiness or minimum-length check on the value. A skill with an empty description passes validation and packages cleanly.

Since `description` is what the selector prompt uses to decide whether a skill is relevant to a user request, an empty description silently drops the skill out of routing — the skill exists but is never selected.

**Reproduce:** Create a minimal SKILL.md with no `description` field; run `validateSkillPackage`.

**Suggested fix:** Either reject empty descriptions in `validateSkillPackage` (matching the doc), or correct the doc to state that description is optional.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] validateSkillPackage accepts empty description that docs forbid

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## Problem

After a remote Shell Execution is accepted, a lost status observation is recorded in two places that disagree.

The shell execution record becomes `unknown` / `unconfirmed`. That means the remote result has not been confirmed. It does not mean the command failed. Inspecting that execution reconciles the record with the Runner by the same Execution ID and does not resubmit the command (see #185).

The provenance execution run written when that observation throws is different. The dispatch error path appends an execution run with `status: "failed"`, `exitCode: null`, and stderr set to the observation error. `ExecutionRun.status` only allows `succeeded`, `failed`, and `cancelled`. Runs are append-only, so a later reconciliation that adopts the Runner's committed result updates the shell execution record and leaves this run unchanged.

Skill distillation and the memory graph read execution runs. They can treat an unconfirmed observation as a job failure, and they still see that failure after the shell execution record has been reconciled to the Runner's real outcome.

## Expected

- An observation that stays unconfirmed is not reported as a successful job or as a failed job by the execution-run record, by skill distillation, or by the memory graph.
- If reconciliation later adopts a committed Runner result for that same Execution ID, those readers see that result.
- A Runner outcome that really failed or was cancelled, including a non-zero exit or a recorded failure with a committed version, is still stored as failed or cancelled.
- The command is not replayed.

## Note

#185 does not choose how to represent an unconfirmed run. `ExecutionRun.status` has no value for "not confirmed", and the run list is append-only. This issue tracks that choice. It is separate from the shell-execution reconciliation fix.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] An unconfirmed shell observation is stored as a failed execution run

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## 范围与证据

汇总 [2026-10-24 Nightly run 40121906605](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605) 的三项剩余问题。运行版本：`9eb45d753b86b94ce67d41032d9511d724c628be`。

#514 / #515 修复的 Ubuntu 26.04 / Python 3.14 依赖准备已通过，本次不再作为阻塞项。以下区分实际运行结果与源码诊断，不据此认定所有 main CI 都失败。

## 1. real research-8 的会话标题断言未跟随显示规则更新

[失败 job 120955308760](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/job/120955308760) 已实际执行该用例，在点击 Add session 后失败：

- [`issue-67-34-inline-cards.spec.ts:221`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/9eb45d753b86b94ce67d41032d9511d724c628be/test/issue-67-34-inline-cards.spec.ts#L219-L228) 期望 `Untitled session`，实际为 `Untitled session 2`。
- #510 已合入同一 Project 多个未命名会话显示序号的行为，实际标题与该规则一致。当前证据支持“测试期望过时”，不能据此认定产品的计划/子任务功能损坏。
- 此前的计划、follow-up、reload 断言已通过；失败后的切回原会话及位置保持断言尚未执行，不能算通过。
- #511 仍讨论编号集合与排序的 UX 口径，本 issue 不替它决定方案，只修复测试对已实现显示规则的错误假设。

## 2. 已执行失败的分片被汇总成 NOT_RUN

[research-8 结果 artifact 12574909042](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/artifacts/12574909042) 的 `e2e-real/tagged/summary.json` 明确记录：

- planned=1、executed=1、passed=0、failed=1；
- 该身份的 `outcome=FAIL`。

但 [汇总 job 120992446082](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/job/120992446082) 输出 executed=18/19、passed=18，并将该用例标为 `NOT_RUN`。

源码诊断：[`.ci/real-report.mjs:19-24`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/9eb45d753b86b94ce67d41032d9511d724c628be/.ci/real-report.mjs#L19-L24) 在失败分片的 `results.push(...summary.results)` 之前抛出 `SHARD_FAILED`，丢掉了其已执行结果。需要保留身份、版本、digest 等校验通过的失败证据，同时继续让 gate 失败。该运行应准确呈现 19 executed、18 passed、1 failed，而不是将执行失败混同为未运行。

## 3. 两项 UT 等待完成超时，原因待查

[UT job 120955273894](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/job/120955273894)：4754 planned / 4754 executed / 4752 passed / 2 failed / 0 skipped。

[UT artifact 12572160563](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/artifacts/12572160563) 中的实际失败：

- `ut/tagged/group-279/worker-1-events.jsonl`：`services/api/src/evolution/orchestrator.test.ts` 的 `a measured run is staged before the sidecar is asked to start`，报 `timed out waiting for the run to settle`。
- `ut/tagged/group-343/worker-1-events.jsonl`：`services/api/src/server.test.ts` 的 `running sessions accept queued runs and start them after the active run completes`，报等待 run 进入 `completed` 超时。

[同一 SHA 较早的 UT job 120785725594](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40064771478/job/120785725594) 在 Ubuntu 26.04 上 4754/4754 通过。现有证据不能区分测试时序、环境或产品状态推进问题，不认定为负载抖动或确定性回归。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 会话切换测试按当前显示规则及明确的 Session 身份校验，补齐“新增会话 → 切回原会话 → 原计划/时间线位置保持”的验证；不删除原行为断言。
- [ ] 为汇总器补充“分片实际执行但失败”的无模型回归测试，保留 executed/failed 计数和失败身份；身份不匹配、缺失、重复、跳过等情况仍不得放行。
- [ ] 使用上述已有结果验证汇总应为 19 executed / 18 passed / 1 failed，退出码仍非零；不通过跳过失败分片把 gate 改绿。
- [ ] 分别定位两项 UT 超时，保留最后运行状态及相关事件等诊断证据，补充针对性回归验证；仅延长超时或重跑成功不能作为已定位的证据。

本 issue 基于已有日志、artifact 与源码核对，未触发新的付费模型调用或 CI 重跑。
closed_recent.title: [Bug] ci: 修复 Nightly 会话标题断言与失败分片统计，排查两项 UT 超时

closed_recent.author: HongyeZhou
closed_recent.body:
## Problem
Desktop workspace upload sends `File.name` into FormData without client-side basename sanitization. Path escape remains a server responsibility (`readWorkspaceFile` notes this), but a crafted name such as `../outside.txt` or a name containing `/` should be rejected or renamed on the client as defense in depth.

## Expected
Before upload, the client strips path segments / rejects unsafe names so only a basename reaches FormData; server still remains the authority and continues to rename/reject escapes.

## Verification cases

1. **Crafted relative name**
   - **Preconditions:** Open session with workspace panel; upload enabled (session not archived).
   - **Steps:**
     1. Upload (or simulate) a `File` whose `name` is `../outside.txt`.
     2. Inspect the FormData filename and the resulting workspace listing.
   - **Expected / pass:** Client does not send `../outside.txt` as-is (sanitize/reject); server listing shows no escape outside the session workspace.

2. **Name with slash**
   - **Preconditions:** Same as (1).
   - **Steps:** Upload a `File` whose `name` contains `/` (e.g. `a/b.txt`).
   - **Expected / pass:** Client basename-only or reject; no nested path created via the client name alone.

3. **Normal basename unchanged**
   - **Preconditions:** Same as (1).
   - **Steps:** Upload `notes.md`.
   - **Expected / pass:** File appears under the session workspace with the expected name (rename-on-conflict still applies).

## Context

closed_recent.author: HongyeZhou
closed_recent.body:
## Problem
A Windows durability fix for CAS directory `fsync` (`O_RDWR` on `win32` because `FlushFileBuffers` needs a writable handle) and `toNamespacedPath` for SQLite paths landed inside the conversational-configuration protocol PR (#553), mixed with unrelated schema/protocol work. On Linux the `win32` branch is never taken, so CI here cannot exercise the failure mode (silently weaker directory sync if the open/handle is wrong).

## Expected
- CAS Windows durable-directory sync ships in its own small PR (or clearly scoped commit series) with Windows verification attached.
- Configuration/protocol PRs do not carry unrelated CAS durability changes.

## Verification cases
1. **Writable-directory sync on Windows**
   - Preconditions: Windows host; CAS `VersionStore` / `RefStore` initialized on a normal NTFS directory.
   - Steps: Create/update a live ref that triggers `syncDirectory`; confirm no throw from `open(..., O_RDWR|O_DIRECTORY)` + `handle.sync()`.
   - Expected / pass: Operation succeeds; refs.sqlite and object dirs remain consistent after process kill mid-write (WAL + FULL sync still hold).
2. **Long / namespaced path**
   - Preconditions: Windows; store path that needs `\\?\` / namespaced form (deep or near-MAX_PATH tree).
   - Steps: Open `RefStore` / lease DBs via the same helpers.
   - Expected / pass: `DatabaseSync(toNamespacedPath(...))` opens; no path-not-found solely from missing namespace prefix.
3. **Negative — read-only directory**
   - Preconditions: Directory without write ACL for the process.
   - Steps: Trigger `syncDirectory`.
   - Expected / pass: Failure is loud (thrown/propagated), not a silent no-op sync; caller sees the error.
4. **Linux unchanged**
   - Preconditions: Linux CI/dev.
   - Steps: Same CAS unit/integration paths as today.
   - Expected / pass: Still uses `O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY`; no behavioral change.

## Context
Refs #553 (CAS hunks in `packages/cas/src/versioning.ts`, `workspace-lease.ts`, `workspace-lifecycle.ts`). Spotted during review of the four-PR configuration stack; out of scope for the shared configuration protocol.
closed_recent.title: [Bug] CAS: isolate Windows durable-directory sync (O_RDWR + toNamespacedPath) from feature stacks

closed_recent.author: zy95-12
closed_recent.body:
## 背景 / 输入

同一 NatureBench 复现会话 `93f897ca-cefe-4e7b-932d-8339cbef1459`：

- 续跑 run：`84d71b8a-77dd-42a7-bc81-15e326b14cb1`（约 14.1 min，`completed`）
- Agent 顺序跑实例：`cl3` → `cl5` → `mop_sc`（EM 估计约 50–60 min）
- 通过 `tools/run_instances.sh` / `tools/run_timed.py` 拉起后台 `python run.py --instances mop_sc`

## 问题是什么

1. **Run / turn 已 `completed`，但 CPU 作业仍在跑**（孤儿进程）。监控时可见 PID 仍以 ~100% CPU 跑 mop_sc，而 API run 状态早已结束。
2. Agent 用「45 分钟定时器再回来」这类自我约定结束 turn，框架**没有跨 turn 的长任务/作业跟踪**，用户与监控只能靠 `ps` 发现。
3. 后台 `print` **块缓冲**时，日志长时间不增长，看起来像卡死（见关联 issue：重定向日志缓冲）。

## 我们怎么规避的

- 宿主侧继续 `ps` / 等 `output/mop_sc/predictions.npy` 落盘（约 26.5 min 后成功）。
- 明确 **不**再起第二轮 SD run 抢同一作业；mop_sn 因体量过大主动 deferred 并杀掉误启动的排队。

## 期望应该是什么样

1. 沙箱/主机上的长命令应挂到 **可查询的 job / process 句柄**（run 级或 session 级）：run 结束 ≠ 计算结束时，UI 仍显示「后台作业进行中」。
2. Agent 结束 turn 时若仍有未收尾子进程，应默认：提示、挂起、或要求显式 `detach`；不要静默孤儿化。
3. 支持「续接同一作业」的会话语义（resume / await job），避免 Agent 用墙钟定时器假装调度。

## 证据

- Run `84d71b8a-…` `completed` 后 PID `647972` 仍在跑 `run.py --instances mop_sc`
- 最终 mop_sc：`predictions.npy` shape `(5693,)`，`wall≈1587.7s`，peak RSS≈953MB
closed_recent.title: [Usability] long CPU jobs become orphans when agent turn/run completes (no cross-turn job tracking)

closed_recent.author: ink999107
closed_recent.body:
## Summary

When the runtime data directory's absolute path is 88 bytes or longer, the sandbox egress gateway cannot bind its Unix socket and **every** `run_shell` fails before any command executes — including a bare `echo`. The Runner still reports `ready: true` and `sandboxNetwork.available: true`, so the failure only appears per execution, inside the tool result, and the agent cannot tell whether the sandbox or its own command is at fault.

On Linux the limit leaves 87 bytes for the data directory; on macOS 83. A checkout whose path is already deep (for example a handoff/archive directory several levels below `$HOME`) reaches 88 bytes with the default `<repository root>/.sciencediscovery-data` and fails by exactly one byte.

## Environment

- ScienceDiscovery `54263a4c` (native local mode, `scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local --no-build --no-jiuwenswarm`), Linux, bubblewrap sandbox.
- Sandbox network access: global settings `mode: "open"` (also reproducible with `domain-allowlist`).
- Runner data directory: `SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR` = `<repository root>/.sciencediscovery-data`, absolute length 88 bytes.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Place the checkout so that `<absolute repository root>/.sciencediscovery-data` is **88 bytes or longer** (equivalently, set `SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR` to an 88+ byte absolute path):

   ```bash
   printf %s "$PWD/.sciencediscovery-data" | wc -c   # 88 or more → reproduces
   ```

2. Start the stack and enable sandbox network access (`open` or `domain-allowlist`) so a session's tool calls need egress.
3. In a session, run any shell command — a trivial `echo` is enough.
4. Observe: every `run_shell` fails with `status: "failed"`, empty stdout, and the same stderr, e.g.

   ```
   Sandbox network access (domain-allowlist and open) is unavailable: the egress socket path is 108 bytes,
   over this platform's 107-byte Unix socket path limit — <dataDir>/eg/<16 hex>.
   The socket has to stay inside the runner data directory, so shorten that directory by at least 1 byte(s)
   (SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR); it must leave 20 bytes for the socket itself.
   ```

5. `GET /health` on the runner and the `check_runner` tool both still report `sandboxUsable: true` / `sandboxNetwork.available: true`, and `sandboxNetwork.modes` still lists `domain-allowlist` and `open`.

## Code path

- `services/runner/src/egress-gateway.ts` — `MAX_UNIX_SOCKET_PATH_BYTES` (107 Linux / 103 macOS), `EGRESS_SOCKET_RELATIVE_BYTES = 20` (`/eg/` + 16-hex digest name), `EgressGatewayRegistry.socketPath()`, and `assertUnixSocketPathFits()` called at the top of `EgressGateway.listen()`. The socket path is therefore `dataDir` length + 20, and a data directory of 88 bytes yields 108 > 107.
- `services/runner/src/executor.ts` — `prepareSandboxEgress()` calls `gateways.acquire()` on the launch path for any `domain-allowlist` / `open` execution, so the failure is charged to every execution, not only the ones that use the network.
- `services/runner/src/server.ts` — `sandboxNetworkCapability()` probes only the egress bridge's host Python interpreter. It never measures the socket path, so the capability report and `/health` claim the modes are available while every execution fails.
- `services/launcher/src/preflight.ts` / `services/runner/src/readiness.ts` — likewise check only sandbox usability (bwrap options, user namespaces), not the socket path.
- Default data directory: `.env` → `SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR=.sciencediscovery-data`, resolved against the repository root in `scripts/start-stack.sh`.

## Why this is reported as a bug

- The constraint "the runtime data directory must be ≤ 87 bytes (Linux) / ≤ 83 bytes (macOS)" is real but is documented nowhere, and nothing at startup warns about it. The default layout silently depends on how deep the checkout sits.
- The failure is discovered per execution rather than at startup, and the only surface that knows the reason (`/health`, `check_runner`) reports the opposite (`available: true`). In our run the agent spent its turns proving the sandbox was broken and could not open a repair card for the blocker, so an antibody-design session ended with zero commands executed.
- Because the launch path needs the gateway for *any* command, an over-long path does not degrade network access — it takes the whole Runner offline while it still advertises itself as healthy. The preflight code already states this failure mode for bubblewrap options: reporting success from a launch the runner would refuse "is exactly the mismatch that let the service look healthy while every tool call failed".

## Suggested direction

1. Report the socket-path condition in the capability/health surface: `sandboxNetworkCapability()` (and the launcher preflight) should measure `socketPath("")` for the configured data directory and return `available: false` with the byte counts, so the blocker is visible before a session starts.
2. Fail loudly at startup: `scripts/start-stack.sh` (and the single-file launcher) should refuse to start, or warn with the exact shortfall, when the resolved data directory exceeds the platform limit.
3. Document the limit next to `SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR` in `docs/{en,zh}/reference/configuration.md`, since it is a hard deployment constraint.
4. Optionally decouple the socket path from the install location — keep the digest-of-revision identity but root the socket directory in a short, runner-owned runtime path (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, or a 0700 directory the runner creates and verifies ownership of) so a deep checkout is not a functional constraint.

Short term, pointing `SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR` at a short path (a symlink keeps the existing 2 GB of state and the absolute paths baked into `envs/` valid) unblocks the Runner.

## Impact

Total loss of code execution on an affected host for every session, with a misleading "Runner is ready" signal; no workaround is reachable from inside a session (the agent cannot change the host's data directory).
closed_recent.title: [Bug] A deep data directory breaks the egress socket path, so every run_shell fails while the Runner reports ready

closed_recent.author: HongyeZhou
closed_recent.body:
## Problem

PR #534 copies a redacted diagnostic to the clipboard and pre-fills a **public** GitHub new-issue URL. Token/secret/Bearer/URL-userinfo redaction is covered, but absolute filesystem paths that embed a username (for example `/home/<user>/...`, `/Users/<user>/...`, `C:\Users\<user>\...`) can still appear in the error title/detail and therefore in the clipboard and the draft URL. That leaks local identity/PII to a public tracker without the user noticing.

This is adjacent to #58 / #534 but was not part of the listed Security acceptance bullets (Authorization/Bearer, token, secret, password, cookie, URL userinfo).

## Expected

Before truncation and before building the GitHub issue URL, diagnostic text (and any exported log metadata strings) must redact home-directory / username path segments so a public draft cannot carry the local account name. Other redaction already required by #58 stays in place.

## Verification cases

1. **Unix home path in error detail**
   - Preconditions: Web UI shows a visible error whose detail contains `/home/alice/.sciencediscovery-data/logs/api.log` (or equivalent fixture).
   - Steps: Click **Copy key diagnostics**; open the GitHub issue draft from the same control.
   - Expected / pass: Clipboard and issue-draft body contain a redacted path form (for example `/home/[REDACTED]/...` or equivalent); the literal username `alice` does not appear. Bundle stays within the existing 4000 / 6500 caps.

2. **macOS / Windows user path**
   - Preconditions: Error detail contains `/Users/bob/project/file.ts` and `C:\Users\bob\AppData\...`.
   - Steps: Copy diagnostics and open the issue draft.
   - Expected / pass: `bob` does not appear in clipboard or draft URL/body; redaction markers are present.

3. **Negative — non-home path retained**
   - Preconditions: Error detail contains a non-user path such as `/tmp/sciencediscovery-test/out.log` or `/var/log/...` with no username segment.
   - Steps: Copy diagnostics.
   - Expected / pass: Path remains useful for maintainers (not over-redacted into uselessness); still no tokens/secrets.

4. **Regression — existing secret redaction**
   - Preconditions: Detail includes `Bearer sk-testsecret` and `api_key=private-value`.
   - Steps: Copy + open issue draft.
   - Expected / pass: Secrets remain `[REDACTED]`; path redaction does not disable prior rules.

## Context

Refs #534 (feat: copy sanitized error diagnostics). Related #58. Security hardening for the public GitHub draft destination.

## Problem

In the artifact / dataset table preview, header cells are left-aligned while body cells use the global `td { text-align: right }` rule. On a wider artifact viewer this mismatch is more visible (noticed while reviewing #428; predates that PR).

## Expected

Column headers and cell values share a consistent alignment (or headers match the numeric/text alignment of their column), so a wide table does not look mis-registered.

## Verification cases

1. **Wide table in artifact viewer**
   - **Preconditions:** A session with an Artifact that renders a multi-column dataset / Markdown table in the artifact viewer; window ≥1280px wide.
   - **Steps:** Open the Artifact; look at any numeric column header vs its cells.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Header alignment matches the column’s cell alignment (no left header over right-aligned numbers for the same column).

2. **Negative — non-table previews unchanged**
   - **Preconditions:** Same session; open a Markdown prose Artifact and a source Artifact.
   - **Steps:** Open each preview.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Prose / source layout is unchanged by any table-alignment fix.

## Context

Refs #428 (noted by author as pre-existing; not in that PR’s scope). Also visible after #309 / large-viewer work.

## Problem
In `apps/desktop` SSE `pump`, frame `data:` is `JSON.parse`d without try/catch. A single malformed frame ends the stream and drops the live run UI even when the server may still be running.

## Expected
A bad frame is skipped or counted, the pump continues (or one toast surfaces), and the run still reaches a terminal/handled state when the server finishes.

## Verification cases

1. **Malformed mid-stream frame**
   - **Preconditions:** Desktop workbench connected; a run is in flight with an open SSE stream.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Inject one malformed `data:` line mid-stream (invalid JSON).
     2. Observe UI and subsequent frames.
   - **Expected / pass:** Pump does not abort solely due to that frame; user sees at most one clear error/toast; later valid frames or a terminal settle still apply.

2. **Clean stream still works**
   - **Preconditions:** Same as (1), no injection.
   - **Steps:** Complete a normal turn end-to-end.
   - **Expected / pass:** Transcript, terminal status, and settle behave as today (no regression).

## Context
Follow-up from review of https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/499 (foundation). Out of that PR's Act-on scope; code-review inference on `api/stream.ts` pump.

# 中文版

## 版本定位

ScienceDiscovery **全面拥抱 jiuwen-swarm 后端的第一个 Beta 版本**：保留科研工作台体验，以 jiuwen-swarm 支撑 Agent 执行，在新架构上整合科研专属能力。

本 issue 用于征集社区对 Release Note、发布范围及阻塞问题的反馈，**不是正式发布公告**。上一版本为 `0.2.0`；建议版本号为 **`0.3.0-beta.1`（待确认）**，开发主线为 `main`（原 JiuwenSwarm 分支已切换为主线），本次发版分支为 `releases/v0.3.0.beta`。

## Release Note 草案

### 重点支持场景

本版本重点保障以下四类场景，不追求一次性迁移全部历史能力或覆盖所有边界情况。

| 场景 | 主要流程与交付 | Domain 文档 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 文献调研 | 检索与获取文献、提取证据、多专家协作，交付带可追溯引用的调研报告 | [文献调研教程](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/zh/domains/literature-research.md) |
| 数据分析 | 读取数据、准备环境、执行分析，交付可复现代码、图表与结论 | [脓毒症数据分析教程](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/zh/domains/analyze-sepsis-endotypes.md) |
| 抗体设计 | 结合领域 Skill、专业模型和科研环境完成设计与筛选；依赖相应模型资源与算力，计算结果不等同于实验验证 | [抗体设计教程](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/zh/domains/antibody-design.md) |
| 算法优化 | 通过科研产物 RSI / Evolve 生成候选、执行评估与迭代，保留结果与过程记录 | [算法优化教程](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md) |

### 核心功能与改进

- **统一 JiuwenSwarm 默认后端**：源码、Docker 和发行包启动器均默认选择 JiuwenSwarm；保留显式 native 切换。主子 Agent 默认通过平台 `task` 委派、由 Swarm 执行，并非全面切换为 Swarm 原生多 Agent 编排。
- **科研执行环境与工作区**：支持本地/远程执行、托管环境、后台任务、文件传递、工作区交接及产物版本关联。
- **记忆图谱**：记录科研任务、文件与产物关系，支持引用追溯；源码及 Docker 部署提供默认本地存储，可选 Neo4j。
- **科研 Skill、MCP 与 Specialist**：支持内置能力和自定义扩展，组合专业专家完成科研任务。
- **科研产物 RSI 与 Idea Tree**：支持产物迭代优化、候选评估和研究思路的树状探索。
- **可观测性与测试**：完善执行轨迹、子任务状态和错误诊断，补充 Mock E2E、真实科研 Benchmark 与质量评估记录。
- **文档与入门体验**：整理中英文文档和四类场景教程，明确 Swarm/native 在上下文、规划、工具、Skill 等方面的行为差异。

这些功能包含已有能力的迁移与增强，并非全部首次引入。

### 官网、社区与交付配套（本版本新增）

- **统一对外网站**：提供[官网与安装入口](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/install/index.html)，集中展示安装指引、使用文档与科研场景教程；网站内容随 `main` 分支同步更新。
- **用户交流社区**：面向海外与中国用户，分别建立 **Slack** 和 **飞书**用户交流群，用于使用交流、问题反馈与社区协作；加入方式见仓库首页。
- **双分支每日 CI**：构建每日质量检查，覆盖 `main` 和 `releases/v0.3.0.beta`。由 main 的定时任务触发两条分支各自的检查，分别保留结果、日志和构建产物，为主线演进与版本发布提供持续质量反馈。
- **多平台、多种安装方式**：支持 Linux、macOS，Windows 可通过 WSL 2 使用；提供源码、Linux 二进制发行包及 Docker 等部署方式。不同系统可用的安装方式与前置条件不同，详见[官网安装页](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/install/index.html)。

### 主要 Bugfix

- **记忆图谱内存与查询性能**：修复折叠查询的路径爆炸，使用共享路径及累计集合预算，避免已复现的高内存分配；超预算返回结构化错误。优化会话索引查询，避免大量无关历史数据拖累新会话（#212，修复 #210）。
- **启动行为一致性**：修复源码与 Docker/发行包默认后端不一致，确保命令行后端选项优先于 `.env`；Docker 转发 Swarm 配置，E2E 显式选择后端（#214）。
- **Swarm/MCP 隔离与恢复**：改进模型、会话、工具绑定隔离，工具刷新、共享连接和权限生命周期（#173、#181、#182）。
- **子任务与远程执行可靠性**：改进并发排队、超时、取消、工作区交接和子 Agent 恢复；远程执行状态查询增加瞬时错误重试（#182、#187、#191）。
- **模型输出与事件流**：改进截断输出恢复，避免执行不完整工具参数，增强工具事件流存活与诊断（#190、#194）。
- **科研数据与交付**：改进 PDF 校验、arXiv 接入兼容性、产物版本关联，以及界面状态、快照作用域和取消诊断（#171、#180、#192、#179、#189、#193）。

## Beta 边界与升级说明

- **Nightly Real E2E 尚不稳定**：自动真实模型 E2E CI 仍在稳定化过程中，当前真实科研场景的验收以本地实际执行并保留记录的结果为准，需注明被测提交、模型和配置。Nightly 结果作为辅助诊断，不单独作为版本质量已达标的依据；跳过或隔离的用例不视为通过。UT/ST/Mock E2E 门禁仍是独立的质量依据。
- **部分安装路径为实验特性**：macOS Docker 以及所有 Windows 安装路径（包括 WSL 2 和 Docker Desktop）尚未全面验证 Agent 执行效果。当前预编译单文件包面向 Linux，不提供原生 macOS/Windows 二进制；macOS 优先使用源码方式，Windows 的 Linux 二进制/源码方式需在 WSL 2 内运行。具体支持范围与依赖见官网安装页。
- **官网与发行版的差异**：官网跟随 main，可能包含尚未进入本次 Beta 的更新；本版本的准确行为与限制以发行分支文档和最终 Release Note 为准。
- **场景验收与效果边界**：四类场景是重点验收范围，效果仍受模型、网络、数据源和算力影响；测试已加入不代表所有真实场景已稳定通过，发布以最终候选版本验收为准。
- **Swarm 初始化与后端切换**：源码首次使用 Swarm 前执行 `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup`。保留原生循环可使用 `--no-jiuwenswarm` 或 `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXECUTOR=native`。
- **记忆图谱升级与故障处理**：升级不会覆盖已保存的记忆功能设置；此前手动关闭的用户需在系统设置中重新开启。已有图谱可通过 `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_DATA_DIR` 指向原目录，不自动迁移。设置 `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_AVAILABLE=0` 可跳过服务；该可选服务启动失败时会报告原因并在禁用图谱的情况下继续启动，修正后需重启。
- **外部数据源限制**：arXiv 406/429、排队超时等外部数据源问题仍由 #208 跟踪。

## 社区反馈

请反馈：版本定位与版本号是否合适、功能或修复有无遗漏、四类场景是否存在发布阻塞，以及哪些限制必须写入正式说明。问题反馈请附配置、复现步骤及日志。

---

# English version

## Release positioning

This is ScienceDiscovery’s **first Beta release embracing the jiuwen-swarm backend**. It retains the scientific workbench experience, uses jiuwen-swarm for Agent execution, and integrates science-specific capabilities into the new architecture.

This issue collects community feedback on the release notes, scope, and blockers; **it is not a release announcement**. The previous version is `0.2.0`. The proposed version is **`0.3.0-beta.1` (to be confirmed)**, with development on `main` (the former JiuwenSwarm branch) and this release prepared from `releases/v0.3.0.beta`.

## Draft release notes

### Priority scenarios

This Beta focuses on four scientific workflows rather than migrating every historical capability or covering every corner case.

| Scenario | Workflow and deliverables | Domain documentation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Literature review | Search and retrieve literature, extract evidence, collaborate across specialists, and deliver a report with traceable citations | [Literature research tutorial](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/en/domains/literature-research.md) |
| Data analysis | Inspect data, prepare an environment, execute analysis, and deliver reproducible code, figures, and conclusions | [Sepsis data analysis tutorial](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/en/domains/analyze-sepsis-endotypes.md) |
| Antibody design | Combine domain Skills, specialized models, and scientific environments for design and screening; requires appropriate model resources and compute, and computational results do not constitute experimental validation | [Antibody design tutorial](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/en/domains/antibody-design.md) |
| Algorithm optimization | Generate, evaluate, and iterate on candidates through scientific-artifact RSI / Evolve, retaining results and execution records | [Evolve a solution tutorial](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md) |

### Core capabilities and improvements

- **Consistent JiuwenSwarm default**: source, Docker, and packaged launchers now select JiuwenSwarm by default, with an explicit native opt-out. Subagents default to platform `task` delegation with Swarm execution—not a complete switch to Swarm-native multi-agent orchestration.
- **Scientific environments and workspaces**: local/remote execution, managed environments, background tasks, file transfers, workspace handoffs, and artifact-version associations.
- **Memory graph**: research-task, file, and artifact relationships with traceable citations; source and Docker deployments provide local storage by default, with optional Neo4j.
- **Scientific Skills, MCP, and Specialists**: built-in capabilities and custom extensions for domain-expert collaboration.
- **Scientific-artifact RSI and Idea Tree**: iterative artifact optimization, candidate evaluation, and tree-based exploration of research ideas.
- **Observability and testing**: improved trajectories, subtask status, and diagnostics, alongside Mock E2E, real scientific benchmarks, and quality-evaluation records.
- **Documentation and onboarding**: reorganized English/Chinese documentation and tutorials for the four workflows, with explicit Swarm/native differences in context, planning, tools, and Skills.

These include migrations and enhancements of existing capabilities, not exclusively new features.

### Website, community, and delivery infrastructure (new in this release)

- **Unified public website**: the [website and installation hub](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/install/index.html) bring together installation guidance, documentation, and scientific workflow tutorials. Website content is kept in sync with `main`.
- **User communities**: **Slack** and **Feishu** groups have been established for international and China-based users respectively, supporting usage discussions, feedback, and community collaboration. See the repository homepage for joining instructions.
- **Daily CI for both branches**: daily quality checks cover `main` and `releases/v0.3.0.beta`. The scheduled main workflow triggers independent runs for both branches, retaining separate results, logs, and build artifacts to support development and release validation.
- **Multiple platforms and installation options**: Linux and macOS are supported, with Windows access through WSL 2. Options include source installation, Linux binary packages, and Docker. Availability and prerequisites vary by platform; see the [installation hub](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/install/index.html).

### Major fixes

- **Memory-graph query performance and memory use**: eliminate path explosion in folded queries, introduce shared paths and cumulative collection budgets for reproduced allocation failures, and return structured budget errors. Indexed session queries avoid scanning unrelated historical data (#212, fixes #210).
- **Consistent startup behavior**: align source defaults with Docker/packages, make CLI backend selection override `.env`, forward Swarm settings through Docker, and select E2E backends explicitly (#214).
- **Swarm/MCP isolation and recovery**: improve model/session/tool binding isolation, tool refresh, shared connections, and permission lifecycle (#173, #181, #182).
- **Subtask and remote-execution reliability**: improve admission queues, timeouts, cancellation, workspace handoffs, and subagent resumption; retry transient remote execution-status failures (#182, #187, #191).
- **Model output and event streams**: recover from output truncation without executing incomplete tool arguments, and improve tool-stream liveness and diagnostics (#190, #194).
- **Scientific data and delivery**: improve PDF validation, arXiv compatibility, artifact-version associations, UI state, snapshot scope, and cancellation diagnostics (#171, #180, #192, #179, #189, #193).

## Beta limitations and upgrade notes

- **Nightly Real E2E is not yet stable**: automated real-model E2E CI is still being stabilized. For now, acceptance of real scientific workflows relies on recorded local runs, identifying the tested commit, model, and configuration. Nightly results provide supplementary diagnostics, not standalone proof of release readiness. Skipped or quarantined cases are not passes; UT/ST/Mock E2E gates remain independent quality evidence.
- **Some installation paths are experimental**: macOS Docker and all Windows paths (including WSL 2 and Docker Desktop) have not been fully validated for Agent execution. Current prepackaged single-file binaries target Linux, not native macOS or Windows. Prefer source installation on macOS; Linux binaries/source installation on Windows run inside WSL 2. Consult the installation hub for platform-specific requirements and support boundaries.
- **Website versus release documentation**: the website follows main and may describe updates not yet included in this Beta. Use the release-branch documentation and final release notes for the exact behavior and limitations of this version.
- **Workflow acceptance and outcome limitations**: The four workflows are priority acceptance targets. Outcomes depend on the model, network, data sources, and compute. Having tests does not establish that all real scenarios pass reliably; release acceptance must use the final candidate.
- **Swarm setup and backend selection**: Before first using Swarm from source, run `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup`. Use `--no-jiuwenswarm` or `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXECUTOR=native` to retain the native loop.
- **Memory-graph upgrades and failure handling**: Upgrades preserve saved memory preferences; users who previously disabled memory must re-enable it in System Settings. Use `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_DATA_DIR` to retain an existing graph directory; data is not migrated automatically. Set `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_AVAILABLE=0` to skip the service. If this optional service fails to start, the launcher reports the cause and continues with memory disabled; correct the cause and restart.
- **External data-source limitations**: External-source failures, including arXiv 406/429 responses and queue timeouts, remain tracked in #208.

## Community feedback

Please comment on release positioning/versioning, missing features or fixes, blockers in the four workflows, and limitations that must appear in the final notes. Include configuration, reproduction steps, and logs for reported problems.

---

2026-09-29：补充官网、Slack/飞书社区、双分支每日 CI、多平台安装与相关边界说明。 / Added website, Slack/Feishu communities, dual-branch daily CI, installation options, and associated limitations.

# English version

## Positioning

ScienceDiscovery now has a [public website](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/) where visitors can learn about the research workspace, explore the home-page demo, and continue to the [installation page](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/install/index.html) and [documentation](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/docs/index.html). This issue expands on the website work mentioned in the [#213 Beta release-note draft](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/213).

This is a request for community feedback on the website's content, navigation, and onboarding experience. It is not a formal software release announcement, and the demo does not establish that every depicted workflow has passed live validation.

## Draft website launch notes

### Home page: understand and explore

- **Product overview and entry points**: the home page introduces the ScienceDiscovery research workflow, a quick Linux installation path, core capabilities, and links to installation and documentation.
- **An interactive demo that starts on its own**: the HTML demo presents a workbench-like interface. When it comes into view, a scripted literature-review workflow plays once. Visitors can follow the task, tool calls, and artifacts without taking any action, much like watching a short video.
- **Hands-on exploration**: visitors can choose another scripted scenario, replay it, click nodes, switch views, and adjust chart or structure controls. The scenarios illustrate literature research, Idea Tree, Evolve, the memory graph, and scientific data visualizations.

The demo uses scripted flows and illustrative data to show product capabilities. It does not run a live research task against the product backend, and its charts and structures are not experimental results.

### Installation page: choose a path for your environment

The [installation page](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/install/index.html) organizes options by Linux, macOS, and Windows and explains the prerequisites and steps for prebuilt Linux binaries, Docker, and source mode. It provides release downloads and SHA256 checksums, post-start checks, and links to the full deployment guide. Some platform paths are marked experimental. Consult the page for current prerequisites.

### Documentation: go deeper

The [documentation](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/docs/index.html) offers English and Chinese entry points, navigation, and full-text site search. Readers can explore getting started, core capabilities, domain guides, advanced setup, reference material, and developer documentation. The website builds these pages from the [ScienceDiscovery repository's `docs/` directory](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/tree/main/docs). Documentation content is maintained upstream. The website provides its presentation and navigation.

## Version relationship and usage notes

The website documentation follows the product repository's `main` branch and may describe changes that are not part of a particular release. Download links on the installation page can also change as the site is updated. Check the [installation page](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/install/index.html) and [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/releases) for the versions available when you visit. For the behavior and limitations of a specific release, use its release notes and version-specific documentation.

## Community feedback

We welcome feedback on whether the home-page demo communicates the product clearly, which interactions or descriptions could be misleading, how easy it is to find an installation path and its prerequisites, and any gaps in documentation navigation, search, or English and Chinese content. For a page issue, please include its URL, browser, and steps to reproduce.

# 中文版

## 定位

ScienceDiscovery 现已提供[公开网站](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/)：访客可以先了解科研工作台、观看并操作首页演示，再前往[安装页](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/install/index.html) 和[文档页](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/docs/index.html)开始使用。这是软件的展示与入门入口，也是 [#213 Beta Release Note 草案](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/213) 中提到的网站配套工作的详细说明。

本 issue 征求社区对网站内容、导航和入门体验的反馈，不是软件正式发布公告，也不代表演示中的每个流程都已通过实际运行验收。

## 网站说明草案

### 首页：从了解产品到动手探索

- **产品介绍与入口**：首页概述 ScienceDiscovery 的科研工作流程，提供 Linux 快速安装入口、核心能力介绍，以及安装和文档链接。
- **自动播放的交互演示**：首页中的 HTML 演示呈现工作台界面。当演示区域进入视野时，预设的文献调研流程会自动播放一次，即使访客不操作，也能像观看短片一样了解任务推进、工具调用和产物呈现。
- **由访客操作**：访客可以选择其他预设场景并观看相应流程，也可以重新播放，或在场景中点击节点、切换视图、调整图表与结构参数。场景涵盖文献调研、Idea Tree、Evolve、记忆图谱及科研数据可视化等。

演示使用预设脚本和示意数据来呈现产品能力，不是连接真实后端的在线科研任务，图表和结构也不是实验结果。

### 安装页：按环境选择路径

[安装页](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/install/index.html) 按 Linux、macOS 和 Windows 展示可选路径，分别说明预编译 Linux 二进制、Docker 和源码运行的适用条件与步骤。页面提供发行包下载及 SHA256 校验值、启动后的检查方式，并链接到更完整的部署指南。部分平台路径标为实验性，具体前置条件应以安装页为准。

### 文档页：深入使用与查阅

[文档页](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/docs/index.html) 提供中英文入口、目录导航与站内全文搜索，可继续阅读快速开始、核心能力、领域教程、进阶配置、参考资料和开发文档。这些内容由网站从 [ScienceDiscovery 主仓库的 `docs/` 目录](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/tree/main/docs) 构建而来，文档正文在主仓库维护；网站仓库负责呈现和导航。

## 版本关系与使用提示

网站文档跟随主仓库 `main` 更新，因此可能描述尚未进入某个已发布版本的内容。安装页的下载入口也会随网站维护而变化，请以访问时的[安装页](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/install/index.html) 和 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/releases) 确认可下载版本。特定版本的行为与限制，以对应的发行说明和版本文档为准。

## 社区反馈

欢迎反馈：首页演示是否清楚地传达产品能力、哪些交互或说明容易造成误解、安装路径与前置条件是否容易找到，以及文档导航、搜索或中英文内容有哪些不足。如反馈页面问题，请附页面链接、浏览器和复现步骤。
