oldest.body:
## Context

Since July 2026 an open-source "science workbench" category has formed, triggered by Anthropic's Claude Science launch (2026-06-30). Three direct open-source alternatives appeared the same week and are now at scale: [synthetic-sci/openscience](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience) (~3.6K★), [aipoch/open-science](https://github.com/aipoch/open-science) (~4.2K★), and [ai4s-research/open-science](https://github.com/ai4s-research/open-science) (~1.7K★). Having compared ScienceDiscovery against them (and against the autonomous-scientist systems: Sakana AI-Scientist, InternScience/InternAgent + MLEvolve), here is a strengths/gaps assessment in the hope it helps prioritization. Facts below are from public repo data collected 2026-09-15.

## Strengths (keep — and communicate)

1. **Sandbox-first security model.** Fail-closed Bubblewrap/Seatbelt execution, operator-scoped NPU chip passthrough, opt-in Broker with fixed entry points and `shell: false`. None of the three competitors communicates a default-isolation story; the highest-engagement technical question on a competitor's launch thread was literally *"are the skills executed within a secure, containerized sandbox by default, or does the user manage isolation?"* — this repo already answers that question, but almost nobody knows it does.
2. **Provenance depth.** CAS with pinned-asset drift rejection, review checks, cross-session/SubAgent citation chains. The strongest provenance story in the category.
3. **Search-camp RSI engine.** The evolve sidecar (flat-PUCT tree + OpenEvolve MAP-Elites, discriminability probe, explicit "no model training, no search-rule modification") is a clean, honest scope with a real cousin in [InternScience/MLEvolve](https://github.com/InternScience/MLEvolve) (#1 on MLE-Bench).
4. **Ascend NPU path.** 910B sandbox passthrough + allowlisted workloads (Protenix/MindScience) is unique in the category and extends machine-verifiable research to device-scale workloads.
5. **Engineering discipline beyond repo age.** Bilingual doc set, CI tiers (UT/ST/mocked E2E), self-documented limitations (e.g., Idea Tree scores are model judgments, not experimental evidence).

## Gaps (ordered by leverage)

1. **Installation/onboarding.** No binaries in Releases — #1 (open since 08-19, rated 1/5) is the only organic user feedback this repo has received, and it is someone who *could not install the product*. All three competitors ship desktop installers and a <10-minute quickstart. This pairs directly with the first-experience goal in #22.
2. **No community surface.** All merged PRs are bots; there are zero human external PRs. For comparison: aipoch merges 6+ human PRs/day; ai4s-research power users file bugs *and* land the fixes (e.g., their stall-guard for looping agents came from a user). A "good first issue" ladder + a contributor guide + weekly maintainer RFC triage would start the flywheel.
3. **Category invisibility + an unverifiable benchmark claim.** 58★ vs 1.7–4.2K for peers; one promotion event found (Sina Finance 2026-08-16) whose headline claim (BiomniBench-DA "业界SOTA") is dual-claimed by aipoch's README badge on the same benchmark. Without published methodology/splits, the claim reads as marketing and hurts credibility with scientists — either publish the eval or drop the superlative.
4. **Adoption levers validated by competitors, still missing here:** headless CLI / task API (repeated cross-repo demand — researchers want CI and agent-to-agent use, not only a GUI), model-provider onboarding (subscription reuse, connectivity-test friction), Windows parity.
5. **Cross-model skill consistency.** The single most-validated complaint in the category: *"one flag switches the model, not whether the skill actually works"* (prompts tuned on one model degrade on smaller/local models). A per-skill model-compatibility matrix or a cross-model smoke-test suite for the 300+ skills would directly differentiate.

## Suggested next steps

- [ ] Ship Linux binaries + a 10-minute quickstart (pairs with #22)
- [ ] Publish evolve/idea-tree efficiency metrics (per-node token cost, CAS reuse rate, surviving-node quality on an independent benchmark) — the pruning+reuse efficiency story is genuinely differentiating and no competitor tells it
- [ ] Benchmark-claim triage: methodology for BiomniBench-DA or remove the SOTA wording
- [ ] Community ladder: CONTRIBUTING good-first-issues + a maintainer-reserved RFC-triage day

Happy to help flesh any of these out.
oldest.title: [Feedback] Strengths and gaps vs. the 2026 open-source science-workbench landscape

oldest.author: Birfy
oldest.body:
## Summary

Both long-running engines — the evolution search and the Idea Tree — can be **started** from the command line but cannot be **observed, controlled, or stopped** from it. Their progress is designed to land on a frontend card, so a terminal user gets a run id and then nothing. I would like `evolve` and `idea` subcommands that reuse the HTTP endpoints the Web UI already calls.

## What happens today

Starting works. `ScienceDiscovery run "/evolve-design --algorithm puct …"` reaches the same control plane as the browser, the agent loads the `evolve-design` skill, and it calls `create_evolve_run`. Then the turn ends — deliberately. The tool's own result text instructs the model:

> The search runs for minutes to hours and its card streams live progress on its own — do not wait for it here, and do not poll `get_evolve_run`.

`create_idea_research` says the same thing:

> After success, report the handoff and end this turn; the existing tree card streams progress. Do not poll or start another research to wait for completion.

That is the right call for the agent loop — polling would burn the budget the search itself needs. But it means **the card is the only progress surface**, and the CLI has no equivalent. `ScienceDiscovery run` prints `Search created: <uuid>` and exits while the search keeps running server-side for hours.

`services/launcher/src/cli-options.ts` has no evolve or idea-tree subcommand and no related flag. So from a terminal today you cannot:

- list the searches or researches that exist;
- see how far one has got;
- fetch a candidate;
- stop one, or pause and resume it.

The only workaround is starting another `run` in the same session and hoping the model calls `get_evolve_run` / `get_idea_research` — a whole model turn spent reading a status field, using tools whose descriptions explicitly tell the model not to poll them.

## The endpoints already exist

The Web UI drives all of this over plain HTTP:

**Evolve**
- `GET /api/evolve/runs`
- `GET /api/evolve/runs/<id>/events?after=<cursor>`
- `GET /api/evolve/runs/<id>/candidates/<codeHash>`
- `POST /api/evolve/runs/<id>/stop`

**Idea Tree**
- `GET /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/research`
- `POST /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/research` — `pause`, `continue`, `stop`, `defaults`
- `GET /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/research/<rid>/events`
- `GET /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/graph`

## The client plumbing also already exists

`services/launcher/src/control-plane-client.ts` has an authenticated generic `request<T>(path, init)` and `subscribeRunEvents()`, a working SSE consumer that "mirrors the Web frontend's `subscribeRunEvents`: fetch with `accept: text/event-stream`, split frames". The launcher also already resolves the bearer token from the data directory. A `watch` subcommand is that SSE reader pointed at a different path — this is wiring, not new infrastructure.

## Proposal

```
ScienceDiscovery evolve list
ScienceDiscovery evolve get <run-id> [--candidate <hash>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve watch <run-id>
ScienceDiscovery evolve stop <run-id>

ScienceDiscovery idea list --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea get <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea watch <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea pause|continue|stop <research-id> --session <id>
```

Conventions, matching what `run` already does:

- **text on a TTY, JSONL when piped.** `run` already switches output mode this way; these commands should not invent a second convention.
- **`watch` resumes rather than replays.** The evolve event endpoint already takes `?after=<cursor>`; a dropped connection should continue from the last event seen.
- **Token and data-dir handling identical to `run`** — sharing a `--data-dir` with `serve` should mean no extra configuration.

One asymmetry to decide: evolve exposes only `stop`, while Idea Tree has `pause` / `continue` / `stop`. Either the CLI mirrors each engine's real capabilities, or evolve gains pause/resume — worth an explicit choice rather than an accident.

## Why it matters

- **Unattended and batch use.** Starting a search from a job script is pointless if the same script cannot poll it, stop it when a budget is spent, or collect the winning candidate.
- **Headless and remote machines.** On a workstation reached over SSH there is no browser to hold the card open. Today that machine can start a multi-hour search it cannot then observe.
- **Consistency.** The CLI is already positioned as the scriptable twin of the Web UI; the two most expensive operations in the product are exactly the ones it cannot drive.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Evolve searches and Idea Tree researches can be listed, inspected, watched, and stopped from the CLI.
- [ ] `watch` streams live and resumes from a cursor after a dropped connection.
- [ ] Output follows the existing TTY/pipe convention, so `| jq` works.
- [ ] No new authentication path: the token comes from the data directory as `run` already does.
- [ ] Commands and options appear in `help` and in the CLI reference.
- [ ] Stopping from the CLI has the same effect as stopping from the UI card.

## Open questions

- Should `run` gain an optional `--wait` that blocks until a started engine finishes? Useful in scripts, but these runs last hours — probably better served by `watch`.
- Should `watch` exit non-zero when the run ends in failure, so a script can branch on it?
- Does `evolve list` need session/project scoping, given `GET /api/evolve/runs` is global today?

Related: [#30](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/30) (introduce the CLI in the README) — that issue is about making the CLI discoverable; this one is about the two workflows it cannot reach.
oldest.title: [Feature] CLI subcommands for the long-running engines — evolve and Idea Tree

## Summary

ScienceDiscovery can already evolve the things a user brings it — a program, a prompt, a protocol. It cannot evolve **itself**. I would like RSI support: given a dataset of tasks, search over the agent's own harness — system prompt fragments, specialist instructions, skill methodology, tool and skill selection — score each variant by running it against that dataset, and surface the winner for a human to adopt.

The search machinery for this already exists in `services/evolve`. What is missing is the candidate being the harness, the evaluation being an agent run, and a reviewed promotion step.

## What is already there

This is deliberately an extension, not a new engine.

- **The search sidecar**, `services/evolve`, runs on `agentdescent>=0.4.6` — `evolve()` / `async_evolve()`, `FlatPuct`, the ledger, the verifier and the policies — behind two engines: flat-PUCT tree search (`puct_engine.py`) and MAP-Elites islands with ring migration (`openevolve_engine.py`).
- **Non-program candidates are first class.** `text_candidate.py` exists precisely because "a prompt or an abstract has no docstring", and `judge_domain.py` states its purpose plainly: it "is what makes `/evolve` work on things that are not programs over tables: a prompt, an abstract, a protocol, a plan". Evolving prompt text is not a new capability — it is the existing one pointed at a different file.
- **Four scoring seams**, already cut: `scorecard_domain` (a metric over a dataset), `test_gate_domain` (a suite's pass rate), `script_domain` (a scorer the drafting model writes), `judge_domain` (a rubric read by a model).
- **Anti-reward-hacking is already solved once.** `test_gate_domain` freezes in two layers — a proposal filter over `frozen` globs in the prompt, and enforcement below it — with the upstream note this issue should quote rather than restate: *"without it the shortest path to a high score is to weaken the thing measuring it."* That is the single most important property RSI needs, and the pattern is in the tree.
- **Held-out splitting exists.** `create_evolve_run` already accepts `caseSplit` with `gateGroups`, `rolloutGroups` and `testGroups`, which is the shape needed to keep a harness from overfitting the tasks it was tuned on.
- **Trajectories are recorded.** `packages/trajectory` captures per-session entries with the context blocks that were actually sent, which is the raw material for judging whether a harness change helped.
- **Parts of the harness are already frozen.** Built-in specialists reject edits to `instructions` / `description` / `name` / `connectorIds` / `enabledSkillIds`; only `enabled` is user-mutable. RSI has to open that door deliberately rather than by accident.

## What is missing

1. **The candidate is never the harness.** Today a candidate is one text-shaped artifact the user owns. The agent's own scaffolding lives elsewhere and is not reachable by a search: prompt assembly (`packages/context/src/prompt-renderer.ts`, `assembler.ts`), specialist instructions (`packages/specialist/src/builtins.ts`), skill methodology (`skills/*/SKILL.md`), and the skill/connector selection for a run.

2. **There is no task-dataset scoring mode.** `scorecard_domain` scores a *program* over a table. RSI needs to score a *harness* over a set of tasks, where each evaluation is a full agent run with its own tool calls, sandboxed execution and artifacts. That is a different cost class and needs its own domain.

3. **There is no promotion path.** An improved harness must be diffable, reviewable, versioned and revertible. Nothing should ever be self-applied.

## Proposal

### 1. A harness candidate

A bundle rather than a single blob: prompt fragments, one or more specialist instruction sets, selected skills, and the run settings that go with them. The mutation prompt sees the bundle and rewrites part of it; the ledger records which part changed, so a win is attributable to something specific.

### 2. A `task_dataset` domain

A dataset entry is a task plus whatever the existing four modes need to score its outcome — a metric, a test suite, a scoring script, or a rubric. Evaluating one candidate means running the agent over the split and aggregating. Reuse `caseSplit` so the reported number comes from tasks the search did not tune against.

The honest problem here is cost: one candidate equals N agent runs, each with model calls and sandboxed execution. The design needs a budget per generation and an early-abandon policy, not just a score.

### 3. Freeze the things a self-improving search must not touch

Same two-layer shape `test_gate_domain` already uses, with a wider frozen set:

- the task dataset and its expected outcomes;
- the scorer, whichever mode it is;
- the permission, sandbox and approval layers — a harness that scores better by asking for fewer confirmations is not better;
- the evolve sidecar's own code and the freeze list itself.

A candidate that edits any of these is rejected at the proposal filter, not merely penalized.

### 4. Promotion is a human step

The winner lands as a reviewable proposal: a diff against the current harness, the score with its held-out number, and the trajectory evidence behind it. Adoption is explicit, versioned and revertible. The skill review flow and the built-in specialists' read-only rules already establish that shape; RSI should reuse it rather than invent a second one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A search can take the agent's harness as its candidate, not only a user artifact.
- [ ] A task dataset can be supplied, and a candidate is scored by running the agent over it.
- [ ] The reported score comes from a held-out split.
- [ ] The dataset, the scorer, and the permission/sandbox layers are frozen against modification by the search, enforced at the proposal filter.
- [ ] An improved harness appears as a reviewable, versioned proposal and is never self-applied.
- [ ] Reverting to the previous harness is one action.
- [ ] A run states its budget and stops at it.

## Open questions

- Should a run evolve one specialist at a time, or the whole bundle? One at a time attributes wins more cleanly; the whole bundle can find interactions.
- Where does a task dataset live — a repository artifact, a workspace file, or a first-class store object?
- Which engine fits better? PUCT refines one starting point; OpenEvolve's islands keep diversity, which may matter more when a prompt change can be good in one dimension and harmful in another.
- What is the minimum dataset size where a win is believable rather than noise, given the non-determinism the judge mode already documents?
- Should this reuse `/evolve-design`'s checkpointed design conversation, or have its own entry point?

Related: [#50](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/50) — the engines can be started but not observed or stopped from the CLI, which matters more for a search whose evaluations are full agent runs.
oldest.title: [Feature] RSI — evolve the agent's own harness against a task dataset, reusing the agentdescent search

### Scope

A layer JiuwenSwarm does not have at all. Extract the existing TS packages (`artifact-manager`, `cas`, `provenance`, `workspace`) into a standalone service, with the adapter as reverse proxy.

### Dependencies

**Prerequisites:**

- #87 Adapter core: auth, connection pool, run and event log, storage and proxy framework: reverse proxy framework

- #97 Science toolset as MCP: artifact ingestion is triggered by tool results

**Depended on by:**

- #101 idea-tree service

- #106 Cross-domain wrap-up: workbench search, dead code cleanup, packaging and startup

### Interface list

32 in total: standalone backend 32. **0 need wrapper adaptation (approximate mapping + adapter-implemented).**

| Method | Path | Handling | Target | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/sessions/:id/workspace/provenance` | standalone backend | artifact/provenance service | File provenance |
| GET | `/api/cas/:sha256` | standalone backend | artifact/provenance service | CAS blob read |
| GET | `/api/projects/:id/artifacts` | standalone backend | artifact service |  |
| DELETE | `/api/projects/:id/artifacts/:artifactId` | standalone backend | artifact service |  |

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claim-Id: dae5b8d1b8af4de3885faca176d3c50a
Branch: dev2/fix/cas-has-corrupt-object
Base: ad34dd7847f6
At: 2026-10-29T05:08:29Z

## What is wrong

`CasStore.has()` in `packages/cas/src/index.ts:74-82` answers the boolean existence question by calling `read()`. `read()` re-hashes the bytes and throws `CAS integrity failure` when a stored object no longer matches its digest, and `has()` only maps `ENOENT` to `false` (`:79`), so a corrupt object makes `has()` throw. Its sibling `verify()` (`:84-92`) deliberately maps the same condition to `false`. Two predicates over the same store therefore disagree: `verify()` says "not valid", `has()` raises.

## Reproduction (live main `ad34dd7847`, file blob `584cf1eaefc7ec9b5c4c2125de7bf13c39039ba0`)

```
$ node --import tsx -e '<put "hello world" via CasStore, then overwrite the blob with "HELLO WORLD">'
put -> b94d27b9934d 11
has before -> true
verify after corruption -> false
has after corruption -> THREW CAS integrity failure
```

The overwrite keeps the byte length, so this is exactly the "same size, different bytes" corruption case the store already detects elsewhere.

## Expected

`has(hash)` is a total boolean predicate: `true` only when the object is present and valid, `false` when it is missing **or corrupt** - the same answer `verify()` gives. A caller deciding "is this object still usable, or must I republish?" must not have to catch an untyped integrity error to find out.

## Why it matters

The store is used as a cache in front of publication paths (`put` / `retain` / republish decisions): those call `has()` to choose between "reuse" and "write it again". With a corrupt blob they crash with `CAS integrity failure` instead of taking the republish branch, and the error is thrown from a method whose contract is a boolean. PR `#657` made vanished refs republish; corrupt bytes are the neighbouring case and still have this shape.

## Fix scope

Extend the `has()` catch to map the integrity failure to `false` the way `verify()` already does (about two lines), plus one test next to the existing `index.test.ts` cases. No new dependency, no behaviour change for a valid or a missing object.

## Summary

Biomni real E2E shows large endpoint-dependent variation in model-request latency and total generation time. Earlier runs through an OpenAI-compatible relay also ended after a terminal model turn with no text or tool call. We need enough safe wire-level diagnostics to tell an upstream empty completion from an SSE/parser defect, and to separate model/API latency from agent work.

This is distinct from #232, which records explicit HTTP 500/503 gateway errors.

## Local measurements

The two Biomni cases were run in parallel on the same Windows/WSL machine, with evaluation disabled, the `task` tool removed (no subagents), and no Jina key. `generation` is the benchmark's generation duration; request timing is the elapsed time of completed `[model-stream]` requests in `stack.log`. All rows below passed delivery. The relay run used `https://yibuapi.com/v1` with model alias `deepseek-v4.1-flash`; the direct runs used `https://api.deepseek.com` with model alias `deepseek-flash`.

| Case | Endpoint / runs | Generation | Completed model requests | Median request | Reported total tokens |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DA-13-3 | relay, r5 | 37.46 min | 71 | 25.16 s | 504,634 |
| DA-13-3 | direct, r6/r7/r9/r10 | 5.71–20.67 min | 26–44 | 6.10–13.93 s | 118,066–140,022 |
| DA-14-1 | relay, r5 | 31.31 min | 63 | 20.18 s | 177,043 |
| DA-14-1 | direct, r6/r9/r10 | 20.75–35.79 min | 54–72 | 11.59–19.01 s | 191,883–284,635 |

The seven direct samples all passed delivery, with zero reported SSE parse errors or SSE error records. Earlier local relay samples had a normalized final model turn with empty text, no tool call, and `finish_reason=stop`, after which the run was marked completed without the expected deliverable. Those older samples did **not** retain raw SSE records, so they cannot establish whether the upstream service sent an empty completion or the local stream adapter lost content. The direct samples also used a local empty-turn guard and SSE parsing fixes, so the passing rate is **not** an isolated endpoint A/B result.

## Why the current evidence is insufficient

- The relay and direct runs used different model aliases. The model's chosen steps, request counts, and token totals varied substantially, so total-duration differences are not an estimate of API latency alone.
- Even with the same direct endpoint, DA-13-3 varied from 5.71 to 20.67 minutes, and DA-14-1 from 20.75 to 35.79 minutes. Agent behavior and task content remain major contributors.
- A normalized empty final turn does not reveal whether the wire response was empty, malformed, or incorrectly mapped locally.

## Requested investigation / acceptance criteria

1. Save privacy-safe per-request diagnostics in real E2E artifacts: endpoint identity and model alias, request ID, HTTP status, dispatch/headers/first byte/first SSE record/completion timestamps, SSE record and parse-error counts, final content/tool-call presence, `finish_reason`, and retry/error classification. Do not save credentials or prompt/response bodies in the default diagnostic log.
2. Treat an empty terminal assistant turn with no tool call as an error rather than a successful final answer. Preserve the upstream request ID and framing summary when this occurs.
3. Compare relay and direct endpoints with the same model, request body, workload, and concurrency. Report per-request latency distributions separately from total agent duration and token use.
4. In CI summaries, identify explicit provider failures, empty completions, and local parse/mapping failures separately from research-quality failures.

I can provide the local benchmark metrics and sanitized `[model-stream]`/`[model-sse-summary]` excerpts if useful. No API keys or prompt contents are included here.
recent.title: [Bug] perf(model): investigate endpoint-dependent Biomni latency and empty terminal turns

## 背景 / 输入

NatureBench 复现会话开启 Automatic review（`reviewerAutomaticReviewEnabled=true`，`reviewMode=auto`，specialist=`quick`）。

- 第一轮 run 结束后主交付（4 实例真实 `predictions.npy`）**缺失**，报告写 blocked
- Artifact：`REPRODUCTION_REPORT.md` 触发 `reviewer_checkpoint` → **PASSED / ACCEPT_AND_PROCEED**，findings 空
- 审阅 JSON 仅 citation 类 check（与文献 case 的 Quick 行为一致，参见 #414）
- 续跑产出真实 cl3/cl5/mop_sc npy 并改写报告后，**未自动重审**；磁盘上旧 ACCEPT 仍对应「blocked」叙事

## 问题是什么

1. **交付物缺失仍 ACCEPT**：复现任务的成功标准是 `output/{instance}/predictions.npy`，Quick 几乎只看 citation 格式，拦不住「没复现成功」。
2. **报告/审阅不同步**：工件已更新，Automatic review 不因新版本自动失效或重跑；用户看到的仍是过期 ACCEPT。

## 我们怎么规避的

- 不以 review ACCEPT 作为复现成功判据；宿主侧用 numpy 核对 npy shape / K，并手改 `REPRODUCTION_REPORT.md` 写清真实现状。
- 体验结论单独记录，不依赖审阅绿勾。

## 期望应该是什么样

1. 复现 / 计算类报告：Quick 之外至少校验「声明的交付路径是否存在、非空」；缺失则 **不能** ACCEPT_AND_PROCEED。
2. Artifact 新版本落盘后：旧 review 标记 stale，或自动触发重审；UI 明确「审阅对应的是哪一版」。
3. 与 #414（文献 claim fidelity）区分但可共用：按 artifact 类型选审查准则，而不是一律 citation-only。

## 相关

- #414 Bug: Quick automatic review accepts literature reports on citation format only

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claim-Id: 887ec7de37ba4023a1cc05f9ad23111f
Branch: dev2/fix/xlsx-1900-serial-epoch
Base: 1e8865838ce8
At: 2026-10-29T04:59:33Z

## What is wrong

`apps/desktop/src/app/xlsx.ts:170` fixes the 1900 date-system epoch at `Date.UTC(1899, 11, 30)` and `serialToText` (`:173-183`) applies it to every serial. The 1899-12-30 epoch is the compensation for Excel's fictitious 1900-02-29 and is only correct from serial 61 on; for serial 1-59 it lands one day early, so every date from 1900-01-01 to 1900-02-28 is displayed one day before the day Excel shows.

## Reproduction (live main `1e8865838ce80b8519063e26b5910a5b23ff2027`, Node v22.23.2)

A mock workbook built with `fflate`, `styles.xml` carrying `numFmtId="14"`, column A holding the serials below, read back through `readWorkbook`:

```
$ node --input-type=module -e '<mock workbook + readWorkbook, serials 1, 59, 60, 61, 45292>'
[["1899-12-31"],["1900-02-27"],["1900-02-28"],["1900-03-01"],["2024-01-01"]]
```

Expected (the Excel 1900 date system): serial `1` -> `1900-01-01`, `59` -> `1900-02-28`, `61` -> `1900-03-01`, `45292` -> `2024-01-01`. Serial `60` is Excel's non-existent 1900-02-29.

## Expected

Serials below 61 are counted from 1899-12-31 and serials from 61 on keep the 1899-12-30 epoch, i.e. a per-serial epoch (about five lines in `serialToText`). The 1904 date system branch is unaffected.

## Why it matters

Spreadsheet cells formatted as dates are one of the two things this preview exists for; silently shifting a whole two-month window in 1900 is a wrong answer with no visible error, and the same helper backs the cell text in the grid.

## Fix scope

One conditional epoch inside `serialToText`; a regression test in `apps/desktop/tests/xlsx.test.ts` (9/9 green today, no coverage for these serials). No new dependency.

## Problem
PR #460 isolates the embedded JiuwenSwarm default local runtime under `$HOME/.sciencediscovery/jiuwenswarm` and documents Docker’s persisted HOME layout. Local coexistence was verified; the **Docker persisted-volume restart** journey was **BLOCKED** (no container engine/socket on the author host) and remains an explicit leftover acceptance item on #257 / #460.

## Expected
After a container restart that keeps the documented persisted volume, ScienceDiscovery’s embedded Swarm registry, workspaces, and related runtime state remain under the SD-owned layout, still isolated from any standalone Swarm data, and SD continues to use its own instance endpoints without adopting a sibling standalone instance.

## Verification cases

1. **Docker volume restart persistence**
   - **Preconditions:** Container-capable host; ScienceDiscovery Docker path with persisted volume as documented after #460; disposable standalone Swarm data available to prove non-interference if co-tested.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Start SD via the Docker path; record embedded registry/workspace identity and a distinguishing config marker.
     2. Restart the container with the same persisted volume.
     3. Confirm SD still binds to the same embedded instance data and does not read/write standalone Swarm registry/config.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Persisted SD state survives restart; isolation from standalone Swarm holds; no silent reconnect to another Swarm service.

## Context
- Env: Author host for #460 lacked container engine/socket; residual Docker journey _not provided_ here beyond that BLOCKED note.
- Refs: Parent #257; fixing PR #460 (merged). Local default-namespace isolation landed in #460; this Issue tracks Docker restart verification only.
recent.title: [Bug] Verify Docker persisted-volume restart for embedded JiuwenSwarm after #460

recent.author: HongyeZhou
recent.body:
## Problem
PR #460 delivered default local namespace isolation for embedded JiuwenSwarm. The product decision on #257 requires a **complete config/runtime boundary**, not only a renamed default directory: SD must not silently adopt standalone Swarm configuration via inherited env vars, home/registry lookup, or runtime service discovery, and must not let port collision silently attach SD to another Swarm service.

## Expected
- Embedded Swarm config and state are owned by ScienceDiscovery; discovering a user’s standalone Swarm (including same instance name) must not replace or merge SD’s model/skill/agent/tool behavior.
- Outer-process Swarm-specific environment variables, default SDK paths, and service discovery must not bypass the SD-owned boundary unless the user explicitly configured an SD-supported override with clear ownership.
- setup/start/status/env/stop, logs, and connection endpoints resolve to the same SD-owned instance; port conflicts are handled without silently connecting to a sibling Swarm.

## Verification cases

1. **Standalone config does not drive SD**
   - **Preconditions:** Disposable home/namespace; standalone Swarm instance (including same name `sciencediscovery`) with deliberately different identifiable config.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Start ScienceDiscovery with default embedded settings.
     2. Change standalone model/skill/agent settings and start/stop the standalone instance.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** SD behavior and backend ownership remain SD’s; standalone changes do not alter SD settings or which instance SD uses.

2. **Env / discovery bypass**
   - **Preconditions:** Outer environment carries standalone Swarm-specific variables and/or occupied ports that could point at a non-SD instance.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Launch SD without an explicit user opt-in to that standalone endpoint.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** SD does not silently read standalone registry/config or connect to the foreign service; conflicts surface safely rather than mis-binding.

3. **SD lifecycle leaves standalone intact**
   - **Preconditions:** Both SD embedded and standalone instances live in the disposable namespace.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Run SD setup/start/stop and change SD settings.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Standalone registry/config/sessions remain unmodified and the standalone process is not stopped by SD lifecycle.

## Context
- Env: Evidence from #257 product decision comment (`embedded-swarm-isolation-decision`) and #460 partial scope (local isolation done; broader boundary still called out).
- Refs: Parent #257; fixing PR #460 (merged). Default path isolation landed in #460; this Issue tracks remaining boundary / env / discovery acceptance from that decision.
- Notes: Do not auto-migrate or delete ambiguous standalone data. Explicit SD-supported overrides remain allowed when ownership is clear.
recent.title: [Bug] Embedded JiuwenSwarm must not adopt standalone config via env or discovery

## Summary

The desktop source viewer closes a triple-quoted string on the first `"""` that follows an odd *or even* number of backslashes. An even count does not escape the delimiter, so a legal, terminated string swallows the rest of the file: every following line is tokenised as `string`.

## Repro (live main `1e886583`)

Node v22.23.2, from the repository root:

```bash
cat > /tmp/t1.ts <<'TS'
import { highlightPython } from "./apps/desktop/src/app/python-source.ts";
const src = 'x = """a\\\\"""\ny = 2\n';
highlightPython(src).forEach((l, i) => console.log(i + 1, JSON.stringify(l)));
TS
node --import tsx /tmp/t1.ts
```

Observed:

```
1 [{"text":"x = "},{"kind":"string","text":"\"\"\"a\\\\\"\"\""}]
2 [{"kind":"string","text":"y = 2"}]
```

Expected: line 2 carries no `string` token, because `"""a\\"""` is a complete Python string (`\\` is one escaped backslash, so the delimiter is unescaped) and `y = 2` is code.

## Cause

`apps/desktop/src/app/python-source.ts:130-132`:

```ts
// An escaped delimiter is part of the string, not its end.
while (end > 0 && source[end - 1] === "\\") end = source.indexOf(delimiter, end + 1);
```

The test is "a backslash precedes the delimiter", not "an odd number of backslashes precedes it". `"""a\\"""` has two, so the real terminator is skipped and scanning resumes at the next `"""` — or at end of file, which is the failure above.

## Expected fix

Count the run of `\\` before the candidate and only skip when the count is odd (~5 lines, same function).

## Suggested red test

`apps/desktop/tests/python-source.test.ts` (exists; 8 tests, none covers an escaped backslash before a delimiter) — `a triple-quoted string ending in an escaped backslash does not swallow the code after it`:

```ts
const lines = highlightPython('x = """a\\\\"""\ny = 2\n');
assert.equal(lines[1]?.some((token) => token.kind === "string"), false);
```

```bash
node --import tsx --test apps/desktop/tests/python-source.test.ts
```

## Dedupe

Searched open+closed for `highlightPython`, `triple-quoted string view`, `"source view" python`: 0 hits. `#537` (closed) added highlighting to the web artifact preview, a different module.

Filed by ScienceDiscovery Product.
recent.title: [Bug] Desktop Python source view colours the rest of the file as a string after a triple-quoted string ending in \\

Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claim-Id: 8a1b7dbd95c149489c75d01defcd079d
Branch: dev1/fix/fetch-document-codepoint-truncation
Base: 1e8865838ce8
At: 2026-10-29T04:57:48Z

## What is wrong

`document()` in `packages/data-source/src/web/native/fetch.ts:105-107` truncates the vendor's text with a raw `slice(0, 4_096)`, so a UTF-16 surrogate pair that straddles the budget is cut in half and the document handed to the model ends with a lone high surrogate.

## Reproduction (live main `1e8865838ce80b8519063e26b5910a5b23ff2027`)

`renderExaContents`/`renderTavilyExtract` both funnel through `document()`. Same logic copied verbatim, run with `node`:

```
$ node -e 'const MAX=4096; const text="x".repeat(MAX-1)+"😀"; console.log(JSON.stringify(text.slice(0,MAX).slice(-2)))'
"\ud83d"
```

The last code unit is `0xd83d` (high surrogate) with no low surrogate after it - an unpaired surrogate in the fetched document.

## Expected

Truncate at a code-point boundary, the way `#663` now does it for the artifact preview: drop the whole character instead of half of it, so the result is never longer than the budget and never contains a new unpaired surrogate.

## Why it matters

`web_fetch` output is fed back into prompts and can be cached and re-serialised as JSON; an unpaired surrogate is invalid UTF-8 text and `JSON.stringify` escapes it into a `\ud83d` sequence the model reads as a broken glyph. The same defect was reported for the artifact preview in `#660` and fixed there by `#663`; this call site is a different module (`packages/data-source/src/web/native/fetch.ts`) and is still raw, so this is not a duplicate.

## Fix scope

One small helper in the same file (or reuse of an existing code-point truncation helper if one is exported) plus its call in `document()`; tests next to the existing `renderExaContents`/`renderTavilyExtract` ones. About 10-15 lines, no new dependency.
recent.title: [Bug] web_fetch document truncation splits a surrogate pair at the 4096-char budget

Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claim-Id: e973d679f15d40cb95aa52543bc510b2
Branch: dev2/fix/html-entity-single-pass
Base: 1e8865838ce8
At: 2026-10-29T04:56:50Z

## What is wrong

`decodeEntities` in `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:35-43` decodes in a loop over the `ENTITIES` table (`:25-33`), feeding each replacement's output into the next one, and the table starts with `&`. Escaped markup therefore decodes twice: `&lt;` becomes `<` and then `<`, `&amp;` becomes `&`. The numeric-reference branch (`:39-42`) accepts the whole `1 .. 0x10FFFF` range, so UTF-16 surrogate code points survive as lone surrogates.

## Reproduction (live main `1e8865838ce80b8519063e26b5910a5b23ff2027`)

The two functions copied verbatim from that blob, run with `node` (no dependencies):

```
$ node -e '...decodeEntities copied verbatim...'
"&lt;" -> "<"
"&amp;" -> "&"
"'" -> "'"
"'" -> "'"
"�" -> "\ud800"
" &lt;" -> " <"
```

## Expected

- One pass: every reference is consumed once and its output is not rescanned, so `&lt;` -> `<`, `&amp;` -> `&`.
- Numeric references that are surrogate code points (`0xD800`-`0xDFFF`) or non-characters (`0xFFFE`, `0xFFFF`) are left as written instead of being turned into invalid text.
- `'` (capital `X`) keeps working like `'`.

## Why it matters

The free search engines read public result pages and hand titles and snippets to `textOf`, which strips tags first (`:45-48`) and then calls `decodeEntities`. After the double decode, escaped markup is indistinguishable from real markup in the returned text, and a lone surrogate can reach JSON output and break UTF-8 encoding downstream.

## Fix scope

A single pass built from the same table: map each reference to its character, run one alternation regex over the input, and reject surrogate/non-character code points in the numeric branch. Tests in `packages/data-source/src/web/native/` alongside the existing ones. No new dependency.

recent.body:
## Problem and user outcome

Researchers need to retrieve domain-specific scientific data through MCP and use it in traceable ScienceDiscovery workflows. Literature search alone does not satisfy this need: the objects are expression datasets, bioactivity measurements, variant assertions, and protein structures.

Provide supported, discoverable connections to **GEO, ChEMBL, ClinVar, RCSB PDB, and AlphaFold Protein Structure Database**, with reliable retrieval, explicit data boundaries, and provenance that survives downstream analysis.

## Context and existing implementation

Request inspired by this article: https://x.com/servasyy_ai/article/2112052770287284550
Related project documentation: https://aipoch.com/docs/guides/connectors/

Source inspection of ScienceDiscovery at baseline `0d31e155` found existing MCP implementations for GEO, ChEMBL, ClinVar, and PDB in `services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/public_biomed_mcp.py`, plus manifests in `packages/mcp-sources/src/public-biomed.ts`. UniProt, Ensembl, and Reactome provide additional reusable patterns. No built-in AlphaFold DB adapter was found in that inspection.

This is a request to complete and validate domain database support, reusing existing adapters. It does not assume these databases are entirely unsupported. The baseline assessment was static inspection, not a live end-to-end availability test; recheck the target version before implementation.

## Requested scope

| Database | Required user-facing capabilities | Domain details to preserve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GEO | Search studies, retrieve study/sample metadata, discover actual processed/supplementary files, and download selected analysis-ready data | GSE/GSM/GPL identifiers, organism, sample conditions, platform, and whether data are raw counts, normalized values, or other processed data |
| ChEMBL | Search molecules/targets, retrieve bioactivity measurements with useful filters, and perform similarity searches | Molecule/target/assay IDs, assay type, organism, relation, value, units, confidence, and source references |
| ClinVar | Search/lookup variants and retrieve individual clinical assertions | VCV/RCV/SCV identifiers where applicable, assembly, condition, review status, dates, and conflicting submissions |
| RCSB PDB | Search/lookup experimental structures and download supported structure files | PDB ID, experimental method, resolution where applicable, chains/entities, ligands, and source/version metadata |
| AlphaFold DB | Retrieve available predictions by protein accession and download model/confidence files when available | UniProt accession, model identifier/version, source URLs, and confidence information |

AlphaFold DB retrieval is separate from running AlphaFold prediction software. New prediction compute infrastructure is outside this request. PubMed and other literature databases are also outside this scope.

## Integration requirements

- Reuse the MCP client, connector selection, permission/audit, and artifact download mechanisms. Prefer official provider APIs behind MCP adapters; do not require providers to expose MCP themselves.
- Make supported sources and operations discoverable, with setup instructions and any credential requirements. Enable the source for the intended Session and support both Inspector validation and Agent use.
- Return structured domain data and standard evidence records with stable identifiers, source links, retrieval time, and provider version/release when available. Retain source caveats and attribution.
- A generic custom MCP connection currently preserves raw/structured content but produces empty standardized `records`; calling a tool successfully alone must not count as complete evidence integration.
- Transfer large datasets and structure files through governed artifact jobs, with source metadata and integrity checks. Keep file bytes out of model context and distinguish a proposed download from a completed, verified artifact.
- Handle pagination, provider rate limits, timeouts, invalid identifiers, missing records/files, and partial failures explicitly. Do not silently present a capped subset as the complete dataset.
- Document scientific limits: GEO standard matrix/SOFT candidate paths do not enumerate all supplementary files; not every expression matrix is suitable for count-based analysis; ClinVar submissions can conflict; experimental and predicted structures must remain distinguishable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the target version, document the existing capability and remaining gap for each of the five databases.
- [ ] All five sources can be configured/enabled and successfully called from the intended Session; tool inputs and results are inspectable and audited.
- [ ] Each database has a representative live provider validation with recorded identifiers, commands/steps, expected results, and actual results. Record unavailable-provider cases as blocked rather than passed.
- [ ] GEO: discover actual files for a public study, retrieve relevant sample annotations, and download/verify a real selected matrix. Validate its data type and dimensions before downstream analysis; report when count-based analysis is inappropriate.
- [ ] ChEMBL: retrieve a target/molecule-linked activity set with explicit assay/measurement constraints, preserving units and relations, and verify pagination or clearly disclosed limits.
- [ ] ClinVar: retrieve assertions and preserve conflicting classifications/review status without reducing them to one unsupported consensus.
- [ ] PDB: retrieve an experimental structure, complete a verified CIF/PDB download, and demonstrate that a downstream analysis step can read the artifact and inspect its metadata.
- [ ] AlphaFold DB: retrieve a known available prediction by accession, verify a model download and available confidence metadata, and clearly identify it as predicted.
- [ ] Returned evidence and downloaded artifacts retain their source identifiers/URLs and retrieval metadata in subsequent analysis outputs.
- [ ] Automated tests cover domain result normalization and representative missing-record, malformed-input, rate-limit, and download-failure paths. Product-level validation covers connector selection, Inspector/Agent execution, and completed artifacts; mocked success alone is insufficient.
- [ ] User documentation describes supported operations, limitations, configuration, and reproducible examples for each source.

Implementation may be split into linked changes, but this feature remains open until the full five-database acceptance scope is verified.

## Child work item — PDB entity and chemical-component identity verification (migrated from #448)

The PDB connector must let researchers verify a structure’s protein target and ligand identity against a ChEMBL record without relying on structure titles or compound names. This is a bounded sub-item of the PDB acceptance scope above, not a separate database integration.

### Required MCP operations

- Expose discoverable polymer and nonpolymer entity identifiers from an entry lookup (or an equivalent bounded entry expansion).
- `pdb_get_polymer_entity(pdb_id, entity_id)`: entity description/type, organism, UniProt/reference mappings, label/auth chain identifiers, sequence/coverage and construct/mutation information where available.
- `pdb_get_nonpolymer_entity(pdb_id, entity_id)`: ligand/component identity, label/auth chain mappings and provider cross-references.
- `pdb_lookup_chemical_component(component_id)`: CCD name, formula/charge, InChI, complete InChIKey, available SMILES and mapped external identifiers with provenance. Extended CCD IDs such as five-character `A1CEA` are valid.

All results must provide structured domain fields and nonempty standardized evidence records with stable identifiers, canonical URLs, retrieval time, attribution and provider version/revision where available. Missing UniProt/InChIKey mappings must remain missing; do not replace them with name-based identity assertions. Preserve salt/parent relationships, stereochemistry-aware complete identifiers, covalent/modified-component qualifications, and label versus author chain IDs.

### Required validation cases

- Positive chain: through MCP, enumerate `9OS6` entities; verify polymer entity `1` maps to UniProt `P00533`, nonpolymer entity `2` maps to CCD `A1CEA`, and `A1CEA` has complete InChIKey `OMZCMEYTWSXEPZ-UHFFFAOYSA-N`, matching ChEMBL free Canertinib `CHEMBL31965`. Preserve the distinct dihydrochloride `CHEMBL545315` and its parent relation. Display protein label/auth chain `A/A` and ligand `B/A` without conflation.
- Negative chain: retrieve `5VCW` polymer entity `1` and show UniProt `Q99640`; it must not be reported as an EGFR complex merely because Pelitinib has EGFR activity elsewhere.
- Complete a selected mmCIF artifact download using the governed artifact path, verify its checksum, read the file downstream and retain the linked cross-database evidence in saved outputs.
- Complete an Agent journey using MCP metadata tools without direct HTTPS/web-fetch fallback; separately record Inspector, stub-model and real-model evidence.
- Cover extended CCD IDs; invalid/missing entities; missing protein/chemical mappings; timeout/rate-limit/partial failure feedback; and label/auth-chain distinctions.
- Add English and Chinese documentation with the positive and negative identity-matching examples and limits.

Official reference endpoints: `/rest/v1/core/polymer_entity/9OS6/1`, `/rest/v1/core/nonpolymer_entity/9OS6/2`, `/rest/v1/core/chemcomp/A1CEA`, and `/rest/v1/core/polymer_entity/5VCW/1` at `data.rcsb.org`.

## Goal

Make literature reports and review outcomes honestly verifiable: readers should see the evidence supporting material claims, know when evidence could not be verified, and never mistake a partial Quick review for full claim-fidelity verification.

## Workstream A — claim-to-evidence excerpts (from #415)

- [ ] For each material quantitative or clinical claim in a literature report, retain a short source excerpt or structured claim-to-evidence table with stable identifier and usable locator (for example PMID/DOI plus abstract/full-text location where available).
- [ ] Include the evidence in saved report/review artifacts without flooding model context; preserve source provenance and retrieval metadata.
- [ ] When an excerpt cannot be obtained, record an explicit evidence gap rather than silently presenting the claim as fully supported.

## Workstream B — visible unverifiable states (from #560)

- [ ] Extend the evidence/review schema with a visible `UNVERIFIABLE` status (or equivalent reasoned states such as identity unresolved and provider unavailable).
- [ ] Preserve the reason, affected claim/citation and review coverage in reports and review summaries. Do not silently discard identity-resolution or provider-availability findings.
- [ ] Keep the existing policy distinction: provider failure is not proof that a citation is false; it is an explicit limitation on verification.
- [ ] Align reviewer Skill instructions and runtime normalization so emitted states are representable and auditable.

## Workstream C — truthful automatic-review scope (follow-up to closed #414)

- [ ] A format/provenance-only Quick review must present itself as partial/format-only and disclose skipped claim checks with a reason.
- [ ] A claim-checked literature review must identify which claims were checked, supported, unsupported or unverifiable.
- [ ] Add regressions for stale report reviews, missing primary deliverables and the prior false-looking `ACCEPT_AND_PROCEED` Quick outcome.

## Validation

- [ ] Reproduce the CRISPR base-editing literature-report scenario from #415 and verify human-readable claim evidence or explicit gaps.
- [ ] Cover identifier mismatch, unresolved identity, unavailable provider, conflicting evidence, missing locator and provider timeout paths.
- [ ] Test Quick/Deep UI and saved artifact semantics independently; mocked provider success alone is insufficient.
- [ ] Document the distinction among supported, unsupported, unverifiable and not-reviewed claims.

Consolidates the unfinished scope of #415 and #560 and retains the relevant transparency regression from closed #414.

## Goal

Track the remaining external-agent interoperability work after PR #424 merged the initial Specialist runtime slice. This issue deliberately keeps two protocol directions separate while coordinating their shared safety, session and artifact requirements.

## Delivered baseline

PR #424 merged support for explicit Specialist tasks using Codex, Claude Code and ACP executables, normalized task/event/handoff behavior, independent concurrent Workspace/Runner execution, configuration cards and thin runtime diagnostics. It does **not** complete either original Issue’s full acceptance criteria.

## Workstream A — ScienceDiscovery hosts external Specialist runtimes (remaining from #385)

Keep the existing Specialist model and require explicit `task(specialistId=…)` targeting for non-native execution. The platform remains the authority for Workspace, permissions, secrets, artifacts, audit and cancellation.

- [ ] Validate and document a successful live-auth matrix for supported Codex, Claude Code and ACP providers, including task completion, cancellation, timeout and declared-artifact handoff. Report unavailable credentials/providers as blocked, never passed.
- [ ] Decide and implement the supported iCode adapter path, or explicitly defer it with product rationale.
- [ ] Complete the Skills/MCP/tool bridge so an external runtime can request platform-governed tools without gaining undeclared native permissions.
- [ ] Finish the product configuration surface aligned with #278: persisted/this-run/alternate credential choices, usable error recovery and no secret leakage to catalog bodies, argv, logs or artifacts.
- [ ] Add the deferred UX: runtime picker/probe, fallback controls and handoff/diagnostics visibility.
- [ ] Add the deferred reliability coverage: multi-SDK stress, escape/isolation regressions, protocol backpressure/error bounds and process-crash recovery semantics.
- [ ] Evaluate deferred orchestration/operations separately: quota/priority/dependency graphs, shared pools only with an isolation design, and fuller metrics/cluster/multi-tenant monitoring.

## Workstream B — ScienceDiscovery is an ACP v1 Agent for editors (remaining from #64)

Editors are ACP Clients; ScienceDiscovery is the spawned ACP Agent. This is not the same as Workstream A, where ScienceDiscovery drives an external agent.

- [ ] Provide a supported ACP v1 stdio JSON-RPC entry point and `initialize` capability negotiation; do not multiplex it with MCP stdio or require a browser first.
- [ ] Implement session lifecycle mapping: `session/new`, `session/prompt`, streaming `session/update`, `session/cancel`, recoverable Project/Session/Run context and absolute workspace mapping.
- [ ] Map ACP permission requests to the existing governance and sandbox path; the ACP route must not be less restrictive than the Web UI.
- [ ] Return standards-compliant JSON-RPC errors and advertise only implemented capabilities; document any research-specific extensions.
- [ ] Verify against an actual ACP Client (for example Zed or a VS Code ACP extension): launch, prompt, streamed text, at least one tool call and denied permission behavior.
- [ ] Add unit, conformance and isolated E2E coverage for version negotiation, cancellation, authentication if enabled, sandbox equivalence and secret/session-body log redaction.
- [ ] Publish editor configuration documentation. ACP Registry publication is a separate product decision and must not block local interoperability.

## Shared boundaries

- Secrets never enter Specialist catalog bodies, argv, artifacts or unauthenticated ACP traffic.
- Existing sandbox, artifact provenance and permission controls remain authoritative.
- ACP v2 remains non-default until it is stable and separately accepted.

Supersedes the remaining scope of #385 and #64. PR #424 is delivered baseline, not proof that the above acceptance is complete.

recent.author: qingkwl
recent.body:
## Summary

This issue is the **desktop shell** of the Windows desktop delivery (#400): the Electron application that turns the platform layer (#639) and the runtime (#643) into a double-clickable Windows product. The shell owns the backend stack lifecycle (start, readiness mirroring, teardown), drives the assisted first-run wizard, loads the web UI with the local access token injected, and packages the backend tree into a per-user NSIS installer.

It lands as a new top-level `win_desktop/` directory, which answers #400's open question about where the shell lives in the repo. It is a build host, not a workspace package: `win_desktop/` keeps its own pnpm workspace (own lockfile) so the root tree is untouched.

## Where the product stands today

| Area | Current state |
|---|---|
| Packaging | No Windows installer; a Windows user runs the backend from a dev checkout. |
| First run | Nothing walks a non-developer through a data-directory choice or port conflicts. |
| Robustness | A single busy service port (e.g. a stale instance still bound) kills startup with a raw bind error; a failed install leaves no install-time log; uninstall leaves shortcuts and >260-char data trees behind. |
| UI entry | No single window that injects the local access token into the SPA. |

## Goals

- **Lifecycle**: start the full stack via `scripts/start-stack.mjs` (delivered by the runtime issue), mirror its readiness stream into a loading stage with per-step heartbeats, and tear everything down on exit — even when the renderer is gone.
- **Assisted first run**: a wizard reduced to the one decision that must precede everything — the data directory (warns at 180 path chars, blocks past 240; the choice is mirrored to a file the uninstaller reads). Boot, self-check and model setup stay in the SPA.
- **Port resilience**: epoch-based allocation that bind-probes the whole service family, not one port, so one busy consumer shifts the family and the URL tracks it.
- **Installer**: per-user NSIS without UAC (license → directory → progress → finish); install diagnostics written into `$INSTDIR\logs`; a clean-uninstall story — shortcuts always removed, long-path-safe data removal, ghost uninstall-registry-key self-heal, silent uninstall never deletes user data.
- **Failure feedback**: when the stack fails, the wizard sees one line per conflicted port plus guidance, and "open log" always has a file to open.

## Non-goals

- No backend logic — everything the shell starts comes from #639/#643.
- No macOS/Linux desktop packaging (the shell is Windows-focused; cross-platform packaging is a separate discussion).
- No auto-update channel (the payload layout is blockmap-friendly by construction; serving updates is out of scope).
- No code signing.

## Root decisions

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Location | top-level `win_desktop/`, standalone workspace | #400 left the shell's home open. A build host with its own lockfile and one `app-builder-lib` patch must not perturb the root workspace — root globs do not match it, so root-level `pnpm -r` is unaffected. |
| Relationship to `apps/*` | the shell *loads* the web UI, never contains it | `win_desktop/` is the Electron host; the frontend it loads stays under `apps/`. |
| Payload layout | backend tree as plain `extraResources` files | No physical split: unchanged big payload blocks keep their blockmap entries, so differential updates never re-download them. |
| Payload source | assembled from this repo's checkout (`--repo` overrides) | One source of truth: `scripts/assemble-backend.mjs` deploys `@sciencediscovery/api`, stages the runner, and rewrites venv trampolines to the install layout. |
| Port allocation | bind-probing epochs per service family | The field case that forced this: a stale instance held one non-epoch port while every epoch port was free — a single-port probe missed it and the stack died on bind. |
| Uninstall data policy | keep by default, opt-in delete, silent never deletes | Automation safety: `/S` must never wipe user data; deletion is an explicit checkbox only. |
| Install diagnostics | markers into `$INSTDIR\logs` | An install-time failure otherwise leaves nothing to look at — the user cannot find user-data logs before first run ever happens. |

## Delivery

- `win_desktop/src/` — main process; wizard (state machine + data-dir evaluation + api); `stack.ts` / `bootstrap.ts` (lifecycle + payload path substitution); `ports.ts` (epochs); `proxy.ts` / `preload.ts` (token injection); `loading-stage.ts` (heartbeat mapping); `window-state.ts`; `ui-retry.ts`.
- `win_desktop/test/` — 14 `node:test` suites, no Electron launch needed.
- `win_desktop/scripts/` — esbuild build, dev runner, backend assembly, icon generator.
- `win_desktop/build/` — NSIS include (presentation, diagnostics, uninstall options), uninstall helper (C# + PowerShell long-path removal), license, icons.
- `win_desktop/patches/app-builder-lib@26.15.3.patch` — NSIS progress-bar presentation fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pnpm -C win_desktop install`, `typecheck`, and `test` green on a real Windows host (113 tests across 14 suites).
- [ ] The root workspace untouched: no root file changes; root globs do not match `win_desktop/`.
- [ ] No internal planning shorthand in comments, test names, or identifiers.
- [ ] Real-machine installer evidence: install log under `$INSTDIR\logs`; uninstall keeps data by default; silent uninstall never deletes.

## Open questions

1. The shell's `node:test` suite needs no Electron — should a `windows-latest` CI job eventually run it (same CI gap as #639/#643)?
2. Update serving is unaddressed (the layout is ready for it) — separate issue if auto-update is wanted.

## Related

- Parent: #400
- Stacks on #639 (platform) and #643 (runtime): assembling a full payload requires the runtime's startup chain, so the merge order is platform → runtime → shell.
- The web UI the shell loads stays under `apps/` and is not part of this issue.

stale.body:
## Context

Since July 2026 an open-source "science workbench" category has formed, triggered by Anthropic's Claude Science launch (2026-06-30). Three direct open-source alternatives appeared the same week and are now at scale: [synthetic-sci/openscience](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience) (~3.6K★), [aipoch/open-science](https://github.com/aipoch/open-science) (~4.2K★), and [ai4s-research/open-science](https://github.com/ai4s-research/open-science) (~1.7K★). Having compared ScienceDiscovery against them (and against the autonomous-scientist systems: Sakana AI-Scientist, InternScience/InternAgent + MLEvolve), here is a strengths/gaps assessment in the hope it helps prioritization. Facts below are from public repo data collected 2026-09-15.

## Strengths (keep — and communicate)

1. **Sandbox-first security model.** Fail-closed Bubblewrap/Seatbelt execution, operator-scoped NPU chip passthrough, opt-in Broker with fixed entry points and `shell: false`. None of the three competitors communicates a default-isolation story; the highest-engagement technical question on a competitor's launch thread was literally *"are the skills executed within a secure, containerized sandbox by default, or does the user manage isolation?"* — this repo already answers that question, but almost nobody knows it does.
2. **Provenance depth.** CAS with pinned-asset drift rejection, review checks, cross-session/SubAgent citation chains. The strongest provenance story in the category.
3. **Search-camp RSI engine.** The evolve sidecar (flat-PUCT tree + OpenEvolve MAP-Elites, discriminability probe, explicit "no model training, no search-rule modification") is a clean, honest scope with a real cousin in [InternScience/MLEvolve](https://github.com/InternScience/MLEvolve) (#1 on MLE-Bench).
4. **Ascend NPU path.** 910B sandbox passthrough + allowlisted workloads (Protenix/MindScience) is unique in the category and extends machine-verifiable research to device-scale workloads.
5. **Engineering discipline beyond repo age.** Bilingual doc set, CI tiers (UT/ST/mocked E2E), self-documented limitations (e.g., Idea Tree scores are model judgments, not experimental evidence).

## Gaps (ordered by leverage)

1. **Installation/onboarding.** No binaries in Releases — #1 (open since 08-19, rated 1/5) is the only organic user feedback this repo has received, and it is someone who *could not install the product*. All three competitors ship desktop installers and a <10-minute quickstart. This pairs directly with the first-experience goal in #22.
2. **No community surface.** All merged PRs are bots; there are zero human external PRs. For comparison: aipoch merges 6+ human PRs/day; ai4s-research power users file bugs *and* land the fixes (e.g., their stall-guard for looping agents came from a user). A "good first issue" ladder + a contributor guide + weekly maintainer RFC triage would start the flywheel.
3. **Category invisibility + an unverifiable benchmark claim.** 58★ vs 1.7–4.2K for peers; one promotion event found (Sina Finance 2026-08-16) whose headline claim (BiomniBench-DA "业界SOTA") is dual-claimed by aipoch's README badge on the same benchmark. Without published methodology/splits, the claim reads as marketing and hurts credibility with scientists — either publish the eval or drop the superlative.
4. **Adoption levers validated by competitors, still missing here:** headless CLI / task API (repeated cross-repo demand — researchers want CI and agent-to-agent use, not only a GUI), model-provider onboarding (subscription reuse, connectivity-test friction), Windows parity.
5. **Cross-model skill consistency.** The single most-validated complaint in the category: *"one flag switches the model, not whether the skill actually works"* (prompts tuned on one model degrade on smaller/local models). A per-skill model-compatibility matrix or a cross-model smoke-test suite for the 300+ skills would directly differentiate.

## Suggested next steps

- [ ] Ship Linux binaries + a 10-minute quickstart (pairs with #22)
- [ ] Publish evolve/idea-tree efficiency metrics (per-node token cost, CAS reuse rate, surviving-node quality on an independent benchmark) — the pruning+reuse efficiency story is genuinely differentiating and no competitor tells it
- [ ] Benchmark-claim triage: methodology for BiomniBench-DA or remove the SOTA wording
- [ ] Community ladder: CONTRIBUTING good-first-issues + a maintainer-reserved RFC-triage day

Happy to help flesh any of these out.

items.author: ink999107
items.body:
Five things went wrong in one round of using the desktop app, and they are fixed
together here because they were found together. The seeded sample Session opened
with every subagent it delegated showing an empty record; a subagent line in the
transcript turned the right panel back into the artifact and workspace tabs when
it was pressed a second time; the first-run wizard asked the provider whether it
answers, and then asked again; and a dropped file whose name carried path
segments was reported as 上传失败 although its bytes were already stored. The
rail also now draws the product's own mark instead of the placeholder flask.

## The sample's children were never in the catalog

A Session that arrives as a recording — the sample is one — is rebuilt by replaying
the run it has on disk. A run stream deliberately keeps `subagent.updated`
snapshots without their steps: the steps are appended to each child's own
`subagent-<id>` substream, which a replay does not read. The catalog
(`SessionStore.catalog.subagents`, served at `GET /api/sessions/:id/subagents`) is
the one place a finished child's execution is complete, and only a *live* child
writes it. The seeding path restored the run and the messages but never the
children, so the panel — which fills a replayed child's steps from the catalog —
had nothing to fill them with.

Seeding now restores the recorded children: the snapshot from the run's own log,
the steps from the substream the snapshot names. A child still marked `running` is
skipped, because loading a run closes it as interrupted and a catalog row would
then contradict the transcript. A row that is already present is left alone, so
running the seed again does not duplicate anything.

## Opening a record is idempotent, and the panel draws its own way back

Pressing a subagent line opened the child in the right panel; pressing the same
line again closed it, because the handler toggled. The line is a row the reader
chose to read, and taking the record away on a second, slightly-off press reads as
a misread rather than a decision. The only way back was that same line, in a
transcript the reader has usually scrolled away from.

Opening is now idempotent: the line asks for that child, and a repeat press asks
for the same thing. The panel gains a back control in its header — 返回产物和文件 /
*Back to artifacts and files* — which is the one explicit way out of a record. Tool
input and result text share the mode, so they follow the same rule.

## The wizard tested the same model twice

测试并继续 saves the provider and its profile and runs the connectivity test; the
开始使用 button that appears once that passes saved the same records a second time
and ran the same test again, so the reader watched the same spinner and the same
连接成功 line twice before the workspace opened.

`ModelForm` is shared by the wizard and 设置, and its 保存 path is written to be
safe on its own: create the provider, add the model, test it, then point the
default at it. That is right when 保存 is the first thing the user presses. It is
not right after 测试 has just done the first three steps with exactly the same
values.

A passing test now hands the saved profile forward, and the action that follows
writes the default onto that record instead of saving and testing it again. The
pass is keyed to the form's contents: every edit that could change what would be
sent — preset, protocol, base URL, key, model name — clears it, so a form that was
changed after being tested still pays for its own test, and so does one where the
user skips 测试 entirely. The verdict on screen is not overwritten, so the reader
does not see a second "testing" state at all. 设置 gets the same behaviour for
free, since it renders the same form.

## A dropped file's card was settled against the wrong name

`uploadWorkspaceFiles` puts only the last segment on the multipart part — the
route stores the file under the name it is given, so `../outside.csv` must travel
as `outside.csv`. The composer's card kept the browser's own name, and
`mergeUpload` matched the answer's `originalName` (which can only be
`outside.csv`) against that. Nothing matched, no entry was found, and the card
fell back to "failed" — the branch that exists for a file the answer did not
mention at all.

The name a part travels under is now one exported function beside the request
that uses it, and the merge compares against the same string. The card still
shows the user's own file name; only the matching changed, and the answer's error
list is looked up the same way.

The browser case for this had stopped covering it: it asserted `已上传 outside.csv`,
the toast copy that the composer-tray rework replaced with cards, and that rework
updated the two neighbouring upload journeys and missed this one. The stale
assertion meant the case never reached the state where the card was drawn. It
asserts the card now — name, size, and that it reads as stored — and a unit test
pins the merge on its own.

## The rail's mark

`apps/desktop/src/views/Rail.tsx` drew a hand-rolled flask SVG. The rail now draws
the product's own `app-mark.png` through the stylesheet, so the mark the desktop
window and the rail show is one asset.

## Validation

Run on head `a7b8eee0`, in this repository's own layers:

| Layer | planned | executed | passed | failed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pnpm ci:l1` | 4 | 4 | 4 | 0 |
| `pnpm ci:ut` | 5524 | 5524 | 5519 | 5 |
| `pnpm ci:st` | 24 | 24 | 22 | 2 |
| `pnpm ci:e2e` | 131 | 131 | 127 | 4 |
| desktop browser suite | 96 | 96 | 96 | 0 |

None of the eleven layer failures is in a path this diff touches: every changed
file is under `apps/desktop/` or `services/api/`. Each failure was attributed by
running it again, and where it reproduced, on unmodified `upstream/main`
(`d72cdf8c`) in a separate worktree:

- **`packages/cas/src/versioning.test.ts`** — flake under parallel load. Run
  alone it passes 13/13 on this head, and fails 12/13 alone on the baseline.
- **`services/runner/src/sandbox-network.test.ts`** — `bwrap: Unknown option
  --disable-userns`: this host's bubblewrap does not have the option, and the
  same case fails on the baseline.
- **`scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`** — `bash .ci/run-research-python.sh race`
  reached the layer's timeout on this host.
- **`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts`** — "the run's
  trajectory is recorded…" fails when run alone on the baseline too (103 of 104
  there, the same single case).
- **`test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts`** (ST, 2 subtests) — it fetches the
  pinned Python runtime from a GitHub release asset, and this host cannot
  download it; a ranged request for the same asset stalls past 60 s.
- **`journey-prepare-environment`** (E2E) — `BLOCKED: managed Python base is not
  ready (failed: micromamba setup failed)`.
- **`journey-local-token-onboarding`** (E2E) — passed when the four failing
  journeys were re-run alone; a timing flake.
- **`journey-artifact-viewer-large-screen`** (774 px against a 760 px limit) and
  **`journey-model-connect-wizard`** (598 px against a 580 px footer) — both
  reproduce on re-run, but they assert pixel bounds of `apps/web` screens
  (`apps/web/src/Markdown.tsx`, `apps/web/src/ModelConnectWizard.tsx`), and
  `git diff --stat <base>..HEAD -- apps/web test/` is empty: this diff cannot
  change what they measure. They read as this host's font metrics rather than
  as behaviour, and the repository's CI runs them in its own image.

Green and covering this change: L1; the desktop unit cases inside the UT layer
(`apps/desktop/tests`, including the two added here); the API seeding test
(`services/api/src/sample-session/index.test.ts`); and the browser cases added
or repaired below.

## E2E user journeys

PASS for the journeys below, on `a7b8eee0`, in a browser against the isolated
local stack.

- **Seeded sample Session → press a delegated subagent's line.** Expected: its
  steps and its answer in the right panel, and a second press keeps the record
  open with a way back. Actual: both, and the panel carries no artifact tabs
  while the record is open. `apps/desktop/e2e/panel-interactions.spec.ts` (new);
  it replays a recorded run and serves the catalog the runner writes.
- **First-run wizard → 测试并继续, then 开始使用.** Expected: the provider is
  asked once. Actual: exactly one `POST /api/models/{id}/test` across both
  presses. `apps/desktop/e2e/setup.spec.ts` (assertion added; it fails with two
  calls before the change).
- **Drop `../outside.csv`.** Expected: the card reads as stored. Actual: one
  card, `is-uploaded`, showing `../outside.csv`, with `outside.csv` in the
  workspace. `apps/desktop/e2e/workspace.spec.ts:116`.

The uploaded-file journey is the one that had stopped covering its own defect:
it asserted a toast the composer-tray rework had replaced, so it never reached
the card. Its assertion now pins the card.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix`
User impact: the seeded sample Session shows what each subagent did — its steps
and its answer — where it used to open empty; a subagent line pressed twice keeps
its record open, with a back control to return to artifacts and files; the
first-run wizard asks the provider once, so 开始使用 no longer waits on a second
connectivity test; a file whose name carried path segments is listed as stored
instead of reporting 上传失败 about bytes the workspace already holds; the rail
draws the product's own mark.
Compatibility and migration: none. The seed only adds catalog rows that are
missing, so a data directory seeded before this change gains the sample's
children on its next start.

Related to #400. Partial fix; keep #400 open.
