Connects configuration requests to runs, tools and conversation cards, including completion/Stop races, accepted-run SSE reconnection and MCP schema-cache initialization. Removes the redundant composer configuration shortcut while preserving natural-language requests, task-driven proposals, secure input and same-run pause/resume.

Refs [#278](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/278) — runtime/chat integration of conversation configuration and task continuation; partial implementation of the umbrella issue. The complete product and backend acceptance criteria remain open.

## Review and release scope

This stack implements the registered in-conversation configuration flow from #278:

- [#553](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/553): shared request/credential/persistence protocol and confirmation card; no later-slice dependency.
- [#554](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/554): supported model/credential and installed-connector adapters/cards; depends on #553, parallel to #555.
- [#555](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/555): scoped reasoning/review/Skills and registered timeout/quota/Idea Tree adapters; depends on #553, parallel to #554.
- [#556](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/556): live waiting, activation/continuation, Stop/reconnect and chat integration; depends on #553, #554 and #555.

All bases remain `main`. #553 and #555 have merged; #554 remains a prerequisite included in this branch. The proposed remaining order is `#554 → #556`. Follow-up commits mean the earlier cumulative counts of 1/2/2/4 no longer describe the current tips. If squash/rebase changes prerequisite SHAs, update and revalidate the remaining branch after #554 lands. Maintainers still decide the merge form and architecture.

Only registered capabilities/scopes are exposed. Redacted Agent discovery/query/describe is on demand, without loading every setting each turn. User-bound confirmation and dedicated secret inputs remain separate from execution permission. Settings pages remain available.

Design documents, generated HTML and private test evidence are excluded.

## Verification and remaining gates

**Current published head: `1afa3a31a34449994386d4607ead26c1be359e23`, normally fast-forwarded at 06:03 UTC.** The generic `mcp_server.py` is restored exactly to upstream-main blob `73623d6e`. Deadline selection now stays in the existing domain-specific `agent_runs.bridge_caller`: only `configuration` / `propose` receives the bounded human-interaction allowance; ordinary tool deadlines are unchanged and cancellation propagates. Ordinary upstream core is unchanged; this does not promise an infinite SDK wait or a 24-hour end-to-end guarantee. Diagnostics distinguish inner `tool.bridge.timeout` from outer `mcp.request.timeout` without changing timeout semantics. Unit tests passed **73/73**. Actual API checks passed the 2-second ordinary-tool / 4-second human-wait / 6-second slow-tool boundary (timeout and ignored late result), plus submit/refuse/Stop, duplicate decisions and independent execution permission. The original full configuration browser journey passed **1/1** on the first attempt (56.6 s) at 06:07:15 UTC with unchanged assertions: confirm/double-click, a separate visible permission decision with Allow once, same Run and one MCP execution, refusal, Stop, and refresh showing that an old card cannot resume the task. Its strict cleanup assertions passed; final screenshot/cleanup evidence review is pending. This is a fresh pass of this journey, not a rerun of the broader d8 suite. Current-head CI/SCA results remain pending independent verification; restoring the file does not establish that SCA is cleared.

**Previous 2ffd evidence (not a current-head rerun):** all actually executed CI jobs and merge-gate passed, static unresolved findings were 0, and five SCA source matches remained. Its targeted 14/14 and API/root typechecks passed; isolated integration against main `ad34dd78`, synthesized tree `7d998d57`, also passed locked install, full API dependency build, types and 14/14. The source branch still has the older eight-field Idea Tree action metadata; the upstream five-field contract requires full integration. Preserve 445 UI, 05c API/Stop and d8 broader evidence at their recorded revisions.

Earlier 445 baseline: **`445e520161aaf996653c1af8fc778d4f90caed73`**. Product code is identical to `05c03511586c81692c603c49d35f6f7347bb38a4`. The follow-up to [review 4408545071](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/556#discussion_r4408545071) settles the original waiter when Stop/generation suppression prevents activation, without weakening configuration authorization or merging it with execution permission. Gated regressions passed **27/27**. Actual configuration UI and unchanged Runner Cancel checks passed on 445; actual configuration API and Stop checks passed on 05c, whose product code is identical. These are focused results, not a full current-head replay of the broader d8 baseline.

The reviewer subsequently retracted the expiry/activation concern and resolved [thread 4408545071](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/556#discussion_r4408757304) in [review 5692948021](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/556#pullrequestreview-5692948021), reporting independent safety checks **9/9** and no remaining findings of their own. Their live-wait test run was not independently completed; this is not an all-green or release-acceptance claim.

The actual **445 static report has zero unresolved findings**. The 445 workflow is terminal: 12 successful checks, one external CodeCheck/SCA failure and four policy skips. Executed Actions jobs, including merge-gate, passed; policy skips are not passes. SCA's five existing 1% source matches remain subject to human review; no acceptance or false-positive disposition is claimed. Static success does not establish an overall green gate.

<details>
<summary>Earlier d8 / 330 / befad verification — retained as historical, not current-head status</summary>

The following was recorded before 445. Head names, pending statuses and test counts below belong to their stated historical revisions and do not supersede the current status above.

Historical d8 head: `d8b5d97603f925a64a5dfffd3952e239a39a53a4`, pushed and independently verified. Configuration waiting now extends the existing ExecutionBlocks lifecycle; its separate Map/poll loop is removed, while configuration validation and tool permission decisions remain separate. Final-code build/typecheck, L1 4/4, focused 122/122, Jiuwen 107/107, Python 20/20 and independent safety 15/15 passed, as did actual Jiuwen 3 browser journeys, 2 existing Runner-wait UI diagnostics, configuration/deleted-target API checks and the normal-tool-timeout versus human-wait boundary. New d8 CI is running independently. The following static-fix results refer to preceding 330, and the browser/API details further below to befad. This adds the two static-assertion fixes and API MCP-gate regression. Its exact code tree passed API/tests typechecks, focused 24/24, complete configuration 195/195 and L1 4/4. New-head Actions executed jobs passed; external CodeCheck/SCA is checked independently. The detailed browser/API results below refer to preceding `befad0f0`, not a fresh full rerun on 330. Remote Actions, CodeCheck/SCA and merge-gate for this head must complete independently; the old `b6f22fcb` green results and counts do not certify this head. Fresh focused validation used actual JiuwenSwarm, ordinary upstream core and owned loopback scripted models/MCP: final-head selected CI browser journeys 3/3 (exit 0), committed configuration API and deleted-connector/deleted-model refusal diagnostics passed; final-head coordinator/live-wait/Stop 29/29 and independent safety/CI checks 15/15 passed. Configuration regressions 192/192 passed before the final test-only cleanup commit, with product source unchanged. Typechecks and API/web builds passed. These are focused checks, not a full repository CI pass. The original shell reviewer journey remains blocked by this cloud sandbox's NETLINK_ROUTE restriction; the additional actual-Jiuwen no-shell journey verifies the review/feedback/skip behavior, not Shell execution. Earlier fixture-cleanup and startup-budget failures were retained; fresh-data reruns passed.
</details>

Native overlay writes require an explicit available task-only choice and preview; persisted choices remain available to recovery validation, without authorizing another apply. Missing/invalid approval uses `CONFIGURATION_CHOICE_APPROVAL_REQUIRED`, separately from an unavailable original task. The earlier source-regression and wheel-preparation counts are historical. Jiuwen configuration now uses a ScienceDiscovery/adapter-managed live wait with ordinary upstream core 0.1.17 from pinned `ad0c9df`; the configuration-specific prepared core wheel and its startup enforcement are no longer required. Existing Swarm compatibility patches remain separate.

Maintainer acceptance is still required for merge unit/order, application-layer live-wait architecture, and persistence/skip/resumption semantics. Jiuwen submit/refuse continues the same live main run; process loss interrupts that run and invalidates stale decisions, rather than promising arbitrary-crash SDK checkpoint resumption. Persisted Reviewer queue recovery is a separate lifecycle. Skipped review is not successful review and creates no fabricated review result or feedback.

The focused results do not establish real-LLM semantic, arbitrary-crash SDK resumption, current-head Windows or Docker/binary release acceptance, or support for every setting/backend. Validated Native paths use a durable same-run checkpoint; activation timing is reported separately and unsupported backend contracts fail closed. Policy-skipped real/distribution jobs are not passes. Keep the umbrella issue open.

<details>
<summary>Earlier validation records — historical, not acceptance of the current head</summary>

Earlier records are preserved verbatim. Their source-specific pending/failure statements are historical; current-head status is above, and broader acceptance is not inferred.

Latest source checks on Windows: API typecheck exit 0; Web typecheck/build exit 0; card + model-client tests 41/41, exit 0. The old #554 client fails the destination-serialization regression; the corrected client passes 2/2. Configuration integration checks executed 148 tests: 146 passed, 2 failed (session deletion SQLite setup and automatic-review completion). Both failures reproduce on the exact unmodified source under the same conditions; they remain unresolved, not waived. Final combined Linux/Chromium incremental checks for these follow-ups are pending.

On the earlier combined Linux candidate 8abfd4ea, the full plan was eventually executed (5075 UT identities, 49 ST identities), with original failures retained. Later isolated retries do not retroactively make the original batches pass. Sandbox proc-mount and research-workspace capacity gates remain open. The unchanged Evolve distribution test subsequently passed once on f339c9c5 using complete SHA-verified official caches (exit 0, 75.144 s); this does not prove the sole cause of earlier download failures. Remote independent review covers that supplement.

Earlier real Chromium tests cover configuration/Stop/reconnect behavior using scripted models, not real-LLM semantic success rates. The isolated WIP trial remains available; retained pending cards and its backend were untouched by these follow-ups. The shortcut removal has been deployed as frontend static assets only, without restarting the trial backend or changing existing sessions/pending decisions. The isolated WSL build exited 0; an actual 1280x720 browser check confirmed the shortcut is absent and the confirmation/refusal controls remain.

The prior heads still failed CodeCheck. A follow-up report identified one remaining TCP-address assertion in #553, one request-body assertion in #554, and snapshot assertions/dead initialization in #555. These have now been addressed with checked TCP/body types and existing system-settings normalizers. API typecheck, system-adapter integration tests 6/6 and model-client tests 2/2 passed on the updated source. The crash/restart fixture still needs Linux execution. New-head CodeCheck results remain pending; the report site is still inaccessible from this browser. Draft-policy skipped UT/ST/E2E jobs are not passes. Complete engineering and semantic acceptance remains pending.

</details>

## Release

Release category: release:feature.
Compatibility: review and merge in the dependency order above; existing settings pages remain available.

Related PRs: [#553](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/553), [#554](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/554), [#555](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/555), [#556](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/556).

## What changed
Refs #398

- Persist original execution identity and recovery context; reconnect, reconcile, and retrieve original results without replaying a running or completed job.
- Add Runner identity/revision evidence, durable reconciliation, idempotent finalization, publication-journal recovery, and fail-closed workspace quarantine when termination is unknown.
- Correct live workspace quota scans to tolerate vanished, already-enumerated children while preserving root and non-ENOENT failures.
- This is the independent #398 implementation only, based directly on main at 7ee6c1d0. It does not include the #401 checkpoint/continuation implementation. Shared-file integration may require later review.

## Verification
Previously recorded evidence, not rerun during this publication:
- Original CPU/mock targeted regression: 283 passed. Build, typecheck, architecture and documentation checks passed for the original candidate.
- Scan correction: 31/31 scanner regressions; combined scanner/Runner/CAS checks 63/63; targeted TypeScript checks passed.
- Same-Linux-host real API registration plus Runner, bwrap and CAS CPU MLP: baseline plus four fault scenarios passed the recorded acceptance checks. Disconnection, API restart and lost ACK retained one launch and completed 2,000 steps with the baseline parameter hash.
- Runner kill remained unknown/quarantined and rejected conflicting work with 409. This is safety behavior, not recovery of a killed training process.
- Published tree f7dc0907395c75f91861122ecf29783281add24c matches the reviewed candidate exactly. Publication commit metadata differs from the local candidate.

## Limitations
- Awaiting CI and further review. No merge or issue closure is requested.
- No cross-machine, NPU/Ascend, or real-LLM decision acceptance; no generic pipeline/batch adapter or new UI.
- No durable process supervisor or model-specific checkpoint continuation. Unknown state must not cause resubmission.
- The correction did not rerun the entire monorepo build/full external E2E suite.

## Release
Release category: release:feature
User impact: recover observation/results of the original execution and prevent unsafe duplicate dispatch.
Compatibility: existing executions without sufficient original identity/context remain conservatively unresolved.

## Reviewed #472 follow-up — 2026-10-23

Published commit: `ef59fd80b540d06cc3b844568885a9b4009508ea`; its tree `e12941badb119b004babaf5ff5739887bbb055c1` exactly matches reviewed local candidate `328d12e0973819c62a27a64c5cb1f7f643c9bacb`. Publication commit metadata differs from the local candidate. This follows the original PR head `f8f1d48ae25ba092d905ddb668a3ff052289a9d8` and addresses structured non-retryable provenance conflicts, fixed safe conflict messages at the persistence boundary, prototype-safe error-code allowlisting, legacy-unknown guidance, and regression-test fixes.

Recorded validation in a fresh isolated Linux clone with its own dependency store:
- Core targeted suites: 75/75 passed (provenance finalization 10, RunnerClient 5, execution manager 25, API shell executions 35); the Unicode cursor regression also passed three separate runs.
- Full independent `pnpm typecheck` passed with exit 0 on the final candidate, including `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`. The complete API shell-execution suite also passed with exit 0 on that candidate.
- Production `pnpm --recursive build` passed with exit 0 at `d0b27dff5598760a8aef9586229caf56aa1e596b`. The remaining changes through the reviewed candidate affect only tests and the report; production sources, build configuration and lockfile are identical, and the build excludes test sources.
- Runner server suite: 28 passed, 23 failed, 1 file-level cancellation. The failures were classified as 18 bubblewrap-dependent and 5 Python-dependent cases in the missing-dependency environment; these cases still need a suitably provisioned CI environment. The file-level cancellation remains recorded. This is partial validation, not a fully passing suite.

Remaining scope: the existing direct `executeShell` error path can still persist remote error text into stderr/CAS; it remains unfixed and uncovered by this follow-up. No new cross-machine, NPU/Ascend, real-LLM or full external E2E acceptance is claimed. No merge, deployment, or #473 change is requested.

Fixes #679

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

## What the problem is

`CasStore.has()` answered the existence question by calling `read()` and mapped only `ENOENT` to `false`. `read()` re-hashes the bytes, so an object whose bytes no longer match its digest made `has()` throw `CAS integrity failure` — from a method whose contract is a boolean. Its sibling `verify()` already maps the same condition to `false`, so the two predicates over one store disagreed:

```
put -> b94d27b9934d 11
has before -> true
verify after corruption -> false
has after corruption -> THREW CAS integrity failure
```

The overwrite keeps the byte length (11 → 11), i.e. exactly the "same size, different bytes" corruption the store detects elsewhere. Callers use `has()` as a cache probe in front of `put` / `retain` / republish decisions: with a corrupt blob they crashed instead of taking the republish branch.

## What changes

`has()` now maps the integrity failure to `false` the way `verify()` does:

```ts
// A corrupt object is not usable, so has() answers as verify() does: absent.
if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT" || (error as Error).message === "CAS integrity failure") return false;
```

`has(hash)` is a total boolean predicate again: `true` only when the object is present and valid, `false` when it is missing **or corrupt**. `read()` still rejects a corrupt object with `CAS integrity failure` — the detection is unchanged, only the boolean answer is. A valid object and a missing object behave exactly as before. Two lines of production code; no new dependency.

## Commits

- `15247383034b21965143ab7e21d0aa681b77a6ad` — the red test only.
- `dfbc783d4a24913d113fcab6e7516271c292ee23` — the fix.

The red test is the first commit, the fix is appended on top; no amend, no force-push.

## Red → green

Red on base `ad34dd7847` (test commit only):

```
cd packages/cas
node --import tsx --test src/index.test.ts

not ok 3 - a corrupted object is absent for has() and verify(), and read() still rejects it
  error: 'CAS integrity failure'
  stack: |-
    CasStore.read (.../packages/cas/src/index.ts:98:43)
    async CasStore.has (.../packages/cas/src/index.ts:76:7)
# tests 4
# pass 3
# fail 1
```

The test pins all three answers in one place: `verify()` is `false`, `has()` is `false`, and `read()` still rejects with `CAS integrity failure` (so the fix cannot be "stop checking digests").

Green on this tip:

```
node --import tsx --test src/index.test.ts
# tests 4 / # pass 4 / # fail 0

node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"

Fixes #674

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

## What the problem is

`serialToText` converts an Excel date serial with a single epoch, `Date.UTC(1899, 11, 30)`. That epoch is correct for the 1900 date system only from serial 61 on. Excel's own phantom leap day (serial 60 is 1900-02-29, a date that never existed) shifts everything before it by one day, so serials 1–59 render one day early:

| serial | Excel shows | this reader showed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1900-01-01 | 1899-12-31 |
| 59 | 1900-02-28 | 1900-02-27 |
| 61 | 1900-03-01 | 1900-03-01 (already right) |
| 45292 | 2024-01-01 | 2024-01-01 (already right) |

Any date-formatted cell in January or February 1900 therefore displayed the wrong day in the sheet panel. The 1904 date system is unaffected: `SERIAL_EPOCH_1904` has no such discontinuity.

## What changes

`serialToText` keeps the epoch it is given, except for the 1900 system below serial 61, where it counts from `1899-12-31`:

- `SERIAL_EPOCH_1900_BEFORE_MARCH = Date.UTC(1899, 11, 31)` is selected when `epoch === SERIAL_EPOCH_1900 && serial < 61`.
- Serial 60 (Excel's phantom 1900-02-29) still resolves to 1900-03-01, the same value it had before, because that date cannot be represented.
- The 1904 branch, the time-of-day path (serial < 1) and all non-date cells are untouched.

Five lines of production code; no new dependency.

Fixes #672

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

## What the problem is

`decodeEntities` applied one `replaceAll` per entry of a table whose first entry is `&`, and only afterwards ran a numeric-reference pass. Each pass sees the output of the previous one, so a page that escaped its own markup is decoded twice:

- `"&lt;"` → `"<"` (the `&` pass produces `<`, the next entry consumes it) instead of the two characters `<`
- `"&amp;"` → `"&"`
- `"&#65;"` → `"A"` (the named pass feeds the numeric pass)

`textOf` runs this on every free-engine title and snippet, so the extracted text no longer round-trips what the page actually said.

The numeric pass also accepted every integer in `1..0x10FFFF`, including the surrogate block, so `"�"` produced the lone surrogate `\uD800`. A lone surrogate cannot be encoded as UTF-8 or carried verbatim in JSON output, so it corrupts anything downstream that serialises the extracted text. Hexadecimal references were not recognised at all (`"A"` stayed literal, `"'"` stayed literal with an uppercase `X`).

## What changes

One pass over the source, replacing every reference exactly once; replacement text is never scanned again:

- A single `RegExp` matches a decimal reference, a hexadecimal reference (`x` or `X`), or a named reference; `String.replace` visits the source once.
- Named references live in a `Map` (`amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot`, `nbsp`) instead of a sequential table.
- Decimal and hexadecimal references are decoded by the same branch; `"'"` and `"'"` both become `'`.
- A code point is decoded only when it can be represented downstream: `1..0x10FFFF`, excluding the surrogate block `0xD800..0xDFFF` and non-characters (`0xFFFE`, `0xFFFF`, and the other `FDD0..FDEF`/`xF FFE..xF FFF` forms). Anything else stays as the literal reference text, which is what the previous code did for out-of-range values.

No new dependency, no new allocation beyond the replacement string, and the number of passes over the input drops from 7 + 1 to 1.

## Commits

- `5027406f27823114631078d87d3944c3dd37569b` — the red test only (4 cases; 3 fail on `1e886583`).
- `7e79fc3a81ce453411ff0636499623d75602e63a` — the fix.

The red test is the first commit and the fix is appended on top; no amend, no force-push.

  actual: '<'

  expected: 'AA'
  actual: 'AA'
not ok 3 - leaves surrogate and non-character scalars as literal text
  expected: '�'
  actual: '\ud800'
# tests 4
# pass 1

```

## What changed

- `splitDelimited` keeps a field as spans of the source (`parts`/`spanStart`) and only joins them when the field ends: an ordinary field costs one `source.slice(...)`, and only a `""` escape closes a span early. A file whose single cell opens a quote and never closes it is one span over the whole file, so that path is linear instead of building one string per character.
- New test `dataset preview keeps an unclosed quote as one field` (64 KiB): it pins the parsed result (one column equal to the whole quoted content, no rows, `totalRows 0`, `truncated false`) and deliberately makes no timing assertion.
- The parser state machine, the blank-line rule, `totalChars` and `truncated` are unchanged.

## Summary

Ready for maintainer review and merge. This PR extracts Idea Tree from the evolve process into an independently runnable Python service and exposes its research capabilities as session-scoped MCP tools.

Current candidate: `d81b7bf3ebc8d9b1ed09914a439768f43a5abd3a` (one squashed commit). Related to #101 and #84; partial delivery of the broader integration acceptance scope, so keep #101 open. This establishes the service boundary ahead of the evolve migration in #102.

## Changes

- Move the Idea Tree engine, service layer, models, prompts and templates out of evolve's vendored implementation into `services/idea-tree`. Preserve the existing research algorithm and remove the old evolve router registrations.
- Add a dedicated FastAPI process with a health endpoint, shutdown cleanup, internal-token authentication and loopback port `4314`. Require a single ASGI worker because active research tasks and short-lived capabilities are process-local.
- Persist research, trees and settings in a service-owned data directory. Copy legacy records once without deleting originals; conflicting destination records fail migration rather than overwrite data.
- Publish `create_idea_research`, `get_idea_research`, `control_idea_research` and `view_idea_tree` through scoped MCP endpoints. Project/session identity and model callback credentials come from the trusted control plane rather than model arguments. Capabilities expire after five minutes; revoking a transport capability does not stop autonomous research.
- Replace the old API Python client with `IdeaTreeServiceClient`. Discover tool schemas from the service, preserve historical graph reads, research-created messages and SSE forwarding, and keep the six existing frontend research/graph/settings routes and response shapes.
- Include the service in stack startup, Docker packaging, isolated browser-test configuration, test discovery and coverage. Update English and Chinese developer documentation.

## Review fixes included

- Restore complete `evolveAvailability` initialization and bootstrap wiring.
- Restore the actual `research_service.py` service layer instead of the accidentally duplicated engine module.
- Migrate remaining tests away from the removed Python client and evolve vendor modules; remove the unused compatibility adapter.
- Remove the Evolve-readiness guard from independent Idea Tree routes.
- Disable Uvicorn access logging in the application lifespan as well as the launcher, preventing MCP capability URLs from being logged with direct `uvicorn ...:app` startup. Include a direct-Uvicorn regression.
- Correct stale developer-document paths and replace the redundant listener-address type assertion identified by CodeCheck with a runtime guard.

## Validation

GitHub Actions for the current candidate: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40816521503

| Check | Current-head result |
| --- | --- |
| L1 static checks | PASS |
| UT | PASS |
| ST | PASS |
| Mocked browser L2: governed, literature, research, standard-config, standard-journeys | PASS, all five shards |
| Coverage | PASS |
| merge-gate | PASS |
| GitCode CodeCheck | PASS |
| GitCode SCA, anti-poison and blacklist checks | PASS |
| CLA | All contributors confirmed signed |

GitCode mirror report: https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/pull/412/check

Real L3/L4/L5, binary release and Docker execution were skipped by this PR's CI policy; they are not counted as passes. The statuses above are job outcomes, not invented test-case counts.

Local validation before squash included full TypeScript checking (including test types), 12/12 protocol compatibility cases, 7/7 public research/client regressions, 7/7 standalone service/security cases and L1 4/4. Full local UT/ST/browser-L2 attempts were interrupted by host/WSL issues and did not produce complete passing summaries; the complete passing UT/ST/browser-L2 results above are from GitHub Actions. The squashed candidate has the identical source tree as the preceding validated head (`6101e330b75bbf6edca2747d1a981a7fd994cf94`).

## Deployment and scope

- Stop the old stack before upgrading. The maintained stack script and Docker packaging start the new service; custom supervisors must provide its process and matching URL/token configuration.
- Session ownership, chat-message writes and model-secret provisioning remain in the API control plane. Research still uses the existing run-bound LLM callback pending #102; provider API keys are not passed to the service.
- Artifact/provenance/CAS ownership remains outside this PR (#98).
- Targeted public-route, SSE and create-time message regressions are included. A complete baseline/candidate differential of all six public routes and a complete chat/agent event-stream golden trace are not claimed. These remaining broader #101 acceptance items must stay tracked explicitly rather than be inferred from green CI.

## Maintainer review and merge request

Please review and merge this PR after confirming acceptance of the independent Idea Tree service boundary: its process/port, internal token, state and settings ownership, one-time migration, and API-to-service protocol. The `needs-human` decision still requires a maintainer; this request does not claim it has already been approved.

The current CI gates and CodeCheck are green, CLA is confirmed, and the previous Draft/do-not-merge wording has been removed. Please re-review the current squashed commit and grant approval if the service boundary and the explicitly documented scope are acceptable for merge. No automatic merge has been enabled.

- `agent-ready` is not on this issue (the fork cannot apply labels, HTTP 403), so this PR is opened ahead of the 24h label window under the owner's deadline.

## Red first — `b6a87d12` (tests only)

Five tests in `services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts`. The artifact content is `"a".repeat(9) + "\u{1F600}" + "tail"` — 9 ASCII characters, then U+1F600 (two UTF-16 units), then `tail` — previewed with `maxChars = "10"`, so a code-unit cut lands between the two halves of the emoji.

1. `markdown preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair` (`markdown-source`)
2. `latex preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair` (`latex-source`)
3. `structure preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair` (`structure-source`)
4. `json-source preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair` (`json-source`, i.e. the `jsonSourceOf` path shared with `rawJson`)
5. `an ascii markdown preview still cuts at exactly maxChars` — pure ASCII must keep today's result byte for byte (`"x".repeat(10)` from 20), the guard against a code-point rewrite quietly changing ordinary text.

Each surrogate test asserts the payload `source` contains no lone surrogate (the issue's regex, `[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])|(?<![\uD800-\uDBFF])[\uDC00-\uDFFF]`) and that the cut sits on a character boundary — the whole U+1F600 is kept or dropped, never half. `totalChars` / `truncated` keep their current meaning and are asserted unchanged.

```console
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern="surrogate pair|ascii markdown preview" src/dashboard.test.ts
not ok 1 - markdown preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair
    source carries a lone surrogate: "aaaaaaaaa\ud83d"
not ok 2 - latex preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair
    source carries a lone surrogate: "aaaaaaaaa\ud83d"
not ok 3 - structure preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair
    source carries a lone surrogate: "aaaaaaaaa\ud83d"
not ok 4 - json-source preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair
    source carries a lone surrogate: "aaaaaaaaa\ud83d"
ok 5 - an ascii markdown preview still cuts at exactly maxChars
# tests 5
# pass 1
# fail 4
```

Every failing payload ends in `\ud83d`, an unpaired high surrogate: invalid UTF-16 that only the web renderer's one path patches (`SourcePreview.tsx:62` strips a trailing high surrogate), while `json-source`, `structure-source` and the raw-JSON view get no guard.

## Fix — `57146c51`

One helper, called by all four truncating paths:

```ts
function truncateAtCodePoint(text: string, maxChars: number): string {
  if (text.length <= maxChars) return text;
  const last = text.charCodeAt(maxChars - 1);
  const next = text.charCodeAt(maxChars);
  const splitsPair = last >= 0xd800 && last <= 0xdbff && next >= 0xdc00 && next <= 0xdfff;
  return text.slice(0, splitsPair ? maxChars - 1 : maxChars);
}
```

Call sites: markdown (`:465`), latex (`:477`), structure (`:521`) and `jsonSourceOf` (`:322`). A character that would straddle the cut is dropped whole, so `source.length <= maxChars` still holds and `totalChars` / `truncated` keep their existing code-unit meaning — the structure flag (`charTruncated || atomTruncated`) is untouched, and `#659`'s flag change stays Dev-2's PR.

```console
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts
# tests 36
# pass 36
# fail 0

$ node_modules/.bin/tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit
$ echo $?
0
```

## Ran / Not run

- Ran: `node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts` → 36/36; targeted pattern → 5/5; `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` → exit 0.
- Not run: repo-wide `pnpm` pipelines (one module and its tests); CI covers UT/ST/E2E on this tip.

## Out of scope

- `#659` / `#655`: the structure truncation flag — different hunk, Dev-2's PR.
- `apps/web/src/SourcePreview.tsx:62`: the web-layer clipping patch; a separate issue if it is to be replaced by trusting the API.

Fixes #654

- Owner: Dev1
- Written-by: Dev-1
- Base: `a074172f60e5667e72ff04246316a0a41552cb46` (live `main` when the branch was cut)
- `agent-ready` is not on this issue: the label could not be applied from the fork (HTTP 403), so this PR is opened ahead of the 24h label window under the owner's deadline. Flagging it here rather than waiting.

## Red first — `cf8f3be6` (tests only)

Four tests in `services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts`, using the file's existing `createFixture` / `seedArtifact` helpers:

1. `a csv dataset preview strips the UTF-8 BOM from the first header cell` — artifact `bom.csv`, `text/csv`, content `"\uFEFFname,note\nAlice,1\n"`; asserts `columns` deep-equals `["name","note"]`, `totalRows === 1`, `rows[0]` deep-equals `["Alice","1"]`.
2. `a tsv dataset preview strips the UTF-8 BOM from the first header cell` — same content with `\t`, `text/tab-separated-values`.
3. `a dataset preview without a BOM keeps every header cell unchanged` — both `csv` and `tsv`, no marker, columns stay `["name","note"]`; the splitting code is untouched, so this is a pure no-regression guard.
4. `a dataset preview keeps a BOM that starts a data row, because only the file prefix is a marker` — header BOM stripped, but a `U+FEFF` at the start of row 1 stays in that cell (`rows[0][0] === "\uFEFFAlice"`). This is the guard against a whole-document `replace(/\uFEFF/g, "")`, which would silently rewrite cell data.

Command (red on `a074172f`, the first three tests are the second commit's fixed tests; this is the red run of the tests-only commit):

```console
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern="BOM" src/dashboard.test.ts
not ok 1 - a csv dataset preview strips the UTF-8 BOM from the first header cell
  ---
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected

      [
    +   '﻿name',
    -   'name',
        'note'
      ]
  ...
not ok 2 - a tsv dataset preview strips the UTF-8 BOM from the first header cell
  ---
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected

      [
    +   '﻿name',
    -   'name',
        'note'
      ]
  ...
ok 3 - a dataset preview without a BOM keeps every header cell unchanged
# tests 3
# pass 1
# fail 2
```

Test 4 was added with the fix commit; red against the unfixed implementation it fails the same way (`columns[0]` is `'﻿name'`), and it is the assertion that a global replace would break.

The BOM is an encoding marker written by Excel's "CSV UTF-8", not part of the first header cell; a client matching headers by name currently misses that column.

## Fix — `b51dc91e`

Strip exactly one `U+FEFF` at the start of the record text, inside `splitDelimited` (`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts:246`), the path both `.csv` and `.tsv` share. It is a single `startsWith` + `slice(1)`, not a global replace: a `U+FEFF` anywhere else in the document is ordinary cell data (test 4 above).

Field splitting and quoting are deliberately untouched: `#650`/`#653` own the quote state machine, and this PR only handles the encoding prefix.

```console
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts
# tests 35
# pass 35
# fail 0

$ node_modules/.bin/tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit
$ echo $?
0
```

items.body:
Closes #666

## Summary

Imports the Windows desktop shell as a new top-level `win_desktop/` directory — an Electron 37 application that owns the backend stack lifecycle, drives the assisted first-run wizard, loads the web UI with the local access token injected, and packages the backend tree into a per-user NSIS installer.

- **Standalone workspace**: own `pnpm-workspace.yaml` + lockfile. The root workspace globs (`config`, `apps/*`, `services/*`, `packages/*`) do not match `win_desktop/`, so root-level workspace behavior is untouched; the one dependency patch (`app-builder-lib@26.15.3`, NSIS progress presentation) is confined to `win_desktop/patches/`.
- **src/** — main process; wizard (data-dir choice: warn at 180 path chars, block past 240, mirrored for the uninstaller); stack orchestration + bootstrap (payload path substitution, venv preparation); bind-probing port epochs; token-injecting proxy + preload; loading stage with heartbeat mapping; window state; retry helpers.
- **test/** — 14 `node:test` suites, no Electron launch required.
- **scripts/** — esbuild build, dev runner, `assemble-backend.mjs` (stages this repo's backend into `build/resources` — `--repo` overrides — rewrites venv trampolines to the install layout, compiles the payload), icon generator.
- **build/** — NSIS include (plain-release presentation, install diagnostics into `$INSTDIR\logs`, clean-uninstall options, silent-never-deletes), uninstall helper (C# + PowerShell long-path removal), license, icons.

## Verification (Windows 11 23H2, Node v24.21.0)

- `pnpm -C win_desktop install` — clean; the `app-builder-lib` patch applies.
- `pnpm -C win_desktop typecheck` — exit 0.
- `pnpm -C win_desktop test` — **113/113 pass** across the 14 suites.

## Merge order

The shell compiles and tests standalone, but assembling a full installer payload stages `scripts/start-stack.mjs` / `scripts/jiuwenswarm.mjs` / `scripts/lib/stack-platform.mjs`, which arrive with the runtime PR (#644). Suggested order: #640 → #644 → this one. No file overlap with either — this PR only adds the new `win_desktop/` tree.

## Risks

- Windows-only toolchain (Electron, electron-builder, NSIS): nothing here runs in the Linux CI today; evidence is real-machine (same gap as #639/#643).
- The `app-builder-lib` patch pins NSIS progress behavior — an electron-builder major bump will need the patch re-evaluated.
- No auto-update channel yet; the payload layout is blockmap-friendly so one can be added later without repackaging.

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
Fixes #646

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

**Label note.** `agent-ready` could not be applied from this account (403 with both REST and the connector, same as #641); this PR is proposed ahead of the 24 h label window because of the owner's sprint deadline. Claim record: issue comment `6486721604`.

## What the problem is

`putWorkspaceFile` re-derived the source digest and then re-read the stored object on every cache hit, so one hit cost two full reads (`unchangedWorkspaceBytes` → `verifyRef`). At 1 MiB that was 9.404 ms median, with the two halves costing the same (source hash 4.591 ms, object hash 4.682 ms): the cost is SHA-256 throughput, not syscall overhead. `services/runner/src/execution-manager.ts:96` snapshots the workspace after every shell execution, so it was paid per execution.

The source re-hash stays. It is the only criterion that survives a same-size in-place rewrite inside one filesystem timestamp tick — that is #641, where metadata-based reuse served stale bytes in 171 of 200 iterations. The object read is the removable half: the object is content-addressed, written once through `link` + `fsync`, and this store already records what it verified in `admitted`, whose entries `checked` revokes on any integrity failure.

## Trust boundary

A `VersionStore` instance verifies a stored object once and then admits it; the source bytes are still re-hashed on every reuse, so a same-size in-place rewrite of the workspace file is still caught. An admission is evidence that *this instance* saw those bytes, not that they are still the verified ones. The admission assumes no writer outside this process changes an object after this process verified it — the same assumption `validateClosureForCommit` has relied on since before this change. Every path that hands bytes to a caller re-hashes and fails closed (`Object integrity failure`), so a tampered or vanished object can never be delivered as good data; a vanished object makes the next cache hit republish it.

Attribution, so this is not read as a regression: `admitted`, and `validateClosureForCommit` skipping already-admitted objects, are pre-existing. #642 brought the source re-hash on reuse, the object verification, and `checked()` clearing admissions. This PR changes exactly one thing: `unchangedWorkspaceBytes` no longer calls `verifyRef` for an already-admitted ref (`packages/cas/src/versioning.ts:146-152`), turning per-reuse verification into per-instance verification, with the #641 fix untouched. A size/mtime shortcut was deliberately not added, and the admission was deliberately not narrowed to a single snapshot or put sequence: the first would reopen the blind spot #642 closed, the second would remove the benefit this PR exists for.

Known limitation, deliberately kept: an admission means only that this instance saw those bytes. Existence is re-checked on every admitted read; content is not. A same-size, same-mtime replacement of an *object* is therefore not detected by the admission itself, and surfaces only as a fail-closed error (`ENOENT` or `Object integrity failure`) at the next read, audit or new-instance rehash that touches those bytes. On the commit path (`validateReachable` with `trustAdmitted`, used by `validateClosureForCommit`) an admitted record is stopped at that existence check: its bytes, and the closure behind them, are not re-read, so a replaced-but-present record is accepted by the commit and fails closed only when something later calls `read` / `readRecord` / `validateClosure` on it. That skip of already-admitted objects is pre-existing — this PR only puts the existence check in front of it. The admission can never make a tampered object be delivered as good data.

## Commits

- `1889093442a7db831c2a22c2932df2387fe0c063` — the red test only: `a cache hit does not re-read the stored object on every call`.
- `f54ef875a78db25f58ad294528b83badf04d4d17` — the fix: admit the object after its first successful `verifyRef` and skip the re-read afterwards (one verification per object per store instance), and document that in `putWorkspaceFile`/`unchangedWorkspaceBytes`.
- `32c45733f7b083c2a3fccaef0cf45670513e4f86` — follow-up to the reviewer finding: a cache hit `stat`s the admitted object before trusting the admission, so a blob that disappeared under a live process falls back to the existing `return undefined` → republish path, plus the regression test for it.

- `da2036e653c1907759816d885405a37885db61f1` — red tests for the second admitted reader: the fail-closed read assertion in the republish case, and a case where an admitted root is removed before the next ref commit.
- `37fb64bdbf673e2b187a3d9aef3883741e2a5075` — the fix for it: one shared `dropIfVanished` helper, called before trusting an admission in **both** readers.

All five commits are on the head branch, in order, each on top of its predecessor; `git fetch` of a bare SHA needs the fork remote or `refs/pull/657/head`. No amend, no force-push.

## Red → green

```bash
cd packages/cas
node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "cache hit does not re-read" src/versioning.test.ts
```

Before (`a074172f` + the red-test commit):

```
  error: |-
    the stored object is verified once per store instance, not once per cache hit

  expected: 1
  actual: 2
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

After (this tip):

```
# pass 1
# fail 0
```

The test also rewrites the file in place afterwards and asserts a new digest is published, so the source re-hash cannot be traded away for the object cache.

Second pair, for the commit path (`da2036e6` red, `37fb64bd` green):

```bash
cd packages/cas
node --import tsx --test src/versioning.test.ts
```

Before (`32c45733` + the red test commit): **18 tests, 17 pass, 1 fail**

```
# Subtest: a ref commit re-verifies an admitted object that disappeared instead of trusting the admission
not ok 18 - a ref commit re-verifies an admitted object that disappeared instead of trusting the admission
  error: 'Missing expected rejection.'
  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
# pass 17
# fail 1
```

After (this tip): **18 tests, 18 pass, 0 fail** in that file, and `src/**/*.test.ts` is **39/39 pass, 0 fail**.

## Cost, measured

Harness: node v22.23.2, single thread, ext4, page-cache warm, 25 iterations after 3 warm-ups, one `putWorkspaceFile` cache hit, median / max in ms.

| file | before (`a074172f`) | after (this tip) | source-hash-only lower bound |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 KiB | 1.202 / 2.225 | 0.617 / 1.467 | 0.596 / 0.788 |
| 1 MiB | 9.404 / 11.050 | 4.748 / 5.339 | 4.701 / 5.167 |
| 8 MiB | 68.317 / 71.872 | 34.062 / 35.194 | 34.103 / 48.020 |

After the fix the hit cost sits on the source hash, i.e. the second read is gone. Aggregate through the real `snapshotWorkspace` on a 64 × 1 MiB workspace, all hits: **588.4 ms → 309.4 ms**. A repeat run on a loaded machine inflated both the after column and the source-only bound by the same factor (9.06 / 9.10 ms at 1 MiB), which is the expected shape when only one read remains.

## Review finding: an admission outlived its object

`sciencediscovery-bot` (review `5692570203`, inline `4408458539`, `versioning.ts:147`, Medium) showed that the admission turned "verified on every hit" into "verified once per process": if the blob disappears while the process lives, the next cache hit reuses the ref instead of republishing, and a record can be committed pointing at a missing object.

Reproduced on `f54ef875` and on `a074172f` with the same probe (put → put → `rm` blob → put → `readData`):

| step | `a074172f` | `f54ef875` |
|---|---|---|
| `BLOB_RESTORED` after the third put | `true` | `false` |
| `readData(ref)` | `OK` | `ENOENT` |

Fix: before trusting an admission, `stat` the object (`ENOENT` → the existing `return undefined` → republish branch). One syscall against a source re-hash that is milliseconds per hit. Regression test: `a cache hit republishes a stored object that disappeared after its first verification` — red on `f54ef875` (`expected: true / actual: false` at the post-republish `existsSync`), green after the `stat`.

Security follow-up (same review, wider scope): the existence check was only on the put path, while `admitted` has two readers — `unchangedWorkspaceBytes` and `validateReachable` (used by `validateClosureForCommit`). Removing an already-admitted record and committing without an intervening put therefore still produced a version that pointed at missing bytes. `dropIfVanished` is now shared by both, uses `lstat` + `isFile()` so an object replaced by a directory or a symlink is treated the same as a missing one, and revokes every admission exactly like `checked()` does; the commit path then reaches `readRecord`/`verifyRef`, which throws `ENOENT`. The helper is existence evidence only — it never claims the bytes are still the verified ones. Scope, so this is not read as a rewrite: `validateReachable` already skipped admitted objects on `main`, so the gap was pre-existing; this PR adds one `dropIfVanished` call at that reader rather than restructuring it. Still out of scope, as directed: a vanished *transitive dependency* of an admitted record (a different change), and any size/mtime shortcut.

## Validation

Ran:
- `cd packages/cas && node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"` on this tip: **39/39 pass, 0 fail**.
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p packages/cas/tsconfig.json` and `--noEmit`: exit 0.
- The red test on `a074172f` + the first commit (output above).

Not run locally:
- repository-wide layers (`ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e`): the pnpm wrapper aborts with `ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY` in this container; this PR's own CI run is the authority for those.

## Release

`release:fix` — label to be applied by a maintainer (labels are not writable from this account, 403).

Python started from Runner shell jobs buffers redirected stdout until process exit, leaving progress logs empty while a long-running job is active. Set PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 for sandbox, macOS launch, and direct-shell environments. Reserve the variable from persisted shell profiles and document explicit unbuffered progress logging in the Code Engineer skill.

Related to #439. This addresses log buffering and agent guidance only. The requested CPU/RSS/last-output heartbeat UI is still pending; this PR must not close the full issue.

## Validation

- Real Linux bubblewrap/Python reproduction before the fix: 0 passed, 1 failed because the live log was empty. After the fix, scientific execution and shell-session tests: 17 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, including reading stdout before releasing the waiting Python process.
- Executor and sandbox launch tests: 16 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- All selected Runner dependency projects built successfully on Linux at eea025dc3ecfaeb7f8605e22b9cfbab84f32d239.
- git diff --check: passed.
- UT, ST, and shared mocked browser E2E entry points attempted on the candidate on Windows: all fail during preparation with spawn pnpm ENOENT before selected layer tests execute. No full-suite pass is claimed.

## E2E user journeys

The regression exercises a real managed Python process launched through the Runner shell sandbox, redirects stdout, reads the log while the process waits, and then releases it. This is a Runner execution-boundary test, not a browser or real-model journey. CPU/RSS heartbeat UI and a full product long-running task journey remain pending. Keep draft.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: Python children inherit unbuffered stdout/stderr so redirected progress is visible while a job is still running.
Compatibility and migration: no stored data migration. Explicit inline command environment settings remain available. Previously captured shell profiles cannot override the Runner default.

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
Fixes #662

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

**Label note.** `agent-ready` could not be applied from this account (403); this PR is proposed ahead of the 24 h label window because of the owner's sprint deadline. Claim record: Lead's pickup-ok on #662 — issue comment 6487523184.

## The defect

`ipv6Blocked` (`packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts:58-69`) extracted an embedded IPv4 only from a dotted-quad tail. IPv4-mapped and IPv4-compatible IPv6 literals written in hex carry no dots, so they fell through to `return false`; `isBlockedAddress` then reported them as public and `assertPublicUrl` accepted them. `web_fetch` takes a model-supplied URL, so this is the SSRF gate itself, not a downstream check.

## What changes

- Expand the IPv6 literal to its eight hextets (compressed `::` and full form both).
- When the address is IPv4-mapped (80 zero bits, then `ffff`) or IPv4-compatible (96 zero bits), rebuild the dotted quad from the last two hextets and hand it to the existing `ipv4Blocked`.
- `ipv4Blocked` and the existing dotted-quad path are untouched; public IPv6 keeps being accepted.

## Commits

- `b9a10c6b1aac5554c6382bee030156f335de871e` — red tests for the hex mapped/compatible literals and the reverse direction.
- `b3d6112fbb228f3787816a6014f0410882b9240d` — red tests for delegation to the existing IPv4 range table and for the resolver path.
- `fc803262da45092ccc184bc27f9c38c9569db00a` — the guard change above.

No amend, no force-push.

## Tests

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/providers.test.ts`:

- `web_fetch judges IPv4-mapped and IPv4-compatible IPv6 literals by their embedded IPv4` — hex mapped and compatible literals are blocked, including the full eight-hextet spelling; the gate rejects them; the dotted-quad path keeps its behaviour.
- Reverse direction in the same test: public mapped and compatible forms stay unblocked and the gate still accepts them, so the change cannot become an over-block.
- Delegation in the same test: embedded addresses outside the `127/10/192.168` prefixes (carrier-grade NAT, benchmarking) are blocked, proving the judgement is delegated to the existing IPv4 range table rather than re-implemented.
- `web_fetch applies the same judgement to resolved addresses, not only literals` — a resolver returning a mapped literal must reject, so the DNS path stays covered.

Before (red-test commits, on `a074172f`):

```
not ok 1 - web_fetch judges IPv4-mapped and IPv4-compatible IPv6 literals by their embedded IPv4
  error: |-
    false !== true
# pass 0
# fail 1

not ok 2 - web_fetch applies the same judgement to resolved addresses, not only literals
  error: 'Missing expected rejection (PublicUrlError).'
# pass 0
# fail 2
```

After (fix commit):

```
# tests 15
# pass 15
# fail 0
```

## Out of scope

The guard still does not decode embedded IPv4 from NAT64 (`64:ff9b::/96` and `64:ff9b:1::/48`), 6to4 (`2002::/16`), Teredo (`2001::/32`), the IPv4-translated range (`::ffff:0:0:0/96`) or the deprecated site-local range (`fec0::/10`). Those are a separate next fix; this PR does not claim the gate is fully closed.

What this change closes: the two spellings that need no translator to reach a target, namely IPv4-mapped (`::ffff:a.b.c.d` in hex) and IPv4-compatible (`::a.b.c.d` in hex), on both the literal path and the resolved-address path. What it does not close: any address family that only reaches a target through a gateway or translator, listed above. Keeping the judgement delegated to the existing IPv4 range table is what makes the next fix a decoder addition rather than a second policy.

## Validation

Ran:
- `cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/web/native/providers.test.ts` — **15/15 pass, 0 fail**.
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p packages/data-source/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.

Not run locally: repository-wide layers (`ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e`), because the pnpm wrapper aborts with `ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY` in this container; this PR's own CI run is the authority for those.

Fixes #647

Owner: Dev1
Written-by: Dev-1
Branch: `dev1/fix/647-web-test-module-resolution`

## Problem

A clean tree cannot run the web test suite. Every workspace package publishes its runtime entry from `dist/` (`packages/*/package.json` → `"default": "./dist/*.js"`) and no `dist/` is committed, so a package-level run that does not build first resolves those imports to files that do not exist:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx
# tests 448
# pass 385
# fail 63
# Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../apps/web/node_modules/@sciencediscovery/operational-logging/dist/diagnostics.js'
#   imported from .../apps/web/src/ErrorDiagnosticActions.tsx
# Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../@sciencediscovery/schema/dist/index.js'
#   imported from .../apps/web/src/Markdown.tsx
```

The repo's own `pnpm test` hides this because it runs `pnpm build` first; the per-package script (`tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx`) does not. The 63 victims are not defects — they fail at import time, before any assertion runs.

The failure is not specific to `operational-logging`: `schema`, `skill`, `plugin-sdk` and their transitive workspace dependencies fail the same way.

## Commits (red first)

1. `test(web): prove the suite dies when the workspace packages are unbuilt` — one test asserting that every `@sciencediscovery/*` entry the web app imports resolves to a file that exists. Red on the unbuilt tree:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/workspace-package-dist.test.ts
not ok 1 - every workspace package the web app imports resolves from its built entry
  error: '@sciencediscovery/artifact-json/manifest resolves to
   .../apps/web/node_modules/@sciencediscovery/artifact-json/dist/manifest.js,
   which does not exist; the workspace packages need building first'
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

Full suite on the same tree: **449 tests / 385 pass / 64 fail** (63 pre-existing + this one).

2. `fix(web): build the workspace packages the test suite imports` — `apps/web`'s `test` script now runs `scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs .` before `tsx --test`. The script walks `apps/web`'s workspace dependencies transitively and builds only the packages whose `dist/` is missing, using the repo's `typescript` and each package's own `tsconfig.json` — exactly what `pnpm build` would produce. It is a no-op once they are built, so the CI path that already ran `pnpm build` pays one directory listing and nothing else.

No test file is modified, and production resolution is untouched: the runtime entry stays `dist/`, which `node dist/server.js` and vite both need.

3. `test(scripts): pin the ensure-workspace-dist skip and build order` — the builder had no test of its own behaviour. Two cases run against a throwaway workspace (a copy of the script, fixture packages, and a stand-in `tsc` that records where it was pointed and writes the `dist/` the compiler would emit, so no TypeScript build is paid for):

- a package without `dist/` is built, a package that already has `dist/` is not rebuilt (its `dist/` is left untouched), and a second run of the script is silent;
- a package is built only after everything it depends on (`leaf` → `middle` → `top`, plus an unrelated sibling, built in that order).

Both cases are green as written. Their red side is a mutation, checked locally on the working tree and not committed: dropping the `dist/` skip fails the first case (`a second run must not rebuild a built package`), and moving `ordered.push(dep)` before the dependency visit fails the second.

## Verification

Red (clean tree, before the fix) → green:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx     # no dist/
# tests 449   # pass 385   # fail 64
$ node scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs apps/web
built workspace packages without dist: @sciencediscovery/operational-logging,
@sciencediscovery/external-urls, @sciencediscovery/schema, @sciencediscovery/cas, …
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx     # deps built
# tests 1131   # pass 1131   # fail 0
```

The suite grows from 449 to 1131 because the files that could not load now run. Typechecks: `apps/web` `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` → 0; repo `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` → 0. A second run of the builder prints nothing (idempotent).

## Labels and timing

`agent-ready` could not be applied to the issue by the team (the token gets 403 on label writes) and the owner's 60-minute deadline takes precedence over the usual 24-hour wait, so this is pushed ahead of the label being restored.

## Ran

- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/workspace-package-dist.test.ts` → 0/1 before the fix, 1/1 after
- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` → 385/449 before, **1131/1131 after**
- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` → 0
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` (repo root) → 0
- `node scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs apps/web` twice → 17 packages the first time, silent the second
- `node --test scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.test.mjs` → 2/2, and the same two cases fail under the two mutations above
- `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` → 70/71: the one failure is `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`, which shells out to `uv` and dies on the read-only `~/.cache/uv` on this host, unrelated to this change
- `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check` → `CI test catalog OK: 7 cases, 24 tags, 4 layers`

## Not run

- The shared tagged plan end to end (`node test/support/tagged/shared.mjs list`): on this tree it stops during collection with `DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION: apps/web/tests/markdown-math.test.ts:16`, a file this branch does not touch and which fails the same way alone at the base commit. The new file was collected on its own instead (`node-collect.mjs` → 2 cases, `category:ut`).
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` verbatim: on this host pnpm's dependency-status check aborts with `ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY` / `EROFS` on the pnpm store (outside the workspace, read-only), so the script's two commands were run directly, in order.

items.body:
﻿Closes #643

> **Note on the diff size**: this branch sits on top of the platform-facade PR (#640), so the diff against `main` currently shows both (~5,100 lines). Once #640 merges, GitHub collapses the shared commits automatically and this PR shows the runtime-only delta (~3,480 lines). Review the platform-facade part under #640; everything below describes the runtime half.

## Summary

This PR delivers the runtime layer of the Windows desktop effort (#400): the startup chain, the execution-provider routing layer, win-64 micromamba environments, and fail-closed permission semantics. It is the runtime half of the closed #478, re-landed per that review's feedback — typecheck green, focused scope, no unresolved internal references, Windows evidence attached.

## What lands

### Native startup chain

`scripts/lib/stack-platform.mjs` is the single platform dispatch point for stack orchestration; `scripts/jiuwenswarm.mjs` is the JiuwenSwarm launcher (wall-clock deadline, TCP-first probing, exec timeouts, heartbeat logging, first-start diagnostics, uv-trampoline bypass via `entry_points.txt`, lazy start, `SCIENCE_AGENT_ENVS_DIR`); `scripts/start-stack.mjs` runs the stack natively on Windows in both source and packaged mode (the NSIS payload path). Both the launcher and the platform layer ship `node:test` suites (23 + 13 tests) so the behavior is pinned, not folklore.

### Execution router

`packages/execution-router` — provider registry, capability probing, downgrade messaging — layered **on top of** the sandbox enum per #400's root decision ("new code is layered on top, so upstream merges continue to apply"). Probing reuses the runner's `/execution-capability` and `/health`; no new wire format. The downgrade hook tightens every `always_allow` session to `ask_for_dangerous` through `setApprovalMode` + `publishApprovalModeChange` (Permission Epoch semantics, server-side). Wired into api bootstrap and `POST /api/execution-provider`.

### Micromamba win-64 environments

Environment-store platform hooks (starter specs, interpreter paths, package-install guidance with win-64 alternatives), launcher preflight, `SandboxKind "none"` in the schema, `scripts/fetch-managed-micromamba.mjs` win-64 pinning. Direct execution can run Python out of the box — the M1 exit criterion ("never touching WSL") depends on this.

### Fail-closed unsandboxed execution

Workspace allowlist via `SCIENCE_RUNNER_EXTRA_WORKSPACE_ROOTS`; the default network policy is a deny-all gateway with audited denials; persistent shell sessions refuse without a sandbox (ephemeral shell runs through the environment's m2-bash — renamed `executeEnvironmentShell` to avoid colliding with main's exported `executeDirectShell`); readiness reports `"none"` honestly. Also: MCP node-client now connects enabled stdio servers concurrently instead of as a serial sum.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/runner typecheck && test` — exit 0, **46 pass + 1 skip** on Windows 11 23H2 / Node v24.21.0. The skip is the m2-bash copy test on machines whose only `bash.exe` is the WindowsApps WSL stub (zero-byte launcher, not copyable); the test now probes for a real bash and skips cleanly instead of failing.
- `node --test scripts/jiuwenswarm-startup.test.mjs scripts/stack-platform.test.mjs` — 13 + 23 pass.
- api execution-provider / agent-run / mcp node-client suites green; `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck` exit 0.
- Real-machine first-run evidence from the desktop build built on this tree: `start-stack` brings the stack healthy natively; the runner executes Python in the micromamba starter env unsandboxed under the deny-all gateway (CSV → pandas → matplotlib round-trip, exit 0, PNG written); the downgrade hook fires correctly when the sandbox capability drops.

## Risks

- Windows-only code paths run only on Windows hosts (CI is Linux-only today, the same gap #482 documents); posix defaults are untouched by construction.
- Provider B (WSL sandbox plugin) remains a stub — direct execution is the only registered Windows provider, which is the intended M1 state.
- `pnpm-lock.yaml` and api's `package.json` gain the `@sciencediscovery/execution-router` workspace dependency; `dist/` is not committed, so CI must build before running tests that import it (the same order upstream CI already uses for other packages).

Part of #400. Supersedes the runtime half of the closed #478 with its review feedback addressed.

items.author: qingkwl
items.body:
Closes #639

## Summary

This PR delivers the platform layer of the Windows desktop effort (#400): OS-adaptation facades for three core packages, plus Windows build support. It is the platform half of the closed #478, re-landed per that review's feedback — typecheck green, focused scope (platform-only, no consumer rewrites), no unresolved internal references, and Windows evidence attached. The runtime consumers (startup chain, execution router, micromamba, permissions) follow as a separate PR stacked on this branch.

## What lands

### Runner facade (`services/runner/src/platform/`)

`terminateTree` — win32 `taskkill /T /F`, posix SIGKILL passthrough (the runner half of #482); `restrictToOwner` — icacls-based owner-only enforcement where the server previously relied on `chmod 0600`; conda delay-load DLL paths and m2-bash shell location helpers. `killSandboxProcess` and the server-side 0600 semantics route through the facade.

### API facade (`services/api/src/platform/os/`)

`restrictToOwner` (SID-based icacls grantee), `renameReplace` (retry/backoff for the transient EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY that AV and indexer tools cause on Windows renames), and DPAPI secret wrapping with a self-describing blob prefix (`wrapSecret`/`unwrapSecret`/`isWrappedSecret`; posix is identity). `loadOrCreateModelSecretKey` persists the master key through the facade and restricts the key file to its owner — the #400 decision ("model keys are stored with DPAPI" on Windows).

### CAS facade (`packages/cas/src/platform/`)

Directory durability through the facade (posix: fsync; win32: documented no-op — NTFS has no directory-fsync semantics and durability relies on volume-level policy) and `lockFileName` (posix keeps the historical full-length digest so coordination files written by main keep working; win32 shortens to 128 bits for MAX_PATH headroom, since SQLite's `-journal` suffix pushed 64-hex names past 260). `versioning`/`workspace-lease`/`workspace-lifecycle` route through the facade; docs in both languages state the Windows semantics (#478's review asked for exactly this).

### Build support

`scripts/build-windows.md` — the Windows build guide; `check-architecture.mjs` keeps forward slashes in source paths (Windows fix).

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/{runner,api,cas} typecheck` — exit 0.
- All eight platform/secrets `node:test` suites — **29/29 pass on Windows 11 23H2, Node v24.21.0**, including a **real DPAPI wrap/unwrap round-trip**, icacls owner-only assertions, a real win32 workspace-lease check, and a **tree-kill against a live child+grandchild pair** (the exact evidence #482's Case 1 asks for, which Linux CI cannot produce).
- cas build + tests green; posix files are passthroughs by construction, so Linux behavior is unchanged.
- The lock-name split is deliberate: existing posix coordination files from main keep working; there are no existing win32 files to migrate.

## Risks

- Windows code paths execute only on Windows hosts; CI is Linux-only today (#482's finding 4), so the suites above are real-machine evidence rather than CI artifacts.
- The win32 directory sync is a no-op — this is documented in EN+ZH docs and in the facade itself; durability relies on volume-level policy.
- The DPAPI blob format is internal to the facade (no persisted blobs exist in main, no compatibility promise needed).

Part of #400. Supersedes the platform half of the closed #478 with its review feedback addressed.

Inherited standalone JiuwenSwarm settings could redirect ScienceDiscovery setup to another instance and overwrite its configuration. This change keeps the existing variable names but requires `SCIENCE_AGENT_JIUWENSWARM_OVERRIDES=1` to enable documented overrides, isolates SDK child environments, and resolves stack endpoints from the SD-owned instance. It also adds a reusable Docker persisted-volume restart journey.

Closes #592. Refs #593 — every acceptance case of #593 is re-verified on this tip (see the journey table); the issue stays open because it still carries `needs-human` for the sanctioned-override policy that this pull request proposes as a breaking change, so closing it is left to the maintainers reviewing it.

## Behavior and compatibility

- Ignore inherited `JIUWENSWARM_*` controls unless explicitly enabled; even then, forward only documented controls.
- Give SDK processes an SD-owned home and a limited OS/proxy environment. The packaged launcher also strips standalone runtime controls and injects its own adapter endpoints.
- Refuse setup/start/status/env/stop against an existing custom SDK runtime without the SD ownership marker. Do not migrate or delete ambiguous standalone state. Preserve the established SD default and Docker persisted layouts.
- Keep ownership state after an invalid setup value so a subsequent corrected setup can recover.
- Update internal callers, Compose examples and deployment documentation. Direct adapter startup with the JiuwenSwarm executor requires opt-in and both explicit endpoints.

## Baseline and tested versions

- Baseline main: `863969c2265a0645aa4d5333e0a8f7d0cae59a1f` (this branch is rebased onto it; the previous base was `76b5a44fcc814a5a69adddb8659eccd2afecc0c9`).
- PR head: `20d8209435224a37ad2e88bd156fca5c194b8f64`.
- Product/build snapshot and every journey driver: `20d820943`. All numbers below come from runs on that SHA, except where a baseline row is labelled as such.
- Validation ran on Linux amd64 with a container engine (Docker 29.9.2), a pinned JiuwenSwarm install at tag `workswarm0.2.6`, and a separate detached worktree on unmodified `origin/main` for the baseline comparison.

## Acceptance and real-service journeys

| Issue / scenario | Entry point and assertions | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #593 inherited env and SDK discovery | `test/api/embedded-swarm-coexistence.py`: pollute home/install/config/data/endpoints/context controls and credentials; repeated default setup must leave standalone configuration unchanged | PASS |
| #593 identifiable same-name standalone configuration | Give standalone different model and agent settings plus a distinct skill; edit those settings while both instances are live; SD configuration, skill visibility and session identity remain separate | PASS |
| #593 occupied ports and endpoint ownership | Run both startup orders with initially overlapping ports; require distinct live PIDs and port groups, correct status/env endpoints and disjoint session lists | PASS |
| #593 independent lifecycle and logs | Repeated setup/start and both shutdown orders preserve the sibling process/state; wrapper log stays in SD's root | PASS |
| #593 supported overrides and refusal | All five lifecycle actions refuse an unowned existing standalone root. A fresh explicitly enabled SD root supports repeated setup, context changes, invalid-value recovery, start/status/env/stop | PASS |
| #592 default Docker persisted restart | `test/api/embedded-swarm-docker-restart.py`: record registry/endpoints, create a config marker and persisted session, restart the same container with the same bind mount, and verify all remain while separate standalone files are unchanged | PASS |
| #592 custom persisted override | Repeat Docker journey with `SWARM_DOCKER_CUSTOM_HOME=1`, opt-in enabled and an SD-only runtime on the persisted mount | PASS |

Representative commands. The operator supplies the image and the pinned SDK source:

```bash
JIUWENSWARM_SRC=<pinned-sdk> PYTHONPATH=services/adapter/src <sdk-python> test/api/embedded-swarm-coexistence.py
SCIENCE_AGENT_IMAGE=<candidate-image> SWARM_IMAGE_REVISION=20d8209435224a37ad2e88bd156fca5c194b8f64 python3 test/api/embedded-swarm-docker-restart.py
SCIENCE_AGENT_IMAGE=<candidate-image> SWARM_IMAGE_REVISION=20d8209435224a37ad2e88bd156fca5c194b8f64 SWARM_DOCKER_CUSTOM_HOME=1 python3 test/api/embedded-swarm-docker-restart.py
```

The Docker journey co-tests standalone registry/configuration files on a separate bind mount; it does not start a live standalone service inside the container, so that observable fact is reported rather than implied. Live standalone service coexistence is verified by the separate CLI journey above.

Candidate image: `sciencediscovery:local`, manifest list `sha256:ac025c046e7f384044553c87d12e9db97c6ca14c89a2f16af9a9cdf1f0b80f68`, built from this tip with the committed `Dockerfile` and `scripts/build-swarm-wheel.sh` at the pinned `workswarm0.2.6` tag. The product Dockerfile is unchanged. Containers are removed after each run.

## Repository checks

| Command | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `pnpm ci:l1` | 4 | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 |
| `pnpm ci:ut` | 5523 | 5523 | 5514 | 9 | 0 |
| `pnpm ci:st` | 24 | 24 | 24 | 0 | 0 |
| `pnpm ci:e2e:real -- --profile merge --backend legacy` (L3) | 9 | 9 | 9 | 0 | 0 |
| `pnpm ci:e2e` (mocked browser subset) | 131 | 131 | 129 | 2 | 0 |
| Baseline `pnpm ci:ut` (`origin/main` `863969c22`) | 5520 | 5520 | 5512 | 8 | 0 |

The runner does not provide a separate blocked count in these summaries. No assertions were weakened and no identities were removed to obtain these results.

### Failure attribution

The candidate UT run has 9 failures; **8 are the same identities the unmodified baseline fails**, and the 9th is a flake that also reproduces on the baseline. The pull request touches none of these areas — its diff is confined to `scripts/`, `services/adapter/`, `services/launcher/`, `jiuwen_swarm/tests/`, `test/api/`, `test/support/`, `docker-compose.yml`, `.ci/` and the deployment docs.

| Failing identity | Baseline `origin/main` | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/cas/src/versioning.test.ts` — unchanged workspace snapshots reuse verified bytes | FAIL | FAIL |
| `packages/workspace/src/workspace.test.ts` — run_shell runs in the workspace with the host path as cwd | FAIL | FAIL |
| `packages/workspace/src/workspace.test.ts` — file tools take a path written with the host path or /workspace | FAIL | FAIL |
| `services/runner/src/scientific-execution.test.ts` — selected environment prefix, denies Python/R egress | FAIL | FAIL |
| `services/runner/src/scientific-execution.test.ts` — persistent R kernel path retains state | FAIL | FAIL |
| `services/runner/src/server.test.ts` — runner NPU Broker runs the Protenix manager workload | FAIL | FAIL |
| `services/runner/src/server.test.ts` — runner NPU Broker rewrites workspace helper directory arguments | FAIL | FAIL |
| `services/runner/src/server.test.ts` — runner NPU Broker loads allowlisted workloads from config | FAIL | FAIL |
| `packages/cas/src/versioning.test.ts` — Linux tree preserves raw names, case, symlinks, empty directories and executable bits | flaky (5 of 8 focused runs on baseline) | flaky (1 of 5 focused runs) |

Details:

- The eight shared failures are host/environment conditions in areas this pull request does not touch: the workspace and R-kernel identities depend on the sandbox and managed-environment preconditions of this host, and the NPU Broker identities require an NPU runtime that is absent here. The unmodified baseline worktree reproduces all eight.
- The ninth identity is a flake, not a regression. It passed in an earlier candidate UT run on the same SHA, and a focused rerun of `packages/cas/src/versioning.test.ts` fails intermittently on the **baseline** as well (5 of 8 iterations there, 1 of 5 on the candidate). The PR leaves `packages/cas/` untouched.
- One earlier candidate UT run additionally failed `check:research-python-ut` with `BLOCKED: need 5368709238 free bytes ... have 1207746560`. That is a free-disk precondition in `test/benchmarks/biomnibench-da/`, a directory this pull request does not touch; it passed once the host had free space.
- The L3 real slice ran with live chat-completions credentials and passed all 9 planned real identities. No credential or quota failure occurred.

The mocked browser subset's 2 failures are likewise pre-existing. Each was re-run on the unmodified baseline worktree and fails there with the identical measured values:

| Failing identity | Candidate | Baseline `origin/main` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `journey-artifact-viewer-large-screen.spec.ts` — J309 artifact viewer keeps a readable paragraph measure | `Expected: <= 760`, `Received: 767` | `Expected: <= 760`, `Received: 767` |
| `journey-model-connect-wizard.spec.ts` — model connection success, failure and config-protection flow | `Expected: < 580`, `Received: 607.234375` | `Expected: < 580`, `Received: 607.234375` |

Both are rendered-layout measurements in the web UI. This pull request changes no frontend source: its diff is confined to `scripts/`, `services/adapter/`, `services/launcher/`, `jiuwen_swarm/tests/`, `test/api/`, `test/support/`, `docker-compose.yml`, `.ci/` and the deployment docs.

## Release

Release category: `release:breaking`.

User impact: ordinary default startup keeps its existing layout. Users who intentionally set documented `JIUWENSWARM_*` overrides must add `SCIENCE_AGENT_JIUWENSWARM_OVERRIDES=1` consistently to setup/start/status/env/stop and stack startup. Custom runtime directories must be fresh or already marked as SD-owned; ambiguous standalone directories are refused. Manual adapter startup must also provide both SD-owned endpoint URLs.
