items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
Session-enabled connectors stayed listed, and the agent received none of their tools, when the MCP server was switched off or could not connect. The catalog already recorded that state. The connector list ignored it.

## Disabled servers stay out of the picker and the agent

A server that is turned off, or that never entered the resolved server table, is reported as `disabled` once a catalog has been applied. `GET /api/connectors` omits those connectors, so the composer, settings, the project form, and the specialist form no longer offer them. Tool injection is unchanged: a disabled source has no available tools, so the agent is not given `mcp__<source>__*` tools even when the session still names the connector. The MCP server settings page still shows the disabled server and its switch, so it can be turned back on. Turning it back on returns the connectors to the picker with the previous selection.

## Connection failures stay visible

An enabled server that fails to connect or to list its tools stays in the connector list. Each of its connectors carries `connectionError`: the server's error text and the time the catalog was checked. The picker shows that text under the connector. The composer control shows a failure count when a selected connector failed. A partial tool mismatch (`degraded`) and a catalog that was never refreshed are left as they were: they are not hidden, and they are not labeled as connection failures.

A direct edit of `extensions_config.json` appears after the next catalog refresh (process start, `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload`, or saving a custom server). That is the same moment the agent sees the change.

## Compatibility

When an applied catalog does not contain a server, source status is `disabled` rather than `unavailable`. The governance broker rejects a call in that case with `MCP server is disabled or not configured: <id>`. Connectors of a disabled server are absent from `GET /api/connectors`.

Related to #325.

## Validation

Recorded on `4c9baed756f8b0ebbb33eaf967197e970e07af53`.

- Typecheck for the web, api, mcp, data-source, schema, and artifact-manager packages, plus `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`: passed.
- Package tests: web 890/890, data-source 51/51, mcp-sources 28/28, schema 12/12, mcp 1/1, artifact-manager 2/2.
- `services/api`: 1128 passed, 3 failed. The failures are PDF extraction tests and exit with `spawn … ENOENT` because `services/paper/.venv` is not present in this checkout. They do not call the connector list.
- `pnpm docs:check`, `pnpm architecture:check`, and `pnpm ci:selftest` (55/55) passed. The E2E meta check reported 0 errors.

`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. Those layers provision JiuwenSwarm outside the repository tree, which this environment does not allow. This pull request is a draft until those layers have results.

## E2E user journeys

PASS for the connector journey on `4c9baed756f8b0ebbb33eaf967197e970e07af53`. Local stack, native executor, runner and API on ports 4480 and 4481.

`test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts`: 3 passed, 0 failed. Two custom MCP servers are used, one healthy and one that exits during the handshake. Both appear, and only the failing one shows its error. Turning the healthy server off removes its connector from the picker and from the next run's tool list; the settings row and switch remain. Turning it on brings the connector back, still selected.

`journey-plugin-composition`: the connector-panel step passed. A later step expects `todo_create`, which the native executor does not provide. That failure is outside this change.

The mocked `pnpm ci:e2e` layer was not run.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: connectors whose MCP server is off disappear from the picker and are not offered to the agent. A connector whose enabled server fails to connect stays listed and shows the connection error.

Compatibility and migration: callers that treated "missing from an applied catalog" as `unavailable`, or that expected those connectors to remain in `GET /api/connectors`, need to handle `disabled` and the shorter list. No configuration change is required.

![The same failure text at a narrow width](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/388977e4-55bc-42b8-9d6d-961c87f31353)

## Summary

Add all **132 DeepResearchBench II tasks** as a release-only L5 benchmark, following the existing tagged Playwright real-E2E framework. L5 now selects **151** real cases (19 inherited + 132 DRB II); L4 remains 19. No new paid cases enter PR/L2 or merge/L3 gates.

## Design and scope

- Statically declare every task identity; collection is offline and cannot silently shrink when data or credentials are absent.
- Each task receives an isolated research worker through the existing matrix/reconciliation path. Preserve original task text and blocked-source instructions; only append artifact delivery instructions. Rubrics are never research-Agent input.
- Do **not** carry over the experimental two-subagent prompt cap. Product quotas still apply and are recorded. Memory Graph is disabled for DRB II workers.
- Download upstream only at execution time: `imlrz/DeepResearch-Bench-II@b38f360603db9531b102aef8c166cedb8509b6f6`, shallow/blob-filtered/sparse checkout of necessary files, locked Python dependencies, and dataset/evaluator hash checks. No upstream dataset or report corpus is vendored. Verified local `.git` size was about 708 KB.
- Reuse upstream rubric prompts and scoring; add strict response completeness/type checks and a non-destructive JSON parser (upstream's repair regex can corrupt valid compact JSON).
- Account for upstream task 116's duplicate rubric texts: 56 raw entries / 50 distinct scored entries, matching upstream text-keyed output rather than making the task fail permanently.
- Record reports, rubric results, per-call Judge usage including retries, model/config identity and separate generation/evaluation durations. Delivery/evaluation failure fails the case; valid low scores are review evidence, **not** hidden failures or an invented quality threshold.

## Configuration and release impact

Uses the existing `nightly-ci-ds` generator/Judge settings. `DRB2_JUDGE_API_STYLE` defaults to `openai`; set it to `deepseek` for DeepSeek transport. Judge output starts at 32,768 tokens and increases on truncation up to 65,536. One Judge request at a time, 15 rubrics per batch, at most three attempts.

Generation budget: 120 minutes/task; evaluation: 30 minutes/task; existing research job ceiling: 240 minutes including preparation. The workflow retains two concurrent jobs. At 30 minutes generation/task, DRB II alone is approximately 66 worker-hours / 33 wall-clock hours, before setup and judging. **A tag-triggered release now incurs this full paid benchmark and waits for its gate.** A timeout is not a spending cap.

DRB II workers do not require DRB I, HF or Jina evaluator prerequisites. Configured research providers may separately require keys. Per-task upstream licenses still apply, notably CC BY-NC for tasks 26 and 110.

## Verification

- CI contract suite: **59/59 passed**, including new selection/sharding, prompt isolation, score completeness and mocked Judge transport tests.
- L1: **4/4 passed**.
- Actual offline Playwright collection: **151 release identities**, exactly **132 DRB II**; daily remains **19**.
- Runtime shallow/sparse preparation and pinned checks: passed.
- Local transport smoke against the **actual pinned upstream evaluator and all 132 task rubrics**, with a synthetic loopback Judge: **132/132 passed**, no LLM tokens. This proves evaluator plumbing, **not research quality**.
- E2E metadata check: 0 errors (existing legacy warnings unchanged).
- Documentation checks, lint of modified runbooks, and `git diff --check`: passed.

## Explicit limitations / not claimed

- Full 132-task paid Agent execution was **not** run as part of this PR. Prior local four-report real experiments are not a full-suite result and are not this branch's E2E verification.
- No historical quality regression threshold and no claim of official leaderboard comparability; Judge model and execution conditions matter.
- Existing session token summaries can omit intermediate/child calls and are labelled **not a billing total**. Judge calls have their own detailed usage ledger.
- This PR does not fix the existing 5-second status-poll recovery policy, long-task resource pressure, or persistence performance. Failures remain failures; assertions are not relaxed to hide them.

Runbook: `test/benchmarks/deepresearchbench-ii/README.md`.

recent_closed_unmerged.body:
A Project could be created from the sidebar but never renamed or removed, so
the name typed at creation was permanent and the only way to drop a project
was to leave the app and edit the data directory. This adds the two writes to
the project fold, using the gestures the neighbouring Session rows already
have.

## Rename from the fold, like a Session

Double-clicking a project's name opens it for editing in place, and the row's
new `⋯` menu offers 重命名 for anyone who does not guess the gesture. The row
shows the Project the server returned rather than the typed text, because the
server is what trims the name and refuses a duplicate. `Renaming` in
`Sidebar.tsx` becomes one union of "project" and "session", so only one field
is open at a time and the input, its Enter/Escape handling and its blur commit
are shared rather than duplicated.

## Delete behind the same gate a Session has

The `⋯` menu's 删除 opens a confirmation dialog — no typing the project name
back, matching the Session dialog. The body states the consequence: the
Project's Sessions, their workspaces and their artifacts go with it. Accepting
calls `DELETE /api/projects/:id` with `confirmationId`, which the server
already requires and already refuses with a 409 while one of the Project's
Sessions has an active run; that refusal reaches the user as a toast and
nothing is removed locally.

When the open conversation belonged to the deleted Project, the app moves the
active project back to the inbox and starts a draft before refreshing the
lists. Without that step the next message would be written to a Project that
no longer exists.

## Tests

`apps/desktop/tests/api-sessions.test.ts` covers the DELETE body
(`confirmationId`) and the PATCH body (`name`) as separate calls, and
`apps/desktop/tests/sidebar.test.tsx` pins the row's two menu items and the
double-click hint. The browser mock now answers `DELETE /api/projects/:id` and
enforces the confirmation-id gate, so a client that stopped repeating the id
would fail rather than pass quietly. A new `apps/desktop/e2e/projects.spec.ts`
proves renaming through a reload, cancelling and then confirming a delete, and
deleting the Project that holds the open Session — which must leave a draft
rather than a conversation whose Session is gone.

## Validation

| Layer | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm ci:ut` | 5252 planned / 5252 executed / 5250 passed / 2 failed |
| `pnpm ci:st` | 24 planned / 24 executed / 22 passed / 2 failed |
| `pnpm ci:e2e` | not completed locally — see *E2E user journeys* |
| desktop browser suite (`apps/desktop/e2e`) | 72 planned / 72 executed / 72 passed / 0 failed |
| `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` | passed |
| `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test` | 564 passed / 0 failed |

The four layer failures are outside this diff, which touches `apps/desktop`
and nothing else:

- UT `packages/executor/src/sandbox-network.test.ts` — this host's bubblewrap
  has no `--disable-userns` (`bwrap: Unknown option --disable-userns`).
- UT `services/api/src/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts` — `unable to open database
  file` while provisioning the Swarm trajectory store.
- ST `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts` — 300 s timeout while installing
  its pinned release, a download from the network.
- ST `check:swarm-sdk-contract` —
  `test_mcp_boundary.py::BoundaryTests::test_100_concurrent_calls_keep_identity_and_execute_once`
  exceeded its 3 s `client.connect()` wait under 100 concurrent calls.

The two UT failures were re-run on unmodified `upstream/main` in a detached
worktree and fail there identically. The two ST failures exercise Python
environment setup and the Swarm SDK; they were not re-run on `upstream/main`
for this pull request. The GitHub Actions layers are the authoritative run.

## E2E user journeys

BLOCKED for `pnpm ci:e2e`; PASS for the desktop subset, which is the only one
that renders this change.

Tested SHA: `91dc6ebf`, one commit on `upstream/main` `76b5a44f`. Surface:
browser (Chromium, mocked API), `apps/desktop`.

`pnpm ci:e2e` runs the mocked **web** subset: its stack serves
`apps/web/dist`, while every file in this diff is under `apps/desktop`, so the
layer executes none of the changed code. It is also red on this host for
reasons the diff cannot cause:

- The reporter's ordering guard `FRESH_JOURNEY_MUST_RUN_FIRST` fires before
  any case runs: `test/journey-approval-defaults.spec.ts` (`@isolation:global`)
  is collected before `test/journey-compact-process.spec.ts`
  (`@isolation:fresh`). Both files, and their tags, are unchanged from
  `upstream/main`; the same guard failed on a freshly reset runtime directory.
- `J309 大屏打开产物时查看器放大且正文保持可读宽度` fails
  `paragraphWidth ≤ 760` with 774. The rule is `max-width: 76ch`, and this
  host has no Inter (`fc-match Inter` → DejaVu Sans), so one `ch` is wider
  here than on the machine where 760 was measured.
- `journey-model-connect-wizard.spec.ts` also failed; it drives the web
  settings surface, which this branch does not modify.

The run was stopped after 81 of 279 cases: the outcome was already decided by
the three failures above, none of which this diff can reach.

The desktop app's own browser suite was run instead, against the same commit:

```bash
apps/desktop/e2e/node_modules/.bin/playwright test \
  --config apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts
```

| Scenario | Expected outcome | Actual outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Double-click a project name, type a new one, reload | `PATCH /api/projects/:id` with `name`; the row keeps the server's name across the reload | PASS |
| `⋯` → 删除 → cancel | nothing written; the Project and its Sessions stay | PASS |
| `⋯` → 删除 → confirm | `DELETE /api/projects/:id` with `confirmationId`; the Project is gone, and the conversation open inside it becomes a draft in the inbox | PASS |
| every other desktop journey (rename/delete regression) | unchanged | PASS — 72 of 72 cases |

Passed / failed / blocked / skipped: 72 / 0 / 0 / 0.

## Release

Release category: release:feature
The GitHub label `release:feature` is not applied: the account opening this
pull request has no write access upstream, so `AddLabelsToLabelable` is
refused. A maintainer needs to add it; without it the change lands in *Other
Changes* in the release note.
User impact: A Project can now be renamed by double-clicking its name or from
its `⋯` menu, and deleted from the same menu after a confirmation that says
what goes with it. Before this change neither write existed in the desktop
app.
Compatibility and migration: None. No API, schema or stored-data change; the
desktop app uses endpoints the server already served.

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

**Label note.** `agent-ready` could not be applied from this account (403 with both REST and the connector, same as #641/#646); this PR is proposed ahead of the 24 h label window because of the owner's sprint deadline. Claim record: Lead's pickup-ok on #651 — issue comment 6487338598.

## The defect

`jsonRecordArray` (`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts:276-281`) validated element *shape* only, so `[{}]` and `[{}, {}]` passed as record arrays. `recordArrayTable` then unioned zero keys into `columns: []`, and the preview returned `mode: "dataset-table"` with one column-less row per record — an empty grid with no way to read the document. The function's own comment already states the invariant: a shape with no row/column mapping must be shown as JSON text.

## What changes

- After the shape filter, require at least one key across the records: `records.some((record) => Object.keys(record).length > 0)`.
- `[{}, {}]` and `[{}]` now route to `json-source` (re-indented document); record arrays with keys keep the table unchanged.
- Single file, no schema change.

## Commits

- `ffea066d0dc58dd74fe49e4949c04b0861e84f6f` — the red tests only: empty-object arrays must render as JSON text, and record arrays with keys must keep the table.
- `fdfce937e0bd9f3524901477ed03653d11be6cf2` — the fix in `jsonRecordArray`.

No amend, no force-push; the fix commit is appended on top.

## Red → green

Tests in `services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts`:

- `a json artifact of empty objects renders as JSON text, not an empty grid` — `[{}, {}]` and `[{}]` must be `json-source` with `source === JSON.stringify(records, null, 2)`.
- `json preview keeps the table when record arrays carry keys` — `[{a:1},{a:2}]` stays `dataset-table` with `columns: ["a"]`, so the guard cannot swallow real tables.

cd services/api
node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "empty objects|carry keys" src/dashboard.test.ts
```

Before (this red-test commit, on `a074172f`):

not ok 1 - a json artifact of empty objects renders as JSON text, not an empty grid
  error: 'empty-two.json: unexpected mode dataset-table'
  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
# pass 1
# fail 1
```

## Validation

Ran on the red-test commit: the command above — `pass 1 / fail 1`, the failure being the empty-object case; the table guard already passed.

Ran on the fix commit (`fdfce937`):

Fixes #655

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

**Label note.** `agent-ready` could not be applied from this account (403 with both REST and the connector, same as #641/#646); this PR is proposed ahead of the 24 h label window because of the owner's sprint deadline. Claim record: issue comment `6487305186`.

## The defect

The structure preview folds the atom budget into the truncation flag (`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts:498-508`): `truncated: charTruncated || atomTruncated`, but only `charTruncated` controls the slice. A 9 000-atom PDB under `maxChars` is returned in full while `truncated` is `true`, so the UI claims a truncated preview and the atom budget is never explained. `source` and `truncated` must agree.

## What changes

- `truncated` follows the bytes actually removed: `truncated: charTruncated`.
- The atom budget is no longer disguised as truncation, and no new field is invented for it: `atomCount` is
  still reported, and the structure viewer applies its own atom budget. The payload type stays unchanged, so
  the red test asserts only `truncated` and `source` (the earlier `note` assertion was removed rather than
  propped up with a cast).
- `atomCount` and `totalChars` are unchanged.

## Commits

- `d6aa264768f0d02daecf60b858acb55f7ebfd234` — the red tests only (three cases: complete return, real `maxChars` cut, exact boundary).
- `92e99117aa38923b9739792ef69077d5bf69b784` — the fix: `truncated: charTruncated`; the atom budget no longer marks a complete payload as truncated. It also drops the now-unused `STRUCTURE_ATOM_TRUNCATION` constant and the one note assertion from the red test, because the payload type is intentionally left unchanged.

Both commits are on the head branch; no amend, no force-push.

## Red → green

Three tests in `services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts`:

- `structure preview does not claim truncation when the whole source is returned` — 9 000 atoms, `maxChars=1000000`: full source, `truncated === false` (before: `true !== false`).
- `structure preview reports truncation when maxChars cuts the source` — 200 atoms, `maxChars=400`: `truncated === true` and `source === pdb.slice(0, 400)`, so the flag cannot be pinned to `false`.
- `structure preview at exactly maxChars returns the whole source without truncation` — 100-char source, `maxChars=100`: no cut, `truncated === false`.

```bash
cd services/api
node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "structure preview" src/dashboard.test.ts
```

Before (this red-test commit, on `a074172f`):

```
# Subtest: structure preview does not claim truncation when the whole source is returned
not ok 3 - structure preview does not claim truncation when the whole source is returned
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly equal:

    true !== false

  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
  expected: false
  actual: true
# pass 4
# fail 1
```

## Validation

Ran on the red-test commit: the command above — `pass 4 / fail 1`, the failure being the new whole-source case.

Ran on the fix commit (`92e99117`):

Not run locally: repository-wide layers (`ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e`), because the pnpm wrapper aborts with `ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY` in this container; this PR's own CI run is the authority for those.

Fixes #649

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

**Label note.** `agent-ready` could not be applied from this account (403 with both REST and the connector, same as #641); this PR is proposed ahead of the 24 h label window because of the owner's 60-minute deadline. Claim record: issue comment `6487087449`.

## The defect

`parseNotebook` (`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts:373-408`) truncated `rawCells.slice(0, maxCells)` *before* dropping cell types the preview does not support, so a `heading` cell (or a malformed entry) consumed the budget and was then discarded: `maxCells=2` over `[heading, code, code]` returned one cell instead of two. `truncated: totalCells > maxCells` inherited the same mistake — it reported truncation against the raw cell count even when every supported cell was on screen.

## What changes

- Map and filter to supported cells first, then `slice(0, maxCells)` the supported list, so unsupported entries never consume the budget.
- Derive `truncated` from the supported count, so dropping an unsupported cell is no longer reported as truncation.
- `totalCells` keeps counting every raw cell, because it describes the document, not the preview budget.

## Red → green

Test: `notebook preview fills maxCells with valid cells after skipping unsupported cell types` — `cells=[heading, code, code]`, `maxCells=2`; it asserts `totalCells===3`, two visible cells, both `code`, and `truncated===false`.

```bash

node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "notebook preview" src/dashboard.test.ts
```

Before (red-test commit `d462439d`, first tip on this branch):

```
  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
  name: 'AssertionError'
  expected: 2
  actual: 1
  operator: 'strictEqual'
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

After (this tip):

```
# pass 3
# fail 0
```

## Validation

Ran:
- `node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts` in `services/api`: **32/32 pass, 0 fail**.
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: exit 0.

Not run locally:
- repository-wide layers (`ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e`): the pnpm wrapper aborts with `ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY` in this container; this PR's own CI run is the authority for those.

## Release

`release:fix` — label to be applied by a maintainer (labels are not writable from this account, 403).

## Known limitation (recorded, not fixed here)

`maxCells` is no longer a work bound for `parseNotebook`. The previous code mapped only the first `maxCells` raw cells; this change maps every raw cell and then filters to the supported ones, so the work scales with the whole notebook and array-form `source` values are joined once per cell.

Measured on extracted copies of the two implementations, 100k cells: array-form source 145 ms / +44 MB before, 200 ms / +75 MB after; string-form source 69 ms / +26 MB before, 93 ms / +38 MB after. That is a linear 1.5-1.7x, with no cliff and no new unbounded path, so it is recorded rather than fixed in this pull request.

If `maxCells` has to bound the work again, the shape to use is a single scan that stops as soon as `maxCells + 1` supported cells have been collected, keeping `totalCells` as the raw count so `truncated` stays accurate.

recent_merged.body:
Fixes #650

Owner: Dev1
Written-by: Dev-1
Branch: `dev1/fix/650-csv-quoted-cells`

## Problem

The dataset preview splits `.csv`/`.tsv` text on raw newlines and then on the raw delimiter, with no quote state:

```ts
// services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts:246 before this change
function splitDelimited(source: string, delimiter: RegExp): string[][] {
  return source.split(/\r?\n/).filter((line) => line.length > 0).map((line) => line.split(delimiter));
}
```

So an RFC 4180 field that contains the delimiter, a newline, or a doubled quote breaks the table: the quoted cell is split into extra columns, and a newline inside quotes inflates `totalRows` and shifts every later row. Any spreadsheet the user exports with a comma in a cell is shown mangled.

## Commits (red first)

1. `test(api): prove quoted csv cells shift columns in the dataset preview` — durable test in `services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts`, input `name,note` / `Alice,"hello, world"` / `Bob,"say ""hi"""`. Red on the unbuilt fix:

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern="parses quoted csv cells" src/dashboard.test.ts
not ok 1 - dataset preview parses quoted csv cells
  Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
  + actual - expected
    [
      'Alice',
  +   '"hello',
  +   ' world"'
  -   'hello, world'
    ]
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

2. `fix(api): split csv and tsv records with quote state` — `splitDelimited` walks the text once with a quote state: a delimiter or newline inside quotes stays in the field, `""` inside quotes is one `"`, a quote opens a field only at its start (so an apostrophe or a quote mid-cell is left alone), CRLF and a trailing newline are handled, and blank lines are still dropped. `parseDelimitedTable` now passes the delimiter as a string (`,` / `\t`). `totalRows`, `truncated` and the row limit keep their meaning; `parseNotebook` and everything else in the file are untouched.

## Verification

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts
# tests 32   # pass 32   # fail 0

$ node_modules/.bin/tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit
exit 0
```

Two cases checked against the built preview with a throwaway copy of the test file (not committed), because they are not in the issue's assertions: a quoted newline stays one cell and `totalRows` counts records (`Alice,"line one\nline two"` with CRLF line endings → 2 rows, row 0 is `["Alice", "line one\nline two"]`), and a TSV quoted tab stays one cell while a blank line in the middle of the file is dropped (2 rows).

## Labels and timing

`agent-ready` cannot be applied to the issue by the team (the token gets 403 on label writes) and the owner's deadline takes precedence over the usual 24-hour wait, so this is pushed ahead of the label being restored.

## Perf follow-up — `5f946116` (spans, not per-character concatenation)

The quote state machine above built every field with `field += char`. An unclosed quote makes the whole file one field, so one malformed csv built one string node per character: Security measured **8 MB → 1.27 s / 359 MB RSS, 16 MB → 4.67 s / 628 MB, 32 MB → 6.27 s / 1.17 GB** on `29a49360`, against 17–58 ms / 68–76 MB for the pre-#650 splitter — 30–100× CPU and 15–35× memory, i.e. seconds of blocked event loop from a single preview request over unauthenticated content.

The field is now kept as spans of the source and joined once when it ends: an ordinary run is a single `slice`, and only an escaped quote (`""`) closes a span early. The state machine, the blank-line rule and `totalChars` / `truncated` are untouched.

New test: `dataset preview keeps an unclosed quote as one field` — 64 KB body, asserts one column that equals the whole quoted body, `rows` empty, `totalRows 0`, `truncated false`. It pins the parsed result only; no timing assertion, since CI machines are noisy.

Behaviour equivalence: 400 randomized csv/tsv inputs (fixed seed; alphabet includes `,`, `\t`, `\n`, `\r`, `"`, spaces, non-ASCII) produce an identical sha256 digest of every payload (`mode`, `columns`, `rows`, `totalRows`, `truncated`) before and after this commit. Security additionally ran 200k random inputs plus 12 targeted cases with identical output.

Local cost of the same unclosed-quote file through `buildArtifactVersionPreview` (one process per size, this host):

| file | before `29a49360` | after `5f946116` |
|---|---|---|
| 8 MB | 1764 ms / 421 MB RSS | 118 ms / 174 MB |
| 16 MB | 3708 ms / 674 MB RSS | 353 ms / 190 MB |

The 32 MB row and the 200k-input differential run are Security's, from their local probe; the 8/16 MB pairs are mine.

## Ran

- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern="parses quoted csv cells" src/dashboard.test.ts` → 0/1 red on the test commit, 1/1 green after the fix
- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts` → **32/32**, and **33/33** with the perf commit (the new unclosed-quote case is the 33rd)
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` → 0
- quoted-newline + CRLF, quoted-tab + blank-line checks described above → both green

## Not run

- The whole `services/api` suite (it is long and needs every workspace package built): only `src/dashboard.test.ts`, the file that owns the preview, plus the package typecheck.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` verbatim: on this host pnpm's dependency-status check aborts on the read-only store (`EROFS`), so the commands were run directly.

Release: fix

Fixes #641

`VersionStore.putWorkspaceFile` decided reuse from `fstat` identity only (`dev`/`ino`/`size`/`mtimeNs`/`ctimeNs`) and returned the cached `DataRef` without reading the file. A same-size in-place rewrite inside one filesystem timestamp tick therefore kept the stale bytes in workspace snapshots. The cached *object* identity had the same blind spot, so a same-size tamper of an existing CAS object was reused with no verification at all. The class comment already said "file metadata is never taken as evidence"; the implementation contradicted it.

Branch cut from live `main` `d72cdf8c` (the issue's `5e56ea77` line is the filing snapshot; `packages/cas` did not change in between, `versioning.ts` is still blob `679f5a61`).

## What changes

- Reuse now requires both: the current bytes hash to the cached ref, and `verifyRef` re-verifies the stored object. Metadata still narrows the work (a changed identity skips the digest pass) but it never decides reuse.
- Changed bytes fall back to the existing streaming publish path; an unchanged file still avoids the temp write, the `fsync`, the `link` and the directory `fsync`, which is the cost the cache exists to save.
- `objectIdentity` is removed: copying the object's stat fields into the cache is exactly what made a same-tick tamper invisible, and the byte verification supersedes it.

## Red → green

Red before the fix — the loop fails on the second round, not merely "sometimes":

```
not ok 1 - a same-size in-place rewrite never reuses stale workspace bytes
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly equal:
    + actual - expected
    + 'bbbbbbbbb0'
    - 'aaaaaaaaa1'
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

Measured on `d72cdf8c` over 200 rounds: `digest_reused=171 first_put_stale_bytes=174 second_put_stale_bytes=171` (the digest-count difference is cross-round reuse of the previous round's ref).

Green after the fix:

```
ok 1 - a same-size in-place rewrite never reuses stale workspace bytes
ok 2 - unchanged workspace bytes are still reused without republishing
# pass 2
# fail 0
```

Same 200-round probe: `digest_reused=0 first_put_stale_bytes=0 second_put_stale_bytes=0`.

## Validation

Ran on `25272529` (local tree; fork commit `abc6f8c5` carries the same tree):

- `cd packages/cas && node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"` — **3 consecutive runs, 36/36 pass, 0 fail each** (34 existing + 2 new).
- 200-round reproduction from the issue (with a byte check on the returned ref): **0/200 stale**, was 171/200 reusing the stale ref.
- `tsc -p packages/cas/tsconfig.json`: build exit 0, `--noEmit` exit 0.

Not run locally: `ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e`. This diff only touches `packages/cas`, whose UT suite is the one above; the full-repo layers are the gate in this pull request's own CI run.

## The existing `Missing expected rejection` flake at `versioning.test.ts:290`

It is the same root cause, not an unrelated flake, and the assertion is unchanged. On this host it passed 20/20 standalone and 3/3 full-suite runs on `d72cdf8c`, so it did not reproduce here; it only fails when the tamper write lands inside the cached object's timestamp tick. A direct probe that tampers the object immediately after caching reproduces the same gap **197/200**, and after this fix that probe is **200/200 `Object integrity failure`, 0 silent reuse** — so the test no longer depends on tick luck.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable: no user-observable path changes. `packages/cas` is internal storage; the CAS suite above is the coverage.

## Release

Release category: release:fix (the GitHub label needs a maintainer; it is pending, not applied)

User impact: a workspace snapshot no longer records stale bytes after a same-size in-place rewrite, and a tampered CAS object is reported instead of being reused.

Compatibility and migration: none.

recent_merged.author: HongyeZhou
recent_merged.body:
Nightly real-model E2E treated a single transient model-gateway HTTP 500/503 the same as a product run that finished and failed to deliver, so one provider outage failed the whole Daily gate while other cases in the same job still passed. This change keeps the provider error visible, soft-classifies those faults, optionally repeats an early fault once, and leaves product failures hard-failing.

**The required real-E2E check now has a floor: a planned case that only faulted is an unverified case, and the check does not pass on it.** A soft classification is not a soft green.

After the optional early repeat, a case that passes on the repeat is a genuine `PASS` and the check may go green; a case that still faults keeps the `PROVIDER_FAULT` status and makes the check non-pass.

Closes #232

## The gate floor

| Outcome | Status | Exit code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Every planned case passed | `PASS` | 0 |
| A provider fault remains, no product failure | `PROVIDER_FAULT` | non-zero |
| A product failure | `FAIL` | non-zero |

The two failure kinds stay apart: a provider fault is still reported as `PROVIDER_FAULT: <case>` and never as `FAIL: <case>`, and a product failure is never softened into an outage. Neither one is a pass. The floor is the same in every place that decides, for the daily, merge L3 and release L5 profiles alike — no profile can turn an outage into a green required check:

- **`verifyResults`** (`test/support/tagged/plan.mjs`): the exit code is 1 whenever a provider fault or a product problem remains; the status is `PROVIDER_FAULT` for a fault, `FAIL` for a product failure, `PASS` only for a run without either.
- **the worker** (`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`): a repeat that did not work is audited in the accounting (`PROVIDER_FAULT_REPEAT_FAILED`, `PROVIDER_FAULT_REPEAT_REPORT_MISSING`) instead of only in the log; a batch that faulted as a whole is probed with a couple of repeats instead of re-running every case; a worker whose only failures were provider faults is not double-counted as an opaque worker failure, and the summary's exit code is 1 while a fault remains.
- **the suite reconcile** (`.ci/real-report.mjs`): a provider-fault shard is valid evidence — the identity checks still apply — whose results are folded into the suite accounting; the suite's exit code comes from that accounting, so a remaining fault makes it non-zero. The provider-fault problems stay visible instead of being flattened into an opaque `SHARD_FAILED`, and a shard cannot hide a fault behind a `PASS` it did not earn.
- **the shared-plan summary** (`.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`): a provider fault is a problem of its own, `planned == executed == passed` is still required, and `passed + provider faults == planned` is no longer enough for green.

## The detector

The provider context has to name the gateway itself: its `181001` model-call code, the wording of a failed model call, the API it answers on, or its own routing failure. Bare words — "provider", "llm", "gateway", "upstream" — are not context: a product delivery failure that mentions one beside a `500` is the product's own failure and stays a `FAIL`. A delivery miss or an assertion diff is the product's own report in the first place and is never soft-classified.

The gateway's own report is unchanged: the `181001` model-call code, the openAI API stream error and the routing failures recorded in the Nightly of 2026-10-06 are still detected as provider faults, and the provider's text is still kept verbatim.

## What changed
- `test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs`: the tightened provider context, the product-report reject, and the audit codes a failed repeat leaves behind.
- `test/support/tagged/plan.mjs`: the exit-code floor in `verifyResults`; the status of a provider fault stays `PROVIDER_FAULT`.
- `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`: the audited repeat, the capped outage probe, and the worker-failure pairing with the attempt whose exit code it explains.
- `.ci/real-report.mjs`: the reconcile keeps a provider-fault shard's evidence and the suite's exit code follows the accounting.
- `.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`: a provider fault is a problem of its own.
- Docs in `.ci/README.md` and `test/support/tagged/README.md`.
- Tests in `.ci/provider-fault.test.mjs`.

Product agent loop, model client, and run orchestration are untouched: only the CI harness and its accounting changed.

## Scenario coverage
| ID | Scenario | Coverage | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S1 | Gateway HTTP 500 / `new_api_error` / 181001 | `.ci/provider-fault.test.mjs` | `PROVIDER_FAULT`, text preserved |
| S2 | Gateway HTTP 503 channel / `model_not_found` | same | `PROVIDER_FAULT` |
| S3 | Product delivery failure | same | hard `FAIL`, exit 1 |
| S4 | Mixed job (PASS + provider fault; PASS + product FAIL) | same + reconcile | passes stay PASS; the job does not pass |
| S5 | 401 / 429 / semantic | same | never soft-classified |
| S6 | Mocked visible-gateway-error journey (#234) | hermetic: still `@mocked`/`@model:mock`; never soft-classified | unchanged |
| S7 | All cases faulted, none passed | same + reconcile | status `PROVIDER_FAULT`, exit 1, no `FAIL:` problem |
| S8 | A product failure that quotes a provider status | same | stays a product `FAIL` |
| S9 | A repeat that did not work | same | audited under the provider-fault family, exit 1 |
| S10 | The shared-plan summary over a faulted layer | same (spawned over a temp results dir) | exit 1, fault visible in the table |

## Validation
| Layer | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Own S1–S10 (`.ci/provider-fault.test.mjs`) | PASS 18/18 |
| `.ci/*.test.mjs` (incl. new) | PASS 101/101 |
| L1 | PASS 4/4 |
| UT | 4857 planned/executed, 4849 PASS, 8 FAIL — the same pre-existing box environment classes as on the base commit (OpenSSH key derivation, workspace host path, scientific R/Python egress, runner NPU broker); the same files fail on the clean tree, and no provider-fault case fails |
| ST | PASS 24/24 |
| L3 merge/e2e-real legacy | PASS 9/9 on `7ec0b43a0e56c7c7c2784fae7a813d0e50f4fe20` |

## E2E user journeys
PASS on SHA `7ec0b43a0e56c7c7c2784fae7a813d0e50f4fe20`; API / real-model; profile `merge`, backend `legacy`, `CI_ALLOW_REAL=1`.

Command: `pnpm ci:e2e:real -- --profile merge --backend legacy`

| Journey | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L3-response: Short response and stream completion | pass | PASS |
| L3-tool: A real command result reaches the final answer | pass | PASS |
| L3-files: Read and edit a workspace file without changing its neighbour | pass | PASS |
| L3-memory: Reopen a Session and recall its previous turn | pass | PASS |
| L3-artifact: A delivered version remains readable after follow-up | pass | PASS |
| L3-workspace: Relative file writes stay in the selected Session | pass | PASS |
| L3-cancel: Cancel a live run and continue the session | pass | PASS |
| L3-runner-wait: real model requests user help and resumes after cancellation | pass | PASS |
| L3-runner-finish: real model honors the request to explain failure without waiting | pass | PASS |

Counts: passed 9 / failed 0 / blocked 0 / skipped 0. Tagged summary: status `PASS`, exit code 0, provider faults 0.

Issue acceptance is covered: a gateway 500/503 is visible as a provider error (S1, S2); it does not mean the same as a product delivery miss (S3, S8); the cases that passed in the same job stay passes (S4); the gate does not treat an outage or an incomplete verification as success (S7, S9, S10 — the floor); and no business main-path file changed.

**What type of PR is this?**
/kind task

**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:
A regular CI run on the same ref can cancel a long manual validation. Add a dispatch-only `Manual validation` workflow with an independent concurrency group.

- Call `.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml` directly with the existing cumulative `l5` profile. This executes the L3+L4+L5 real-model E2E slice, including all BiomniBench-DA public 50 cases and their existing completeness/metrics gates. It does not run the L1/L2 or mocked CI jobs.
- Default to `jiuwenswarm` and four concurrent real E2E workers; expose only `backend` (`jiuwenswarm` / `legacy`) and `max-parallel` (1 / 2 / 4). No new profile or case-selection policy is introduced.
- Use `manual-validation-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true`: regular CI cannot cancel this workflow; a newer manual dispatch on the same ref cancels the previous manual run and its unfinished work.
- Retain `permissions: contents: read`, `secrets: inherit`, and the reusable workflow's existing `nightly-ci-ds` environment/model/judge credentials.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
No linked issue.

**What scenarios were tested, and what were the verification results（Function, performance, reliability, etc.）**：
- Inspected the final PR diff: one new workflow; existing profiles, gates and reusable workflow execution logic are unchanged.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Local test cases were not run, as requested. This manual workflow has not been dispatched, so its end-to-end execution remains unverified.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:
The entry appears in Actions after merge to the default branch. It has no automatic push, pull request or schedule trigger. A dispatch uses shared real-model/judge budget and may take hours, depending on case/model latency and the worker limit; this is not a measured runtime estimate. fix(desktop): keep the carried newline when the next chunk normalizes to nothing

## Why this is a separate PR

#621 was merged at `863969c2265a0645aa4d5333e0a8f7d0cae59a1f` — the merge queue's group commit, built from that PR's **pre-fix** head `e5e8cecf`. What landed on `main` is therefore the tree as it stood before the last fix in that PR: `apps/desktop/src/api/stream.ts` blob `6c7ffb2cac0711b61474a54c6c372306df24513e` (no `if (chunk === "") return [];`), tests at 30. The fix commit `514ba9faa7e99592c3fc64c41f10397651bad5b3` is not an ancestor of `main`.

The defect below is on `main` now. This PR carries that one-line guard and its two tests, rebased onto current `main`, and nothing else: `stream.ts` `+5/−0` (4 comment lines and the guard), tests `+34/−0` (two tests, 30 → 32).

## The defect, on current `main`

While the decoder is discarding an oversized frame, a chunk that ends in `\n` sets `sawOneNewlineWhileDiscarding`. If the next chunk normalizes to the empty string — a lone `"\r"`, i.e. the CR of a CRLF blank line arriving in its own read, or an empty chunk — `stream.ts:106` runs `this.sawOneNewlineWhileDiscarding = chunk.endsWith("\n")` and clears the carry. The chunk after that then has its own `\n\n` taken as the dropped frame's terminator, so that legal frame is consumed, never parsed, and the skip counter still says one.

Reachability: entering the state needs a frame past `MAX_FRAME_CHARACTERS` (8 MiB) first, so an honest server never gets there and a sender that got there already owns the stream — impact on both is nil. It is a correctness defect in the state machine #621 added, not a widening of the security surface.

Red on `main`'s blob `6c7ffb2c`, probe importing the real `SseFrameDecoder` (`node --experimental-strip-types`):

```
A lone-CR-then-frame-8: frames: [] skipped: [null]                     <- frame 8 swallowed
B empty-chunk-then-frame-9: frames: [] skipped: [null]                 <- frame 9 swallowed
C control (no empty chunk): frames: [{"data":"{}","id":10}] skipped: [null]
```

The two tests added here, lifted verbatim and run against that same blob:

```
not ok 1 - an empty chunk does not lose the carried newline while discarding
  Expected values to be strictly deep-equal: + actual [] - expected [ { data: '{"type":"run.status"}', id: 8 } ]
not ok 2 - a lone carriage return between the two halves of a blank line keeps the resync
  Expected values to be strictly deep-equal: + actual [] - expected [ { data: '{"type":"run.status"}', id: 9 } ]
# tests 2  # pass 0  # fail 2        (ERR_ASSERTION, exit 1)
```

Run against this tip's blob the same two tests pass, and the pre-existing CRLF-split test is green on both blobs, so the red is specific to the two new paths and the normal path is unaffected.

## The fix

`if (chunk === "") return [];` immediately after normalization and before the `discarding` branch: an empty chunk carries no information, so the carry, `pendingCarriageReturn` and the buffer all stay as they were. `pendingCarriageReturn` is set before that point, so the early return cannot lose a held `\r`.

Same probe after the fix: A `[{"data":"{\"type\":\"run.status\"}","id":8}]`, B `[{"data":"{}","id":9}]`, C unchanged.

## Verification

On this tip (rebased onto `863969c2`, current `main`):

- `apps/desktop/tests/api-client.test.ts`: **32/32 pass**
- full desktop suite: **663/663 pass** (92 suites) — the count is larger than the one in #621 because `main` has gained tests since that branch was cut
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: **exit 0**
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`: **exit 0**

## Queue facts behind the merge (stated, not argued)

- The queue entry predates the fix commit: `enqueuedAt 2026-10-29T00:35:29Z`, group commit `863969c2` built from head `e5e8cecf`.
- The fix `514ba9fa` was pushed at `2026-10-29T00:59:16Z`; the same second GitHub recorded `review_dismissed` on that PR.
- The group's checks finished green and the queue merged `863969c2` at `2026-10-29T01:06:36Z`. The `merge-gate` job aggregates only the current event's job results (`.ci/tier-policy.mjs gate`, `ci.yml:817-849`), so it reported success while `reviewDecision` was `REVIEW_REQUIRED`.
- Net effect: `main` received the pre-fix tree. This PR is the follow-up.

Follow-up to #621; the original report is #619.

Release: fix

recent_merged.author: HugoXK
recent_merged.body:
fix(desktop): cap the SSE frame decoder buffer so an unterminated frame stays bounded

Status: `514ba9fa` supersedes the approved `e5e8cecf`. The approval given at `e5e8cecf` is void by this push — `514ba9fa` is the only tip to score. Re-reading that approved code turned up one more edge (fourth, below); it is fixed here with two red-first tests.

## Problem

`SseFrameDecoder` keeps a partial frame in memory until it sees the `\n\n` terminator, and nothing bounds that buffer while the stream is open. A writer that keeps sending bytes for a frame it never terminates therefore grows the retained buffer for as long as the stream lives — the live window, which is exactly the case of a running run. Because `drain` re-normalised the whole buffer on every chunk, the work also grew quadratically: measured on the old code, 5 000 pushes cost 181 ms, 10 000 cost 1 056 ms, 20 000 cost 4 350 ms for 680 000 characters.

This is pre-existing on `main` and is a framing failure, not a `JSON.parse` failure: no complete frame is ever handed to the parser. #616 covered the end-of-stream tail and the unparseable payload; this closes the live window.

## Contract as the issue now states it

The ceiling is a module constant, `MAX_FRAME_CHARACTERS = 8 * 1024 * 1024` — no setting, consistent with #505.

Past the ceiling the frame is dropped **once**: bytes are discarded up to and including the next `\n\n` (that terminator closes the oversized frame, it does not start a new one), the dropped tail never reaches `JSON.parse`, and parsing resumes after the terminator, so later well-formed frames still arrive and one bad frame does not end a live run. The skip is reported through the skipped-frame path that #616 added: `skipped += 1` and `onEvent(null, id)` in `pump`, with the single existing "Skipped N updates that could not be read." notice — no second notice and no new error mode.

The cursor of a dropped frame comes only from an `id:` line that was fully received (newline-terminated) before the drop; an `id:` line still waiting for its newline may be the prefix of a longer number, so it yields nothing and the replay cursor stays at the last fully received frame. Bytes after the drop are never parsed, so a crafted `data:` line in the tail cannot be re-interpreted as a new event.

Also included, as the issue's optional item: only newly arrived text is normalised now (`pendingCarriageReturn` plus an `unscanned` search offset), which removes the quadratic term while keeping a `\r\n` split across chunks a single line break.

Out of scope and unchanged, as the issue says: a peer that simply stops writing still keeps the stream open (stall/liveness, not memory), and a clean close with no parsed terminal remains silent on the follow path (`use-workspace.ts`, `closeRunStream` sets `terminal: true`). This change does not address either.

## Red-first evidence (first round)

The cap test, with the ceiling guard disabled:

```
not ok - a frame that never terminates stops at the cap and is reported as a skipped frame
Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
+ actual [] - expected [ 4 ]
```

The terminator test, with the drop reset at the drop point instead of discarding through `\n\n` (so the crafted tail reaches the parser):

```
not ok 1 - the decoder resynchronises at the next blank line after a dropped frame
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected

    + [
    +   {
    +     data: '{"type":"injected"}more tail'
    +   }
    + ]
    - []

  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
  operator: 'deepStrictEqual'
  stack: TestContext.<anonymous> (apps/desktop/tests/api-client.test.ts:273:10)
```

Both probes exit 1; the code was restored afterwards and the tree is clean.

## First review round: the discard could swallow the next frame

`zy95-12` (blocking) and the upstream bot (Medium) found this on `6e1d2dfc09`: while `discarding` was true the decoder looked for `"\n\n"` only inside the current chunk, so a blank line split across two chunks (`push("\n")` then `push("\n")`) never matched, `discarding` never cleared, and the next well-formed frame was discarded as if it belonged to the oversized one — with `takeSkipped()` undercounting.

Observed before the fix, at `6e1d2dfc09`:

```
skipped after overflow: [7]
push('\n'): []
push('\n'): []
valid frame after it: []        <- id: 8 swallowed
```

Fixed by carrying one newline across the chunk boundary on the discard path (`sawOneNewlineWhileDiscarding`, the same idea as `unscanned` on the assemble path), plus a red-first test `a dropped frame ends when its blank line arrives split across chunks`. The same probe after the fix:

```
push('\n'): []
push('\n'): []
valid frame: [{"data":"{\"type\":\"run.status\"}","id":8}]
skipped total: []
```

## Second review round: the carry must win over the next frame's own terminator

`zy95-12` blocking review `5680942212` and `HongyeZhou` review `5680995412` at `45388fb5` found the remaining ordering hole: with a carried `\n` pending, `push` still searched the chunk for `\n\n` first, so a chunk shaped `"\n" + a complete next frame` had that frame's own `\n\n` taken as the oversized frame's terminator — the next frame was discarded and `takeSkipped()` undercounted. Fixed by testing the carried newline before the in-chunk search: those two bytes close the dropped frame and the rest of the chunk assembles normally.

Two boundary defects from our own Security read at the same tip, fixed and pinned in the same push:

- `frameCursor` returned the first fully received `id:` line while `parseFrame` uses the last, so a dropped frame with two ids moved the replay cursor by the wrong one;
- a legal frame whose content is exactly `MAX_FRAME_CHARACTERS` was dropped when its blank line arrived split, because the first terminator byte made the buffer `MAX + 1`; one trailing `\n` is framing, not payload, and no longer counts toward the cap.

Each blocking finding has its test:

| Finding | Test |
|---|---|
| `zy95-12` `5680942212` / `HongyeZhou` `5680995412`: in-chunk `\n\n` beats the carried newline and swallows the next frame | `a dropped frame does not swallow a complete frame carried in the same chunk` |
| internal: `frameCursor` used the first `id:` line while `parseFrame` uses the last | `a dropped frame moves the cursor by the last id line it fully received` |
| internal: a frame exactly at the ceiling was dropped when its terminator split | `a frame exactly at the ceiling still parses when its terminator is split` |
| internal (found by re-reading the code after the `e5e8cecf` approval): an empty or lone-CR chunk in the middle of a discard cleared the carried newline, so the next legal frame was swallowed | `an empty chunk does not lose the carried newline while discarding`; `a lone carriage return between the two halves of a blank line keeps the resync` |

Red on `45388fb5` (its `stream.ts` blob `ce2db31d` is identical to `af16898b`). The three tests failed there:

```
(a) a dropped frame does not swallow a complete frame carried in the same chunk
    + actual [] - expected [ { data: '{"type":"run.status"}', id: 8 } ]
(b) a frame exactly at the ceiling still parses when its terminator is split
    + actual [] - expected [ { data: 'zzz…' (8 388 580 chars), id: 9 } ]
(c) a dropped frame moves the cursor by the last id line it fully received
    + actual 3 - expected 4
```

The old decoder observed directly shows the same three failures: `skipped [7]` then `frames []` after the carry, `skipped [9]` with `0` frames at the cap boundary, and `skipped [3]` instead of `[4]`.

## Fourth edge, found after the approval

Review re-read at `e5e8cecf` (this is the same blob this PR was approved on, `stream.ts` `6c7ffb2c`) found one more way for the discard path to swallow a legal frame — the invariant the previous two rounds closed, with an edge neither review nor I had covered.

Shape: while `discarding` is true, a chunk that ends with `\n` sets `sawOneNewlineWhileDiscarding`. If the **next** chunk normalizes to the empty string — a lone `"\r"`, i.e. the CR of a CRLF blank line arriving in its own one-byte read, or an empty chunk — line 106 ran `this.sawOneNewlineWhileDiscarding = chunk.endsWith("\n")` and cleared the carry. The chunk after that then had its own `\n\n` taken as the dropped frame's terminator, so that legal frame was consumed and never parsed, and the skip counter still said one.

Reachability: entering the state needs a frame past `MAX_FRAME_CHARACTERS` (8 MiB) first, so an honest server never gets there and a malicious one already owns the stream — impact on both is nil. It is a correctness defect in this new state machine, not a widening of the security surface.

Reproduced at `e5e8cecf` with a probe importing the real `SseFrameDecoder` (`node --experimental-strip-types`), before the fix:

```
A lone-CR-then-frame-8:  frames: []  skipped: [null]                     <- frame 8 swallowed
B empty-chunk-then-9:    frames: []  skipped: [null]                     <- frame 9 swallowed
C control (no empty chunk): frames: [{"data":"{}","id":10}] skipped: [null]
```

Fixed by returning early from `push` when the normalized chunk is empty (`if (chunk === "") return [];` right after normalization): an empty chunk carries no information, so the carry, `pendingCarriageReturn` and the buffer all stay as they were. Same probe after the fix: A `[{"data":"{\"type\":\"run.status\"}","id":8}]`, B `[{"data":"{}","id":9}]`, C unchanged. Two red-first tests pin it: `an empty chunk does not lose the carried newline while discarding` and `a lone carriage return between the two halves of a blank line keeps the resync`. Both fail on the approved blob unpatched (`6c7ffb2c`, `ERR_ASSERTION`, exit 1):

```
(a) an empty chunk does not lose the carried newline while discarding
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual [] - expected [ { data: '{"type":"run.status"}', id: 8 } ]
(b) a lone carriage return between the two halves of a blank line keeps the resync
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual [] - expected [ { data: '{"type":"run.status"}', id: 9 } ]
```

## Verification

On tip (rebased onto `080a8c80`, current `main`):

- `apps/desktop/tests/api-client.test.ts`: **32/32 pass**
- full desktop suite: **579/579 pass** (89 suites)
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck`: **exit 0**
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: **exit 0**

Tests added or strengthened in `apps/desktop/tests/api-client.test.ts`:

- `a frame that never terminates stops at the cap and is reported as a skipped frame` — exactly at the ceiling nothing is dropped; one character past it the frame is skipped once with its cursor, and `flush()` returns nothing.
- `the decoder resynchronises at the next blank line after a dropped frame` — a crafted `data: {"type":"injected"}` tail yields no frame and no extra skip; the terminator closes the frame and a following valid frame arrives intact.
- `a dropped frame moves the cursor only by an id line that fully arrived` — `[undefined]` when the `id:` line never completed.
- `a dropped frame ends when its blank line arrives split across chunks` — after a drop, `push("\n")` then `push("\n")` ends the discard, and the following `id: 8` frame is delivered while the drop is still counted once.
- `a dropped frame does not swallow a complete frame carried in the same chunk` — after a drop, `push("\n")` then a chunk that starts with `\n` and carries a complete `id: 8` frame closes the drop and delivers id 8; that frame's own `\n\n` is not mistaken for the drop's terminator.
- `a frame exactly at the ceiling still parses when its terminator is split` — content exactly `MAX_FRAME_CHARACTERS`, first newline alone, second closes it; the frame is delivered and nothing is skipped.
- `a dropped frame moves the cursor by the last id line it fully received` — `id: 3` then `id: 4` before the drop yields `[4]`, matching `parseFrame`.
- `a live stream keeps delivering frames after an unterminated one is dropped`.
- `a frame below the ceiling still parses in full` — a 1 MiB report frame.
- `the frame ceiling is a module constant, not a configurable setting` — `MAX_FRAME_CHARACTERS === 8 * 1024 * 1024` and `SseFrameDecoder.length === 0` (zero-argument constructor, so no options object can carry a cap in).
- `a CRLF split across chunks is still one line break`.
- `an empty chunk does not lose the carried newline while discarding` — after a drop, a chunk ending in `\n` then `push("")`; the carry survives and the following `id: 8` frame is delivered.
- `a lone carriage return between the two halves of a blank line keeps the resync` — the same, with the empty-slot chunk being a lone `"\r"` (a CRLF blank line split across two reads): the frame is still delivered.

## Why 8 MiB

`MAX_BODY_BYTES` 1.5 MB for the largest request the client sends, `DEFAULT_TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES` 50 KiB for a whole tool result, a workspace listing capped at 500 entries (about 125 KB of paths and sizes), and `artifact.upserted` carrying a CAS reference rather than the artifact's bytes. The largest legitimate frame is a long model report — a few hundred KiB even with a raised token budget — so 8 MiB leaves well over an order of magnitude of headroom while still bounding a stalled writer.

Fixes #619

Release: fix

The desktop SSH credential dialog only sends nonempty replacements, so users cannot ask the API to forget stored credentials. Add one explicit checkbox in the existing dialog to forget the saved password, private key and passphrase on save. Blank fields still preserve stored values by default; the forget selection disables replacement fields until unchecked, and users can save new credentials later.

Fixes #507.

## Validation

- Before the fix, the new browser regression fails because no forget control exists.
- After the fix, all 14 desktop remote-host Chromium journeys pass (0 failed, 0 skipped), including blank-save preservation, explicit null payloads for all three credential fields, cleared password/key flags, and a later replacement password. HTTP responses are mocked; no real SSH connection is claimed.
- The new three-step journey also checks the forget control is reachable at 390px and 1280px; screenshots were inspected. Existing narrow machine-card header wrapping remains outside this credential-change scope.
- Desktop TypeScript check and git diff --check: passed.
- UT/ST/shared browser E2E were attempted on Windows and stop in preparation with spawn pnpm ENOENT before selected tests execute. Full Linux gates for this exact head remain pending; this stays draft.

## E2E user journeys

PASS: 14 desktop browser journeys at 55819b42, with mocked HTTP API and actual rendered controls. The new journey verifies keep → forget → replace. Real SSH probing/authentication and persistence against a live backend are not covered by these browser mocks and remain a validation gap.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: users can explicitly remove stored SSH secrets without deleting and recreating the remote host.
Compatibility and migration: none; default blank-field preservation and write-only credential behavior are unchanged. No secret is read back into the dialog.

recent_merged.body:
## Problem and change

A host data symlink can exist in a Session workspace yet resolve to an unreadable location inside the sandbox. A command can then silently take a synthetic-data fallback and report success. Check workspace symlink readability in the actual execution sandbox before Shell or Python/R evaluation, and reject inaccessible links with the link path and actionable copy/upload guidance.

Valid relative, chained, sandbox-visible absolute and runtime links remain supported. Reused Shell/scientific sessions recheck their mounted workspaces. Filenames are passed as NUL-separated raw bytes, preserving Linux filenames and avoiding shell interpolation. English and Chinese documentation explains workspace paths, materialization and the managed-workspace-only scope of `workspace_transfer`.

## Scope and issue disposition

Refs #433. Partial fix; keep #433 open pending complete repository verification and review.

The operator selected explicit rejection and import guidance instead of automatic copying. This PR does not introduce an arbitrary-host-directory mount/import UI. Validation happens before evaluation; this is not a filesystem watcher and does not guarantee detection of unmanaged changes after preflight or links created within the same command. Direct host execution is unchanged.

## Baseline and candidate

- Reproduction baseline: `7bef5b2661e92fb881d96eb50f94f4b2775652d2`. Through production Runner HTTP, an absolute host data link caused `SYNTHETIC_FALLBACK`, exit code 0, and an execution marker.
- Tested implementation: `576db3d098b15edd54d925a45fbae21112e42305` on Linux with bubblewrap, isolated data/ports, matching service lockfiles, and the previously installed pinned `workswarm0.2.6` environment. Editable Python packages point at the tested checkout.
- PR head: `de9ee975c` rebased onto main `3d223ede7bce633de8f954e2ec8a23c695a5de23`. The unrelated coverage change from the reproduction baseline is excluded. Results below belong to the tested implementation SHA; no complete current-head CI pass is claimed.

## Acceptance evidence

| Scenario | Expected and observed result | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Host-only absolute data link | Reject before Shell code, name the link, explain real-file import; no execution marker | Production Runner HTTP journey, step 2 |
| Python and accepted background Shell | Python rejects; background state is queryably failed with guidance; neither writes its marker | HTTP journey, step 3 |
| Materialize real data, then use a relative link | Same workspace recovers; Shell and Python both compute and persist 5 from the real input | HTTP journey, steps 4–5 |
| Valid relative/chained/sandbox-absolute/runtime links and raw filenames | Remain readable and usable | Runner regression tests |
| Relative escapes, dangling/cyclic links and special filenames | Reject clearly without executing injected filename content | Runner regression tests |
| Read-only parent and reused Shell | Use actual nested mount paths; recheck on reuse and recover while retaining Shell state | Runner regression tests |
| Import guidance | Describe sandbox visibility and copy/upload/managed transfer boundaries | English/Chinese reference docs; L1 |

## Repository checks

Recorded at `576db3d098b15edd54d925a45fbae21112e42305`:

| Command | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed | Skipped | Status |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `pnpm ci:l1` | 4 | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 | PASS |
| `pnpm ci:ut` | 4440 | 4440 | 4437 | 3 | 0 | FAIL; details below |
| `pnpm ci:st` | 24 | 24 | 22 | 2 | 0 | FAIL; details below |
| `pnpm ci:e2e` | 100 | Not final | Not final | Not final | Not final | Still running when this draft was opened; research fixture finished 20/20 passing |
| Focused Runner regressions plus existing Shell-session tests | 14 | 14 | 14 | 0 | 0 | PASS |
| `pnpm typecheck` | — | — | — | — | — | PASS |

Known full-suite failures:

- UT: the Agent-created Skill draft assertion (`0 !== 1`), sandbox-network test (`bwrap: Unknown option --disable-userns` on the host's old bubblewrap), and research Python check (pinned `pandas==2.3.3` needs a compatible cached distribution under offline preparation). Each was reproduced with targeted checks at the unmodified `7bef5b26` baseline; this is not a claim that the full baseline suite passed.
- ST: the pinned standalone Python distribution download failed (`fetch failed`), and the MCP 100-concurrent-call contract timed out. The MCP failure also reproduces in a targeted baseline check. These checks remain failures; assertions and selection were not weakened.

## E2E user journey

`node test/api/workspace-data-visibility-journey.mjs`: **PASS**, planned/executed/passed **5/5/5**, failed/skipped **0/0**, tested SHA `576db3d098b15edd54d925a45fbae21112e42305`.

The driver starts the production Runner CLI, sends authenticated HTTP requests, observes rejection and durable background failure, materializes a real fixture, and verifies persistent Shell/Python calculation results. It uses no model or external data service. This validates data visibility and recovery, not a complete NatureBench scientific reproduction. The mocked browser slice is reported separately above and is not substituted for this journey.

## Remaining gaps

Keep this PR as a draft: the broad browser run is still in progress, full UT/ST are not green, and full verification after rebasing onto current main is pending. Do not close the issue from this PR yet.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix`.

Users receive an explicit sandbox-data error instead of silently proceeding with inaccessible input. Existing workspaces with broken links must remove those links and copy/upload real data or use valid workspace-relative links before retrying.
